ADJUSTMENTS

Vehicle Lean Correction

 CAUTION: Frame twisting should not be attempted to correct vehicle lean because 
it can cause frame damage. 

Before attempting any correction, the cause for excessive lean must be 
determined. The following measurements must be made without payload on the 
vehicle and with all vehicle fluid levels at full.

Place the vehicle on a flat surface, and fill all tires to the 
recommended inflation pressures. Measure and record the ride height (ride 
height is the perpendicular distance between the top of the axle and the 
bottom of the frame rail). Measure and record the distance between the lower 
flange of the bumper ends and ground for both the left and right side of the 
vehicle.

Corrections should not be attempted on vehicles with a bumper-to-ground 
right-to-left height variation of 25.4 mm (1 inch) or less. Corrections should 
not be made if the right height variation is 12.7 mm (1/2 inch or less).

If a front spring spacer is needed to correct a vehicle lean condition, 
use the following procedure: 

Raise the vehicle by the frame until the tire comes off the ground and 
place a jack stand under the frame to retain that height. 

Raise the axle slightly with a jack to remove the weight from the 
spring. 

Remove the U-bolt nuts and the U-bolts. 

Lower the axle slightly to allow enough clearance between the bottom of 
the spring and the top of the axle so the 3/4-inch spacer can be installed. 

 NOTE: If a spacer is in place, remove the spacer on the opposite side to 
eliminate the lean condition. 

Install the spacer between the spring and axle, making sure that the 
locating pin is facing down.

[FIGURE: F7725B.gif]

Raise the axle to the spring and reinstall the applicable U-bolts with 
hardened flatwashers and attaching nuts. Refer to Spring Spacer Usage Chart.

ADJUSTMENTS

Steering Stop

The steering wheel stop bolt does not normally require adjustment. To 
check for proper length, measure from the machined surface on the steering arm 
or spindle to the top of the bolt. The correct dimension for different tire 
zones, wheelbase and axle combinations is given in the Front Wheel Turn Angle 
Specifications chart. Refer to the tire zone tables in the Specifications 
portion of this section to determine the tire zone.

ADJUSTMENTS

Drive Axle Adjustments 

 Hendrickson Walking Beam Suspension 

Misalignment of Hendrickson Walking Beam Suspension must be checked. 
Although no single point for alignment adjustment is currently provided, frame 
attachment brackets, axle attachments and spring-to-saddle location are all 
items to be checked. 

Correct a misalignment condition through the following procedures: 

Loosen the frame bracket retaining bolts and the spring-to-saddle bolts 
to allow freedom of movement. 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to move the off-axle hanger brackets with respect to the 
axle housing. The welds at this interface are critical to the structural 
integrity of the axle housing. If axle misalignment cannot be corrected by the 
above procedure and is determined to be caused by the off-axle brackets, 
review the condition with the service manager and contact the axle 
manufacturer's representative. 

Move the axles until square to frame (within 5 mm [3/16 inch]) and 
parallel to each other (within 3 mm [1/8 inch]).

Retighten all fasteners to original torque specifications.

 NOTE: The following steps should be performed after all service has been 
completed and all suspension fasteners have been tightened to specified torque 
values.

Begin alignment by checking rear rear drive axle first. Use a trammel 
bar or its equivalent to measure from straightedge to centerline of rear rear 
drive axle on both sides of vehicle (Ll and Lr in the illustration). If both 
sides measure within 5 mm (3/16 inch) of each other, alignment of rear rear 
drive axle is acceptable.

[FIGURE: F37051A.gif]

If Ll and Lr differ by more than 5 mm (3/16 inch), adjust rear rear 
drive axle by loosening up torque rod bar pin lock nuts on center spring 
hanger, and add drop-in shims. Torque rod bar pin must always be mounted 
adjacent to forward face of spring hanger legs. No more than four shims can be 
used (1/4 inch maximum total thickness). Snug torque rod bar pin lock nuts, 
but do not tighten to specification yet.

[FIGURE: F3706F.gif]

SPECIFICATIONS

 Tire Zone Description 

Specified wheelcuts and turning diameters are based on the tire zone 
concept. Tire zones are determined by the combination of tire and rim. Any 
tire by itself does not fall into a particular zone and, in fact, the same 
tire can be in more than one zone. Only a tire and rim combination uniquely 
determines the tire zone.

The main reason for using the tire zones is to take advantage of 
greater wheel offsets on certain rims, which allows increased wheelcuts and, 
therefore, tighter turning diameters.

To determine wheel turn angle, first determine the tire zone for the 
rim/tire combination installed on the vehicle using the tables below and then 
use the corresponding column in the Front Wheel Turn Angle Specifications 
chart that follows the tire zone tables.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension

The front suspension consists of the following major components:

axle

leaf springs

shock absorbers

When servicing the front axle, wheel hubs or suspension, replace any 
component that is damaged or out of specification. All major axle and 
suspension components are heat treated and, therefore, cannot be bent, 
twisted, welded, heated or reconditioned without experiencing a strength or 
fatigue life reduction.

Following are examples of specific prohibited operations:

hot or cold bending or twisting of I-beam, tie rod assemblies, 
spindles, steering arms or tie rod arms for any reason

welding of, or to, steering arms, tie rod arms, I-beams, steering 
spindles, spindle pins or tie rod assemblies

redrilling or reboring of I-beam spindle pin holes for a bushing

milling or machining of any component

spray welding of bearing diameters or other machined surfaces

redrilling or reboring of draw keyholes

relocation or removal of tie rod clamps

================================================================================
PAGE 2463
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Components

Spindle

Provides steering pivot point. The spindle pivots on a pin installed 
through the end of the axle. Bushings provide bearing surface between spindle 
and pin. The front wheel and brake drum are mounted on the spindle. Opposed, 
tapered roller bearings are installed in the wheel hub to support the weight 
of the vehicle on the spindle.

Shock absorber 

Hydraulic, direct-acting type. Provides continuous damping effect 
under compression and extension. Connected to frame and bracket located below 
the leaf spring. Rubber bushings are used to isolate the shock absorbers from 
their attaching points.

Leaf spring 

Multi-leaf unsymmetrical or parabolic taper leaf springs are used to 
support the front of the vehicle. The leaf spring is an over-the-axle 
installation with U-bolts used to attach the spring to the axle. The spring is 
attached to the frame by a single pivot and bracket at the front, and a 
shackle and bracket arrangement at the rear.

Axle

I-beam, non-driving type axle is attached to the frame through leaf 
springs and stabilizer bar. Spindle pin and camber angles are built into axle 
and are not adjustable.

================================================================================
PAGE 2464
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Component Replacement

Shock absorbers must be replaced as an assembly. They are not 
serviceable. It is not necessary to replace shock absorbers in pairs. Replace 
only the worn or damaged shock absorber.

Leaf springs can be replaced individually. Bushing in spring eyes and 
spring pins are serviceable as separate components.

Spindle assembly can be replaced as an assembly. Since spindle pin 
bushings are serviceable items, it is not necessary to replace the spindle 
assembly.

Spring, shock and stabilizer mounting brackets are serviceable as 
separate components.

================================================================================
PAGE 2465
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fasteners, Suspension

 CAUTION: All front suspension fasteners are important retaining parts in that 
they can affect the performance of vital parts and systems and result in major 
service expense. Any part must be replaced with one of the same part number or 
with an exact equivalent part if replacement becomes necessary. Do not use a 
replacement part of lower quality or substitute design. Torque values must be 
used as specified during assembly to ensure proper retention of suspension 
parts. 

Never attempt to heat, quench or straighten any front suspension part. 
Replace with a new part.

================================================================================
PAGE 2466
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel Bearing and Wheel Hub

 CAUTION: Wheel seals on front axles must be replaced any time the axle 
lubricants are changed from the factory-installed mineral lube to synthetic 
lube or vice versa. 

Each front wheel and tire assembly is bolted to its respective front 
hub and brake drum or hub and rotor assembly. Two opposed tapered roller 
bearings are installed in each hub. A wheel seal is installed at the inner end 
of the hub to prevent lubricant from leaking into the drum or onto the rotor. 
The entire assembly is retained to its spindle by an adjusting nut and cotter 
pin.

Is self-locking, eliminating any other retainers (such as cotter keys).

Allows precise wheel bearing adjustment to within 0.051-0.076 mm 
(0.002-inch-0.003-inch).

Is easy to install and service.

Is reusable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring, F700 and F800 with 6K, 7K and 9K Front Axles, and B800 with 8K 
and 9K Front Axles

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle frame until the weight is off the front spring with 
the front wheel still touching the floor. 

Disconnect the shock absorber from the brackets. 

Remove the nut, bolt and sleeve that retains the spring to the front 
bracket. 

Remove the nut and bolt that retains the spring to the rear bracket. 

Remove insulator assembly if so equipped and hold for reinstallation.

Remove the four U-bolt nuts and washers and the two U-bolts. Remove the 
spring. 

 Installation 

Position the spring at the spring seat and align the spring eye with 
the front spring bracket. 

Install the washer and nut. Tighten the 3/4-inch slotted nut to 163-230 
Nm (120-170 lb-ft). Install the cotter pin. 

Raise rear end of spring into the bracket. 

Reinstall insulator assembly.

Install the through-bolt, sleeve and 1/2-inch nut. Tighten nut to 
102-142 Nm (75-105 lb-ft). Install cotter pin. 

Place the U-bolts in position over the spring and through the holes in 
the axle. Make sure the spring center bolt is centered in the recess of the 
axle. Install the nut and washers on the U-bolts. 

Lower the vehicle to the floor and tighten the U-bolt nuts to 204-277 
Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Install the shock absorber. 

Remove the jack.

Axles, and B800 with 8K and 9K Front Axles (Except F-Series Low Profile)

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring, F-, FT-Series with 10K and 14.6K Front Axles

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle until the weight is off the front springs, with the 
wheels still touching the floor. Remove the shock absorber, if so equipped.

Remove the bolts that secure the pin in the front bracket. 

Remove the retaining pin from the front bracket. 

Remove the four through-bolts and then the two shackle pins securing 
the shackle assembly. Remove the shackle from the spring and rear bracket. 

Remove the two U-bolts that attach the spring to the axle. 

Lift the spring from the axle, noting the position of any caster wedges 
or spacer.

 Installation 

Position the spring on the spring seat and align the spring front eye 
with the spring bracket. 

Remove the lube fitting from the spring pin. Position the pin with the 
notches aligned with the attaching bolt holes in the front bracket and the 
lubricator opening facing outward. Drive the pin through the bracket and 
spring, then install the retaining bolts, washers, and lock nuts. Install the 
lube fitting in the pin. 

Align the shackle assembly upper holes with the rear bracket holes, and 
the shackle lower holes with the spring eye. Drive one shackle pin through the 
upper hole and bracket and the other pin through the lower hole and spring 
eye. 

 NOTE: Make sure the notches in the shackle pins are aligned with the 
retaining (pinch) bolt holes in the shackle and that the lube openings face 
outward.

Install the pinch bolts and nuts and tighten to specification. 

Place the spacer on the axle. 

Position the U-bolts over the lower shock bracket and spring, and 
through the holes in the axle. Make sure the spring tie bolt is centered in 
the recess of the axle, spacer or caster wedge.

Install the shock absorber lower bracket to the underside of the axle 
with the U-bolt ends entering the holes in the bracket. Install the 
flatwashers and lock nuts on the U-bolts. 

Lower the vehicle to the floor.

Tighten the spring U-bolt nuts to 299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft). 

Lubricate all pins with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or 
-K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B.

After removing the upper and lower spindle caps, remove the upper and 
lower spindle pin seal on 6K, 7K, 8K, 9K, 10K and 12K axles. Drive out the 
threaded lock pins with a bronze drift; then, drive out the spindle pin from 
the top of the axle with a bronze drift.

Remove the spindle assembly from the axle. 

 Installation 

Place the spindle in position on the axle. Insert the spindle pin 
thrust bearing between the bottom of the axle and the spindle.

Pack the thrust bearing and coat all mating surfaces of spindle and 
axle parts with Motorcraft Premium Long Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B prior to assembly. On all axles, the 
thrust bearing must be installed with the retainer lip facing down. The shim 
(or shims) is placed between the top of the axle and the spindle. Use shims as 
required to maintain a 0.076-0.254-mm (0.003-0.010-inch) axle-to-spindle 
clearance on all axles. 

On front axles with air or hydraulic brakes, line up the notches in the 
spindle pin with the lock pin holes in the axle. Drive the spindle pin through 
the axle with a drift until the notches and holes are in line. Install the 
lower (longer) lock pin first and seat by striking prior to installing nut. 
Install the upper (shorter) lock pin and seat by striking prior to installing 
nut. Tighten nuts to 68-95 Nm (50-70 lb-ft). Do not install both lock 
pins from same side of axle. 

Install the brake backing plate on the spindle. On 6,000-pound and 
larger axles, install the spindle arms before installing the brake backing 
plate. 

Lubricate the spindle bushings until lubricant is visible at the 
spindle-to-axle area. 

Install the hub and drum assembly and the wheel. Adjust the wheel 
bearings. Refer to Wheel Bearings, Front, in the Adjustments portion of this 
section. 

Check and adjust the toe-in. Refer to Section 04-00 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hub and Rotor, Wheel Seal, Bearing Cones and Cups

 CAUTION: Sodium-base grease is not compatible with lithium-base grease and 
should not be intermixed. Therefore, do not lubricate front or rear wheel 
bearings without first determining the type of original wheel bearing 
lubricant. Mixing incompatible bearing lubricants can result in premature 
lubricant breakdown. 

 CAUTION: If bearing adjustment does not eliminate looseness or rough and noisy 
operation, the hub and bearings should be cleaned, inspected, and repacked or 
filled with specified wheel lubricant. If the bearing cups or the cone and 
roller assemblies are worn or damaged, they must be replaced. 

 CAUTION: Wheel seals on front axles must be replaced any time the axle 
lubricants are changed from the factory-installed mineral lube to synthetic 
lube or vice versa. 

 NOTE: Wheel bearing lubricant is a lithium-base grease, Motorcraft Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B, or Motorcraft SAE 90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant C6AZ-19580-E or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESW-M2C105-A.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle until the tires clear the floor and install safety 
stands to support the front axle.

Remove wheel. Remove the hub cap and gasket from the hub.

 CAUTION: Do not use chisel, hammer, or impact tool to remove the Axilok wheel 
bearing adjustment nut to prevent damaging essential elements of this product 
and creating a safety hazard.

Use only the proper size, 6-point socket, as stamped on the Axilok nut 
to remove or install this product. Do not use 12-point sockets. Sockets must 
be of proper size and in good repair to properly disengage the nut's locking 
mechanism. 

Push the correct size, 6-point socket onto the wheel bearing adjusting 
nut and firmly seat the socket to "unlock" the nut.

Use a hand tool to remove the nut.

Inspect the condition of the spindle and nut threads to ensure a free 
turning nut when reassembling.

Remove the outer bearing cone. Using a Rotunda Heavy-Duty Wheel Dolly 
014-00030 or equivalent to support the hub and drum assembly, pull the hub and 
drum assembly off the spindle.

 CAUTION: Be careful not to damage the bearing cone cage. 

Remove the inner bearing cone and seal using Seal Remover TOOL-1175-AC 
or equivalent and Impact Slide Hammer T50T-100-A. 

[FIGURE: F7553B.gif]

 Installation 

Remove all traces of old lubricant from the bearings, hubs and axle 
spindle. Inspect the cups for pitting, spalling or unusual wear. If either cup 
is worn or damaged, remove it with a brass drift.

Clean the inner and outer bearing cone and roller assemblies with 
solvent and dry them thoroughly. Do not spin the bearings dry with compressed 
air.

Inspect the cones and rollers for pitting, spalling or unusual wear. 
Closely inspect the rollers for end wear and flat or rough spots. Replace all 
worn or damaged assemblies. It is recommended that the cone and roller 
assemblies and cups be replaced in sets.

Cover the spindle with a clean cloth and brush all loose dust and dirt 
from the brake assembly. Remove the cloth from the spindle carefully to 
prevent dirt from falling on the spindle.

If the cups are worn or damaged, replace them with new assemblies. 
Install the new inner and outer bearing cups in the hub with an appropriate 
bearing driver tool. Check for proper seating of the new bearing cups by 
trying to insert a 0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between the bottom face 
of the cup and the wheel hub seat. You should not be able to insert the feeler 
gauge.

[FIGURE: F24741E.gif]

If wheel lubricant is grease, pack the inside of the hub with 
lithium-base wheel bearing grease such as Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease 
XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. Fill the 
hub until the grease is flush with the inside diameters of both bearing cups.

Pack the bearing and roller assemblies with wheel bearing grease. Use a 
bearing packer for this operation. If a packer is not available, work as much 
lubricant as possible between the rollers and cages. Lubricate the cup 
surfaces with grease.

Place the inner bearing and roller assembly in the inner cup and 
install the wheel seal with the appropriate tool. Be sure the seal is fully 
bottomed in the hub.

On all synthetic-type seals, coat the seal lips with wheel bearing 
grease such as Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B before installing the hub and drum. On 
seals not coated on the outside diameter with sealer by the manufacturer, coat 
the grease seal bore in the hub with a thin coat of non-hardening sealer prior 
to installing the grease seal.

 CAUTION: Keep the hub centered on the spindle to prevent damage to the wheel 
seal or the spindle threads. 

Install the hub and drum on the wheel spindle using Rotunda Heavy-Duty 
Wheel Dolly 014-00030 or equivalent. 

Install the outer bearing cone and roller assembly. Adjust wheel 
bearings. Refer to Wheel Bearings, Front, in the Adjustment portion of this 
section.

 Front Hub Seal Installation 

Chicago Rawhide and Stemco unitized seals, available as regular 
production options, provide sealing where oil is used for bearing lubrication. 
The tools required for Stemco seal installation are only available from the 
Stemco warehouse. Refer to Special Service Tools/Equipment at the end of this 
section for the tooling required. The Chicago Rawhide oil seal requires no 
installation tools.

 Chicago Rawhide and Stemco Unitized Oil Seals 

For Chicago Rawhide Scotseal oil seals (10K, 12K, 13K and 14.6K front 
axles) and Stemco unitized oil seals (7K and 9K front axles with air brakes 
and 8K and 9K front axles with hydraulic brakes), refer to the following 
procedure.

[FIGURE: F7554A.gif]

 CAUTION: Wheel seals on front axles must be replaced any time the axle 
lubricants are changed from the factory-installed mineral lube to synthetic 
lube or vice versa. 

Place seal assembly on spindle so the metal side is facing the spindle 
knuckle. If installing a C.R. Industries seal, push the seal onto the spindle 
by hand until the seal bottoms against the spindle shoulder. For the Stemco 
Seal, install the seal on the spindle using appropriate tool until it seats 
against the spindle shoulder. Refer to Special Service Tool Chart. Apply a 
light coating of Rear Axle Lubricant EOAZ-19580-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESP-M2C154-A to rubber outside diameter of the seal and to seal 
bore in hub.

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B, before installation.

Place inner bearing on spindle and slide it back against the seal.

 CAUTION: Do not push wheel onto seal by hand. Wheel will be pushed onto seal 
when nut is tightened. 

With wheel mounted on Rotunda Heavy-Duty Wheel Dolly 014-00030 or 
equivalent, carefully push in onto spindle until it contacts seal. Keep the 
hub centered on the spindle to prevent damage to the oil seal or the spindle 
threads.

Place outer bearing on spindle and slide into bearing cup.

Install the adjusting nut. Make the final bearing adjustment. Refer to 
Wheel Bearings, Front, in the Adjustments portion of this section.

Install the gasket and hub cap.

Remove the hub cap plug and add Motorcraft SAE 90 Premium Rear Axle 
Lubricant C6AZ-19580-E or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESW-M2C105-A. 
After the oil has been allowed to flow through the bearings, recheck the oil 
level. The oil level must be between the ADD and FULL level lines on the hub 
cap window.

 Stemco Two-Piece Seals 

For Stemco two-piece seals (6,000- and 7,000-pound front axles with 
hydraulic brakes), refer to the following procedure.

Clean all parts thoroughly.

Oil the spindle and push the seal ring flush against the axle face 
where applicable.

Remove all burrs from the wheel hub bore seal area, and clean again.

Pack grease between the spring and the seal lip. This will prevent the 
spring from dislocating when the seal is installed.

[FIGURE: E21241D.gif]

Position the seal in the hub bore (part number up). Drive the seal into 
position using the correct tool. It must be perfectly square with the bore and 
bottom evenly.

Install the wheel and adjust the bearings. Refer to Wheel Bearings, 
Front, in the Adjustments portion of this section. Install the gasket and hub 
cap.

Remove the filler plug and add Motorcraft SAE 90 Premium Rear Axle 
Lubricant C6AZ-19580-E or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESW-M2C105-A. 
After the oil has been allowed to flow through the bearings (which takes a few 
minutes), double check the oil level before releasing the vehicle for service. 
Oil level must be between the ADD and FULL oil level lines on the hub cap.

[FIGURE: F2633D.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Shock Absorber

 Removal 

Remove the self-locking nut, steel washer, and rubber bushings at the 
upper and lower ends of the shock absorber. 

Remove the shock absorber. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: When installing a new shock absorber, use new rubber bushings. 

Position the shock absorber on the mounting brackets with the large 
diameter at the top. 

Install the rubber bushing, steel washer, and self-locking nut. 

Tighten the nut until it rests against the shoulder of the stud. 
Tighten to specifications listed at the end of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Spindle 

 Removal 

On a spindle with bronze or low friction (Garlock) bushings, press the 
bushing out of the spindle with a tool that is slightly smaller than the 
spindle bore.

[FIGURE: F14531B.gif]

Clean the spindle bores thoroughly, and make certain lubricating holes 
(if so equipped) are not plugged. 

 Installation 

Position a new bushing in the spindle bore with the lubricating hole in 
line with the lubricating fitting and the open end of the oil groove toward 
the axle. Press the bronze or low friction (Garlock) bushing into the spindle 
with a driver that pilots in the bushing.

[FIGURE: F14541B.gif]

Press the bushing until there is 3.4-4.1 mm (0.133-0.161 inch) between 
the bottom of the bushing and the bottom of the top bore.

[FIGURE: F9372A.gif]

Turn the spindle over and install the remaining bushing in the same 
manner. 

Ream bronze or low friction (Garlock) bushings 0.025-0.076 mm 
(0.001-0.003 inch) larger than the diameter of a new spindle pin.

[FIGURE: F56401A.gif]

Clean all the metal shavings from bronze bushings after reaming, and 
coat the bushing and pin with lubricant prior to assembly.

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Spring Eye and Shackle

If vehicle owner/operator feels the front spring bushings have not 
provided the expected service life, it should be explained that the cause of 
premature bushing wear is the use of non-specified or incompatible grease.

As part of the following repair procedure, the bushings are lubricated 
with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C which meets Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. If this grease is not readily available, comparable greases are 
available from retail outlets. Refer to the Ford Lube Approved Source List in 
the Specifications portion of this section.

These greases are formulated to maintain their lubrication qualities 
under high load applications. They also are compatible with one another. If 
mixed, they will not break down or deteriorate.

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE TOOLS SPECIFIED IN THIS PROCEDURE MUST BE USED WITH A PRESS. USE OF 
A HAMMER CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE SPRING EYES, BUSHINGS AND TOOLS. EYE OR 
OTHER PERSONAL INJURY IS ALSO A POTENTIAL HAZARD, IF A HAMMER IS USED WITH 
THESE TOOLS. 

If portable press is not available, remove spring and shackle bracket. 
If necessary, refer to appropriate spring removal procedure in this section.

If portable press is available, proceed as follows:

Disconnect lower ends of shock absorbers.

Raise front of vehicle until vehicle weight is removed from springs. 
Wheels must be touching floor and body must be supported on safety stands.

Support weight of axle using floor jack.

Remove spring and shackle pin lock bolts.

Remove spring pins and rear shackles.

Lower axle until eyes of front springs clear mounting brackets.

 CAUTION: Use care when removing bushing to prevent gouging or other damage to 
shackle bracket bushing bore. 

Press bushings from shackle brackets using Non-Expanding Arbor 
D94T-3110-B or equivalent.

 CAUTION: Use care when removing bushings to prevent gouging or other damage to 
spring eye. 

Press bushings from spring eyes using Expanding Arbor D94T-3110-C or 
equivalent.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B must be used as the bushing lubricant. Failure to 
observe this caution or later lubrication of the bushing with an incompatible 
grease can result in breakdown of the grease and premature bushing wear. 

For a list of equivalent, compatible lubricants, refer to the Ford Lube 
Approved Source List in the Specifications portion of this section.

 CAUTION: Use care when installing bushing to prevent gouging or other damage to 
shackle bracket bushing bore. 

Press replacement bushings into shackle brackets using Broach 
D94T-3110-A or equivalent.

 CAUTION: Use care when installing bushing to prevent gouging or other damage to 
spring eyes. 

Press replacement bushings into spring eyes using Expanding Arbor 
D94T-3110-C or equivalent.

Lubricate the bushing pins with a light coating of Motorcraft Premium 
Long Life Grease XG-1-C or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B.

 CAUTION: Do not ream a bushing. Reaming can result in damage to lubricant 
grooves in bushing. Press Broach D94T-3110-A through bushing. Cutting edge of 
broach will properly size bushing in single pass without damage or oversizing. 

Test fit the bushing pins. The pin should slide through the bushing 
using hand pressure. Do not use a hammer to force the pin through the bushing.

If the bushing pins are a slip fit in the bushings, proceed to Step 5.

If the bushing pins bind or require excessive pressure to install, do 
not ream the bushings.

If removed, install spring and shackle bracket. If necessary, refer to 
appropriate spring installation in this section. If portable press was used, 
proceed as follows:

Raise axle until spring eyes and shackles are aligned.

Install bushing pins.

Install bushing pin lock bolts. Tighten attaching nuts to 102-142 
Nm (75-105 lb-ft).

Install lubrication fittings in bushing pins.

Lubricate bushing pins with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. Advise customer that 
bushing will provide expected service life if lubricated at recommended 
6,000-mile intervals.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Axle, Front

 Removal 

Loosen wheel retaining nuts.

Raise and support vehicle at frame rails.

Remove wheels.

If equipped with disc brakes, remove the caliper. To prevent brake hose 
damage, use a length of wire to hang the caliper from the frame.

Remove hub and brake drum/rotor.

Remove retaining bolts and brake backing plate/adapter. To prevent 
damage to drum brake hose, hang backing plate from frame.

Disconnect drag link from steering spindle arm.

Support axle on suitable jack.

Remove U-bolt attaching nuts.

Lower axle and remove from vehicle.

 Installation 

Position axle in vehicle and install U-bolt retaining nuts. Tighten 
3/4-inch nuts to 299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft), 5/8-inch nuts to 204-277 
Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Connect drag link. Use new cotter pin and tighten attaching nuts to 
149-203 Nm (110-150 lb-ft).

Install brake backing/adapter plate. Tighten the retaining nuts to 
245-325 Nm (180-240 lb-ft).

Install hub and drum/rotor assembly. Adjust wheel bearings.

Install wheels and lower vehicle.

Tighten wheel nuts to specified torque. Refer to Specifications at the 
end of this section.

================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings, Front

 CAUTION: Wheel seals on front axles must be replaced any time the axle 
lubricants are changed from the factory-installed mineral lube to synthetic 
lube or vice versa. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall Axilok nut if axle keyway tab (D flat on Axilok nut) 
is bent, cracked, or broken to prevent creating an unsafe condition. The axle 
keyway tab (D flat) is an essential mechanism that allows the nut to lock on 
the axle. If the tab is bent, cracked or broken, replace the nut with a new 
one. Do not attempt to repair the Axilok nut. Re-use of a damaged Axilok nut 
can create an unsafe condition. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall Axilok nut if spring clips are missing or damaged. Do 
not attempt to repair the spring clips. Replace the damaged Axilok nut. The 
two (2) spring clips that engage the adjustment/locking slots in the retainer 
cage provide an essential mechanism of the locking element. Use of this nut 
with damaged, broken, or missing spring clips can create an unsafe condition. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut if the retainer cage is cracked or 
broken to prevent creating an unsafe condition. Visually inspect the retainer 
cage for cracks or broken sections. If there are any cracks, or if any part of 
the cage is broken, replace the Axilok nut with a new one. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut if the threads are damaged to prevent 
creating an unsafe condition. Visually inspect Axilok nut threads for damage 
prior to every installation. Damaged threads may not have sufficient strength 
for nut retention. If threads are damaged, do not attempt to repair. Replace 
the Axilok nut. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut on spindles with slots not milled into 
the bearing journal or thread relief area to prevent damaging the Axilok 
retainer cage tab and/or spindle threads and creating an unsafe condition. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut on spindles with severely worn threads 
and/or with a severely worn slot to prevent creating an unsafe condition. 
Axilok installation on a spindle with either or both of these conditions may 
damage the retainer cage tab and allow it to rotate out of the slot under 
torsion. Rotation out of the slot will damage spindle and/or nut threads, 
resulting in an unsafe condition. 

Inspect Axilok nut to locate wrench size stamped into nut. Using the 
appropriate, 6-point socket, push socket onto wheel bearing nut to unlock the 
nut.

Hand-start (using socket) the wheel bearing nut onto spindle.

Rotate the wheel assembly.

 CAUTION: Always use a properly calibrated torque wrench to install each Axilok 
nut. Do not exceed the equipment manufacturer's recommended installation 
torque to prevent creating an unsafe condition. 

With the wheel assembly rotating, tighten the nut to 150-200 lb-ft of 
torque.

Back the nut off (loosen) one full turn, 360°.

Tighten nut to final adjusting torque according to following chart:

Nut Size

Wheel assembly must rotate freely with an end play of 0.001-inch to 
0.005-inch.

Periodically check the oil level on oil-lubricated front axle bearings. 
Keep oil level between ADD and FULL marks shown on the hub cap. Do not 
overfill. Overfilling can result in oil on brake linings.

[FIGURE: F2633D.gif]

Front hub assemblies and bearings must be cleaned, inspected and 
lubricated whenever the hub assemblies are removed or at the mileage/time 
periods indicated in the maintenance schedule.

New wheel seals must be installed when the hub is removed. A damaged or 
worn seal can permit bearing lubricant to reach the brake linings, resulting 
in ineffective brake operation and necessitating premature replacement of 
linings.

Install the gasket and hub cap, and adjust the brakes.

Section 04-02A: Suspension, Rear

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension, Rear

Semi-elliptic, leaf-type rear springs are used on all except tandem 
vehicles. The springs are mounted to the frame sidemembers and held in place 
on the axles by U-bolts.

The front end of the springs is mounted on the frame side rails by a 
spring hanger bracket connected to a radius leaf. The rear end of the springs 
is mounted with a supporting slipper bracket and rebound pin.

================================================================================
PAGE 2482
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-02A: Suspension, Rear

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Components

 Shock Absorber, Rear 

The hydraulic shock absorbers are of the direct, double-acting type. 
They provide a continuous dampening effect on both compression and rebound. 
These shock absorbers are of telescopic design with rubber grommets at the 
mounting points for quiet operation. The shock absorbers are sealed, 
non-adjustable units and must be replaced as complete assemblies.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Suspension, Rear

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify vehicle operator's concern by road testing to duplicate the 
concern.

 Symptom Chart — Rear Suspension 

 REAR SUSPENSION 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Rear Leaf Spring Squeaks

Loose attachments at the front or rear spring eyes.

TIGHTEN rear spring front and rear retaining bolts and rear shackle to 
specifications listed at the end of this section.

Individual leaf springs rubbing against each other or leaf ends sliding.

RAISE vehicle so rear axle hangs freely. REMOVE spring clips if 
necessary to allow leaves to spread. MAKE sure area is clean and dry. 
LUBRICATE tip of each leaf with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. REINSTALL spring clips. 
TIGHTEN to 68-95 Nm (50-70 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring, Leaf, with Cast Spring Brackets

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle frame until the weight is off the rear springs with 
the wheels still touching the floor.

Remove the nuts and washers from the spring U-bolts and drive the 
U-bolts out of the spring seat cap. Remove the auxiliary spring and spacer (if 
so equipped).

Support the spring and remove the radius leaf pin (lower pin) and 
rebound pin (upper pin). The upper pin is held in place by a cotter pin, and 
the lower pin by lock bolts.

Remove the rear rebound pin, which is held in place by a cotter pin, 
and remove the spring.

 Installation 

Position the spring in the rear bracket and install the rebound pin and 
cotter pin.

Position the spring in the front bracket. Install the upper pin and 
secure with a cotter pin.

Using a C-clamp or jack, force the front eye of the spring up into the 
bracket until the eye is aligned with the holes in the bracket. Install the 
lower (radius leaf) pin through the front bracket and spring eye. Align the 
pin groove with locking bolt hole in the bracket and install the locking bolt, 
nut and washer. Tighten to specifications listed at the end of this section.

Position the spring seat and wedge (if so equipped) between the axle 
and spring. If equipped, install the auxiliary spring and spacer. Place the 
U-bolt pad on top of the spring at the tie bolt, and put the U-bolt over the 
spring assembly and axle.

Install the spring cap on the U-bolt and install the nuts and washers 
on the U-bolts.

Lower the vehicle to the floor and tighten the 3/4-inch spring U-bolt 
nuts to 299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft). Tighten 7/8-inch nuts to 489-650 
Nm (360-480 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring, Leaf, with Stamped Spring Brackets

 Removal 

 NOTE: The primary differences in the F-Series low profile suspension occur in 
the spring and shock absorber bracket configurations. Refer to the 
illustrations following this procedure. 

Raise the vehicle frame until the weight is off the rear springs with 
the wheels still touching the floor.

Remove the nuts and washers from the spring U-bolts and drive the 
U-bolts out of the spring cap. Remove the auxiliary spring and spacer (if so 
equipped).

Support the spring and remove the front spring bolts and rebound pins. 
The spring bolts are held in place by a slot nut and cotter pin and the lower 
rebound pin is held in place by a self-locking pin and washer.

Remove the rear rebound pin, which is held in place by a self-locking 
pin and washer, and remove the spring.

 Installation 

Position the spring in the rear bracket and install the rebound pin, 
self-locking pin and washer.

Position the spring in the front bracket. Install the rebound pin and 
secure with a self-locking pin and washer.

Using a C-clamp or jack, force the front eye of the spring up into the 
bracket until the eye is aligned with the holes in the bracket. Install the 
lower spring bolt through the front bracket and spring eye. Install the slot 
nut and washer. Tighten to specifications listed at the end of this section. 
Align the slot opening of the slot nut with the hole on the spring bolt in a 
tightening direction and secure with a cotter pin.

Position the spring seat and wedge (if so equipped) between the axle 
and spring. If so equipped, install the auxiliary spring and spacer.

Install the spring cap on the spring U-bolt and install the spring 
U-bolt nuts and washers on the U-bolts.

Lower the vehicle to the floor and tighten the 3/4-inch spring U-bolt 
nuts to 299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft). Tighten 7/8-inch nuts to 489-650

 Removal

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

A unitized wheel bearing seal is a standard item on all rear axles. The 
unitized wheel seal combines the functions of a wear sleeve and seal in one 
self-contained unit, with the seal and sleeve surface inside. The unitized 
design provides maximum protection for the sealing surface during installation 
and operation. The tools required for unitized seal installation are available 
only from C.R. Industries.

A two-piece seal is available as a regular production option. The seal 
consists of a lip-type oil seal and a wiper sleeve. The seal is installed in 
the wheel hub, and the wiper sleeve is installed on the axle tube housing. 
When the hub is installed, a seal is formed between the wear sleeve and seal 
lip. The tools, required for Stemco seal installation are available only from 
the Stemco warehouse.

New hub seals must be installed whenever the hub is removed. A damaged 
or worn seal can permit bearing lubricant to reach the brake linings, 
resulting in ineffective brake operation and necessitating premature 
replacement of linings.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Hubs

 Removal 

Raise the rear wheels off the floor and place safety stands under the 
rear axle housing so the axle is parallel with the floor. Back off the rear 
brake adjustment. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 06 for procedure. 

Remove the axle shaft stud nuts and lockwashers. 

If tapered dowels are installed in the axle shaft flange, place a drift 
in the center of the flange and strike it sharply to loosen the dowels.

[FIGURE: E73621A.gif]

Remove the axle shaft. 

 CAUTION: Do not use chisel, hammer, or impact tool to remove the Axilok wheel 
bearing adjustment nut. To prevent damaging essential elements of this product 
and creating a safety hazard, use only the proper size, 6-point socket, as 
stamped on the Axilok nut to remove or install this product. Do not use 
12-point sockets. Sockets must be of proper size and in good repair to 
properly disengage the nut's locking mechanism. 

Push the correct size, 6-point socket onto the wheel bearing adjusting 
nut and firmly seat the socket to unlock the nut. Use a hand tool to remove 
the nut.

Using Rotunda Wheel Dolly 014-00030 or equivalent, raise the wheel so 
that all wheel weight is removed from the wheel bearings.

[FIGURE: E69531A.gif]

Remove the outer bearing cone. Pull the wheel straight out and away 
from the axle.

 CAUTION: Do not use a chisel to cut through the wear sleeve as damage to the 
spindle can occur. 

If the old seal is a two-piece design, remove the old wear sleeve by 
striking the ring surface several times with a ball peen hammer.

[FIGURE: E43491A.gif]

Thoroughly clean the spindle of the axle housing. 

With a piece of hard wood that will just clear the outer bearing cup, 
or a brass drift, carefully drive the inner bearing cone and inner seal out of 
the wheel hub. 

Clean all the old grease or axle lubricant out of the wheel hub. 

Inspect the bearing races and rollers for pitting, galling, and erratic 
wear patterns. Inspect the rollers for end wear.

[FIGURE: E67831A.gif]

If the bearing cups are to be replaced, refer to Bearing Cup 
Replacement (Aluminum Hubs) in the Removal and Installation portion of this 
section for procedure.

 Installation 

If bearing cups are removed, install new bearing cups using the 
appropriate bearing cup replacer. Refer to Bearing Cup Replacement (Aluminum 
Hubs) in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Check for proper seating of the new bearing cups by trying to insert a 
0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between the bottom of the cup and the 
wheel hub seat. You should not be able to insert the feeler gauge. 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. 

Place the inner bearing cone and roller assembly in the wheel hub. 
Install a new wheel seal as described under Hub Seal, Rear, Two-Piece, or Hub 
Seal, Rear, Unitized, in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Apply a light film of lithium-base grease, Premium Long-Life Grease 
XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the axle 
spindle, and position a seal protector tool over the axle spindle threads. 

With the hub centered on the axle spindle, carefully slide hub assembly 
straight (to avoid seal damage) onto the axle housing spindle. Then, remove 
the seal protector from the axle spindle. 

Fill the wheel cavity with rear axle lube before installing the outer 
bearing. 

Install the outer wheel bearing and start the bearing adjuster nut. 
Remove the wheel dolly. 

Adjust the wheel bearings as outlined under Wheel Bearing Adjustment in 
this section. 

Install the axle shaft, a new gasket, lockwashers and axle shaft 
retaining nuts. Tighten the nuts to specifications listed at the end of this 
section. 

Adjust the brakes. 

Check the rear axle lubrication level and add oil, if required. 

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle.

================================================================================

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bearing Cup Replacement (Aluminum Hubs)

 WARNING: DO NOT USE OXY-ACETYLENE OR SIMILAR EQUIPMENT TO HEAT THE HUB. THIS CAN 
CAUSE OVERHEATING IN LOCALIZED AREAS WHICH WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF STRENGTH 
THAT CAN CAUSE FAILURE OF THE HUB ASSEMBLY AND ULTIMATELY LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL. 

Remove the wheel(s). 

Remove the outboard-mounted brake drum (if applicable). 

Remove the hub from the spindle. 

Remove the inboard-mounted brake drum or disc assembly from the hub (if 
applicable). 

 CAUTION: Be careful not to damage the seal bore. 

Remove the seal and bearing cone from the hub.

Thoroughly clean and degrease the hub with a non-flammable solvent. 

Heat the hub evenly throughout in an oven to 79°-96°C 
(174°-205°F). 

 WARNING: REPLACE DAMAGED HUBS. USING A DAMAGED HUB ON A VEHICLE CAN RESULT IN 
HUB FAILURE AND ULTIMATELY IN LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL. 

 CAUTION: Take care to avoid damage to the bearing cup bore and shoulder. 

 NOTE: Variations in tolerances of materials and oven temperatures may allow 
bearing to drop in and out easily.

Remove the hub from the oven, and quickly press out the bearing cup.

Heat the hub evenly again, as in Step 7. 

 CAUTION: Take care to avoid damage to the bearing cup and shoulder. 

Remove the hub from the oven and quickly press in the new bearing cup. 
Be sure that the cup is properly aligned and fully seated.

[FIGURE: E1739E.gif]

Check for proper seating of the new bearing cups by trying to insert a 
0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between the bottom of the cup and the 
wheel hub seat. You should not be able to insert the feeler gauge. 

Reassemble the drum or disc assembly to the hub. Refer to the 
appropriate section in Group 06. 

Reinstall the hub and drum or disc assembly. Refer to the appropriate 
section in Group 06.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hub Seal, Rear, Unitized 

 Removal 

With a piece of hard wood that will just clear the outer bearing cup, 
or a brass drift, carefully drive the inner bearing cone and inner seal out of 
the wheel hub. 

Remove and discard the old seal. If a wear sleeve is in place on the 
spindle, carefully remove and discard the wear sleeve. Unitized seals will 
leak if installed over a wear sleeve. Thoroughly clean all grease and dirt 
from the spindle, spindle threads, seal bore and wheel cavity. 

Remove all burrs from the shoulder of the spindle and seal bore in the 
hub with emery cloth. Remove any nicks or scratches from the seal bore or 
spindle with emery cloth. 

Scratches in the hub seal bore might be too deep to be dressed out by 
light polishing with an emery cloth. In this case, apply a thin layer of non- 
hardening sealer such as Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A to the colored outside 
diameter of the new seal prior to installation.

 Installation 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
grease, such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B, before installation. 

Position the inner bearing cone in the bearing cup. 

Seat smaller outside diameter of seal in the recess of the tool 
adapter. The required adapters are available only from C.R. industries.

Insert centering plug of tool in bore of inner bearing cone. The plug 
prevents cocking of the seal in the bore. 

Hold the tool handle firmly and strike until the sound of the impact 
changes to a ringing as the seal bottoms out. Use a 1.8-2.3 kg (4-5 lb.) 
hammer and hold the tool firmly to avoid bouncing and unseating of the seal 
from the tool. After seal is bottomed in the bore, check for freedom of 
movement by manually moving interior rubber component of seal backward and 
forward. A slight movement indicates damage-free installation. 

[FIGURE: E43501A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 2493
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-02B: Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hub Seal, Rear, Two-Piece 

 Removal 

Remove and discard the old seal. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CHISEL TO CUT THROUGH THE WEAR SLEEVE. DAMAGE TO THE 
SPINDLE CAN OCCUR. 

If the old seal is a two-piece design, remove the old wear sleeve by 
striking the ring surface several times with a ball peen hammer.

 Installation 

Thoroughly clean the axle spindle with a wire brush. Remove all burrs 
with an emery cloth. 

If the spindle shoulder is scored or pitted, apply a thin coat of 
non-hardening sealant such as Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A. 

Install the wiper sleeve to the axle housing using suitable tools as 
shown in the following illustration. Do not use heat on the wiper sleeve to 
facilitate installation.

[FIGURE: E1928F.gif]

After bottoming, rotate the tool while applying several light hammer 
blows to make sure that the seal ring is flush and square with the face of the 
shoulder. The sleeves are designed with flanges to eliminate the possibility 
of installing them backwards. 

Remove all burrs and protrusions from the seal area of the wheel hub. 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B, before installation. 

Position the inner bearing cone in the bearing cup. 

Pack grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B between the spring and seal lip to 
prevent the spring from dislocating when the seal is installed. 

Position the seal at the mouth of the bore and drive it squarely into 
position using the correct tool. The seal must be evenly bottomed.

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall Axilok nut if axle keyway tab (D flat on Axilok nut) 
is bent, cracked, or broken to prevent creating an unsafe condition. The axle 
keyway tab (D flat) is an essential mechanism that allows the nut to lock on 
the axle. If the tab is bent, cracked or broken, replace the nut with a new 
one. Do not attempt to repair the Axilok nut. Re-use of a damaged Axilok nut 
can create an unsafe condition. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall Axilok nut if spring clips are missing or damaged. Do 
not attempt to repair the spring clips. Replace the damaged Axilok nut. The 
two spring clips that engage the adjustment/locking slots in the retaining 
cage provide an essential mechanism of the locking element. Use of this nut 
with damaged, broken, or missing spring clips can create an unsafe condition. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut if the retainer cage is cracked or 
broken. An unsafe condition can result. Visually inspect the retainer cage for 
cracks or broken sections. If there are any cracks, or if any part of the cage 
is broken, replace the Axilok nut with a new one. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut if the threads are damaged. An unsafe 
condition can result. Visually inspect Axilok nut threads for damage prior to 
every installation. Damaged threads may not have sufficient strength for nut 
retention. If threads are damaged, do not attempt to repair. Replace the 
Axilok nut. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut on spindles with slots not milled into 
the bearing journal or thread relief area. Damage to the Axilok retainer cage 
tab or spindle threads can occur, and can result in an unsafe condition. 

 CAUTION: Do not reinstall the Axilok nut on spindles with severely worn threads 
or with a severely worn slot. An unsafe condition can result. Axilok 
installation on a spindle with either or both of these conditions can damage 
the retainer cage tab and allow it to rotate out of the slot under torsion. 
Rotation out of the slot will damage spindle or nut threads, resulting in an 
unsafe condition. 

Inspect Axilok nut to locate wrench size stamped into nut. Using the 
appropriate, 6-point socket, push socket onto wheel bearing nut to unlock the 
nut.

Hand-start (using socket) the wheel bearing nut onto spindle.

Rotate the wheel assembly.

 CAUTION: Always use a properly calibrated torque wrench to install each Axilok 
nut. Do not exceed the equipment manufacturer's recommended installation 
torque. An unsafe condition can result. 

With the wheel assembly rotating, tighten the nut to 150-200 lb-ft of 
torque.

Back the nut off (loosen) one full turn (360 degrees).

Tighten nut to final adjusting torque according to following chart.

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson U2- and RT2-Series Tandem Axle

1999 FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension

Six Hendrickson tandem suspensions are available for FT900 Series 
vehicles: U2-340, UE2-340, RT2-400, RTA2-380, RTE2-400, and RTEA2-380. 

The prefix letters U2 and RT2 indicate the type of suspension. The 
prefix letter A indicates that the suspension is equipped with an aluminum 
equalizing beam. The prefix letter E stands for extended leaf springs, which 
provide a two-stage spring action, offering a superior ride whether empty or 
loaded. The prefix number 2 indicates the latest, most updated, lightweight 
version of these suspensions. 

The suffix numerals 340, 380 and 400 indicate the rated capacity at 
ground. Suspensions are available in capacities of 34,000 pounds (340), 38,000 
pounds (380) and 40,000 pounds (400).

================================================================================
PAGE 2498
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson U2- and RT2-Series Tandem Axle

1999 FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

U2- and RT2-Series Suspensions 

The U2 and RT2 steel leaf suspensions have conventional stacked leaf 
springs. Equalizing beams and the below-axle load design absorb strain, twist 
and road shock. 

U2-Series suspensions attach the leaf spring to the equalizing beam 
with U-bolts. RT2-Series suspensions attach the leaf spring to the equalizing 
beam with bolts and a spring top pad. The equalizing beam design distributes 
the load equally between the axles.

================================================================================
PAGE 2499

1999 F and B-Series

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson U2- and RT2-Series Tandem Axle

1999 FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Leaf Springs, Extended 

The extended leaf suspension consists of conventional stacked leaf 
springs with the top two leaves extended to the rear. A two-stage spring 
action on the tandem suspension is created when the top spring leaves come 
into contact with a second, inner hanger. When the vehicle is empty, the 
spring weight is carried by the rearmost hanger and most of the spring 
deflection is through the top two leaves. As the load increases, the inner 
hanger comes in contact with the spring. At contact the effective spring 
length is reduced, increasing the spring rate.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring

 Removal 

Raise the rear of the vehicle and position blocks under the frame 
behind the rear axle. 

Remove the wheels and the hub and drum from the forward rear axle. 

Position a jack under the front end of the equalizing beam. 

Remove the caps from the lower side of the saddle. 

Remove the spring pin lock bolts from the spring front hanger and 
remove the spring eye pin. 

Remove rebound bolt at rear hanger.

Lower the spring and saddle and remove the spring from the equalizing 
beam.

U2 and UE2 suspension only — remove the U-bolt nuts and remove 
the saddle and U-bolts from the spring. 

RT2, RTA2, RTE2 and RTEA2 suspension only — remove the spring top 
pad retaining bolts and nuts. Loosen the set screws and remove the saddle and 
spring top pad from the spring. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Lubricate the threads of all bolts with SAE-20 oil. The axle must also 
be in the operating position before the saddle caps are tightened. 

U2 and UE2 suspension only — position the saddle to the spring 
and install the U-bolts and nuts. Tighten the U-bolt nuts to specification. 
Hit the U-bolts on the top of the U firmly with a hammer and retighten the 
U-bolt nuts. 

RT2, RTA2, RTE2 and RTEA2 suspensions only:

Position the saddle on the leaf spring assembly and install the top pad 
on the leaf spring. 

Install the four top pad bolts and nuts. Alternately and evenly tighten 
the nuts until snug to hold the assembly in place (top view in the following 
illustration). 

Tighten the setscrew in the saddle and tighten to 136-203 Nm 
(100-150 lb-ft) before final tightening of the top pad bolts (side view in the 
following illustration). 

Tighten the lock nut on the setscrew until the lockwasher is locked 
(side view in the following illustration). 

Tighten the nuts on the bolts retaining the top pad to the saddle. 
Tighten the nuts alternately and evenly in the sequence shown in top view of 
the following illustration. Tighten the nuts to 373-406 Nm (275-299 
lb-ft). 

If removed, install the saddle cap stud in the saddle and tighten to 
75-88 Nm (55-65 lb-ft) (side view in the following illustration). 

[FIGURE: F3586C.gif]

Position the spring and saddle into the front and rear spring hangers. 

Align the spring with the front hanger and install the spring eye pin 
and lube fitting. 

Pressure lubricate with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B until lubricant appears at 
both ends of spring eye bushing. 

Install the spring pin lock bolts and tighten the nuts to 
specifications listed at the end of this section. 

Assemble the rebound bolt with spacer and lock nut through the legs of 
the rear spring hanger. 

Reset the wheel speed sensor (refer to Group 06). 

Install the hub and drum and wheels on the forward rear axle. 

 NOTE: The weight of the vehicle must be on the suspension (axle in operating 
position) when the saddle cap retaining nuts are tightened. 

Lower the saddle on the equalizing beam center bushing. Install the 
saddle caps and tighten the nuts to specifications listed at the end of this 
section with the gap equal on each end of cap. 

Remove the jack from the support beam and the blocks from the rear of 
the frame.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring Eye Pin 

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle frame and place safety stands under the frame. 

Remove the spring pin lock bolts from the spring front hanger. 

Remove the lubrication fitting from the spring eye pin and remove the 
spring eye pin from the spring and spring hanger. 

 Installation 

Position the spring eye pin to the spring hanger. Align the spring with 
the spring eye pin and install the pin. 

Install the spring pin lock bolts and retaining nuts and tighten the 
nuts to specifications listed at the end of this section. 

Install the spring hanger pin lubrication fitting and lubricate the pin 
with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring Bushing 

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle frame until the load is removed from the spring eye 
pin and place safety stands under the frame. 

Remove the spring eye pin. 

Raise the rear of the vehicle until the bushing clears the hanger. 

Install a bushing puller to remove the bushing from the spring, then 
remove the bushing from the puller. 

 Installation 

Install the new bushing in the spring with the split in the bushing 
installed to the top of the spring eye. 

Lower the vehicle frame until the spring bushing is aligned with the 
spring hanger bore and install spring eye pin.

Install the lock bolts and attaching nuts and tighten the nuts to 
specifications listed at the end of this section.

Install the lubrication fitting in the hanger pin and lubricate the pin 
with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Remove safety stands and lower the vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Equalizing Beam 

 Removal 

Block the front wheels and both tandem axles to prevent the vehicle 
from moving. 

Drain the air from the air brake system. Mark and disconnect all air 
lines to the rear axles. Plug all lines to prevent the entry of dirt.

Unlock all mechanically set safety brakes on the tandem axles. Refer to 
 Section 06-08D or Section 06-08E .

 CAUTION: The axle is free to pivot on the beam ends. Use necessary blocking to 
prevent damaging the interaxle driveshaft, power divider and differential 
carriers. 

Remove the U-bolts and nuts and disconnect the driveshaft from the 
forward/rear tandem axle. 

Remove the bolts retaining the torque rods to the axle bracket ends and 
disconnect the torque rods.

Remove the nuts and washers from the saddle studs and remove the saddle 
caps. If a stud is removed along with a nut during saddle cap removal, remove 
the nut from the stud. Clean the stud threads and install the stud in the 
saddle with an appropriate stud installation tool. 

Raise the rear of the vehicle with an overhead hoist or A-frame, and 
roll the tandem axles and equalizing beams out as an assembly. Support the 
frame with safety stands of an appropriate capacity. 

 WARNING: ALWAYS PLACE AN APPROPRIATE SUPPORT UNDER THE END OF THE EQUALIZING 
BEAM ASSEMBLY. THE BEAM CAN DROP UPON REMOVAL OF THE OPPOSITE BAR PIN END BOLTS. 

Begin removal of the bar pin beam end connection by applying 
penetrating oil to the threads of the two one-inch diameter bolts and lock 
nuts that connect the end bushing inner casting to the bar pin axle bracket.

[FIGURE: F8904B.gif]

 WARNING: DO NOT REUSE THE FASTENERS. AFTER ALL FASTENERS ARE REMOVED, DISCARD 
THEM. 

Remove the bar pin beam end connection on the opposite side of the 
equalizing beam.

With both ends of the equalizing beam removed, pull the beam off the 
crosstube.

Inspect the mounting surfaces of the beam axle bracket for gouges, 
cracks or excessive wear. Any cracks detected near the top of the axle bracket 
legs require replacement of the axle bracket. If any of these conditions 
exist, contact the axle manufacturer for instructions.

The dimension between the inside surfaces of the axle bracket must be 
57-58 mm (2.263-2.313 inches).

[FIGURE: F8905B.gif]

 Installation 

Coat the connection holes in the axle bracket legs with an appropriate 
anti-seize compound. 

On equalizing beams with rubber center bushings, insert the crosstube 
into the center bushing inner sleeve of both equalizing beam rubber center 
bushings. On equalizing beams with bronze center bushings, apply Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B to the bushing and inner sleeve.

Coat the inner and outer surfaces of the rubber end bushings with an 
appropriate anti-seize compound. 

Install the equalizing beams onto the crosstube. Position the two beams 
and crosstube under the drive axle assembly. 

 WARNING: WHEN USING THE SHIM STYLE BAR PIN BUSHING, A SHIM MUST BE INSTALLED AT 
EACH BOLT LOCATION. THE SAME PART NUMBER SHIM IN THE SAME ORIENTATION MUST BE 
USED AT BOTH BOLT LOCATIONS ON ANY ONE BUSHING ASSEMBLY. DO NOT INSTALL OR 
STACK MORE THAN ONE SHIM AT EACH BOLT LOCATION. USE GENUINE HENDRICKSON SHIMS. 
DO NOT USE STANDARD WASHERS. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS WARNING CAN RESULT IN THE 
FRACTURE OF EITHER THE BRACKET OR BAR PIN, WHICH COULD RESULT IN THE LOSS OF 
VEHICLE CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

 CAUTION: Once the retaining nuts are removed, they must be replaced. The nuts 
incorporate a self-locking feature that is damaged upon removal. 

Raise the beam end into the axle bracket and support it with a jack. If 
the axle pinion angle causes difficulty in assembly, disconnect the upper 
torque rod and rotate the axle so the bar pin slips into the bracket. Minor 
alignment adjustments to the inner metal of the bushing can be made with OTC 
tooling or an open end wrench.

Disconnect the longitudinal torque rods and assemble the bolts, washers 
and lock nuts. Do not tighten the nuts at this time.

With the equalizing beams attached to the axles, roll them under the 
center of the saddle, making sure that the center bushing of each equalizing 
beam is lined up with the center of the saddle legs. Lower the frame and 
center saddles on the equalizing beam center bushings. Install the saddle 
caps, washers, and new nuts. Do not tighten the nuts at this time.

Connect the torque rods to the axle brackets and frame brackets. 
Install lock nuts and tighten to 238-305 Nm (175-225 lb-ft).

Tighten the equalizing beam end nuts to 611-813 Nm (450-600 
lb-ft).

With the vehicle weight on the center bushings, evenly tighten the 
saddle cap lock nuts to 170-196 Nm (125-145 lb-ft) for U2-Series and 
306-372 Nm (226-274 lb-ft) for RT2-Series. Maintain an even gap between 
the saddle cap and saddle during torquing to avoid distortion of saddle caps.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Beam End Bushing, Equalizing 

 Removal 

Remove the equalizing beam. 

Remove the confinement washer from one end of the bushing for pushing 
tool clearance. If required, use a chisel where the washer has been staked to 
the inner casting of the bushing.

[FIGURE: F8907A.gif]

Cut the protruding rubber on the same end of the beam end as shown. 
This permits the pushing tool to contact the outer metal of the bushing.

[FIGURE: F3529B.gif]

 WARNING: WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING BUSHINGS IN EQUALIZING BEAMS, FOLLOW 
PROCEDURES DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION. DO NOT USE A TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING 
OUTER METAL PRESSED IN THE BEAM. WELDING, TORCHING OR ATTACHING MATERIAL TO 
THE EQUALIZING BEAM MUST NEVER BE PERFORMED. ALL EQUALIZING BEAMS (ALUMINUM 
AND STEEL) ARE HEAT TREATED FOR STRENGTH AND SERVICE LIFE. THE USE OF HEAT CAN 
ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THE BEAMS. AFTER REMOVING EQUALIZING BEAM 
BUSHINGS, THOROUGHLY INSPECT THE BEAM BORES. IF THE BEAM BORES ARE DAMAGED, 
REPLACE WITH A NEW EQUALIZING BEAM. 

If Suspension System Bushing Tooling 014-00943 is to be used, follow 
the instructions provided with the tooling.

If Suspension System Bushing Tooling 014-00943 is not used, fabricate a 
piece of steel tubing 102 mm (4 inches) long and 108 mm (4-1/4 inches) OD with 
12.7-mm (1/2-inch) wall thickness to press out the bushing. The press should 
have a capacity of at least 80 tons.

[FIGURE: F3531C.gif]

 Installation 

Inspect the bushing bores for nicks and burrs. Remove any nicks or 
burrs with emery cloth. 

Coat the bushing bore with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Clean the outer sleeve of the bushing with an emery cloth to remove the 
phosphate coating that acts as a rust preventative. 

If Suspension System Bushing Tooling 014-00943 is to be used, follow 
the instructions provided with the tooling.

A shop-made installation tool can be fabricated using a steel tube 127 
mm (5 inches) long, 127 mm (5 inches) OD and 12.7-mm (1/2-inch) wall 
thickness. The installation tool must be split in half, then bolted or clamped 
together to compress the rubber to allow contact with the bushing outer metal.

[FIGURE: F8909B.gif]

Place the equalizing beam in the shop press with the beam end securely 
supported on the bed. Before pressing in the bar pin bushing, the holes in the 
end of the bar pin bushing must be in line with the centerline of the 
equalizing beam. Press the bushing into the bore with a press of at least 
72,570 kg (80 tons).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Center, Bronze, Beam Removed

 Removal 

Remove the equalizing beam. 

Remove the lube fitting. 

Remove the seal on the pushing side of the beam hub. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the equalizing beam is securely supported at the center bore 
area of the press bed to avoid bending the equalizing beam. 

Remove the bushing with Bushing Remover Tool Set 1745 and adapters as 
shown in the following illustration.

[FIGURE: F3527C.gif]

Installing Adapter

If the tool is not available, press the bushing out in a press with a 
capacity of at least 45,359 kg (50 tons). Use a piece of tubing with a 
diameter of 117 mm (4-5/8 inches) and a length of 178 mm (7 inches).

[FIGURE: F3533C.gif]

 Installation 

Inspect the center bore for any nicks or burrs. Remove burrs or nicks 
with an emery cloth. 

Apply a thin coating of Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the outer metal of the 
bushing and the inside diameter of the bore. 

 NOTE: Do not install a bronze center bushing in an aluminum equalizing beam. 

Position the bushing in the bore so the lube groove lies along the 
vertical centerline of the equalizing beam. 

Install the bushing using Bushing Remover Tool Set 1745 and adapters as 
shown in the removal portion of this procedure. If the tool set is not 
available, press the bushing into place with a press with a capacity of at 
least 45,359 kg (50 tons). Use a piece of tubing with a diameter of 117 mm 
(4-5/8 inches) and a length of 178 mm (7 inches). Allow equal space on both 
ends of the bushing for placing seals in position. 

Install two thrust washers (total four) on the inboard and outboard 
side of the bushing. 

Install the lube fitting. 

Install the equalizing beam. 

[FIGURE: F3534C.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Center, Bronze, Beam Installed 

 Removal 

Block the front wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving. 

Remove the nuts retaining the saddle caps to the saddle. Remove the 
saddle caps. 

Raise the rear of the frame until the saddle cap studs clear the 
equalizing beam assembly. 

If required remove and replace the lube fitting in the equalizing beam 
assembly. 

Remove the thrust washers and center sleeves from the equalizing beams. 
Remove the crosstube from the beam center bushing bore. 

Remove the bushings using Bushing Remover Tool Set 1745 and adapters as 
shown in the illustration under Bushing, Center, Bronze, Beam Removed. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Do not install a bronze center bushing in an aluminum equalizing beam. 

Position the bronze center bushing in the bore so the lubricant groove 
lies along the vertical centerline of the equalizing beam. 

Press the bronze bushing and seals into the bore. 

Coat the bushing inside diameter and the center sleeve with Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. 

 NOTE: When installing thrust washers on the center sleeves, install washers 
until the gap is less than one washer. 

Install two thrust washers (total four) on the inboard side of each 
bronze bushing. Install the crosstube and center sleeves. Install two thrust 
washers (total four) on the outboard side of each bronze bushing. 

Install the zerk fitting in the equalizing beams. 

Lower the frame until the saddle is in position over the equalizing 
beams and crosstube assembly. 

 NOTE: The weight of the vehicle must be on the suspension (axle in operating 
position) when the saddle cap retaining nuts are tightened.

Install the saddle caps. Install the washers and nuts on the studs and 
tighten the nuts to 306-372 Nm (225-275 lb-ft) for RT2-Series and 
170-196 Nm (125-145 lb-ft) for U2-Series. 

Pressure lubricate both center bushings with Premium Long-Life Grease 
XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B.
