DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve, Double Check 

The double check valve is used in an air brake system to direct a flow 
of air into a common line from either of two sources, whichever is at the 
higher pressure. It may be used for directing airflow for specific functions 
or to select the higher pressure of either of two sources of air as a supply 
source. 

 Double Check Valve 

[FIGURE: H4167D.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Inlet Port (Part of 2K119)

2

—

Delivery Port (Part of 2K119)

3

—

Shuttle (Part of 2K119)

4

—

Body (Part of 2K119)

5

—

Shuttle Guide
(Part of 2K119)

6

—

O-Ring (Part of 2K119)

The double check valve is used in several parts of the brake system. It 
is used in the brake system for tractors to make sure both the service brake 
force and the spring force of a brake air chamber are not applied at the same 
time, which could damage the brake system. If the parking brakes are applied, 
the air is released from the spring hold-off side of the brake air chamber to 
provide spring application of the brakes. To make sure that the service 
chamber force is not applied at the same time, the double check valve routes 
air pressure to the spring brake hold-off side of the brake air chamber during 
a service brake application, relieving the spring force proportional to the 
service brake application. 

The double check valve used in the parking brake supply line serves to 
make sure that if a failure occurs in either the primary or secondary air 
supply system, the remaining system will provide sufficient air for control of 
the spring brake release. 

The double check valve operates as follows: air under pressure enters 
either of the double check valve inlet ports. The moving shuttle is pushed 
away from a higher pressure inlet port to seal a lower pressure inlet port. 
The airflow continues out the delivery port of the double check valve. The 
position of the shuttle will reverse if the pressure levels are reversed.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Low-Pressure Indicator Switch 

The low air pressure switch is a safety device designed to give an 
automatic warning to the driver whenever air pressure in the air brake system 
is below 414 kPa (60 psi), the safe minimum for normal vehicle operation. It 
is used to operate an electrical buzzer and warning lamp, which are audible 
and visible to the driver. The low air pressure switch is located on the 
parking brake control valve. 

The low air pressure switch is also used in the primary and secondary 
air supply lines. 

The low air pressure switch is designed so that the electrical contacts 
remain closed by the spring force until the air brake system pressure is above 
the spring set point (force). The setting and piece number are marked on a 
label on the low air pressure switch body. If a label is not present, the 
vehicle manual should be consulted for the proper setting. The minimum setting 
of the low air pressure switch is 511-593 kPa (74-86 psi). 

The low air pressure switch operates as follows: when air pressure at 
the supply port and under the diaphragm is above 552 kPa (80 psi), the 
electrical contacts remain open because the force exerted by air pressure 
underneath the diaphragm overcomes the force exerted by the spring above the 
diaphragm. 

When air pressure below the diaphragm drops below 552 kPa (80 psi), the 
spring exerts a force that is greater than the force exerted by the air 
pressure below the diaphragm. This causes a piston to move and allows the 
electrical contacts to close. When the ignition switch is on, this closes the 
electrical circuit to the warning device, warning the driver of low air 
pressure in the system.

 Low Air Pressure Switch 

[FIGURE: H8324B.gif]

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Brake, Air, Parking/Emergency System

 Inspection and Verification 

 WARNING: BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO WORK ON AN AIR BRAKE SYSTEM, CERTAIN PRECAUTIONS 
SHOULD BE OBSERVED. AIR UNDER COMPRESSION MAY BE COMPARED TO THE ENERGY IN A 
COILED SPRING AND WHEN RELEASED, MAY PRESENT A HAZARD IF NOT PROPERLY 
RECOGNIZED. 

Follow the safety measures listed below.

The wheels of the vehicle should always be blocked by some means other 
than the air brake system so that depletion of air will not permit the vehicle 
to roll.

In draining the system, do not look into the air jets or direct them 
toward a person as dirt or sludge particles may be carried in the air stream. 
Hoses which contain air pressure should not be disconnected under pressure 
since they will whip as air escapes from the line.

Follow the manufacturers' recommended procedures in working on any air 
device so as to avoid injury or damage from parts which, when released, are 
subject to mechanical (spring) or pneumatic propulsion.

As system pressure is drained and the emergency brakes applied, hands 
should be away from brake air chamber push rods and slack adjusters which will 
apply automatically with the loss of pressure. This also applies when checking 
a service brake system.

Reservoirs that are closest to the source of compressed air (compressor 
or auxiliary source) should contain a safety valve in known working order and 
sufficient capacity to limit the reservoir pressure to a safe maximum level.

Old, used reservoirs should not be used as replacements. The safety 
valves should not be reset higher than specified by the reservoir 
manufacturer, vehicle manufacturer, or code to which the reservoir had been 
manufactured.

Brake air chambers contain large internal steel springs that require 
special disassembly procedures. Note and be guided by the warning tags on such 
units.

 Symptom Chart — Air, Parking/Emergency System 

 AIR, PARKING/EMERGENCY SYSTEM 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Braking Is Uneven. Vehicle Pulls to One Side

 NOTE: Brake-pull evaluation should be conducted on a smooth, level surface.

Low tire pressure or worn tires.

INFLATE tires to recommended pressure. REPLACE worn tires. REFER to 
 Section 04-04 .

Improperly adjusted brakes.

 NOTE: VERIFY that the air chamber push rod clevis position is to 
specifications.

ADJUST brakes to recommended specifications. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Worn or damaged brake air chambers.

APPLY brakes and CHECK brake air chamber operation. CHECK for leaking 
diaphragm, bent push rod or other damage. SERVICE brake air chamber components 
as required. REFER to Section 06-08C , Section 06-08D or Section 06-08E .

Improper push rod-to-slack adjuster connection.

CHECK connection from push rod to slack adjuster. Connections must be 
the same on both ends of the axle. Clevis should be free moving. Lengths from 
clevis pin to center of brake camshaft must be the same.

Worn or damaged brake camshaft.

 NOTE: Do not use heat to free brake camshaft. The brake camshaft contains 
nylon bushings that can be damaged.

CHECK for frozen or restricted brake camshaft. LUBRICATE brake camshaft 
and WORK free or DISASSEMBLE and SERVICE. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Worn or damaged brake components.

CHECK for contaminated brake linings or damaged hoses, rollers, brake 
shoes and return springs. If linings are contaminated, REPLACE linings. 
SERVICE worn or damaged components as required. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Worn or damaged air lines.

CHECK for equal air pressure delivery to the brake air chambers at both 
ends of the axle. SERVICE leaking, collapsed or damaged air lines. CHECK for 
internal restrictions in the air lines, fittings or valve ports. REFER to 
 Section 06-08A or Section 06-08B .

Worn or damaged bearing or overtightened wheel bearing nut.

RAISE each wheel with brakes released. CHECK for free wheel rotation. 
If wheels do not rotate freely, CHECK for worn or damaged bearings. CHECK 
bearing nut torque. TIGHTEN to specifications. REFER to Section 04-01 or 
 Section 04-02B .

Low Air Pressure Buzzer Is Sounding or Air Pressure Gauge Reading Is 
Above 414 kPa (60 psi)

Damaged or worn low pressure indicator switch.

DISCONNECT terminal to low pressure indicator switch. If buzzer 
continues, CHECK for other electrical wiring ground. SERVICE wiring. If buzzer 
stops with terminal disconnected, CHECK instrument panel air gauge. SERVICE or 
REPLACE low pressure indicator switch. REFER to Section 06-08A .

Damaged or worn air pressure gauge.

CHECK air pressure at inlet to air pressure gauge with a test gauge. If 
pressure is below 414 kPa (60 psi), REPLACE the instrument panel air gauge. 
REFER to Section 13-10 .

Braking Inadequate

Excessive brake air chamber push rod travel.

ADJUST slack adjuster as described in Section 06-08C .

Glazed or worn brake linings.

REPLACE brake shoe and linings. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Grease or oil on brake linings.

REPLACE brake shoe and linings.

Worn, heat-spotted or cracked brake drums.

REPLACE brake drums. REFER to Section 06-02A .

Excessive brake air chamber push rod length.

ADJUST slack adjuster as described in Section 06-08C .

Brake air chamber improperly positioned in bracket slot.

REPOSITION brake air chamber. REFER to Section 06-08D or Section 06-08E .

Broken or bent cam brake components.

REPLACE components. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Brake linings do not contact brake drum during brake application.

SERVICE damage in foundation brake system. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Flat spot on brake camshaft or rollers.

REPLACE brake camshaft or rollers. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Parking Brake Is Inoperative or Slow to Apply

Damaged or worn parking brake control valve.

 WARNING: BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO REPAIR A BRAKE AIR CHAMBER, READ AND FOLLOW THE 
SERVICE PROCEDURES IN THE APPROPRIATE BRAKE AIR CHAMBER SECTION. THE SPRING 
BRAKE CHAMBERS CONTAIN A POWERFUL SPRING THAT MUST BE DISENGAGED CAREFULLY. 

DISCONNECT the air line from the delivery port of the parking control 
valve carefully — air and debris may come out. ALLOW air to exhaust from 
the line and CHECK if parking brakes apply. If parking brakes apply, SERVICE 
or REPLACE the parking brake control valve. REFER to Valve, Parking Brake 
Control in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Damaged or worn double check valve.

REMOVE the jounce hose to axle at double check valve. PUSH the parking 
brake control valve to the release or off position and CHECK if air escapes 
from the double check valve. SERVICE or REPLACE the double check valve. REFER 
to Valve, Double Check in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Damaged or worn brake air chamber.

DISCONNECT the slack adjuster clevis pin and MOVE the slack adjuster 
arm out of the way. APPLY the parking brake control and CHECK if the brake air 
chamber push rod moves to the fully extended position. If not, SERVICE or 
REPLACE the brake air chamber. (VERIFY spring brakes are not held off with 
cage bolts.) REFER to Section 06-08D and Section 06-08E .

Damaged or worn foundation brake.

APPLY the parking brake control (on position), and CHECK for movement 
of the slack adjuster. MOVE the parking brake control to the released or off 
position and APPLY the service brakes. If the brakes do not apply, SERVICE or 
LUBRICATE the foundation brakes. REFER to Section 06-08C .

Parking Brake Will Not Release or Is Slow to Release

Leaking air lines.

With the parking brake in the released position, CHECK for leakage in 
the parking brake system. Leakage can be from lines and hoses to the brake air 
chambers from the double check valve, or the lines to the double check valve 
from the parking brake control valve. SERVICE leakage as required. REFER to 
Removal and Installation in this section.

Leaking brake air chamber.

SERVICE or REPLACE the brake air chamber. Diaphragm may require 
replacement. REFER to Section 0

Air Lines 

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE THE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST FROM THESE COMPONENTS CAN BE INJURIOUS TO YOUR HEALTH AND 
COULD CAUSE CANCER OR ASBESTOSIS. COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED 
TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE DRUMS, CLUTCHES AND ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE A VACUUM

WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST SHOULD BE CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR 
DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED HIGH EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR 
AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. USE NON-ASBESTOS 
REPLACEMENT PARTS WHENEVER POSSIBLE.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Low Pressure Indicator Switch

 Parking Brake Control Valve Location 

 Removal 

Block or hold the vehicle by means other than the brakes and drain 
system air pressure to 0 kPa (0 psi).

Disconnect the wire to the low air pressure switch terminal.

Remove the lower pressure indicator switch from the fitting in the foot 
control valve.

 Installation 

Place Teflon® tape or equivalent around the low air pressure 
switch threads to act as a seal.

Install the switch in the fitting in the foot control valve.

Connect the wire to the low air pressure switch terminal.

Charge the system with air and check for leaks.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Valve, Modulating

The modulating valve should be replaced if it is leaking or operating 
improperly. If disassembly is required, observe the following procedure: 

 Disassembly 

Remove exhaust cover screw, exhaust cover and exhaust diaphragm. 

Remove four capscrews and lockwashers and cover. Remove O-ring from 
cover. 

Remove control piston and remove three O-rings from control piston. 

Remove large retaining ring from body and remove inlet/exhaust valve 
assembly. 

Remove ring from inlet/exhaust valve assembly. Remove O-ring retainer 
and remove O-ring from O-ring retainer. Remove washer and spring. Remove valve 
retainer and valve from modulating valve body. 

 CAUTION: Do not disturb adjusting screws unless adjusting spring brake hold-off 
pressure. 

Remove bottom cover and inner and outer springs. 

Remove balance piston. Remove O-ring from balance piston. 

 NOTE: To ease removal of supply adapter, a pipe nipple can be screwed into 
the adapter. 

Remove retaining ring from supply port and remove supply adapter and 
double check valve assembly. Remove O-ring from supply adapter. Remove double 
check valve from shuttle guide.

 NOTE: If single check valve is difficult to remove, it can be dislodged 
inside bore of modulating valve body. 

Remove Allen head plug from single check valve service port. Remove 
single check valve assembly. 

 Assembly 

Before assembly, lightly lubricate all O-rings, bores and mating 
surfaces with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M13P4-A. 

Install single check valve assembly and Allen head plug. Tighten 
securely. 

Install O-ring on supply adapter, shuttle guide over supply adapter and 
double check valve in shuttle guide. 

Install adapter and double check valve assembly in supply port. Install 
retaining ring, making sure the retaining ring is engaged in groove. 

Install O-ring on balance piston and install balance piston in bore of 
body. 

 NOTE: Cone shaped protrusion on spring seat faces springs. 

Install inner and outer springs and spring seat.

Install bottom cover. Tighten screws to 5 Nm (44 lb-in).

Assemble the inlet/exhaust valve assembly. Install valve retainer, 
spring and washer. Install O-ring on O-ring retainer. Install O-ring retainer, 
compress retainer and install retaining ring, making sure retaining ring is 
engaged in groove of valve body. 

Install inlet/exhaust valve assembly in body. Install retaining ring 
making sure the retaining ring is engaged in groove in bore of body. 

 NOTE: Large diameter stem should point up.

Install three O-rings on control piston. Install control piston in body. 

Install O-ring on upper cover. Install upper cover with four capscrews 
and lockwashers. Tighten to approximately 11 Nm (8 lb-ft). 

Install exhaust diaphragm and exhaust cover.

Section 06-05B: Brake, Hydraulic, Parking/Emergency System

1999 P800, F700, F800, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Control Assemblies

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, the parking brake system is 
composed of a parking brake control valve (TW-11), a parking brake unitized 
valve (HR-1), an engine-driven brake pump and remote reservoir, and two 
parking chambers that are spring operated. The parking brake is applied by the 
parking chamber spring acting through the brake wedge and is released by the 
engine-driven brake pump which provides hydraulic pressure through the HR-1 
valve to release the parking brakes. 

 Parking Brake Chamber 

[FIGURE: H40901A.gif]

 WARNING: DO NOT MIX THE FOLLOWING FLUIDS. 

The service brake system uses Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A 
and is serviced at the master cylinder reservoir. 

The Hydro-Max booster/parking brake system uses Motorcraft 
MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent, and is serviced at 
the engine-driven brake pump reservoir. 

The parking brake control valve (TW-11) controls the application of the 
parking brakes to the applied or the released mode. The vehicle operator 
applies and releases the parking brake by actuating the TW-11 control valve. 
The TW-11 valve is actuated by either a push-pull knob (F-Cab Series) or an 
up-down lever (F-Cowl and B-Series).

The parking brake unitized valve (HR-1) controls the pressurizing and 
exhausting of fluid during the apply and release mode. It also sets and 
maintains operating pressure and serves the functions of a diverter valve, a 
pressure check valve, a relay valve and a pressure relief valve.

if the parking brakes are in the SET or OFF modes.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Initial Charge, Parking Brake Chamber Spring Applied 

With the engine running, power steering fluid from the engine-driven 
brake pump flows through the Hydro-Max booster into the HR-1 (parking brake 
unitized valve) supply port (marked SUP). The fluid is simultaneously directed 
via internal passages to the closed diverter valve, and the single check 
valve. Slight hydraulic pressure will open the single check valve, allowing 
the fluid to flow to the diverter valve piston and to the closed inlet valve. 

 Parking Brake Control Valve 

[FIGURE: H4092F.gif]

Parking Brake Control Valve Delivery Port (Part of 2B195)

Fluid passing through the single check valve will also flow out the 
HR-1 delivery port (marked TW DEL) to the supply port of the TW-11 parking 
brake hand control valve. With the parking brakes applied (chamber springs in 
extended position), the TW-11 parking brake hand control valve will be in the 
brake applied position (knob out or lever up) and the inlet valve will be 
closed. Hydraulic pressure will build in the HR-1 and delivery line until it 
reaches 689-1034 kPa (100-150 psi), at which time the diverter valve piston 
will move, opening the diverter valve. 

When the diverter valve opens, fluid flows out the reservoir port 
(marked RES) of the HR-1 to the fluid reservoir. The check valve closes as the 
diverter opens (as supply pressure drops) and traps fluid pressure behind the 
check valve. A constant 689-1034 kPa (100-150 psi) pressure is maintained in 
the valve in this manner.

 Applying Parking Brakes 

The TW-11 parking brake hand control valve is moved to the applied 
position (knob out or lever up) when the vehicle operator wishes to apply the 
parking brakes. This action closes the inlet valve and opens the exhaust valve 
of the TW-11. Fluid above the HR-1 relay piston (CON port) and in the control 
line is returned to the engine-driven brake pump reservoir via the TW-11 
exhaust port through the HR-1 exhaust port and exhaust line. Removal of 
pressure from the control port causes the HR-1 delivery pressure to move the 
relay piston away from the exhaust valve, opening the exhaust valve and 
closing the inlet valve. Fluid in the spring chambers flows back through the 
HR-1 through the open exhaust valve and out the exhaust port to the 
engine-driven brake pump reservoir. 

 Parking Brake Control Valve (TW-11), Cutaway View 

[FIGURE: H7274C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

(Part of 2B195)

Exhaust (Part of 2B195)

As pressure is removed from the spring chambers, the springs extend, 
forcing fluid out of the chambers, through the HR-1 valve to the brake pump 
reservoir, and forcing the expander wedge into the brake and applying the 
parking brakes. 

 Releasing Parking Brakes 

The TW-11 parking brake hand control valve is pushed to the released 
position (knob in or lever down) when the vehicle operator wishes to release 
the parking brakes. 

When the TW-11 valve is actuated, its exhaust port closes and the 
supply port is opened to the delivery port. The diverter valve closes and the 
single check valve opens allowing fluid under pressure to flow through the 
TW-11 and out its delivery port to the HR-1 control port (marked CON). 
Hydraulic pressure moves the relay piston, closing the exhaust valve and 
opening the inlet valve. Fluid flows past the open inlet valve and out the 
HR-1 delivery port (marked DEL) to the parking brake actuators to compress 
their springs and release the parking brakes. 

[FIGURE: H7997A.gif]

When the chamber springs are fully compressed and the chamber pressure 
reaches 689-1034 kPa (100-150 psi), the diverter will open and the single 
check valve will close. This causes fluid under pressure (689-1034 kPa 
[100-150 psi]) to be trapped between the single check valve and the 
spring chambers, holding the parking brake in the released position. It also 
allows brake pump fluid flow to pass through the HR-1 valve at low pressure 
(SUP to RES). 

Fluid pressure being delivered to the spring brakes is also present at 
the HR-1 internal safety valve. If delivery pressure rises to between 
1172-1275 kPa (170-185 psi), the safety valve will open. This allows fluid to 
flow out the HR-1 exhaust port (marked EXH) and return to the engine-driven 
brake pump reservoir until the pressure drops to 689-1034 kPa (100-150 psi). 

If the parking brake system pressure falls below 689 kPa (100 psi), the 
diverter valve will close causing fluid to flow from the engine-driven brake 
pump to the spring chambers. When the pressure in the chambers reaches 
689-1034 kPa (100-150 psi) the diverter valve opens. This allows the brake 
pump fluid flow to return to the pump and the single check valve closes, 
trapping fluid pressure (689-1034 kPa [100-150 psi]) in the spring 
chambers, holding the parking brake in the released position. 

In the event of failure of the engine-driven brake pump or supply line 
to the hydraulic booster, the HR-1 internal check valve will maintain pressure 
in the parking brake system.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Brake, Hydraulic, Parking/Emergency System

 Inspection and Verification 

For diagnostic and testing procedures other than described below, refer 
to Section 06-00 . 

Traces or weepage of fluid at the booster or park brake circuit 
components is considered normal and should not be a cause for component 
replacement. Traces of fluid on the bottom of the booster, between the booster 
and master cylinder, below the HR-1 valve at the mounting bracket, or on the 
bottom of the parking brake chambers between the chamber and end cap are 
considered normal. A very small amount of fluid at any of these areas will be 
spread by air currents, either the fan in the engine compartment or airflow 
over the parking brake chambers. 

To determine the presence of a fluid leak, refer to the hydraulic leak 
test in Section 06-00 .

 Installation 

Install the elbows and connectors in their correct ports on the valve. 

Uncap each line and connect the lines to the correct ports on the valve 
as identified in the removal process. 

Attach the electrical connector to the parking brake lamp signal switch.

on the instrument panel. Install the two screws to attach the valve and the 
plate to the instrument panel. 

Bleed the parking brake system. Refer to Brake System Bleeding in the 
Adjustments portion of this section.

the parking brakes applied. If required, fill the reservoir to the specified 
level with Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent.

modes. Repair as required.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Valve, Control, F- and B-Series with Cummins B5.9 Diesel Engine

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE A BRAKE LINE OR HOSE UNDER PRESSURE. 

 CAUTION: The TW-11 control valve is to be serviced as an assembly only. 

 Removal 

Place chocks under the wheels to prevent vehicle movement. 

With the engine turned off, release pressure in the system by slowly 
pushing the control valve knob in. After the valve has seated, pull it out.

Remove the electrical connector from the parking brake lamp signal 
switch on the valve. 

Mark each line to the ports on the valve to identify the correct 
location during assembly. 

Remove and cap each line. 

Remove nut and shoulder bolt holding the rod clevis to the control 
valve. 

Remove the two screws holding the control valve to the bracket and 
remove the valve. Mark all elbows in relation to the valve ports for correct 
reassembly. Remove elbows from valve. 

If required, loosen jam nut at clevis and remove clevis and jam nut 
from the control rod. 

From inside the cab, remove the pin retaining the knob to the control 
rod and remove the knob. Remove the control rod and boot from the dash panel. 

 Installation 

Install the control rod through the instrument panel. Position the knob 
on the rod and install the retaining pin. 

Position the boot on the control rod. Apply adhesive around the hole in 
the dash panel for the boot. Position the control rod through the hole and 
install the boot in the hole. Install the nut on the control rod but do not 
tighten. 

Install the elbows on the valve in the correct ports. Position the 
valve in the bracket and install and tighten the two screws retaining the 
valve to the bracket. 

Move the control valve lever to the parking brake released position 
(toward the front of the vehicle). Align the holes in the lever and the clevis 
and insert the shoulder bolt. 

Check the clearance in the cab, between the back of the knob and the 
dash panel or bezel. Clearance should be between 1/16 inch and 3/16 inch. 
Adjust clearance by removing shoulder bolt and turning clevis. Install 
shoulder bolt and install lock nut and tighten. Install jam nut against 
clevis. 

Uncap each line and connect each line to the correct port on the valve 
as marked during removal. 

Attach the electrical connection to the parking brake signal lamp 
switch. 

Bleed the parking brakes. Refer to Brake System Bleeding in the 
Adjustments portion of this section.

Check the fluid level in the engine-driven brake pump reservoir with 
the parking brakes applied. If required, fill the reservoir to the specified 
level with Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent. 

Check operation of the system. Check for leaks in the release and apply 
modes. Service as required.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring Chamber 

 WARNING: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO REMOVE SPRING CHAMBER FROM BRAKE ASSEMBLY BEFORE 
MANUALLY CAGING THE BRAKE CHAMBER SPRINGS. 

 CAUTION: Parking chamber is under spring load. Do not attempt to disassemble the 
spring chamber. If spring chamber is not functioning properly, it must be 
replaced. 

 NOTE: Droplets of fluid on the capscrews retaining the end cap to the housing 
of the parking brake chamber indicate a normal operating condition. It does 
not indicate a leak in the chamber. Refer to the hydraulic leak test in 
 Section 06-00 . 

[FIGURE: H4103C.gif]

2225

Parking Brake Spring Chamber

 Removal 

Place chocks under the wheels to prevent vehicle movement. 

 CAUTION: Do not use an impact wrench to cage the spring. Air tools can damage 
the piston and prevent proper spring caging. 

 NOTE: If parking brake hydraulic pressure is available, caging of the spring 
can be done more easily by first releasing the parking brake by pushing in the 
TW-11 knob (or push lever down) in the cab.

Cage the spring in the chamber by turning the release bolt and nut 
counterclockwise. The spring is caged when the release bolt extends 50.8-53.8 
mm (2.00-2.12 inches) from the spring chamber filter retainer to the bottom of 
the release nut. 

With the engine shut off, remove system pressure by slowly pushing the 
TW-11 valve in or down until the valve has fully seated, and then pull it out 
or up. 

 WARNING: DO NOT REUSE FLUID AFTER IT HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE SYSTEM. 

Disconnect the fluid line from the fitting and cap the line. Remove the 
inlet fitting and bleeder screw from the chamber. 

Loosen the jam nut that retains the chamber to the wheel 
cylinder/parking brake expander. Rotate the chamber counterclockwise until the 
fluid inlet port points downward and the fluid drains out. Discard the fluid. 

Rotate the chamber counterclockwise and remove the chamber from the 
wheel cylinder/parking brake expander. Cap the fluid inlet fitting to prevent 
the entry of contaminants into the chamber. 

 Installation 

Prior to installing the chamber, make sure the spring is caged. The 
spring is caged when the release bolt extends 50.8-53.8 mm (2.00-2.12 inches) 
from the filter retainer to the bottom of the release nut as shown.

If removed, install the O-ring seal on the mounting tube groove and the 
jam nut on the mounting tube until the nut reaches the end of the threads at 
the chamber cylinder end of the mounting tube. 

Center the brake wedge rod in the brake expander threaded opening by 
pushing the wedge rod in approximately 13 mm (1/2 inch) and then centering and 
releasing it slowly. 

Position the chamber on the wheel cylinder/parking brake expander. 
Rotate the chamber clockwise until it stops in the cylinder. Make sure the jam 
nut does not interfere with the cylinder. 

Rotate the chamber in a counterclockwise direction so that the bleeder 
screw is facing straight up and the fluid inlet port faces away from the axle 
(less than one complete turn). 

 CAUTION: Use the fluid inlet fitting removed from the vehicle or a fitting 
supplied with a chamber service kit. Use of a non-standard (non-SAE) fitting 
may cause a piston interference condition possibly causing piston damage and 
severe chamber fluid leakage. 

Tighten the jam nut to 190-223 Nm (140-165 lb-ft), making sure 
the chamber does not rotate out of position. Remove the caps and install the 
bleeder screw adapter, plug and fluid inlet fitting in the chamber. 

 CAUTION: Do not allow any foreign material to enter into the system. The fluid 
may become contaminated and may result in O-ring failure, leakage and reduced 
service life. 

Tighten the bleeder fitting. Uncap the fluid line and the chamber fluid 
inlet port. Connect the fluid line to the chamber. 

Check the fluid level in the engine-driven brake pump reservoir. If 
required, fill the reservoir to the specified level with Motorcraft 
MERCON® ATF XT-QDX or MERCON® equivalent. 

Bleed the parking brake chambers. Refer to Brake System Bleeding in the 
Adjustments portion of this section. 

Check for leaks with the parking brakes in the applied position and in 
the released position. Service as required. 

 NOTE: If fluid pressure is available for the parking brake system, uncaging 
may be done more easily by first releasing the parking brake (push the TW-11 
knob in or lever down). Uncage the spring. Apply parking brake (pull the TW-11 
knob out or lever up). 

Uncage the spring by turning the nut on the release bolt clockwise 
until the nut is snug against the filter retainer. Tighten the nut to 27-40 
Nm (20-30 lb-ft). Uncaging may be done more easily by first releasing 
the parking brake (push the TW-11 knob in or push lever down). Uncage the 
spring and then apply the parking brake.

 Disassembly 

Remove the parking brake spring chamber.

 CAUTION: Do not use an impact wrench to uncage the spring. The piston may be 
damaged and prevent proper spring caging. 

 NOTE: To facilitate the spring uncaging procedure, apply 689-827 kPa (100-120 
psi) of air pressure to the fluid inlet port. Remove air pressure when the 
spring is uncaged. 

Uncage the spring by rotating the release bolt and nut clockwise until 
the nut is against the spring chamber filter retainer. Do not tighten the nut 
against the filter retainer. 

Drive the roll pin from the release bolt and nut. Unscrew the nut and 
remove the filter retainer and filter. 

[FIGURE: H41071A.gif]

Insert a screwdriver in the slot located at the end of the release bolt 
and rotate the release bolt clockwise until the bolt is completely beneath the 
end cap and all threads are disengaged. 

[FIGURE: H41081B.gif]

 CAUTION: The press must have a minimum capacity of 1134 kg (2500 lb) and a 
minimum press ram travel of 152 mm (6 inches). 

Place the chamber assembly in a press with the mounting tube supported 
by tube-type press stock and the end cap assembly facing the press ram. Bring 
the press ram down firmly on the end cap and make sure that press ram is 
centered on the end cap. 

[FIGURE: H4109B.gif]

Description

2225

Tube-Type Press Stock

 NOTE: Do not relax press ram pressure at this time.

Remove the six capscrews retaining the end cap to the chamber assembly. 

Slowly relax the pressure on the press ram and allow the spring to 
expand until it raises the end cap 152 mm (6 inches) above the chamber 
housing. Remove the spring and end cap from the chamber housing. 

[FIGURE: H41101A.gif]

Drive the piston assembly from the chamber housing with a brass drift 
and mallet as shown. 

[FIGURE: H41111A.gif]

With the piston supported as shown, drive out the release bolt and 
socket by striking the release bolt with a hammer. Discard the release bolt. 

[FIGURE: H41121B.gif]

Position a brass drift through the mounting tube so it rests against 
the insert and drive out the insert. Remove and discard all the O-rings and 
the insert. 

[FIGURE: H41141A.gif]

Inspect all parts for wear or damage and replace as required. If the 
spring shows signs of rust or corrosion, replace the spring or replace the 
chamber as an assembly. 

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: All parts must be clean before assembly. Foreign particles such as dirt 
or metal chips in the chamber may result in premature O-ring replacement, 
leakage and reduced service life. 

Coat the three new O-rings for the insert with Motorcraft 
MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent. Install the 
O-rings on the insert. 

[FIGURE: H41151A.gif]

Coat all interior surfaces of the chamber housing with Motorcraft 
MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent.

Place the insert in position in the mounting tube and carefully tap 
into place with a brass drift and mallet until locking tabs seat in groove.

Coat the piston and new O-ring and piston bearing with Motorcraft 
MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent. Install the O-ring 
and bearing on the piston.

[FIGURE: H41161C.gif]

Place the piston assembly in the chamber housing. Compress the O-ring 
and bearing assembly into the piston groove with a suitable tool (such as a 
plastic tie wrap) as shown. 

[FIGURE: H41171A.gif]

Carefully line up the piston rod with the hole in the insert. Gently 
tap the piston assembly into the chamber housing. The compressor tool should 
be loose. Remove the tool. Continue to tap the piston into the chamber until 
completely seated. 

[FIGURE: H41181A.gif]

 CAUTION: The press must have a minimum capacity of 1134 kg (2500 lb) and a 
minimum travel of 152 mm (6 inches). 

 NOTE: When using the press ram, do not allow the pressure it creates in the 
housing to be released.

Position the chamber housing assembly in a press so the mounting tube 
portion is supported by an appropriate-size tube-type press stock and the end 
cap portion of housing is facing upward. 

Insert the spring in the chamber and place the end cap on top of the 
spring. Make sure the capscrew holes in the end cap are aligned with the holes 
in the housing. Slowly and carefully bring the press ram down to compress the 
end cap and spring. Make sure the press ram is centered on the end cap and the 
end cap is in alignment with the housing. Compress the spring until the holes 
in the end cap and housing are aligned. DO NOT RELEASE PRESSURE. 

Install the six capscrews retaining the end cap to the chamber. Tighten 
the capscrews alternately and evenly to 5-6 Nm (44-53 lb-in). 

[FIGURE: H41191A.gif]

Install a new release bolt through the mounting tube and piston. Insert 
a 5/16-inch hex driver and rotate the bolt through the end cap. Tighten the 
bolt by hand until the bolt protrudes through the end cap and is snug. 

[FIGURE: H41201A.gif]

Install a new filter and the filter retainer over the release bolt. 
Screw on the release nut until the nut slots align with bolt hole. Install the 
roll pin. 

 CAUTION: Do not use an impact wrench to cage the spring. Air tools may damage 
the piston and prevent proper spring caging. 

 NOTE: To facilitate spring caging, apply 689-827 kPa (100-120 psi) of air 
pressure to the fluid inlet. Release air pressure after the spring is caged. 

Cage the spring by rotating the release bolt and nut counterclockwise 
until the bolt and nut project 50.8-53.8 mm (2.00-2.12 inches) from the bottom 
of the nut to the top of the filter retainer. 

Place the chamber assembly in a press so the end cap rests on the press 
bed. Position the rod socket into the end of the piston rod as shown.

[FIGURE: H41211A.gif]

Press the rod socket securely in place. 

[FIGURE: H41221A.gif]

Check that the rod socket is properly installed by measuring the 
distance between the spherical base of the rod socket and the top of the 
mounting tube. The distance should be 81.53 ± 0.76 mm (3.21 ± 
0.03 inches). 

[FIGURE: H41231B.gif]

Install the spring chamber. If the chamber is not being installed, 
install inlet closures in the inlet port and bleed ports to prevent entry of 
contaminants into the chamber.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Fluid Level Check

 WARNING: DO NOT MIX THE FOLLOWING FLUIDS. 

The service brake system uses Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A 
and is serviced at the master cylinder reservoir. 

To minimize parking brake system release and actuation during 
continuous cold weather operation (constant operation below -18°C 
[0°F]), fill and bleed the parking brake system with Esso UNIVIS-N-22 
hydraulic oil or equivalent. 

Check the fluid level in the engine-driven brake pump reservoir with 
the parking brakes applied. If required, fill the reservoir to the specified 
level with Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent. 

Whenever the hydraulic fluid level is checked, the parking brake must 
be applied. If the parking brake is not applied, the dipstick will show a 
false low reading that will create an overflow condition if brake fluid is 
added.

If the fluid is properly checked and found to be at the correct level, 
but there was a fluid discharge when the parking brake is released, there may 
be air in the system (the fluid may also be pink in color instead of red).

If air is present in the system, the brake system must be bled to 
remove the trapped air.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake System Bleeding 

Apply the parking brakes by pulling the parking brake control knob 
(TW-11) out (or push lever up). Check the fluid level in the brake pump 
reservoir. 

Place chocks under the vehicle tires to prevent vehicle movement. 

Fill the reservoir of the engine-driven brake pump with Motorcraft 
MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent fluid to level 
indicated by the dipstick. 

Start the engine and run at normal curb idle speeds for two to three 
minutes to purge all air from the lines in the system before the parking brake 
unitized valve (HR-1). 

Pump the brake pedal several times. 

Check the fluid level in the reservoir. If necessary, fill with 
Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent. 

With engine running, cycle the parking brake hand control valve (TW-11) 
to the released and applied positions five times, allowing 5-10 seconds 
between each position. 

With the engine running, push the parking brake control (TW-11) knob in 
(or push lever down). Bleed the left-hand spring chamber first by opening the 
bleed screw at the spring chamber allowing hydraulic fluid from the chamber to 
run out. Continue until the hydraulic fluid from the chamber runs clear and 
shows no signs of bubbles in the fluid (approximately 5-15 seconds). Close the 
bleed screw. Do not allow the engine-driven brake pump reservoir to empty. 

Check the fluid level in the reservoir. If necessary, add to the 
reservoir with Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent to bring the fluid level to approximately 76.3-88.9 mm (3.0-3.5 
inches) from the bottom of the reservoir. 

Repeat above two steps for the right-hand spring chamber. 

 NOTE: If the reservoir is overfilled with the parking brake released, fluid 
may be expelled through the reservoir overflow tube when the parking brake is 
applied. 

Check the fluid level in the reservoir. The fluid level should be 
approximately two to three inches from the bottom of the reservoir. Add or 
remove fluid from the reservoir as necessary. 

Pull the parking brake control (TW-11) knob out (or push lever up). 
Shut off engine. 

Check the fluid level in the reservoir. Add or remove fluid from the 
reservoir as necessary to achieve the level indicated on the dipstick.

ADJUSTMENTS

Chamber Spring Caging

 WARNING: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO REMOVE SPRING CHAMBER FROM BRAKE ASSEMBLY BEFORE 
MANUALLY CAGING THE BRAKE CHAMBER SPRINGS. 

 CAUTION: Parking chamber is under spring load. Do not disassemble unless a press 
is used and appropriate safety precautions are taken.

Cage the spring by rotating the release bolt and nut counterclockwise 
until the bolt and nut project 50.8-53.8 mm (2.0-2.12 inches) from the bottom 
of the nut to the top of the spring chamber filter retainer. 

[FIGURE: H4095D.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an impact wrench to cage the spring. Air tools may damage 
the piston and prevent proper spring caging. 

If parking brake hydraulic pressure is available, release the parking 
brake to ease caging of the spring. After spring is caged, pull the parking 
brake control (TW-11) knob out or push lever up.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System

The dual or "split" hydraulic brake system provides two separate 
hydraulic subsystems, one of which actuates the front disc brakes (secondary 
subsystem) and the other (primary subsystem) which actuates the rear drum 
brakes. Hydraulic leakage or complete failure in one subsystem does not affect 
function of the other subsystem. 

The dual hydraulic system master cylinder contains two separate 
pressure chambers, primary and secondary, for actuation of the two separate 
brake subsystems. Each pressure chamber has a piston/actuator subassembly 
containing a preloaded spring and a return spring. In the released position, 
actuators of both the primary and secondary pistons are in contact with their 
respective compensating valve stems which project into the cylinder bore. This 
maintains the valves in an open position, which allows hydraulic fluid in the 
reservoir to replenish any fluid displaced from the cylinder bore. 

As the brake pedal is depressed, the initial primary piston moves 
forward moving the primary actuator away from its compensating valve 
counterpart, permitting the valve to seat. Closure of this valve shuts off the 
passage between the primary pressure chamber and the reservoir section serving 
the primary chamber. 

Further movement of the primary piston creates a pressure in the 
primary pressure chamber, causing the secondary piston and actuator to move. 
As the secondary piston and actuator move, the secondary compensating valve 
closes, shutting off the passage between the secondary pressure chamber and 
the reservoir section serving the secondary chamber. Additional movement of 
the primary piston causes both chambers to build pressure. 

When the load on the primary piston is removed, fluid pressure in each 
chamber, combined with return spring force, causes the primary and secondary 
pistons to return to their initial released positions. Each actuator opens its 
respective compensating valve, reopening the passage between the individual 
reservoir sections and its associated pressure chamber. 

Should the rate of release be great enough to cause a partial vacuum in 
a chamber or should additional fluid be required because of brake adjustment 
or lining wear, the compensating valve will open to allow replenishment of 
fluid in the cylinder bore. 

Any excess fluid remaining at the end of the stroke due to "pumping" 
and/or volume change due to temperature fluctuation is released as the 
compensating valve ports open.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Pedal and Bracket

 Removal 

Remove the stoplamp switch from the pedal bracket. 

Remove the cotter pin, washer, bushing and booster push rod. 

Remove the retainer clip and spring washer from the pedal shaft. Slide 
the shaft to the left and remove the brake pedal. 

Remove the bushing from the pedal. 

 Installation 

Coat all bushings and the pedal shaft with a small amount of Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B.

Position the nylon bushings in the pedal shaft bore. 

Position the brake pedal assembly in the pedal support bracket. Slide 
the shaft to the right and through the pedal and support bracket. Secure with 
spring washer and retainer. 

Position the nylon bushing in the bore of the push rod. Connect the 
push rod to the brake pedal. Secure with flatwasher and cotter pin. 

Install the stoplamp switch in the pedal bracket as far in as possible. 
Pull the pedal to its farthest return position to properly reset the stoplamp 
switch. 

Check the brake system and brake stoplamps for proper operation.

Master Cylinder

 Bench Bleeding Dual System Brake Master Cylinder 

 NOTE: The purpose of bench bleeding is to remove air from the master cylinder 
so, when installed on the vehicle, brake bleeding will be reduced. If tools 
are not available for bench bleeding it can be easier to bleed the master 
cylinder on the vehicle. 

 NOTE: As air is bled from master cylinder, resistance to primary piston 
travel will not allow 25.4 mm (1 inch) stroking of master cylinder when 
outlets are plugged. 

Plug the outlet ports and fasten the master cylinder in a vise with the 
front end tilted slightly down. 

Fill the reservoir with clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid 
C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 brake fluid meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M6C25-A. Using a suitable tool with a smooth rounded end, depress and 
release the primary piston several times, approximately 25.4 mm (1 inch). 

Reposition master cylinder in the vise with the front end of the master 
cylinder tilted slightly up. Again depress 25.4 mm (1 inch) and release the 
primary piston several times. 

Add clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or 
equivalent DOT 3 brake fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A to a level 
even with the bottom of the rings as indicated on the master cylinder 
reservoir. 

 NOTE: The master cylinder is ready for installation on the vehicle. Normal 
bleeding procedures should be followed after the master cylinder is installed. 

Install and tighten the reservoir caps on the master cylinder. 

 Installation 

Position the master cylinder onto the booster until the mating surfaces 
come together. 

Install the attaching nuts, and tighten the mounting bolts to 34-41 
Nm (25-30 lb-ft). 

Remove all plugs and caps from ports and plumbing. Loosely connect the 
hydraulic brake system lines to the master cylinder. 

Connect electrical connector to master cylinder. 

 NOTE: If pressure bleeding, DO NOT EXCEED 35 psi or damage to the reservoir 
may result. 

Bleed the hydraulic brake system. Refer to Hydraulic System Bleeding in 
the Service Procedures portion of this section. Fill the master cylinder 
reservoirs to within 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) of the top of the filler neck with 
clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 
3 brake fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A. Install the caps on the 
master cylinder.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Brake Master Cylinder 

 Disassembly 

Remove master cylinder from vehicle. 

Remove the reservoir caps and drain the fluid from the reservoir. 

Remove the four bolts that secure the body to the reservoir. 

Remove the small O-ring and the two compensating valve seals from the 
recessed areas on the bottom side of the reservoirs. 

Depress the primary piston, using a suitable tool, 25.40 ± 1.27 
mm (1.00 ± 0.05 inch). Spring loads are approximately 90 lbs. It is very 
difficult to depress piston by hand. Then remove the compensating valve 
poppets and the compensating valve springs. Remove the piston stop pin from 
its bore in the master cylinder body. 

 WARNING: IF AIR PRESSURE IS USED TO REMOVE THE SECONDARY PISTON, PLACE THE OPEN 
END OF THE CYLINDER BORE APPROXIMATELY 25.4 MM (1 INCH) FROM A PADDED 
WORKBENCH OR OTHER SURFACE TO CATCH THE PISTON WHEN IT COMES OUT OF THE BORE. 
APPLY LOW AIR PRESSURE VERY CAREFULLY TO EASE THE PISTON OUT OF THE BORE. 
NEVER POINT THE OPEN END OF THE BORE AT ANYONE WHEN APPLYING AIR PRESSURE. THE 
PISTON MAY COME OUT OF THE BORE WITH CONSIDERABLE FORCE AND CAUSE PERSONAL 
INJURY. 

Using snap ring pliers, remove the snap ring at the end of the master 
cylinder bore. Then release the piston and remove the primary and secondary 
piston assemblies from the cylinder bore. It may be necessary to plug the 
front outlet port and to apply low air pressure to the front compensating 
valve port to remove the secondary piston assembly. 

Remove the differential pressure valve by removing the primary and 
secondary fittings. 

Remove tube seat inserts with a screw extractor.

 Assembly 

Lubricate the secondary piston assembly and the master cylinder bore 
with clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent 
DOT 3 brake fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A. 

Assemble the secondary return spring (smaller of the two springs) in 
the open end of the secondary piston actuator and assemble the piston 
secondary actuator spring (larger spring) in the open end of the secondary 
piston. 

Insert the secondary piston assembly, actuator end first, into the 
master cylinder bore, and push assembly to the bottom of the bore. 

Assemble the primary piston, primary actuator spring, and primary 
actuator together and secure assembly with the retaining ring. 

Insert the primary return spring into the master cylinder bore. 

Lubricate the primary piston assembly with clean brake fluid. Insert 
the primary piston assembly, actuator end first, into the bore. 

Place the lock ring over the rounded end of a suitable tool and depress 
the pistons in the bore. 

Install the lock ring in the groove in the cylinder bore. 

Assemble the compensating valve seals and the small O-ring seal in the 
recesses on the bottom of the reservoir. Be sure that all seals are fully 
seated. 

While holding the primary piston stroked 25.40 ± 1.27 mm (1.0 
± 0.05 inch), assemble the compensating valve springs and the 
compensating valve poppets in the compensating valve ports. Install the piston 
stop pin in its bore. 

Holding the pistons depressed, position the reservoir on the master 
cylinder body and secure with the four mounting bolts. Tighten the bolts to 
20-23 Nm (15-17 lb-ft). 

Attach the differential pressure valve using new seal bushings. Tighten 
special fittings to 68-72 Nm (50-53 lb-ft). 

Press new tube seat inserts into the outlet ports with tube nuts. 

Bench bleed (optional) and install the master cylinder. Refer to Brake 
Master Cylinder in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. To 
bleed brakes, refer to Hydraulic System Bleeding in the Service Procedures 
portion of this section.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Hydraulic Line Repair

Steel tubing is used in the hydraulic lines between the master cylinder 
and the front brake tube connector and between the rear brake tube connector 
and the rear brake cylinders. Steel tubing is also used to connect the master 
cylinder to the flexible brake hose at the rear axle. Flexible hoses connect 
the brake tube to the front brake cylinders and to the rear brake tube 
connector.

When replacing hydraulic brake tubing, hoses, or connectors, tighten 
all connections securely. After replacement, bleed the brake system at the 
wheel cylinders and at the master cylinder. Refer to Hydraulic System Bleeding 
in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

 WARNING: COPPER TUBING SHOULD NOT BE USED IN THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. USE ONLY SAE 
J526 OR J527 STEEL TUBING, OR EQUIVALENT. 

 NOTE: If a section of the brake tube is damaged, replace the entire section 
with tubing of the same type, size, shape, and length. Be careful not to kink 
or crack the tubing when bending it to fit the frame or rear axle forms.

Double flare brake tubing as described below should provide good 
leakproof connections.

 NOTE: Always clean the inside of a new brake tube with clean isopropyl alcohol.

 Flaring a Line (Split-Die Type) 

Cut off and straighten the required length of line (a tubing cutter 
tool will simplify making a clean and square cut).

Square off the ends of the line with a file and chamfer the end of the 
line to be flared.

Select the split die for the line to be used, clean out all filings, 
and insert the die into the tapered hole in the body.

Push the tube through the die until the line is even with the face of 
the die. Lock the line in this position by tightening the wing nut securely.

The punches are marked Op. 1 and Op. 2. Slide the first operation punch 
into the hole in the center of the body and tighten the screw securely to form 
the single flare.

[FIGURE: H20931A.gif]

Release the screw and replace the first operation punch with the second 
punch and tighten the screw to form the double flare.

Release the screw, wing nut, punch, and dies.

 NOTE: The finished flare must be square with the line, free of cracks and 
have a smooth mating surface to make sure connection is leakproof.

Remove the line and inspect the flare for cracks or poor flare form. If 
the flare is not correct, cut it off and repeat the process.

[FIGURE: H46841A.gif]

 Flaring a Line (Flaring-Bar Type) 

Cut off and straighten the required length of line (a tubing cutter 
tool will simplify making a clean and square cut).

Square off the ends of the line with a file and chamfer the end of the 
line to be flared. Make sure to clean out all filings.

Insert the line through its appropriate ribbed hole in the bar assembly 
until the end of the line sticks out about as far as the thickness of the 
adapter above the bar, or even with the bar, depending on the tool used.

Fit the adapter onto the line and slide the bar into the yoke. Lock the 
bar in position with the line beneath the yoke screw.

Form the single flare by tightening the yoke screw securely.

Release the screw and remove the adapter.

Form the double flare by tightening the yoke screw again, with second 
adapter fitted, depending on the tool used.

Release the screw bar and flared line.

Inspect the flare for cracks or poor flare form, and repeat the process 
if the flare is not correct.

[FIGURE: H46851A.gif]

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Brake Hose

 NOTE: The wet appearance of the outer cover of rubber brake hoses is called 
"sweating." This is a normal condition for neoprene rayon braid hose. This 
"sweating" condition is not evidence of a brake fluid leak and will not result 
in a loss of pressure in the system.

Replace a flexible brake hose if it shows signs of softening, cracking 
or other damage.

When installing a new brake hose, position the hose to avoid contact 
with other vehicle parts.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Hydraulic System Bleeding

When any part of the brake hydraulic system has been disconnected for 
service, air will enter the system. To remove the air, the system must be bled 
using either Rotunda Brake Bleeder 104-00064 or equivalent, or the manual 
method. If only one system has been opened, normal feel can usually be 
restored by bleeding only the opened system.

 System Priming 

When a new brake master cylinder has been installed, or the brake 
system emptied or partially emptied, fluid may not flow from the wheel 
cylinder bleeder screws during normal bleeding. It may be necessary to prime 
the system using the following procedure:

Use a tubing wrench to remove the brake tubes from the brake master 
cylinder.

Install short brake tubes in the brake master cylinder and position 
them so that they point back into the brake master cylinder reservoir, and the 
ends of the brake tubes are submerged in brake fluid.

Fill the brake master cylinder reservoir with new Ford High Performance 
DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or DOT 3 equivalent fluid meeting Ford 
Specification ESA-M6C25-A.

Cover the brake master cylinder reservoir with a shop towel.

 CAUTION: Brake fluid is harmful to painted and plastic surfaces. If brake fluid 
is spilled onto a painted or plastic surface, immediately wash it with water. 

Pump the brakes until clear, bubble-free fluid comes out of both 
temporary brake tubes.

Remove the short brake tubes and reinstall the brake tubes.

Bleed each brake tube at the brake master cylinder using the following 
procedure:

Have an assistant pump the brake pedal 10 times and then hold firm 
pressure on the brake pedal.

Loosen the rearmost brake tube fittings with a tubing wrench until a 
stream of brake fluid comes out. Have an assistant maintain pressure on the 
brake pedal until the brake tube fitting is tightened again.

Repeat this operation until clear, bubble-free fluid comes out from 
around the brake tube fitting.

Repeat this bleeding operation at the front brake tube fittings.

If any of the brake tubes have been removed, it can be helpful to prime 
the system by gravity bleeding it. This should be done after the brake master 
cylinder is primed and bled.

To prime the brake system:

Fill the brake master cylinder reservoir with new Ford High Performance 
DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or DOT 3 equivalent fluid meeting Ford 
Specification ESA-M6C25A.

One at a time, loosen both the wheel cylinder bleeder screws and leave 
them open until clear brake fluid flows out. Be sure to check the brake master 
cylinder reservoir fluid level often and not let it run dry.

Tighten the wheel cylinder bleeder screws to 6-8 Nm (53-70 lb-in).

One at a time, loosen the front disc brake caliper bleeder screws. 
Leave the front disc brake caliper bleeder screws open until clear fluid flows 
out. Be sure to check the brake master cylinder reservoir level often and not 
let it run dry.

Tighten the front disc brake caliper bleeder screws to 6-8 Nm 
(53-70 lb-in).

After the brake master cylinder has been primed, the brake tubes bled 
at the brake master cylinder, and the brake system primed, normal brake system 
bleeding can resume at each wheel.

 Manual Bleeding 

Clean all dirt from the brake master cylinder filler cap area.

If the brake master cylinder is known or suspected of having air in the 
bore, it must be bled before any of the brakes are bled. To bleed the brake 
master cylinder, follow the procedures described in this section.

 CAUTION: The brake master cylinder must be at least three-quarters full during 
air bleeding. 

To bleed the front disc brake calipers and rear wheel cylinders proceed 
as follows:

Begin at the rear wheel cylinder bleeder screws.

Attach a rubber hose to the wheel cylinder bleeder screw. The end of 
the hose should fit snugly around the end of the wheel cylinder bleeder screw.

 CAUTION: Brake fluid is harmful to painted and plastic surfaces. If brake fluid 
is spilled onto a painted or plastic surface, immediately wash it with water. 

 NOTE: Never reuse brake fluid.

Submerge the free end of the hose in a container partially filled with 
clean brake fluid.

Have an assistant pump the brake pedal 5-10 times and maintain pressure 
on the brake pedal after the last stroke.

Loosen the wheel cylinder bleeder screw approximately 3/4 turn. It is 
very important that the assistant maintain constant pressure on the brake 
pedal until the brake pedal drops all the way down and the wheel cylinder 
bleeder screw is closed again. If brake pedal pressure is released, air will 
be drawn back into the system.

Tighten the wheel cylinder bleeder screw to 6-8 Nm (53-70 lb-in).

Repeat this operation until the fluid is clear and air bubbles no 
longer appear at the submerged end of the rubber hose.

Repeat these steps at the other rear wheel cylinder or rear disc brake 
caliper and then the front disc brake calipers.

 Pressure Bleeding 

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF IRRITATION 
PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET MEDICAL 
ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

Bleed the longest lines first. Be sure the bleeder tank contains enough 
specified brake fluid, Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA 
or DOT 3 equivalent fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A to complete 
the bleeding operation. Charge the tank with approximately 69-206 kPa (10-30 
psi) of air pressure. Never exceed 345 kPa (50 psi) of pressure. Never re-use 
brake fluid that has been drained from the hydraulic system.

Clean all dirt from the master cylinder cap.

Remove master cylinder reservoir cap, and fill the master cylinder 
reservoir with the specified brake fluid.

 NOTE: Master cylinder pressure bleeder adapter tools are available from 
various manufacturers of pressure bleeding equipment. Follow the instructions 
of the manufacturer when installing the adapter.

Install pressure bleeder adapter Rotunda Brake Bleeder 104-00064 or 
equivalent to the master cylinder, and attach bleeder tank hose to fitting on 
adapter.

Place a 3/8-inch box wrench on right rear brake wheel cylinder bleeder 
fitting. Attach a bleeder tube snugly around bleeder fitting.

Open valve on bleeder tank to admit pressurized brake fluid to the 
master cylinder reservoir.

Submerge free end of tube in a partially filled container with clean 
brake fluid and loosen bleeder fitting.

When air bubbles no longer appear in the fluid at the submerged end of 
the bleeder tube, close bleeder fitting and remove tube.

Continue bleeding the system, going in order from the left rear brake 
wheel cylinder to the front right brake wheel cylinder, and ending with front 
left brake wheel cylinder.

When the bleeding operation is completed, close bleeder tank valve and 
remove the tank hose from adapter fitting.

Remove the pressure bleeder adapter tool.

Fill master cylinder reservoir to maximum fill level line indicated on 
reservoir.

Install master cylinder cap.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Brake Master Cylinder

Wash all parts to be reused in clean Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake 
Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or an equivalent DOT 3 brake fluid meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M6C25-A. Be sure that all foreign matter is removed from the 
bottom of the reservoir.

Master cylinder repair kits are available which contain all the parts 
ordinarily required when overhauling master cylinders. Refer to the applicable 
parts book for the part number of repair kit. The cylinder may be repaired, if 
necessary, as follows: 

Examine the cylinder bore for scoring or corrosion. It is best to 
replace a corroded cylinder. Corrosion can be identified as pits or excessive 
roughness. 

 CAUTION: Do not hone the master cylinder bore when the brake master cylinder is 
overhauled. It is recommended that the cylinder body be replaced rather than 
"cleaned up" by honing the bore. Honing may damage the bore surface, leaving a 
softer and rougher surface which will cause more rapid wear of rubber 
components. 

Polish any discolored or stained area with crocus cloth by revolving 
the cylinder on the cloth supported by a finger. Do not use emery cloth or 
sandpaper. Clean the cylinder thoroughly after polishing. 

Inspect parts for damage and excessive wear and replace as required.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Brake Lines and Hoses

Inspect the brake tubes under the vehicle for damage and proper 
routing. Check the front brake hoses and rear wheel brake hoses for any signs 
of damage, cracking or setting. The front and rear wheel brake hose fittings 
must be tight without signs of leakage.

1999 P800, F700, F800, B800 Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Brake Fluid Leakage

If signs of leakage are not present but the brake master cylinder is 
definitely low, it is possible that evidence of fluid leakage may have been 
washed off by rain or snow because brake fluid is water soluble. To determine 
if a leak exists, proceed as follows:

Refill the system.

Bleed the system.

Apply the brakes several times.

Examine the system to verify that the brake master cylinder reservoir 
level is actually dropping.

Locate and correct the external leak.

Internal and external leaks are two problems that can affect a brake 
hydraulic system. The hydraulic brake system will not cause the vehicle to do 
any of the following:

vibrate

pull

grab

squeal

allow the brake pedal to pulse

In most cases the hydraulic system will not even cause the brakes to 
drag. The sources of these problems are found elsewhere in the brake system, 
but it is always a good policy to first check the entire hydraulic system for 
leaks before continuing to diagnose any other brake problems.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Pedal Linkage

Remove lower end of rod and brake master cylinder push rod bushing from 
bellcrank pin and loosen jam nut.

Hold brake pedal up against rubber stop and turn rod until lower hole 
lines up with bellcrank pin.

Slide rod and brake master cylinder push rod bushing onto bellcrank pin 
and reinstall washer and locking pin.

Tighten jam nut.

Electric Motor Relay

 Fluid Flow 

During system operation normal flow from the engine-driven hydraulic 
brake pump enters the inlet pressure port of the Hydro-Max booster, flows 
through the poppet valve, power piston and flow switch, exits from the outlet 
return port to the parking brake valve and returns to the engine-driven brake 
pump.

Force applied to the brake booster rod by the vehicle operator 
activates a poppet valve restricting flow through the power piston. The 
resulting pressure acting on the power piston applies a force to the master 
cylinder. The reaction piston provides the operator with the desired feel 
during an application of force to the brake booster rod. 

The pressure regulator assembly limits the maximum internal booster 
pressure developed during a full application. 

Fluid flow through the flow switch opens the reserve electric pump and 
motor assembly electrical circuit during normal operation. A separate check 
ball in the electric pump and motor assembly prevents backflow through the 
electric pump and motor assembly during normal power applications.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Brake, Power, Hydro-Max Booster

 Inspection and Verification 

 NOTE: After any major brake system or component overhaul, the system should 
be purged of old fluid.

Always make the following preliminary checks before testing the brake 
system:

Before testing the brake system, always check the service brake system 
fluid level in the brake master cylinder reservoir. If the fluid level is not 
to the level of the bottom of the rings on the master cylinder reservoir, add 
Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 
fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A.

Check the parking brake system fluid level in the brake pump reservoir 
with the engine off and the parking brake applied. The fluid level must show 
between the ADD and FULL markings on the dipstick. If the fluid is below the 
ADD mark, add Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® 
equivalent.

 Component Tests 

 Dual Brake Warning Lamp System 

Key to RUN. If the light on the red brake warning lamp remains on, 
there may be a shorted or broken switch, grounded switch wires, or an 
uncentered pressure differential valve. Apply and release the brake pedal. If 
light does not go out, check for fluid leaks. Check for a grounded switch 
connector or wire and service or replace the wire assembly. If the wire is in 
good condition, replace the brake warning lamp switch.

Key to START. If the red brake warning lamp does not light, check the 
light and wiring and replace or service wiring, if necessary.

When both brake systems are functioning normally, the equal pressure in 
the pressure differential valve will keep the valve centered during brake 
pedal application. The brake warning lamp will light only when the ignition 
key is in the START position.

If the brake warning lamp does not light when pressure is not equal in 
both brake systems, the warning lamp may be burned out, the warning lamp 
switch may be inoperative or the switch-to-lamp wiring may have an open 
circuit. Check the bulb and replace it, if required. Check the switch-to-lamp 
wires for an open circuit and service or replace them, if required. If the 
warning lamp still does not light, replace the switch.

 Brake Warning Indicator Stays On (Red Lens) 

Indicates bulb check during start. 

Indicates primary/secondary hydraulic brake system is functioning 
improperly on vehicles equipped with dual hydraulic brake systems. 

Indicates the engine-driven brake pump system is functioning improperly 
(in combination with the BRK ELEC MTR lamp and buzzer). 

 Brake Electric Motor Indicator Stays On (Amber Lens), Buzzer, Audible 
Warning 

Indicates bulb check/functional check during start. 

Indicates that the electric pump and motor assembly backup system is 
inoperative. 

Indicates operation of the electric pump and motor assembly during 
brake application. 

Indicates inadequate fluid flow from the engine-driven brake pump (in 
combination with the red brake lamp).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hydro-Max Booster

 CAUTION: The Hydro-Max booster for the 1-3/4-inch, and 2-inch master cylinders 
produce different boost pressures. The 2-inch master cylinder requires a 
higher boost pressure output from the engine-driven brake pump. Failure to 
replace the 2-inch master cylinder booster with a like unit will result in 
substantially degraded braking performance. Installation of a 2-inch booster 
on a 1-3/4-inch master cylinder will result in overly sensitive brakes and 
excessive pressure output from the master cylinder. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the negative battery cable. 

Disconnect the brake booster rod at the brake pedal. 

Disconnect the electrical power lead to the electric motor relay, and 
the flow switch wire from the flow switch contact assembly.

 CAUTION: Do not depress the brake pedal while the hydraulic fluid supply line is 
disconnected. The inlet pressure port check ball may be dislodged which will 
result in a non-functional backup system. 

Disconnect the hydraulic fluid supply line from the booster inlet 
pressure port. Cap or plug both the supply line and the inlet pressure port. 

Remove the hose clamp and disconnect the fluid return line. Cap or plug 
both the fluid return line and the outlet return port. 

Remove the capscrew securing the electric motor relay to the booster 
housing. Remove the electric motor relay. 

Loosen the four nuts attaching master cylinder to the Hydro-Max 
booster, while supporting the master cylinder. 

 NOTE: Hydraulic brake lines may remain attached. However, added support of 
the master cylinder is required. 

Separate the master cylinder from the Hydro-Max booster by pulling it 
straight apart.

Loosen the four bolts attaching the Hydro-Max booster to the dash 
panel. Remove the two bottom bolts and lockwashers and, while supporting the 
Hydro-Max booster, remove the two upper nuts. 

Pull the Hydro-Max booster straight out from the dash panel, and lift 
it from the engine compartment. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: The Hydro-Max booster operates on automatic transmission fluid only. 
Prior to assembly, all parts should be clean and free from contamination from 
other fluids.

If the brake booster rod was removed, install the brake booster rod in 
the Hydro-Max booster. Make sure a new brake booster rod grommet is used. 

Insert the Hydro-Max booster through the dash panel. Make sure the 
brake booster rod eye is on the correct side of the brake pedal arm. 

Install the four bolts with lockwashers. Hand-tighten the upper two 
bolts and then the bottom two bolts. Tighten the bolts to 42-57 Nm 
(31-42 lb-ft), the upper bolts first. 

Install the electric motor relay. Tighten the capscrew to 4-6 Nm 
(35-53 lb-in). 

Remove the plug from the outlet return port of the Hydro-Max booster, 
and slide the master cylinder straight onto the Hydro-Max booster until the 
mating surfaces come together. 

Continue to support the master cylinder and install the upper two nuts, 
hand-tight. Remove the master cylinder support and install the bottom two 
nuts, hand-tight. Tighten each nut to 34-41 Nm (25-30 lb-ft), the upper 
nuts first. 

Remove the cap from the outlet return port. Connect the fluid return 
line and tighten the hose clamp. 

Make sure the O-ring for the supply line is in place. Remove the cap 
from the pressure inlet port. Carefully start the supply line fitting and 
tighten to 22-34 Nm (16-25 lb-ft). 

Connect the brake booster rod with bushing to the brake pedal arm. 
Install the flatwasher and a new cotter pin. 

Reconnect the electric power lead to the electric motor relay, and the 
negative battery cable to the battery.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Filling Hydro-Max with Fluid 

With the engine off and the parking brake applied, fill the reservoir 
of the engine-driven brake pump, supplying the Hydro-Max booster. Use 
Motorcraft MERCON® ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent. 

Crank the engine over several times. Use either remote starter switch 
or ignition key. 

Check and refill the brake pump reservoir. Crank the engine over 
several times again. 

Refill the brake pump reservoir to the level indicated on the dipstick. 
The Hydro-Max booster, hydraulic lines and engine-driven brake pump should now 
be filled with fluid.

================================================================================

1999 P800, F700, F800, B800 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

System Checkout 

With the engine off, depress the brake pedal. The electric pump and 
motor assembly should run, the amber warning lamp should be lit and the 
warning buzzer should sound. 

Start the engine and push the brake pedal several times. There should 
be no warning signals and the electric pump and motor assembly should not run. 

Stop the engine, check the brake pump reservoir and add power steering 
fluid as needed.

1999 P800, F700, F800, B800 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Pump, Electric Motor

 Removal 

Disconnect the negative battery cable. 

Disconnect the electric power lead from the electric motor relay. 

 NOTE: Two to three cups of fluid will drain from the Hydro-Max booster. 

Place a catch basin or pan under the Hydro-Max booster. 

 NOTE: Do not allow the mating surfaces to scrape against one another. 

Remove the two bolts attaching the electric pump and motor assembly to 
the bottom of the Hydro-Max booster.

Remove the electric pump and motor assembly from the Hydro-Max booster 
and carefully remove it from the engine compartment. 

 NOTE: Replace sealing O-rings with new ones for every reassembly.

Replace two sealing O-rings between the electric pump and motor 
assembly and the Hydro-Max booster.

 Installation 

Clean the mating surfaces and install two new O-rings into their 
grooves in the pump housing. 

Before installing the electric pump and motor assembly on the Hydro-Max 
booster housing, make sure the check ball and retainer are in place in the 
discharge port. 

Place the electric pump and motor assembly against the bottom of the 
Hydro-Max booster. Be careful not to scrape either surface or to disturb the 
location of the O-rings. 

Insert the two bolts and tighten them evenly to 24-34 Nm (18-25 
lb-ft). 

Connect the electric power lead to the electric motor relay, and the 
negative battery cable to the battery. 

Refill the brake pump reservoir to the level indicated on the dipstick. 
Refer to Filling Hydro-Max with Fluid and System Checkout in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.
