 Disassembly 

Remove the shift bar housing retaining capscrews and lockwashers. Jar 
the housing lightly to break the gasket seal. Remove the shift bar housing and 
gasket from the transmission.

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears. Remove the yoke 
nut and the yoke or flange. Remove the mainshaft rear bearing cap retaining 
nuts and lockwashers. Remove the mainshaft rear bearing cap. Remove the 
speedometer rotor.

[FIGURE: C7415B.gif]

Using a soft hammer, tap the front end of the drive gear to move the 
mainshaft toward the rear approximately 6.35 mm (1/4 inch). Use pry bars to 
remove the rear bearing cup and snap ring.

[FIGURE: C64781B.gif]

Remove the main drive gear bearing cover capscrews. Using a soft 
hammer, tap on the threaded end of the mainshaft to move the mainshaft toward 
the front of the transmission housing.

[FIGURE: C90421A.gif]

Working from front of transmission, remove main drive gear bearing 
cover and shims. Remove main drive gear and bearing assembly.

Using a sling and Rotunda Hand Chain Hoist 164-R1713 or equivalent, 
lift the mainshaft assembly from the transmission housing. The mainshaft 
assembly can be removed by hand but is quite difficult to handle.

[FIGURE: C71581A.gif]

Remove reverse idler lock and countershaft rear bearing cap capscrews. 
Remove countershaft rear bearing cap and shims.

[FIGURE: C8896C.gif]

Remove countershaft rear taper bearing cup.

[FIGURE: C88971A.gif]

Remove the reverse idler shaft with a suitable pry bar.

[FIGURE: C64831A.gif]

 NOTE: Idler gear has loose needle rollers in it. Do not lose these rollers.

Lift the reverse idler gear with roller bearings, spacers and thrust 
washers from the case. Remove needle rollers and spacers from inside reverse 
idler gear.

[FIGURE: C64841A.gif]

Move the countershaft assembly and lift it from transmission case.

[FIGURE: C64871C.gif]

 Assembly 

If the transmission case or countershaft front taper bearing cup was 
replaced, install bearing cup location ring. From inside of case, install 
bearing cup. Coat outer diameter of bore plug with Gasket and Trim Adhesive 
D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M11P17-A and 
ESE-M2G52-A, and install bore plug in case.

[FIGURE: C66301A.gif]

Turn transmission case on end as shown. Position countershaft assembly 
into front bearing cup. Install rear bearing cup over rear taper bearing, and 
tap cup into place.

[FIGURE: C66331A.gif]

Coat the reverse idler thrust washers with Premium Long-Life Grease 
XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B and position 
them in the housing with tang of washer in housing groove, if so equipped.

[FIGURE: C64921A.gif]

Coat inside diameter of reverse idler gear with Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. This 
will hold needle rollers in position while assembling. Insert one roller spacer.

[FIGURE: C64931A.gif]

Position first row of needle rollers on spacer.

[FIGURE: C64941A.gif]

Place roller spacer on first row of rollers.

Position second row of needle rollers.

[FIGURE: C64951A.gif]

Place roller spacer on second row of rollers. Grease rollers to hold in 
place.

 CAUTION: Do not disrupt needle rollers. 

 NOTE: Idler shaft lock groove must line up with the lock screw hole. 

Carefully position reverse idler gear in housing. Insert idler shaft 
through case and idler gear needle rollers. Drive shaft into position. Install 
capscrew and tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Position the same shims that were removed at disassembly over 
countershaft rear bearing cup. Install countershaft rear bearing cap. Install 
and tighten capscrews to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C6634B.gif]

 NOTE: Each time a change is made, tighten capscrews and roll countershaft.

Roll countershaft to be sure bearings and bearing cups are seated. 
Position Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent as shown. Pry 
on countershaft to get countershaft end play. End play must be between 0.05 mm 
and 0.20 mm (0.002-0.008 inch). Add shims for more end play or remove shims 
for less end play.

[FIGURE: C6635B.gif]

At final assembly, coat both sides of each shim with Gasket and Trim 
Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M11P17-A 
and ESE-M2G52-A. Position shims over countershaft rear bearing cup. Install 
countershaft rear bearing cap. Apply a band of Pipe Sealant with 
Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
WSK-M2G350-A2 and ESR-M18P7-A to bearing capscrews, 3 mm (0.118 inch) from end 
of threads, 9 mm (0.354 inch) long. Do not dip capscrews. Install and tighten 
capscrews to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C6496B.gif]

Tilt the rear of the mainshaft assembly downward and insert the end of 
the shaft through the output bore in the housing. Lower the front end of the 
mainshaft until it is in line with the pilot bearing opening of the main drive 
gear.

[FIGURE: C71581A.gif]

Position mainshaft rear bearing cup in housing bore. Using soft hammer, 
tap rear bearing cup until cup snap ring is seated against housing.

[FIGURE: C64971B.gif]

Install speedometer rotor on mainshaft. 

Shellac new gasket on mainshaft rear bearing cap and install the cap. 
Use care not to cover the oil return grooves. Install cap on housing with oil 
grooves aligned with oil hole in case. Apply Pipe Sealant with Teflon® 
D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-A2 and 
ESR-M18P7-A to the stud threads. Install bearing cap lockwashers and nuts. 
Tighten nuts to 81-95 Nm (60-70 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7415B.gif]

Install roller bearings, washer and retainer ring in end of main drive 
gear.

Lubricate bearings with Premium Long Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft Taper Bearing Adjustment

 NOTE: The mainshaft rear taper bearing and main drive gear taper bearing must 
have 0.20-0.30 mm (0.008-0.012 inch) end play after assembly of transmission 
is complete. The mainshaft rear taper bearing and bearing cup are not 
adjustable. The main drive gear taper bearing cup is located in the main drive 
gear bearing cover. The required taper bearing end play is achieved by 
inserting shims of different sizes between the bearing cover and transmission 
housing. 

Tighten four bearing cover capscrews to 3.39 Nm (30 lb-in). 
Position two feeler gauges at the capscrew locations as shown, record gap 
between bearing cover and housing. Take an average of the two measurements and 
add 0.406 mm (0.016 inch). For example, if one measurement were 1.066 mm 
(0.042 inch) and the other 1.016 mm (0.040 inch), the average would be 1.041 
mm (0.041 inch). Adding the 0.406 mm (0.016 inch) and 1.041 mm (0.041 inch) 
produces a total of 1.447 mm (0.057 inch). This total represents the thickness 
of the shim pack required to start end play measurement. 

[FIGURE: C10931A.gif]

After determining the size of shim pack required, remove bearing cover 
from housing and install shim pack and bearing cover, making sure that oil 
grooves are up. Install and tighten capscrews to 20-34 Nm (15-25 lb-ft).

Place transmission in vertical position with main drive gear pointing 
down. Install companion flange or yoke. Tighten flange or yoke retaining nut 
to 407-475 Nm (300-350 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Each time a change is made, retighten stud nuts and roll mainshaft. 

Rotate the input shaft six times in each direction to seat front and 
rear taper bearings. Position Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or 
equivalent, as shown. Pry on output flange to get mainshaft end play. End play 
must be between 0.20-0.30 mm (0.008-0.012 inch). Add shims for more end play 
or remove shims for less end play. 

[FIGURE: C6503C.gif]

At final assembly, remove bearing cover. Apply Gasket and Trim Adhesive 
D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M11P17-A and 
ESE-M2652-A to both sides of each shim. Install shims and bearing cover. Apply 
Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications WSK-M2G350-A2 and ESR-M18P7-A to the screw threads. Then, 
install and tighten capscrews to 20-34 Nm (15-25 lb-ft).

With the transmission and shift forks in neutral and a new shift bar 
housing gasket in place, position the shift bar housing over the gears, 
aligning the shift forks with the gearshift hubs. Install shift bar housing 
onto transmission case. If the shift bar housing is in neutral and the 
transmission is in neutral, the transmission main drive gear should turn 
without the output mainshaft turning. Install the center rear capscrews, then 
the center front capscrews. Install the remaining capscrews and tighten to 
47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Lever Housing 

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. USE CARE TO PROTECT EYES WHEN REMOVING SPRING. 

Remove shift lever grip and boot from shift lever. Secure assembly in a 
vise with bottom of housing up. Use a large screwdriver to twist between 
spring and housing, forcing spring from under lugs in housing. Do one coil at 
a time.

[FIGURE: C71671A.gif]

[FIGURE: C7168B.gif]

Remove spade pins from bores in housing.

[FIGURE: C71691A.gif]

With shift lever housing secured in vise, install spade pins in bores 
of housing.

[FIGURE: C71691A.gif]

install tension spring washer over ball, dished side up.

 WARNING: SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. USE CARE TO PROTECT EYES WHEN REMOVING SPRING.

time. Use of a spring driving tool is recommended.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

[FIGURE: C7344F.gif]

The Eaton FS-6205 transmission has five forward speeds and one reverse 
speed with gear ratios as follows: 

First 7.22:1 

Second 3.89:1 

Third 2.22:1 

Fourth 1.39:1 

Fifth 1.00:1 

Reverse 7.22:1 

Countershaft end play is controlled by shims located in the 
countershaft rear bearing cap. Mainshaft end play is controlled by shims 
located in the mainshaft rear bearing cover. The shift forks are single-piece 
forged and are equipped with bronze wear pads that can be replaced.

Section 07-03C: Transmission, Manual, Eaton FS-6205 Five-Speed

1999 F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the following Power Flow 
illustration.

The transmission transfers torque from the engine to the driveshaft 
through the following route: 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the input shaft and 
drive gear. 

The input shaft drive gear transfers torque to the countershaft drive 
gear.

The countershaft drive gear turns the countershaft and all countershaft 
gears. 

Torque from the countershaft gear is transferred to the mainshaft gear 
that is currently engaged. 

The external clutching teeth of the engaged mainshaft gear transfer 
torque to the mainshaft through the synchronizer assembly. 

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the driveshaft through the 
rear yoke.

 Power Flow, FS-6205 

[FIGURE: C7421C.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many of these gear oils, 
particularly 85W140, break down above 110°C (230°F) and coat seals, 
bearings and gears with deposits that can cause premature failures. If these 
deposits are observed (especially a coating on seal areas causing oil 
leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger® CD50 transmission fluid, 
heavy-duty engine oil, mineral gear oil or, Emgard 2924 Synthetic Transmission
Lubricant SAE 50 or equivalent to ensure maximum component life and to maintain your
warranty with Eaton. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Correct lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in a bath of oil circulated by the motion of gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if the following procedures are closely 
followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with filler opening. Because you can reach oil 
with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 25.4 mm 
(one inch) is equal to approximately 3.7 liters (one gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at bottom of case. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. Do not overfill — this will cause oil to be forced out 
of the transmission. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from side of case. Fill 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to level of both openings. The exact amount of oil will 
depend on the transmission inclination and model.

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission Installation Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The following chart illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which 
the transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For 
example: if you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight 
degrees (or 14 percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you 
have a zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 
12-degree (21-percent) grade.

Anytime the transmission operating angle of 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time, the transmission should be equipped with an oil 
pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is correctly lubricated.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one-half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Correct lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 With Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, Heavy Duty 
Engine Oil, Mineral Oil, or Emgard 2924 Synthetic Transmission Lubricant SAE 50 

The transmission should not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent operating temperatures to 
149°C (300°F) will not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 
120°C (250°F), the transmission may require more frequent oil changes 
or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCW's over 40 824 kg 
(90,000 lb)

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). In addition, 
transmission oil coolers are not recommended with these gear oils, since the 
oil cooler materials may be attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature 
limit and oil cooler restriction with these gear oils generally limit their 
success to milder applications.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission 

 Removal 

Raise hood.

Disconnect battery(s).

Remove floor mat and floor plate.

Position shift lever in neutral. Remove four screws retaining shift 
lever housing to shift bar housing. Jar housing lightly to break the gasket 
seal. Remove shift lever housing and gasket. Cover opening in the shift bar 
housing.

Position a suitable drain pan under transmission. Remove drain plug and 
drain the transmission oil. Reinstall drain plug and tighten to 61-75 
Nm (45-55 lb-ft).

Remove driveshaft. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Disconnect speedometer sensor and backup lamp switch.

Position Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent under the transmission.

Fabricate two guide pins from standard bolts as shown.

[FIGURE: C52661A.gif]

Remove two lower screws and washers retaining the transmission to the 
clutch housing. Install the two fabricated guide pins into the lower holes. 
Remove the two upper screws and washers retaining the transmission to the 
clutch housing.

Remove transmission from the clutch housing. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Lower transmission from vehicle.

 Installation 

If removed, reinstall the two fabricated guide pins into lower holes of 
clutch housing.

Using Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent, raise and align transmission to the clutch housing. Install 
transmission to the clutch housing. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Install two upper transmission-to-clutch housing retaining screws and 
washers and tighten to 197-210 Nm (145-155 lb-ft).

Remove fabricated guide pins. Install two lower transmission-to-clutch 
housing retaining screws and washers and tighten to 197-210 Nm (145-155 
lb-ft).

Connect speedometer sensor and backup lamp switch.

Install driveshaft. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Clean the shift lever housing gasket mating surfaces. Make sure the 
shift block and yoke notches are aligned in the neutral position. Install 
gasket and the shift lever housing. Apply Threadlock and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the screw threads. 
Then, install and tighten the retaining screws to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Install floor plate and floor mat.

Fill transmission with the appropriate type and quantity oil. Refer to 
Specifications.

Connect battery(s).

Close hood.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Transmission 

 Disassembly 

Remove capscrews and separate shift bar housing and gasket from case. 

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears with mainshaft 
sliding clutches.

Remove the yoke nut and the yoke or flange.

[FIGURE: C71361B.gif]

Remove the six capscrews and tap the input shaft bearing cover with a 
rubber mallet to separate the cover from the case. Remove the cover. 

[FIGURE: C7138B.gif]

If necessary, remove the oil seal from the input shaft bearing cover. 
Refer to Input Shaft Bearing Cover in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of 
this section.

Remove the input shaft assembly from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71591A.gif]

Remove the four nuts and lockwashers that hold the mainshaft rear 
bearing cover to the transmission case. Insert screwdrivers into the notches 
on either side of the mainshaft rear bearing cover and gently separate the 
cover from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71391A.gif]

Remove shims (if they did not come off when mainshaft rear bearing 
cover was removed) and speedometer rotor.

[FIGURE: C71401A.gif]

Wrap a sling around the second/third synchronizer. Using Rotunda Hand 
Chain Hoist 164-R1713 or equivalent, remove mainshaft assembly from case. 

[FIGURE: C5274C.gif]

 NOTE: Countershaft may slide rearward and out of bearing bore. 

Remove the four capscrews and remove the countershaft rear bearing cap, 
shims and bearing cup from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C7141B.gif]

Using Impact Slide Hammer D79P-100-A or equivalent, remove reverse 
idler gear shaft. Remove locating ball once it is exposed.

[FIGURE: C7143C.gif]

Remove reverse idler gear, bearings, spacer and thrust washers.

[FIGURE: C73471A.gif]

Move countershaft assembly to the rear and lift it from the case. 

[FIGURE: C73481A.gif]

If countershaft front bearing cup is to be replaced, use a suitable 
driver and bearing cup remover to drive the bore plug through the front of the 
transmission case and drive the bearing cup toward the rear of the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71461A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: The snap ring should be installed with open end aligned with lube 
trough in the case. 

If removed, install snap ring, countershaft front bearing cup (from 
inside of case) and bore plug using a suitable driver. Coat outer diameter of 
bore with Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESE-M2G52-A and ESR-M11P17-A before installing.

[FIGURE: C71471A.gif]

Turn transmission case onto end with the rear of the transmission 
facing up. Stand countershaft assembly into front bearing cup.

[FIGURE: C73491A.gif]

Use Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B on reverse idler thrust washers to hold them in 
place. Position tangs of washers in groove of housing.

[FIGURE: C7149B.gif]

Install bearings and spacer in reverse idler gear.

[FIGURE: C73501A.gif]

 NOTE: Gear can be installed either way. 

Position reverse idler gear in transmission case.

[FIGURE: C73511A.gif]

Insert reverse idler gear shaft through transmission case, bearings, 
spacer and thrust washers. Line up notch in shaft with notch in case. Install 
locating ball and drive the shaft into position.

[FIGURE: C7152B.gif]

Coat outer diameter of countershaft rear bearing cup with Gasket and 
Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESE-M2G52-A and ESR-M11P17-A. Install countershaft rear bearing cup into case.

[FIGURE: C71531A.gif]

Temporarily install new shims over countershaft rear bearing cup.

Install the countershaft rear bearing cap and capscrews. Tighten 
capscrews to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

Rotate countershaft to seat the bearings. Position Dial 
Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent on the shoulder of one of 
the countershaft gears. Lift countershaft to measure end play. End play must 
be between 0.15-0.25 mm (0.006-0.010 inch). Add shims for less end play or 
remove shims for more end play. Once end play is correct, remove rear bearing 
cap. Apply a light coat of Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A to both 
sides of shims and to the rear bearing cap and reinstall them.

[FIGURE: C7155D.gif]

Coat threads of capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® 
D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and 
ESR-M18P7-A and tighten to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12970A.gif]

Place transmission in a horizontal position. Shift second/third 
mainshaft synchronizer into third gear.

Place a sling or rope around the second/third synchronizer assembly. 
Using Rotunda Hand Chain Hoist 164-R1713 or equivalent, carefully lower the 
assembly into the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C5274C.gif]

Align clutching teeth on main drive gear with teeth in fifth speed 
synchronizer cup. Install input shaft into aligned teeth.

[FIGURE: C71591A.gif]

If removed, install input shaft oil seal and bearing cup into input 
shaft bearing cover. Refer to Input Shaft Bearing Cover in the Disassembly and 
Assembly portion of this section for procedure. 

 NOTE: Top of input shaft bearing cover is marked for proper installation. 

Install gasket and input shaft bearing cover. Apply Pipe Sealant with 
Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A to the threads of the capscrews and tighten to 
20-34 Nm (15-25 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7160B.gif]

Install speedometer rotor.

[FIGURE: C71611A.gif]

 NOTE: Top of mainshaft rear bearing cover is marked for proper installation. 

If removed, install bearing cup and oil seal into mainshaft rear 
bearing cover. Refer to Mainshaft Rear Bearing Cover in the Disassembly and 
Assembly portion of this section for procedure. Temporarily install shims and 
mainshaft rear bearing cover. Tighten nuts to 81-95 Nm (60-70 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7162C.gif]

Place transmission in a vertical position (with the rear of the 
transmission facing up). Engage two mainshaft gears to lock transmission. 
Install yoke or flange and nut. Tighten nut to 407-475 Nm (300-350 
lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Once end play is correct, remove yoke or flange and mainshaft rear 
bearing cover and apply a light coat of Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B 
or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESE-M2G52-A and ESR-M11P17-A to both 
sides of shims. 

Rotate input shaft and mainshaft to seat bearings and races. Position 
Dial Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent so it contacts the end 
of the output shaft as shown in the illustration. Pry up on output shaft to 
measure end play. End play must be between 0.15-0.25 mm (0.006-0.010 inch). 
Add shims for more end play. Remove shims for less end play.

[FIGURE: C7163F.gif]

 NOTE: Top of mainshaft rear bearing cover is marked for proper installation. 

Install mainshaft rear bearing cover. Apply Pipe Sealant with 
Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
WSK-M2G350-A2 and ESR-M18P7-A to studs and tighten nuts to 81-95 Nm 
(60-70 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C71641B.gif]

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears. Install yoke or 
flange and nut. Tighten nut to 407-475 Nm (300-350 lb-ft). 

With the transmission and shift yokes in neutral, and a new shift bar 
housing gasket in place, position the shift bar housing over the gears, 
aligning the shift yokes with corresponding synchronizers and sliding clutch. 
Install shift bar housing onto transmission case.

Apply Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A to the threads of 
the capscrews. Install two capscrews into alignment holes of shift bar housing 
and tighten to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7354B.gif]

Install remaining capscrews and tighten to 47-54 Nm (35-40 
lb-ft). Do not install the shift lever assembly until the transmission is 
installed in the vehicle.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Shift Lever Housing 

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. USE CARE TO PROTECT EYES WHEN REMOVING SPRING. 

Remove shift lever grip and boot from shift lever, secure assembly in a 
vise with bottom of housing up. Use a large screwdriver to twist between 
spring and housing, forcing spring from under lugs in housing. Do one coil at 
a time.

[FIGURE: C71671A.gif]

Remove tension spring, washer and shift lever from housing.

[FIGURE: C7168B.gif]

Remove spade pins from bores in housing.

[FIGURE: C71691A.gif]

 Assembly 

With shift lever housing secured in vise, install spade pins in bores 
of housing.

[FIGURE: C71691A.gif]

Position shift lever in housing with spade pins in lever ball slot and 
install tension spring washer over ball, dished side up.

[FIGURE: C7170B.gif]

 WARNING: SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. USE CARE TO PROTECT EYES WHEN REMOVING SPRING. 

Install tension spring under lugs in housing, seating one coil at a 
time. Use of a spring driving tool is recommended.

[FIGURE: C71711A.gif]

Remove assembly from vise. Install rubber boot over shift lever and 
against housing. Install shift lever grip.

 Disassembly 

Lay shift bar housing on workbench. Remove all capscrews and retainers.

[FIGURE: C7355B.gif]

Remove first-reverse yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C73561A.gif]

Remove second/third yoke assembly and interlock pin.

[FIGURE: C73571A.gif]

Remove fourth/fifth yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C73581A.gif]

If yoke replacement is required, remove yoke by driving the roll pin 
through the yoke and rail. If the yoke pad inserts are to be replaced, remove 
worn pad from shift fork, install new pad, and bend tabs over top and bottom 
of fork. 

 NOTE: Remove interlock and detent balls before removing springs. 

Remove interlock balls, detent balls and springs.

[FIGURE: C73591A.gif]

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER ARE UNDER SPRING PRESSURE. 

If the removal of the reverse plunger is necessary, secure the shift 
bar in a hand press. Depress the retainer washer and spring and remove the 
snap ring.

Remove the retainer washer.

Remove the inner and outer springs.

Remove the washer and the reverse plunger.

 Assembly 

If reverse plunger was removed, install reverse plunger and washer in 
reverse shift block.

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER WILL BE UNDER PRESSURE WHEN INSTALLED. 

Install outer and inner springs.

Place the shift bar in a hand press. Depress retainer washer and spring 
and install the snap ring.

 NOTE: Balls and springs can be used interchangeably. 

Install interlock balls, detent balls and springs in the following 
sequence:

Position three balls into reverse lamp switch bore and install 
first-reverse detent spring and ball.

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install second/third 
detent spring and ball.

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install fourth/fifth 
detent spring and ball.

 NOTE: All yoke assemblies must be installed in the neutral position. 

Position first-reverse yoke in housing.

[FIGURE: C73601A.gif]

Install interlock pin in second/third yoke assembly and install in 
housing. Position yoke in housing as shown in the illustration.

[FIGURE: C73611A.gif]

Position fourth/fifth yoke assembly in housing as shown in the 
illustration.

[FIGURE: C7362B.gif]

 NOTE: If a new housing is being used in the assembly, the bores for the 
retainer capscrews are not tapped. The capscrews that are used are 
thread-forming and can be reused on a new housing. 

 NOTE: Support yokes in the proper position while installing retainers. 

Install front retainer over shift bars. Coat threads of retainer 
capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A.

Install capscrews and tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12972A.gif]

Position shift yokes as shown and install center retainer. Coat threads 
of retainer capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A.

[FIGURE: C7363B.gif]

Position rear retainer over shift bar. Coat threads of retainer 
capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-A2 and ESR-M18P7-A.

[FIGURE: C7364B.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft 

 Disassembly 

Install mainshaft assembly in a soft-jawed vise or use wood blocks to 
prevent damage. Position mainshaft in vise with the front of the shaft facing 
up. Remove the fourth/fifth synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C7366B.gif]

Use a suitable puller such as 2-Jaw Puller D80L-1002-L and Bearing 
Pulling Attachment D84L-1122A or equivalent mounted behind the fourth/fifth 
shift hub and remove the hub and bearing.

[FIGURE: C12472A.gif]

Remove fourth gear, bearings, and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C73681A.gif]

Remove snap ring, thrust washer and locating ball from third gear.

[FIGURE: C73691A.gif]

Remove third gear, bearings and spacer.

[FIGURE: C73701A.gif]

Remove second/third speed synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C7371C.gif]

Remove snap ring and second/third shift hub.

[FIGURE: C7372C.gif]

Remove second gear, bearings and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7383C.gif]

Remove snap ring, thrust washer and locating ball from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7374C.gif]

Remove first gear, bearings and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7375C.gif]

Remove mainshaft sliding clutch gear.

[FIGURE: C7376C.gif]

Reposition mainshaft in vise with the rear of the shaft facing up.

[FIGURE: C73771A.gif]

Using 2-Jaw Puller D80L-1002-L or equivalent, remove the reverse gear, 
washer and rear bearing.

[FIGURE: C12473A.gif]

Remove reverse gear bearings and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C73791A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: All parts must be lubricated with recommended transmission lubricant 
when reassembling. No part should be reassembled dry. Refer to Recommended 
Lubricants Chart under the Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Install mainshaft in vise equipped with wood or brass jaws, rear of 
mainshaft facing up. Lubricate reverse gear bearings, and install with spacer 
between bearings.

Install reverse gear with clutching teeth of gear down.

[FIGURE: C73801A.gif]

Install reverse gear washer. Washer can be installed either way.

[FIGURE: C73811A.gif]

Using a sleeve-type bearing driver, install rear bearing.

[FIGURE: C73821A.gif]

Reposition mainshaft in vise with front of mainshaft facing up. 
Lubricate friction surface, and install mainshaft sliding clutch gear.

[FIGURE: C7376C.gif]

Lubricate and install first gear bearings and spacer. Install first 
gear, clutching teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C7375C.gif]

Install locating ball and thrust washer. Washer can be installed either 
way. Install snap ring.

[FIGURE: C7374C.gif]

Lubricate and install second gear bearings and spacer. Install second 
gear, clutching teeth facing up.

[FIGURE: C7383C.gif]

Install second/third shift hub with stepped face of hub facing up. 
Install snap ring in groove of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7372C.gif]

Lubricate friction surface, and install second/third speed synchronizer 
and cups.

[FIGURE: C7371C.gif]

Lubricate and install third gear bearings and spacer. Install third 
gear, clutching teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C73701A.gif]

Install locating ball and thrust washer. Washer can be installed either 
way. Install snap ring.

[FIGURE: C73691A.gif]

Lubricate and install fourth gear bearings and spacer. Install fourth 
gear, clutching teeth facing up.

[FIGURE: C73681A.gif]

Install fourth/fifth shift hub with shouldered end of hub facing down.

[FIGURE: C7384B.gif]

Install synchronizer cup. Lubricate friction surface, and install 
fourth/fifth speed synchronizer assembly and fifth speed synchronizer cup.

[FIGURE: C7366B.gif]

Using a suitable sleeve-type driver, install main drive gear bearing.

[FIGURE: C7386B.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Countershaft 

 Disassembly 

Position 2-Jaw Puller D80L-1002-L or equivalent behind rear 
countershaft bearing and remove bearing.

[FIGURE: C12474A.gif]

Position countershaft in vise with the front of the shaft facing up. 
Position puller jaws into notches behind the front countershaft bearing and 
remove bearing.

[FIGURE: C73881A.gif]

Remove drive gear retaining snap ring from front of shaft. 

Using the rear face of the drive gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft using Rotunda 25-Ton Capacity General Purpose Press 014-00085 or 
equivalent.

[FIGURE: C73891A.gif]

Remove the drive gear locating key and spacer from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C73901A.gif]

Using the rear face of the fourth gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft. Remove the fourth gear locating key from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C73911A.gif]

 NOTE: Be sure that the fourth speed gear key has been removed before removing 
third gear from countershaft. 

Using the rear face of the third speed gear as a base, press it from 
the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C73921A.gif]

Using the rear face of the second speed gear as a base, press it from 
the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C73931A.gif]

 Assembly 

Press second speed gear on countershaft, long hub of gear to front of 
shaft (i.e., pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: C73941A.gif]

Press third speed gear on countershaft, long hub of gear to rear of 
shaft (i.e., pointing up in the press).

[FIGURE: C73951A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure that keyway in gear is aligned with key in shaft before 
pressing gear on. Serious damage will result if key and keyway are not 
aligned. 

Install fourth and drive gear keys on countershaft. Align keyway of 
fourth speed gear to key on shaft. Press fourth speed gear on, long hub of 
gear to front of shaft (i.e., pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: DC0278A.gif]

Remove drive gear key from countershaft and install spacer. 

[FIGURE: C73971A.gif]

Reinstall key and align keyway of drive gear with key on countershaft. 
Press drive gear on shaft, long hub of gear to rear of shaft. 

Install snap ring in groove at front of countershaft.

Install front countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C73981A.gif]

Install rear countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C73991A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

[FIGURE: C12536A.gif]

The transmission has six forward speeds and one reverse speed with gear 
ratios as follows: 

First 9.01:1 

Second 5.27:1 

Third 3.22:1 

Fourth 2.04:1 

Fifth 1.36:1 

Sixth 1.00:1 

Reverse 8.63:1 

All gears are helical cut. Countershaft end play is controlled by shims 
located in the countershaft rear bearing cap. Mainshaft end play is controlled 
by shims located in the mainshaft rear bearing cover. The shift forks are 
single-piece forged and are equipped with bronze wear pads that can be replaced.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow

 NOTE: The numbered steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
Transmission Power Flow Cross Section View illustration.

The transmission transfers torque from the engine to the driveshaft 
through the following route: 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the input shaft and 
drive gear. 

The input shaft drive gear transfers torque to the countershaft drive 
gear. 

The countershaft drive gear turns the countershaft and all countershaft 
gears. 

Torque from the countershaft gear is transferred to the mainshaft gear 
that is currently engaged. 

The external clutching teeth of the engaged mainshaft gear transfer 
torque to the mainshaft through the synchronizer assembly. 

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the driveshaft through the 
rear yoke.

 Transmission Power Flow — Cross Section View 

[FIGURE: C9484B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many of these gear oils, 
particularly 85W140, break down above 110°C (230°F) and coat seals, 
bearings, and gears with deposits that can cause premature failures. If these 
deposits are observed (especially a coating on seal areas causing oil 
leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger® CD50 transmission fluid, 
heavy-duty engine oil, mineral gear oil, or Emgard 2924 Synthetic Transmission 
Lubricant SAE 50 or equivalent to ensure maximum component life and to
maintain your warranty. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Correct lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath by the motion of the gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if the following procedures are closely 
followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 
25.4 mm (one inch) is equivalent to approximately 3.7 liters (one gallon) of 
oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at case bottom. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from case side. Fill the 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If the transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to the level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil depends on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this causes oil to be forced out of the case 
through the front bearing cover. 

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission Installation Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example, if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12-degree 
(21-percent) grade.

Anytime the transmission operating angle of 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time, the transmission should be equipped with an oil 
pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is lubricated correctly.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one-half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Correct lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 With Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, Heavy Duty 
Engine Oil, Mineral Oil, or Emgard 2924 Synthetic Transmission Lubricant SAE 50 

The transmission should not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent operating temperatures to 
149°C (300°F) will not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 
120°C (250°F), the transmission may require more frequent oil changes 
or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCW's over 40 824 kg 
(90,000 lb).

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). In addition, 
transmission oil coolers are not recommended with these gear oils, since the 
oil cooler materials may be attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature 
limit and oil cooler restriction with these gear oils generally limit their 
success to milder applications.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission

 Removal 

Raise hood.

Disconnect battery(s).

Remove floor mat and floor plate.

Position shift lever in neutral. Remove four screws retaining shift 
lever housing to shift bar housing. Jar housing lightly to break the gasket 
seal. Remove shift lever housing and gasket. Cover opening in the shift bar 
housing.

Position a suitable drain pan under transmission. Remove drain plug and 
drain the transmission oil. Reinstall drain plug and tighten to 61-75 
Nm (45-55 lb-ft).

Remove driveshaft. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Disconnect speedometer sensor and backup lamp switch.

Position Rotunda Heavy-Duty Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or equivalent 
under the transmission.

Fabricate two guide pins from standard bolts as shown.

[FIGURE: C52661A.gif]

Remove two lower screws and washers retaining the transmission to the 
clutch housing. Install the two fabricated guide pins into the lower holes. 
Remove the two upper screws and washers retaining the transmission to the 
clutch housing.

Remove transmission from the clutch housing. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Lower transmission from vehicle.

 Installation 

If removed, reinstall the two fabricated guide pins into lower holes of 
clutch housing.

Using Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent, raise and align transmission to the clutch housing. Install 
transmission to the clutch housing. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Install two upper transmission-to-clutch housing retaining screws and 
washers and tighten to 197-210 Nm (145-155 lb-ft).

Remove fabricated guide pins. Install two lower transmission-to-clutch 
housing retaining screws and washers and tighten to 197-210 Nm (145-155 
lb-ft).

Connect speedometer sensor and backup lamp switch.

Install driveshaft. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Clean the shift lever housing gasket mating surfaces. Make sure the 
shift block and yoke notches are aligned in the neutral position. Install 
gasket and the shift lever housing. Apply Threadlock® and Sealer 
EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to the 
screw threads. Then, install and tighten the retaining screws to 27-34 
Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Install floor plate and floor mat.

Fill transmission with the appropriate type and quantity oil. Refer to 
Specifications.

Connect battery(s).

Close hood.

 Disassembly 

Remove capscrews and separate shift bar housing and gasket from case. 

[FIGURE: C71651A.gif]

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears.

[FIGURE: C71351B.gif]

Remove the yoke nut and yoke or flange.

[FIGURE: C71361B.gif]

Remove six capscrews and tap the input shaft bearing cover with a 
rubber mallet to separate the cover from the case. Remove the cover. 

[FIGURE: C7138B.gif]

If necessary, remove the oil seal from the input shaft bearing cover. 
Refer to Input Shaft Bearing Cover in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of 
this section. 

Remove the input shaft assembly from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71591A.gif]

Remove the four nuts and lockwashers that hold the mainshaft rear 
bearing cover to the transmission case. Insert screwdrivers into the notches 
on either side of the mainshaft rear bearing cover and gently separate the 
cover from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71391A.gif]

Remove shims (if they did not come off when mainshaft rear bearing 
cover was removed) and speedometer rotor.

[FIGURE: C71401A.gif]

Wrap a sling around the third/fourth synchronizer. Using Rotunda Hand 
Chain 164-R1713 or equivalent, remove mainshaft assembly from case. 

[FIGURE: C71581A.gif]

 NOTE: Countershaft may slide rearward and out of bearing bore. 

Remove the four capscrews and remove the countershaft rear bearing cap, 
shims and bearing cup from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C7141B.gif]

Using Impact Slide Hammer D79P-100-A or equivalent, remove reverse 
idler gear shaft. Remove locating ball once it is exposed.

[FIGURE: C7143C.gif]

Remove reverse idler gear, bearings, spacer and thrust washers.

[FIGURE: C71441A.gif]

Move countershaft assembly to the rear and lift it from the case. 

[FIGURE: C71451A.gif]

If countershaft front bearing cup is to be replaced, use a suitable 
driver and bearing cup remover to drive the bore plug through the front of the 
transmission case and drive the bearing cup toward the rear of the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71461A.gif]

 Assembly 

If removed, install snap ring, countershaft front bearing cup (from 
inside of case) and bore plug using a suitable driver. Coat outer diameter of 
bore with Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESE-M2G52-A and ESR-M11P17-A before installing.

[FIGURE: C71471A.gif]

Turn transmission case onto end with the rear of the transmission 
facing up. Stand countershaft assembly into front bearing cup.

[FIGURE: C71481A.gif]

Use Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B on reverse idler thrust washers to hold them in 
place. Position tang of washers in groove of housing.

[FIGURE: C7149B.gif]

Install bearings and spacer in reverse idler gear.

[FIGURE: C71501A.gif]

Position reverse idler gear in transmission case with long hub of gear 
toward the front of the case (i.e., pointing down).

[FIGURE: C7151B.gif]

Insert reverse idler gear shaft through transmission case, bearings, 
spacer and thrust washers. Line up notch in shaft with notch in case. Install 
locating ball and drive the shaft into position.

[FIGURE: C7152B.gif]

Coat outer diameter of countershaft rear bearing cup with Gasket and 
Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A. Install countershaft rear bearing cup into case.

[FIGURE: C71531A.gif]

Temporarily install new shims over countershaft rear bearing cup.

Install the countershaft rear bearing cap and capscrews. Tighten the 
capscrews to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

Rotate countershaft to seat the bearings. Position Dial 
Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent, on the shoulder of one of 
the countershaft gears. Lift countershaft to measure end play. End play must 
be between 0.15-0.25 mm (0.006-0.010 inch). Add shims for less end play or 
remove shims for more end play. Once end play is correct, remove rear bearing 
cap and apply a light coat of Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A to both 
sides of shims and to the rear bearing cap and reinstall them. 

[FIGURE: C7155D.gif]

Coat threads of capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® 
D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and 
ESR-M18P7-A and tighten to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12970A.gif]

Place transmission in a horizontal position. Shift third/fourth 
mainshaft synchronizer into fourth gear.

[FIGURE: C71571A.gif]

Place a sling around the third/fourth synchronizer assembly. Using 
Rotunda Hand Chain Hoist 164-R1713 or equivalent, carefully lower the assembly 
into the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71581A.gif]

Align clutching teeth on main drive gear with teeth in fifth speed 
synchronizer cup. Install input shaft into aligned teeth.

[FIGURE: C71591A.gif]

If removed, install input shaft oil seal and bearing cup into input 
shaft bearing cover. Refer to Input Shaft Bearing Cover in the Disassembly and 
Assembly portion of this section for procedure. 

 NOTE: Top of input shaft bearing cover is marked for proper installation. 

Install input shaft bearing cover and gasket. Apply Pipe Sealant with 
Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A to the threads of the capscrews and tighten to 
20-34 Nm (15-25 lb-ft).

 Shift Bar Housing, Eaton FS-5306A and FS-6306A Transmissions

 Disassembly 

Lay shift bar housing on workbench. Slide fifth/sixth yoke into fifth 
position and remove all capscrews and shift bar retainers.

[FIGURE: C7178B.gif]

Remove reverse yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C71791A.gif]

Remove first/second yoke assembly and interlock pin.

[FIGURE: C71801A.gif]

Remove third/fourth yoke assembly and interlock pin.

[FIGURE: C71811A.gif]

Remove fifth/sixth yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C71821A.gif]

If yoke replacement is required, yokes can be removed by driving the 
roll pin through the yoke and bar. If the yoke pad inserts are to be replaced, 
remove worn pad from shift yoke, install new pad, and bend tabs over top and 
bottom of fork. 

Remove interlock balls, detent balls and springs.

[FIGURE: C71831A.gif]

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER ARE UNDER SPRING PRESSURE. 

If the removal of the reverse plunger is necessary, secure the shift 
bar in a hand press. Depress the retainer washer and spring and remove the 
snap ring.

Remove the retainer washer. 

Remove the inner and outer springs.

Remove the washer and the reverse plunger.

 Assembly 

If reverse plunger was removed, install reverse plunger in reverse 
shift block. 

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER WILL BE UNDER PRESSURE WHEN INSTALLED. 

Install washer, outer and inner springs.

Place the shift block in a hand press. Depress retainer washer and 
spring and install the snap ring.

 NOTE: Balls and springs can be used interchangeably. 

Install balls and springs in the following sequence: 

Position three balls into reverse lamp switch bore and install reverse 
detent spring and ball. 

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install first/second 
detent spring and ball. 

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install third/fourth 
detent spring and ball. 

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install fifth/sixth 
detent spring and ball.

[FIGURE: C74101A.gif]

 NOTE: All yoke assemblies must be installed in the neutral position. 

Position reverse yoke assembly in housing.

[FIGURE: C71871A.gif]

Install interlock pin in first/second yoke assembly and install 
assembly in housing.

[FIGURE: C71881A.gif]

Install interlock pin in third/fourth yoke assembly and install 
assembly in housing.

[FIGURE: C71891A.gif]

Position fifth/sixth yoke assembly in housing.

[FIGURE: C71901A.gif]

 NOTE: If a new shift bar housing is being used in the assembly, the bores for 
the shift bar retainer capscrews are not tapped. The capscrews that are used 
are thread-forming and can be reused on a new housing.

 NOTE: Support yoke in the proper position while installing retainers.

Install front retainer over shift bars. Coat threads of retainer 
capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A. Install the 
capscrews, and tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7191B.gif]

Position shift yokes as shown and install center retainer. Coat threads 
of retainer capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A. Install 
and tighten capscrews to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: C7192B.gif]

Position rear retainer over shift bars. Coat threads of retainer 
capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A. Install and tighten 
capscrews to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Make sure interlocking system is working — can't shift into two

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Countershaft 

 Disassembly 

Position a suitable puller behind rear countershaft bearing and remove 
bearing.

[FIGURE: C72301A.gif]

Position countershaft in vise with the front of the shaft facing up. 
Position puller jaws into notches behind the front countershaft bearing and 
remove bearing.

[FIGURE: C72311A.gif]

Remove drive gear retaining snap ring from front of shaft. 

Using the rear face of the drive gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft with Rotunda 25-Ton Capacity General Purpose Press 014-00085 or 
equivalent. Remove the drive gear locating key from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C7232B.gif]

Using the rear face of the fifth gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft. Remove the fifth gear locating key from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C72331A.gif]

 NOTE: Be sure that fifth and sixth gear keys have been removed before 
removing fourth gear from countershaft. 

Using the rear face of the fourth speed gear as a base, press it from 
the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C7234B.gif]

Using the rear face of the third gear as a base, press third gear from 
the countershaft.

[FIGURE: C72351A.gif]

 Assembly 

Press third gear on countershaft, splined end of gear hub to front of 
shaft (i.e., pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: C72361A.gif]

Press fourth gear on countershaft, long hub of gear to rear of shaft 
(i.e., pointing up in the press).

[FIGURE: C72371A.gif]

Install fifth and sixth gear keys on countershaft. Align keyway of 
fifth gear to key on shaft. Press fifth gear on, long hub of gear to front of 
shaft (i.e., pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: C7239B.gif]

Align keyway of drive gear to key on countershaft. Press drive gear on, 
long hub of gear to rear of shaft. 

[FIGURE: C7238B.gif]

Install snap ring in groove at front of countershaft.

Install front countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C72401A.gif]

Install rear countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C72411A.gif]

DESCRIPTION

Identification

[FIGURE: C10055B.gif]

The Fuller RT-6609A series transmission features a twin countershaft. 

The twin-countershaft design, which splits torque evenly between the 
two countershafts, provides a high torque capacity-to-weight ratio. Because of 
torque splitting, each gear set carries only half of the load, greatly 
reducing the face width of each gear. 

The design employs a floating gear. The mainshaft gears, when not 
engaged, float between the countershaft gears, eliminating the need for gear 
sleeves and bushings. All gears are constant mesh with spur-type teeth. 

The RT-6609A transmission has five low range speeds, four high range 
speeds and two reverse speeds with gear ratios as follows:

LO Range

LO 12.72:1

First 8.61:1

Second 6.27:1

Third 4.66:1

Fourth 3.42:1

HI Range

Fifth 2.52:1

Sixth 1.83:1

Seventh 1.36:1

Eighth 1.00:1

Reverse

LO 12.08:1

HI 3.53:1

DESCRIPTION

Power Flow, Front Section: LO Range Direct

The transmission transfers torque from the engine to the driveshaft to 
the vehicle's rear wheels through the following route.

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration. 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft. 

Input shaft splines engage internal splines of main drive gear. 

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears. 

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross-section views illustrate a first/sixth speed gear 
engagement. 

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch. 

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

DESCRIPTION

Power Flow, Auxiliary Section

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross section views illustrate a first/sixth speed gear 
engagement.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both auxiliary countershafts to engaged gear 
on the output shaft.

Torque is transferred to the output shaft through the sliding clutch.

Output shaft delivers torque to driveline.

 LO Range 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross section views illustrate a first/sixth speed gear 
engagement.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged LO range gear 
on the range mainshaft or output shaft.

Torque is transferred to the range mainshaft or output shaft through 
the sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered to the driveline as LO range first.

 Power Flow, LO Range, LO Range Direct and Auxiliary Section

 HI Range 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's

Input shaft splines engage internal splines of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multipurpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multipurpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many of these gear oils, 
particularly 85W140, break down above 110°C (230°F) and coat seals, 
bearings, and gears with deposits that can cause premature failures. If these 
deposits are observed (especially a coating on seal areas causing oil 
leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger® CD50 transmission fluid, 
heavy-duty engine oil, mineral gear oil or Emgard 2924 Synthetic Transmission
Lubricant SAE 50 or equivalent to ensure maximum component life and to
maintain your warranty with Eaton. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this
section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Correct lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath by the motion of the gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if these procedures are closely followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 
25.4 mm (one inch) is equal to approximately 3.7 liters (one gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at case bottom. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from case side. Fill the 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If the transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to the level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil depends on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this causes oil to be forced out of the case 
through the front bearing cover.

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission Installation Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example: if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12-degree 
(21-percent) grade.

Any time the transmission operating angle of 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time the transmission should be equipped with an oil 
pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is lubricated correctly.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one-half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Correct lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 With Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, Heavy-Duty 
Engine Oil, Mineral Oil or Emgard 2924 Synthetic Transmission Lubricant SAE 50 

The transmission should not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent operating temperatures to 
149°C (300°F) will not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 
120°C (250°F), the transmission may require more frequent oil changes 
or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCW's over 40 824 kg 
(90,000 lb)

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). In addition, 
transmission oil coolers are not recommended with these gear oils, since the 
oil cooler materials may be attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature 
limit and oil cooler restriction with these gear oils generally limit their 
success to milder applications.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission

 Removal 

Drain air system and disconnect air lines at Roadranger® valve 
and position out of way. Refer to Section 07-06 .

Drain transmission oil.

If required, remove safety belt and seat assembly. Refer to appropriate 
Group 01 section.

Clean the area around the shift lever housing. Remove the capscrews, 
then jar the housing lightly to break the gasket seal. Remove the shift lever 
housing and gasket. Cover the opening in the shift bar housing.

Disconnect wiring connectors.

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Disconnect and remove fuel lines and bracketry as required. Refer to 
 Section 10-01B .

Remove exhaust system as required.

Remove driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Disconnect air lines at transmission. Refer to Section 07-06 .

If so equipped, disconnect low oil level indicator sensor.

Disconnect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Remove clutch housing cover.

Position heavy-duty truck transmission jack or equivalent under the 
transmission and install jack.

Remove transmission clutch housing-to-engine retaining bolts and raise 
transmission slightly with jack.

Remove top engine support to bracket retaining nut and insulators.

Remove both jam nuts and insulators.

Lower transmission from vehicle.

 Installation 

Use transmission jack to lift transmission into place.

Install insulator retainer assembly.

 NOTE: For installing and aligning clutch discs, plates, flywheel and shafts, 
refer to Section 08-01 .

Install and align clutch assembly and install clutch housing-to-engine 
retaining bolts.

Position rear engine support bracket on transmission. Install 
insulators and tighten jam nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). Tighten 
remaining jam nut finger tight and apply two additional turns.

Install insulators and top rear engine support bracket retaining nut. 
Tighten nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Remove transmission jack.

Install clutch housing cover.

Connect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Install fuel lines and bracketry. Refer to Section 10-01B .

If so equipped, connect low oil level indicator sensor.

Connect air lines to transmission. Refer to Section 07-06 .

Install exhaust system, if removed.

Install driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Lower vehicle.

Reconnect all wiring connectors.

Install the gasket and shift lever housing on the shift bar housing, 
fitting the lever into shift block yoke notches. Lightly oil capscrew threads. 
Then, install and tighten the capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb ft).

Connect air lines to Roadranger® valve. Refer to Section 07-06 .

Install safety belt and seat assembly, if removed. Refer to appropriate 
Group 01 section.

Refill transmission with appropriate type and quantity oil. Refer to 
Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Shift Bar Housing 

 Removal 

Remove the Shift Bar Housing retaining capscrews. Jar the housing to 
break the gasket seal. Lift the shift bar housing from the transmission case. 
Remove the gasket.

[FIGURE: C100641A.gif]

 Installation 

Place all three mainshaft sliding clutches in the neutral position. 
Position the shift bar housing gasket on transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100651A.gif]

Install the shift bar housing assembly on the transmission case, 
fitting the shift yokes into the corresponding sliding clutch slots. Lightly 
oil threads of capscrews. Then install and tighten the capscrews to 47-61 
Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

1999 F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Output Yoke, Auxiliary Section and Clutch Housing 

 Removal 

Lock the transmission by engaging the two mainshaft gears with the 
mainshaft sliding clutches.

[FIGURE: C100571A.gif]

Use a large breaker bar to turn the nut from the output shaft. Pull the 
yoke straight to the rear and off the output shaft.

Remove the six nuts with lockwashers that hold the clutch housing to 
the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100581A.gif]

Remove the two capscrews that hold the clutch housing to the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100591A.gif]

Jar the clutch housing with a rubber mallet to break the gasket seal. 
Pull the clutch housing from the transmission case and remove the gasket.

 NOTE: There are three capscrew lengths. Note their locations. 

Remove the 15 capscrews that hold the auxiliary section to the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100601A.gif]

Insert three capscrews in the housing flange tapped holes. Tighten 
evenly to move the auxiliary section back; leave a space wide enough to attach 
a chain hoist.

[FIGURE: C100611A.gif]

Remove the puller capscrews and attach a chain hoist to the auxiliary 
section. Pull the auxiliary section off and remove the gasket.

[FIGURE: C100621A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Make sure the synchronizer is in neutral, and the auxiliary front 
countershaft bearings are installed in the front case. 

Position a new gasket on the auxiliary housing. Attach a chain hoist to 
the auxiliary section. Move the assembly evenly into the front case rear, 
piloting it on the dowel pins. As the assembly is moved forward, the 
countershaft drive gears will mesh with the auxiliary drive gear. 

 NOTE: There are three capscrew lengths. Make sure the capscrews are in their 
proper locations. 

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install the 15 capscrews in the 
auxiliary housing flange and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

Position the corresponding new gasket on the clutch housing mounting 
surface. Install the clutch housing on the case front, piloting on the six 
studs and the front bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C100631A.gif]

Install the six nuts with lockwashers. Tighten to 244-271 Nm 
(180-200 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12973A.gif]

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install and tighten the 
capscrews to 108-136 Nm (80-100 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12974A.gif]

Install the yoke on the output shaft splines and move it into the rear 
bearing cover. 

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears with their 
sliding clutches. 

Lightly oil output shaft threads. Then, install the nut on the output 
shaft. Tighten the nut to 542-610 Nm (400-450 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Input Shaft 

 Special Procedure for Changing Input Shaft 

Some cases of service can require replacement of the input shaft 
because of clutch wear on the splines. In these instances the input shaft can 
be removed without disassembling the transmission other than removing the 
shift bar housing. Removal of the clutch housing is optional.

[FIGURE: C10066C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

7025

Bearing

2

7A059

Spacer

3

7017

Input Shaft

4

7005

Case

5

7064

Snap Ring

6

Drive (Fourth) Gear

7

—

Bushing (Part of 7017)

Front Bearing Cover (Pull-Type)

Gasket

 Removal 

Remove the shift bar housing from the transmission case. Refer to Shift 
Bar Housing in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Remove the retaining capscrews, front bearing cover and gasket. Service 
the oil seal of model covers so equipped. 

Remove the bearing retaining snap ring from the shaft groove. 

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing. 

Use pry bars or screwdrivers to complete removal of the bearing. 

Remove the spacer and the snap ring. 

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive (fourth) gear and 
case. 

 Installation 

If necessary, replace the bushing in the input shaft pocket. Install 
input shaft into drive (fourth) gear.

Install the snap ring in the snap ring groove inside the drive (fourth) 
gear. 

Install the spacer on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing retainer snap ring. 

Install the front bearing cover and gasket. Make sure to align the oil 
return hole in the case with the hole in the cover. Lightly oil capscrew 
threads. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

Install the shift bar housing. Refer to Shift Bar Housing in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.
