DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Auxiliary Section 

 Bearing Cover, Rear, Removal 

Remove the capscrews and the rear bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C100671A.gif]

If necessary, remove the oil seal from the rear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C100681A.gif]

Remove the speedometer rotor or replacement spacer from the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C100691A.gif]

Remove the washer from the output shaft.

 Auxiliary Countershafts, Removal 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershafts forward through the 
countershaft bearings and remove them from the auxiliary housing.

[FIGURE: C100701A.gif]

Remove the countershaft bearings from the auxiliary case bearing bores.

[FIGURE: C100711A.gif]

 NOTE: The vise should be equipped with soft jaws or wood blocks to prevent 
damage to the countershaft. 

If necessary, secure assembly in a vise and remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing race from the countershaft with a jaw puller and 
clamp.

If necessary, secure assembly in a vise and remove the auxiliary 
countershaft rear bearing race. 

 Range Cylinder Assembly, Synchronizer Assembly, LO Range Gear and 
Output Shaft, Disassembly 

Secure the auxiliary housing in a vise. Remove the capscrews and the 
range cylinder cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C100721A.gif]

Remove the yoke bar nut and washer.

[FIGURE: C100731A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not damage the piston. 

Push range yoke bar to the transmission rear. Use a screwdriver to 
remove the piston.

Remove the copper gasket from the yoke bar.

[FIGURE: C100741A.gif]

 NOTE: The following step will damage the bearing and should not be attempted 
unless bearing replacement is planned. 

Use pullers and a clamp to remove the bearing from the output shaft 
front.

Move the synchronizer assembly, shift yoke and yoke bar forward and out 
of the housing assembly.

[FIGURE: C100751A.gif]

Remove the yoke bar and shift yoke from the synchronizer assembly. Cut 
the lockwire and remove the two lock screws. Remove the shift yoke from the 
yoke bar.

[FIGURE: C100771A.gif]

[FIGURE: C100761A.gif]

Remove the dust seal and air port extension from the range cylinder 
housing top.

[FIGURE: C100781A.gif]

Remove the cylinder housing. If necessary, remove the O-ring from the 
small bore in the cylinder.

[FIGURE: C100791A.gif]

 LO Range Gear and Output Shaft, Removal 

 NOTE: When applying force to the output shaft rear, do not damage threads. 

Using a soft bar and maul, drive or press against the output shaft rear 
to move assembly forward and out of the rear bearing.

Remove the rear washer and LO range gear from the shaft rear.

[FIGURE: C100801A.gif]

Remove the spline washer from the LO range gear hub.

[FIGURE: C100811A.gif]

Move the output shaft rear bearing to the rear and out of the housing.

 Synchronizer 

 Disassembly 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring on the bench. Cover the 
assembly with a shop towel to prevent losing the three springs released from 
the HI range synchronizer at the pin locations. Pull the HI range synchronizer 
from the blocker pins.

[FIGURE: C100821A.gif]

Remove the synchronizer springs from the HI range synchronizer ring bore.

[FIGURE: C100831A.gif]

Remove the sliding clutch from the synchronizer LO range pins.

[FIGURE: C100841A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Pins on the LO range synchronizer must be lined up with the chamfered 
holes on the sliding clutch bottom. 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring race down on the bench with 
the pins up. Place the sliding clutch, recessed side up on the pins of the LO 
range synchronizer.

[FIGURE: C100851A.gif]

Install the three springs in the HI range synchronizer ring bore. 

Place the HI range synchronizer ring, seating springs against the pins. 

Apply downward pressure to the HI range synchronizer ring while 
twisting counterclockwise to compress the springs and fully seat the ring on 
the LO range synchronizer blocker pins.

[FIGURE: C100861A.gif]

 LO Range Gear and Output Shaft, Assembly 

 NOTE: Make sure the magnetic discs are installed in the auxiliary housing. 

 NOTE: Mark timing teeth on the LO range gear. A highly visible color of 
toolmaker's dye is recommended. 

Mark any two adjacent gear teeth. Then mark two adjacent teeth which 
are directly opposite the first set marked. There should be the same number of 
teeth between the markings on each gear side.

[FIGURE: C100871A.gif]

Place splined washer on the output shaft, with shoulder facing up as 
shown.

[FIGURE: C100881A.gif]

Install the LO range gear over the output shaft rear and against 
shoulder or splined washer.

[FIGURE: C100891A.gif]

Install the LO range gear rear washer on the output shaft and against 
the gear, with the chamfer side facing up.

[FIGURE: C100901A.gif]

Stand the output shaft on end with the shaft rear facing up. Place the 
auxiliary housing over the shaft so the output shaft extends through the rear 
bore.

[FIGURE: C100911A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not heat the bearing above 135°C (275°F). 

Using a heat lamp or hot plate and oil, heat the output shaft rear 
bearing and install on the output shaft. Seat the bearing securely on the 
shaft and in the bore.

[FIGURE: C100921A.gif]

Install the bearing in the housing bore with the appropriate driver.

[FIGURE: C100931A.gif]

 Range Cylinder, Assembly 

If removed, install the O-ring in the cylinder small bore slot. 
Lubricate the O-ring with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. 

Install the range cylinder in the housing with the cylinder air port 
aligned with the air port in the auxiliary housing.

[FIGURE: C100941A.gif]

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to air port extension threads. 
Install the dust seal and air port extension through housing and into the air 
cylinder bore.

[FIGURE: C100781A.gif]

 Range Cylinder Assemblies and Synchronizer, Installation 

Place the shift yoke on the yoke bar, with the long hub toward the bar 
front. Align slots in the yoke bar and install the two lock screws. Tighten 
lock screws to 68-88 Nm (50-65 lb-ft) and secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12975A.gif]

Place the yoke in the sliding clutch slot, threaded end of the yoke bar 
toward the larger LO range synchronizer. Place the entire assembly in the 
auxiliary housing, engaging the sliding clutch splines with the output shaft 
and inserting the yoke bar through the cylinder bore.

[FIGURE: C100751A.gif]

Install the copper gasket on the yoke bar threaded end.

[FIGURE: C100741A.gif]

Install the O-ring on the piston outer diameters. Apply a light coat of 
Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M13P4-A to the O-ring.

[FIGURE: C100951A.gif]

Install the piston on the yoke bar and against the copper gasket, 
piston flat side out.

[FIGURE: C100961A.gif]

Install the lockwasher and nut on the yoke bar and tighten to 81-95 
Nm (60-70 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12976A.gif]

Install the gasket and cylinder cover with the HI range port to the 
right. Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install and tighten the four 
capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12977A.gif]

 Auxiliary Countershafts 

 Assembly 

Install the bearing inner race on the countershaft front.

[FIGURE: C100971A.gif]

Install the bearing inner race on the countershaft rear.

[FIGURE: C100981A.gif]

 NOTE: Countershaft gear teeth must be marked for timing the auxiliary 
section. Mark with a highly visible color of toolmakers' dye. 

Mark the tooth on the countershaft gear which is stamped with an O.

[FIGURE: C100991A.gif]

 Installation 

Seat the outer races of the countershaft rear bearing only partially in 
the housing bores, just far enough to stay in place.

[FIGURE: C101001A.gif]

 NOTE: Time the countershaft gear with the LO range gear. As the countershaft 
is installed, mesh the marked LO range gear tooth on each countershaft between 
each set of marked gear teeth on the LO range gear. 

Place the countershaft into position in the auxiliary housing, 
inserting the inner race into the partially installed rear bearing. 

[FIGURE: C101011A.gif]

With the countershaft in position, complete the installation of the 
countershaft rear bearings on the shaft and into the case bore. Seat securely. 

Install the washer, flat side to the rear, on the output shaft and 
against the bearing. 

Install the speedometer rotor or replacement spacer on the output shaft. 

 NOTE: Use the proper seal driver to install the seal. 

If previously removed, install the oil seal in the rear bearing cover, 
with seal lip to the rear.

Install the rear bearing cover with the speedometer bore up and to the 
left. Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then, install and 
tighten the capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12978A.gif]

Install the bearing on the output shaft front, with chamfered side to 
race rear.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Front Section 

 Input Shaft, Removal 

Remove the four capscrews retaining the front bearing cover. Remove the 
bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C101021A.gif]

Remove the bearing retaining snap ring from the shaft groove.

[FIGURE: C101031A.gif]

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear, through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing. 

Use pry bars to complete the bearing removal.

[FIGURE: C101041A.gif]

Remove the spacer from the input shaft. 

Remove the snap ring from the groove inside the drive (fourth) gear.

[FIGURE: C101051A.gif]

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive (fourth) gear and 
case. 

Check the bushing in the input shaft pocket, replace if worn.

[FIGURE: C101061A.gif]

 Auxiliary Drive Gear 

 Removal 

Straighten the lock tangs. Remove the four capscrews and two bearing 
retainers from the case.

[FIGURE: C101071A.gif]

Remove the snap ring from the mainshaft rear, located inside the 
auxiliary drive gear bore.

[FIGURE: C101081A.gif]

With two screwdrivers, pry the auxiliary drive gear off the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C101091A.gif]

 Disassembly 

Remove the snap ring from the auxiliary drive gear. 

Press or use a driver to remove the bearing from the auxiliary drive 
gear. 

 Assembly 

Press the bearing on the auxiliary drive gear. 

Install the bearing retaining snap ring in the auxiliary drive gear 
shoulder groove. 

 Upper Countershaft Bearings, Removal 

Remove the upper countershaft snap ring from the case rear bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C101101A.gif]

Use a soft bar and maul against the countershaft rear and move the 
countershaft assembly forward as far as possible until the snap ring groove in 
the front bearing is exposed. 

Install the snap ring removed from the rear bearing bore in the exposed 
snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: C101111A.gif]

 NOTE: Steps four and five may have to be repeated several times to unseat the 
front bearing. 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft assembly to the rear 
as far as possible. This will move the front bearing forward on the 
countershaft. 

From the case rear, use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft 
forward to unseat the front bearing from the case bore.

Use puller or pry bars to remove the front countershaft bearing. 

 NOTE: Removal procedure damages the bearings. Removal should not be attempted 
unless bearing replacement is planned. 

Block the countershaft and use a maul and punch from inside the case to 
drive the rear countershaft bearing from the case bore and countershaft.

[FIGURE: C101121A.gif]

 Upper Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, Removal 

Use inside jaw pullers or an impact puller to remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing from the left reverse idler gear bore. 

Remove the plug from the reverse idler gear shaft rear.

[FIGURE: C101131A.gif]

Use a socket wrench to remove the stop nut from the reverse idler gear 
shaft front. Remove the washer.

[FIGURE: C101141A.gif]

Use an impact puller with a 1/2-inch 13-threaded end to remove the 
reverse idler gear shaft from the case bore.

[FIGURE: C101151A.gif]

As the reverse idler gear shaft is moved to the rear, remove the thrust 
washer and reverse idle gear from the case. 

If necessary, remove the bearing from the reverse idler gear bore.

[FIGURE: C101161A.gif]

 Mainshaft Assembly 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: After performing this step, note that the drive gear will be free and 
can fall from the shaft. 

Block the right countershaft assembly against the case wall. Slide the 
drive gear to the rear and engage with the sliding clutch splines. Use a hook 
around first/second sliding clutch. Tilt the mainshaft front up and lift the 
assembly from the case.

[FIGURE: C101171A.gif]

 Disassembly 

Secure the mainshaft, with drive (fourth) gear up, in a vise. Remove 
the drive (fourth) gear and the third/fourth speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101181A.gif]

Remove third gear hub snap ring from the mainshaft groove.

[FIGURE: C101191A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and third gear.

[FIGURE: C101201A.gif]

Remove second gear and tolerance washer.

[FIGURE: C101211A.gif]

Remove first/second speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101221A.gif]

Remove mainshaft key from mainshaft keyway.

[FIGURE: C101231A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and first gear.

[FIGURE: C101241A.gif]

Remove LO speed gear and tolerance washer.

[FIGURE: C101251A.gif]

Remove LO/reverse speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101261A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and reverse gear.

[FIGURE: C101271A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: If previously removed, install the corresponding snap rings in the 
inside diameter of the mainshaft gears. 

Secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped with brass jaws or wood blocks, 
shaft pilot-end down. If previously removed, install the roll pin in the 
keyway. 

Install the reverse gear tolerance washer in the groove near the 
mainshaft rear.

[FIGURE: C101281A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure the mainshaft key is positioned with the word TOP to the 
outside. 

Rotate the tolerance washer in the mainshaft groove to align the washer 
splines with the mainshaft splines. Install the mainshaft key in keyway to 
lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: C101291A.gif]

Install the reverse gear on the tolerance washer with clutching teeth 
facing down.

[FIGURE: C101301A.gif]

Install the auxiliary drive gear on the mainshaft with clutching teeth 
facing up.

[FIGURE: C101311A.gif]

Install the snap ring in the mainshaft rear groove.

[FIGURE: C101321A.gif]

Insert two screwdrivers between the reverse gear hub and the auxiliary 
drive gear. Apply slight downward pressure on the screwdriver handles to 
spread the gears evenly apart. Make sure the gear hubs are parallel. Insert a 
feeler gauge between the hubs. The gap must be between 0.127-0.305 mm 
(0.005-0.012 inch). If the clearance is less than the minimum 0.127-mm 
(0.005-inch) tolerance, the tolerance washer in the reverse gear should be 
replaced by a thinner tolerance washer. This increases the axial clearance 
between gears. If the clearance checked is greater than the maximum 0.305-mm 
(0.012-inch) tolerance, a thicker tolerance washer should be installed in the 
reverse gear. This would decrease the axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: C101331A.gif]

Washers are available in the following thicknesses to obtain the 
correct limits. Select the appropriate washer as required.

[FIGURE: C101421A.gif]

sliding clutch slot with key and engage clutch with third gear.

toolmakers' dye.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft Assembly, Input Shaft, Drive Gear Assembly and Upper 
Countershaft Assembly, Installation 

Place the upper countershaft assembly into position in the case. 
Support the countershaft assembly against the case wall as far as possible. 

Place the mainshaft assembly into position in the case. 

Mesh the lower countershaft marked tooth with either of the two marked 
teeth on the main drive (fourth) gear.

[FIGURE: C101591A.gif]

If previously removed, install the input shaft bushing. 

Install input shaft through case bore and into the drive (fourth) gear 
splines. Installation of the input shaft prevents the mainshaft from dropping 
to the case bottom.

[FIGURE: C101601A.gif]

Center the mainshaft in the case rear bore and install the auxiliary 
drive gear. 

Seat the auxiliary drive gear bearing in the case rear bore.

[FIGURE: C101611A.gif]

Install the bearing lower retainer plates. Lightly oil threads of 
capscrews. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

Bend the lock tangs. 

Install the top retainer plates and bend the lock tangs.

[FIGURE: C101621A.gif]

Move the mainshaft assembly to the rear to expose the mainshaft snap 
ring groove. Install the snap ring.

[FIGURE: C101631A.gif]

Install snap ring into drive (fourth) gear groove.

[FIGURE: C101641A.gif]

Install the spacer on the input shaft, chamfered side to the front.

[FIGURE: C101651A.gif]

Install the drive gear bearing.

[FIGURE: C101661A.gif]

Install the bearing retainer snap ring.

[FIGURE: C101671A.gif]

Install the front bearing cover and gasket, making sure oil return hole 
aligns with cover hole. 

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install the bearing cover 
capscrews and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12979A.gif]

Engage the third/fourth speed sliding clutch into third mainshaft gear. 
This prevents drive (fourth) gear from dropping to cause a timing error.

[FIGURE: C101691A.gif]

Mesh the upper countershaft marked timing tooth with the main drive 
(fourth) gear two marked timing teeth, making sure the lower countershaft 
remains in time.

[FIGURE: C101701A.gif]

 NOTE: Use a large screwdriver or bar to block the countershaft from moving.

Hold the countershaft in position and partially install the rear 
countershaft bearing.

[FIGURE: C101711A.gif]

Install the case rear bore snap ring into the groove.

[FIGURE: C101721A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not shift the transmission into two gears at the same time. This 
prevents the transmission from rotating. 

Shift the mainshaft sliding clutches into all the gear positions with a 
screwdriver. The front box is properly timed if the sliding clutches can be 
shifted into all the mainshaft gears.

[FIGURE: C101731A.gif]

Use a flanged driver to complete installation of the front countershaft 
bearing.

[FIGURE: C101741A.gif]

Subassemblies 

 Shift Lever Housing 

 Disassembly 

 WARNING: SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. USE CARE TO PROTECT EYES WHEN REMOVING SPRING. 

Remove the boot from the shift lever and secure assembly in a vise with 
the housing bottom up. Use a large screwdriver to twist between the spring and 
housing, forcing the spring from under the lugs in the housing. Do one coil at 
a time.

[FIGURE: C101751A.gif]

Remove the tension spring, washer and shift lever from the housing.

[FIGURE: C101761A.gif]

Remove the spade pin from the housing bore tower. If necessary, remove 
the O-ring from the tower groove.

[FIGURE: C101771A.gif]

 Assembly

housing tower bore. If previously removed, install the O-ring in the tower 
groove. 

Position the shift lever in the housing with the spade pin in the lever 
ball slot. Install the tension spring washer over the ball, dished-side up.

[FIGURE: C101781A.gif]

Install the tension spring under the housing lugs, seating one coil at 
a time. Use a spring driving tool.

[FIGURE: C101791A.gif]

Remove the assembly from the vise. Install the rubber boot over the 
gear shift lever and against the housing.

[FIGURE: C101801A.gif]

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in the order of 
removal to facilitate reassembly. Shift bars not being removed must be kept in 
the neutral position or interlock parts will lock bars.

housing top. Remove the three tension springs installed under the cover.

[FIGURE: C101811A.gif]

bores.

[FIGURE: C101821A.gif]

Secure the assembly in a vise with the air valve actuating shaft up. 
The housing front will be to the right.

[FIGURE: C101831A.gif]

 NOTE: When removing the shift bars, start with the upper shift bar. Move all 
the bars to the right and out the rear boss bore. Cut the lockwire and remove 
the lock screws from each bar just before their removal. 

Move the LO/reverse shift bar to the right and out of housing, removing 
the shift yoke from bar.

[FIGURE: C101841A.gif]

Move the first/second shift bar to the right and out of housing, 
removing shift yoke from bar. As the neutral notch in bar clears the front 
web, remove the interlock pin from the neutral notch bore.

[FIGURE: C101851A.gif]

[FIGURE: C101861A.gif]

Remove the air valve actuating shaft from rear web.

[FIGURE: C101871A.gif]

Move the third/fourth shift bar to the right and out of housing,

balls from front web.

[FIGURE: C101881A.gif]

If necessary, remove the plug, spring and reverse plunger stop from

[FIGURE: C101891A.gif]

 Assembly

yoke.

[FIGURE: C12980A.gif]

Install interlock ball in front web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101921A.gif]

Install air valve actuating shaft in rear web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101931A.gif]

Install the first/second speed shift bar in center bore, and install 
shift yoke on bar; insert interlock pin in detent notch. Install lock screw. 
Tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C101941A.gif]

Install interlock ball in front web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101951A.gif]

Install LO/reverse shift bar in upper bore, detent notches to the 
front. Install yoke on bar, fork to the rear. Install lock screw and tighten 
to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C101961A.gif]

Remove assembly from vise and install the three detent balls, one in 
each bore in housing top. Keep yokes in neutral.

[FIGURE: C101971A.gif]

Install the three tension springs, one in each bore, in housing top.

[FIGURE: C101981A.gif]

Then, install and tighten the two capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

Section 07-05: Transmission, Automatic, External Controls

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shift Selectors

Vehicle manufacturers may choose different types of shift selectors for 
their equipment. The shift selector in an Allison-equipped vehicle will be 
similar to one of those shown below.

[FIGURE: D13161A.gif]

 Push-Button Shifter 

The push-button shift selector has reverse, neutral, drive, up and down 
arrows, a mode button, and a digital display. When a range button has been 
pressed, a tone will sound, the SELECT indicator will display the chosen 
operation (if the ECU determines the shift is acceptable), and the 
transmission will shift to the starting range as indicated on the monitor 
display. In DRIVE, selection of a specific gear can be accomplished by 
pressing the up or down arrow buttons. Conditions resulting in the DO NOT 
SHIFT light located on the instrument panel will disable the pad and no tones 
will be heard.

 Shift Lever 

The shift lever is an electromechanical control. The pattern of 
positions can vary according to the shift lever installed. Positions R, N, and 
D are selected by pressing a hold override button and choosing the desired 
gear. It is possible to move between forward drive positions without pressing 
the hold override button. A mode button (a dash-mounted switch can be used) is 
located on lever and push-button shift levers to activate a second shift 
schedule or specialized function when desirable. The mode being used is 
identified above the mode button. The display will indicate MODE ON for most 
programmed functions.

 Mode Button 

This feature is located on the shift lever and push-button shifters and 
can be used to activate a second shift schedule (this is typically programed 
for economy, which will enable the transmission to shift at a lower engine rpm 
to conserve fuel).

 Display Mode 

A display mode button is included on the shift lever to allow access to 
diagnostic code information. The capability is included on the push-button 
selector by pressing the up and down arrow buttons at the same time.

This button is included on the shift lever to allow access to 
diagnostic code information. The capability is included on the push-button 
selector by pressing the up and down arrow buttons at the same time.

 Allison MD3060 and MD3560 

With an Allison MD-equipped vehicle, selecting the right moment to 
upshift or downshift during changing road and traffic conditions is not 
necessary. The Allison MD does it for you. However, knowledge of the gear 
ranges and when to select them will make vehicle control and driving even 
easier.

 WARNING: THESE TRANSMISSIONS HAVE NO PARK POSITION. BEFORE LEAVING THE DRIVER 
SEAT EVEN MOMENTARILY, WHETHER THE ENGINE IS RUNNING OR SHUT OFF, ALWAYS SHIFT 
INTO N (NEUTRAL) AND SET THE PARKING BRAKE OR EMERGENCY BRAKE. ALWAYS USE 
WHEEL CHOCKS. UNEXPECTED AND POSSIBLY SUDDEN VEHICLE MOVEMENT MAY OCCUR IF 
THESE PRECAUTIONS ARE NOT TAKEN. 

 NOTE: The vehicle must be completely stopped before shifting from forward to 
reverse or from reverse to forward. The select indicator will display R and 
the monitor will display R when reverse is attained.

The MD3060 and MD3560 automatics are six-speed transmissions that have 
five forward driving ranges, as described below. These transmissions are 
electronically controlled and are available with a push-button or shift lever 
shifter.

Reverse: The vehicle must be completely stopped before shifting from 
forward to reverse or from reverse to forward. The select indicator will 
display R and the monitor will display R when reverse is attained.

Neutral: Place the transmission in neutral before starting the engine. 
The engine will not start in any other gear (if it does, the neutral start 
circuit must be serviced immediately). Neutral is also used during stationary 
operation of the power takeoff (if so equipped).

 WARNING: DO NOT ALLOW THE VEHICLE TO COAST IN NEUTRAL. TRANSMISSION BRAKING IS 
NOT AVAILABLE IN NEUTRAL. THIS PRACTICE CAN RESULT IN TRANSMISSION DAMAGE. 

Drive: The vehicle will attain first gear when drive is selected, and 
as the speed increases, the transmission will automatically upshift through 
each gear. As the vehicle slows down, the transmission will automatically 
downshift.

5-2: Occasionally, the road conditions, load, or traffic conditions 
will make it desirable to restrict the automatic shifting to a lower gear. 
These positions also provide progressively greater engine braking for going 
down grades (the lower the gear, the greater the braking effect).

First gear: Use this gear when pulling through mud and deep snow, when 
maneuvering in tight spaces, or while driving up or down grades. Low gear 
provides the vehicle with its maximum driving power and maximum engine braking 
power.

 NOTE: The MD3060 and MD3560 transmissions incorporate a hold feature to 
prohibit upshifting above the gear selected during normal driving. For 
downhill operation, the transmission may upshift above the highest gear 
selected when the engine governed speed is exceeded, and damaging the engine 
is a possibility.

 NOTE: In case of engine shutdown (i.e., running out of fuel) while the 
transmission is in gear, the transmission will remain in gear until the 
ignition key is turned to the OFF position. After the ignition key has been 
turned to the OFF position, the transmission will automatically shift to 
neutral and the monitor on the shift pad will display NEUTRAL when the 
ignition key is in the ON position. If the vehicle is equipped with a shift 
lever shifter, the transmission will return to neutral (when the ignition key 
is turned to OFF) but the engine cannot be restarted until the shift lever has 
moved to the NEUTRAL position.

Power takeoff operation: The PTO drive gear on these transmissions is 
engine-driven and provides direct engine power. The power takeoff can be 
operated when the vehicle is moving or stopped.

The PTO gear is in constant mesh with the drive gear in the converter 
housing. A friction clutch or constant drive is used to transmit power to the 
PTO output.

DO NOT SHIFT: If this light illuminates (accompanied by eight seconds 
of short beeps from the shift selector) while the vehicle is in operation, it 
indicates the ECU has detected the transmission operating parameters have been 
exceeded and the shifts are being restricted (i.e., upshifts and downshifts 
may be restricted). Also, the SELECT digit on the shifter display will be 
blank. A diagnostic code will be recorded in the ECU if this happens. The 
transmission will continue to operate in order to seek service assistance. If 
the vehicle is equipped with a push-button shifter, it will not operate. If 
equipped with a shift lever and the lever is moved, a continuous alarm will 
sound until the original shift lever position is restored.

1999 F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Throttle Linkage Check 

 NOTE: Whenever the throttle linkage has been adjusted, adjust the throttle 
modulator linkage. 

When the throttle linkage is properly adjusted, maximum engine 
performance in starting and accelerating a heavily loaded truck is obtained 
automatically. The driver need only press the accelerator pedal to the WOT 
position and hold it there. With the accelerator pedal held at the WOT 
position, the transmission will stay in the starting gear until engine 
crankshaft speed approaches the engine governed speed (maximum engine 
performance), then it will shift into the next higher gear. The automatic, 
full throttle (at detent) shifting just under governed speed will continue 
until the highest gear or desired road speed is reached.

Diagnostic Codes, MD-Series

The following is a list of some of the most common diagnostic codes. 
For a complete listing accompanied by service information, see the Allison

The diagnostic codes are broken down into a two-digit main code and a 
two-digit sub-code.

 CODES 13/12 AND 13/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

13

23

Battery voltage to the ECU is too high

If the condition is intermittent, closely inspect the vehicle wiring 
for transmission system power and grounds. Check for loose, dirty or painted 
connections. Check the vehicle interface module (VIM) for loose, incorrect or 
overheating relays or fuses. Check for wires that are chafed and touching 
other components.

 CODES 21/12 AND 21/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

Throttle position sensor failed low

21

23

Throttle position sensor failed high

This code indicates the throttle position sensor has been released or 
pulled by its linkage into an error zone, a fault with the sensor or the 
wiring to the sensor of the ECU. Perform Pinpoint Test A.

 NOTE: Main Code 21 in conjunction with Main Code 33 indicates the potential 
loss of common ground between the throttle and temperature sensors.

 CODES 24/12 AND 24/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

24

12

Oil temperature cold

24

Oil temperature hot

This code indicates the ECU has detected a high or low temperature in 
the transmission sump. All shifts are inhibited when Code 24/12 is set. No 
upshifts are allowed above a calibration range when Code 24/23 is set. All 
inhibits are cleared when the temperature conditions are normal.

Should the hot oil code appear (24/23), shift the transmission to 
neutral and accelerate the engine to 1200-1500 rpm to allow the transmission 
to return to normal temperature 71-104°C (160-220°F) before operation 
can take place. Check the transmission oil level.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Slave Valve, Preselection 

An air valve shaft protruding from the shift bar housing prevents the 
actuating piston in the slave valve from moving while the shift lever is in a 
gear position and releases the piston when the lever is moved to or through 
neutral.

[FIGURE: C9523B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3124
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 07-06: Shift Controls, Manual Transmission, Air

1999 F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Range Cylinder 

In low range, air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the low 
range port in the range cylinder. This air pressure forces the range cylinder 
piston to the rear, engaging the low range gearing. Air pressure on the back 
of the piston and in the high range air line is exhausted out the slave valve. 

In high range, air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the 
high range port of the range cylinder cover. This air pressure forces the 
range cylinder piston forward, engaging the high range gearing. The air 
pressure that was on the front side of the piston and in the low range air 
line during low range operation is exhausted out the slave valve.

[FIGURE: C95241A.gif]

PAGE 3125
================================================================================

1999 F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Roadranger® Valve A-5010 

Constant air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the S port of 
the Roadranger® valve. In the low range (range lever down), air passes 
through the lever and out the P port of the Roadranger® valve. This 
air returns to the slave valve to the end port or P port depending on the type 
of slave valve used. In high range (control lever up) the lever prevents the 
air from passing through the Roadranger® valve. Air pressure that was 
in the outlet line is exhausted out the bottom of the Roadranger® valve.

 Component Tests 

 Air Filter 

The air filter contains a replaceable filter element that can be 
removed by turning out the end cap. This element must be cleaned or replaced 
at each oil change, or more often under high humidity conditions. 

 Air Regulator 

With normal vehicle air pressure and the shift lever in neutral, check 
the breather port on the side of the regulator. There should be no air leaking 
from the port. If there is a steady leak of air from this port, this indicates 
a damaged regulator that must be replaced. 

Cut off the vehicle air pressure and install an air gauge in the output 
port of the regulator. Bring the vehicle air pressure back to normal. 
Regulated air pressure range is 396-431 kPa (57-62 psi). 

 Slave Valve, Poppet-Type (19470) 

The poppet-type slave valve is a non-serviceable valve. Should this 
valve prove to be damaged, the complete assembly must be replaced. Perform the 
following preliminary checks prior to replacing the valve. 

Check air fittings and air lines between the slave valve and range 
valve for restrictions. A restriction in the line between the outlet port of 
the range valve and the P port of the slave valve can cause a constant air 
leak out the exhaust port of the slave valve. 

Check the torque of the four 1/4-inch slave valve mounting capscrews. 
Tighten to 11 Nm (97 lb-in) and determine if the valve functions 
properly. If the capscrews are not tightened correctly, an air leak between 
the slave valve and the transmission case can result. 

If retightening the four slave valve capscrews eliminates the air 
leaks, remove the valve from the transmission and tighten the three No. 10 
Phillips head base plate screws on the back of the valve to 61 Nm (45 
lb-ft). If the four slave valve retaining capscrews are equipped with star 
washers, install flatwashers under the star washers to prevent them from 
fretting into the valve. Reinstall the valve and tighten capscrews to 11 
Nm (97 lb-in). 

If the valve continues to leak after the above checks have been made, 
the valve should be replaced. 

 Slave Valve, Piston-Type (A-5000) 

The piston-type slave valve (A-5000) is a serviceable valve. It can be 
disassembled and parts replaced as necessary. 

 Slave Valve, Troubleshooting 

The four O-rings and two U-seals are indicated by circled letters on 
the illustration. If any of these are damaged, there will be a constant air 
leak out the exhaust or the atmosphere. In normal operation exhaust will occur 
only for an instant when the range shift is made. Use the following 
illustration and chart to identify damaged O-rings or U-seals.

 Range Cylinder 

If any of the O-rings in the range shift cylinder are worn the range 
shift will be affected. The degree of lost air will govern the degree of 
failure, from slow shift to complete failure to shift. 

Remove the stop nut from the yoke bar.

Apply air to the low range air line to pop the piston from the cylinder 
housing. Use caution.

Remove the O-rings from the outside diameter and inside diameter of the 
piston.

Install new O-rings. Lubricate with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A and reassemble the cylinder 
assembly.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Roadranger® Valve 

 Removal 

Drain the air from the system. 

Remove the screws in the side of the shift handle skirt, and slide the 
skirt down on the shifter shaft.

[FIGURE: C91471A.gif]

 NOTE: If you experience difficulty removing the air line from the fitting, a 
slight impact to the tool used on the release sleeve helps remove the secured 
line. 

Remove the air line fittings from under the valve. 

The release sleeve must be pressed to remove the air line. A 5/32-inch 
open-end wrench or equivalent can be used to press the sleeve. 

To remove the air line, apply pressure evenly to both sides of the 
release sleeve and pull the tubing from the fitting. 

Loosen the lock nut and unscrew the valve from the shifter shaft.

[FIGURE: C9149B.gif]

 Installation 

Install the shift control valve on the shifter shaft and tighten the 
lock nut. 

Install the air lines to the valve. 

The air line cut end must be smooth and square. Use a plastic tubing 
cutter or a sharp razor knife. Do not use diagonal cutters; they deform the 
tubing. If the air line end is deformed or burred, the internal O-ring can be 
damaged which causes leaks. 

To install the air line, insert the cut tubing into the fitting. Make 
sure the tubing is seated fully (approximately 3/4 inch.) Give a slight tug to 
make sure the air line is secured.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Slave Valve, Piston-Type (A-5000) 

 Disassembly 

Disconnect all air lines, turn out the four capscrews and remove the 
slave valve from the transmission. 

Turn out the three capscrews and remove the side cap. 

Remove the seal from the piston and remove the O-ring from the seal. 

Remove the spring from the piston. 

Turn out the end cap from the valve body and remove the piston from the 
bore. 

Remove the U-seal from the piston. 

Remove the nylon plug from the piston and remove the O-ring from the 
plug. 

Remove the snap ring from the bore in front of the valve body. 

Remove plug, spring, washer and U-seal from valve body bore. Remove 
O-ring from plug. 

Lubricate all O-rings and U-seals with silicone lubricant and 
reassemble the slave valve. 

 Assembly 

Follow disassembly procedure in reverse order. When reinstalling the 
end cap, do not use more than 54 Nm (40 lb-ft) of torque. 
Overtightening can result in binding the piston in the valve bore.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch System

The purpose of the clutch is to transfer power from the engine to the 
drivetrain. It connects and disconnects a manually-operated transmission and 
the remainder of the drivetrain from the engine. This permits starting and 
stopping the vehicle, shifting and changing speeds that correspond to the 
engine speed through gear reductions for both forward and reverse directions.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Pressure Plate 

Inspect the surface of the pressure plate for burn marks, scores, 
flatness or ridges. If the pressure plate is badly heat-checked or deeply 
scored, replace the pressure plate and cover assembly.

Inspect friction surface of the pressure plate for damage or 
distortion. If friction surface is badly warped or dished in excess of 0.254 
mm (0.010 inch), replace with new pressure plate. Smooth and flat pressure 
plate surfaces must be used for satisfactory clutch life.

Clean the pressure plate and flywheel surfaces with a suitable 
commercial solvent to be sure that surfaces are free from any oil film. 

 CAUTION: Do not use cleaners with a petroleum base, and do not immerse the 
pressure plate in the solvent. 

 NOTE: If a substantial difference in lever wear exists, the heavily worn 
lever is binding. Replace the pressure plate.

Using a straightedge and a feeler gauge, check the face runout of the 
pressure plate. If the runout is greater than the service limit, replace the 
clutch cover assembly. 

Service limit: 0-.508 mm (0-.02 inch) 

[FIGURE: C11476A.gif]

 NOTE: Always check the condition of the engine flywheel for cracks, heat 
checks or other damage whenever the clutch is inspected, removed or replaced.

 Clutch Wear 

[FIGURE: C8083B.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Disc/Discs

 NOTE: For adjustment-free clutch, go to step 2.

Block the release bearing with wood blocks (1/2 x 1/2 x 3 inches for 
two-plate and 1/2 x 1 3/4 x 3 inches for single-plate) using the tool provided 
in Spicer Clutch Service Kit CSK 1 or equivalent tool, as shown.

[FIGURE: C10321A.gif]

Remove the clutch from the flywheel. Refer to Section 08-01 . 

 NOTE: For dual clutch disc assemblies, the front and rear disc may have 
different thicknesses.

Check the driven disc. 

Using a vernier caliper, measure the gauge (facing) thickness in three 
or four areas around each disc. If less than the service limit, replace clutch 
disc.

Gasoline Engines

Standard: 10.16 mm (0.400 inch)

Service: 7.62 mm (0.300 inch)

Diesel Engines

Standard: 11.4 mm (0.450 inch)

Service 9.65 mm (0.380 inch)

[FIGURE: C11477A.gif]

If the thickness varies by more than 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) on the 
facing surface, replace the disc. Measurements are taken on pad in similar 
location and distance from the outer edge of clutch disc.

[FIGURE: C10322A.gif]

Check the driven disc hub spline for burrs or uneven wear. If either is 
evident, replace the clutch disc. 

Using a feeler gauge, measure the clearance between the clutch disc 
spline and the transmission input shaft spline. If the clearance is greater 
than the service limit, replace the clutch disc.

Standard: 0.05-0.15 mm (0.002-0.006 inch)

Service Limit: 0.5 mm (0.02 inch)

[FIGURE: C11478A.gif]

Check the flywheel surface for: 

concavity 

runout 

allowable grind for a reground flywheel 

Refer to Flywheel under Cleaning and Inspection in this section.

 NOTE: When installing a new disc, be careful when handling not to drop it or 
contaminate it with oil or grease.

Check the pilot bearing. If the bearing is rough, replace it. 

Inspect the clutch disc facings for oil or grease. Eliminate the source 
of any oil or grease before replacing the disc. An excessive amount of grease 
on the bearing hub will find its way to the disc facings. Too much lubricant 
in the transmission or a plugged transmission vent will force the transmission 
lubricant out of the input shaft and onto the disc facings. Leaking rear 
engine seals will allow engine oil to flow onto the disc facings. 

Perform the following checks:

Check the clutch disc for worn or loose facings.

Check the disc for warpage and for loose rivets at the hub.

Check for broken springs. Springs loose enough to rattle will not cause 
noise when the vehicle is operating.

Replace the clutch assembly if any of these conditions are present.

[FIGURE: C10818B.gif]

 Two-Disc Clutch with Positive Separator, 350-mm (14-Inch) Applications 

When reinstalling the intermediate plate assembly, be sure that the 
four separator pins are flush with the cast surface of the intermediate plate 
lug (pressure plate side).

[FIGURE: C10323C.gif]

Install the intermediate plate assembly as shown with the drive straps 
toward the pressure plate.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel

Inspect the flywheel. If it is heat-checked or warped, resurface or 
replace the flywheel as necessary. Check flywheel runout. To remove or replace 
the flywheel, refer to Section 03A-01 , Section 03B-01 or Section 03C-01 . To

[FIGURE: C9448C.gif]

misalignment. Refer to Flywheel Housing Alignment in the Adjustments portion 
of this section.

flywheel. If the teeth are worn or damaged, replace the ring gear or the 
flywheel. To replace the ring gear, refer to Section 03A-01 , Section 03B-01 or 
 Section 03C-01 .

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel Runout Check

Position Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to the 
engine flywheel housing with gauge finger on the face of the flywheel near the 
outer edge. Rotate flywheel, making sure to hold it in the full forward or 
rearward position so that crankshaft end play will not be indicated as 
flywheel runout. Maximum allowable runout is 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) per inch of 
the flywheel diameter. For example, 0.178 mm (0.007 inch) runout is allowable 
for a 356-mm (14-inch) clutch.

[FIGURE: C9451C.gif]

If the clutch face runout exceeds specification, remove the flywheel 
and check for burrs between the flywheel and the face of the crankshaft 
mounting flange. If no burrs exist, check the runout of the crankshaft 
mounting flange. Replace the flywheel or machine the crankshaft flywheel 
mounting face sufficiently to correct the surface if the mounting flange 
runout exceeds the specification of 0.2 mm (0.008 inch).

If the crankshaft mounting flange is not the cause of the runout, 
resurface or replace the flywheel as necessary. To resurface, refer to Section 03-00 . To remove or replace the flywheel, refer to Section 03A-01 , Section 03B-01 or Section 03C-01 .

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Release Bearing

Wipe all oil and dirt off the release bearing. The bearing is 
prelubricated and should not be cleaned with solvent.

Inspect the release bearing as follows:

 NOTE: A light intermittent clicking noise may result during pedal application 
(to limit of pedal free travel), and upon further pedal depression, a normal 
bearing noise may be audible. Some noise under these situations will not 
adversely affect clutch function and does not necessarily indicate a failed 
release bearing or out-of-plane pressure plate release levers. Inspection of 
these components is not required unless the noise is excessive.

Hold the bearings, hub and back plate and rotate the outer race while 
applying pressure. If the bearing rotation is rough, replace the bearing. If 
bearing is good, remember to refill grease in inside diameter pocket.

Inspect/remove any surface scoring or burrs that may affect the sliding 
motion of the release bearing on the transmission input shaft retainer. Any 
scoring or burrs should be polished off with fine grade emery paper.

Inspect release bearing hub groove for freedom from nicks and burrs or 
lever wear. Replace the bearing only if there is excessive wear on lever 
groove from release lever contact surface.

Prior to reinstallation, lubricate release bearing hub with 
lithium-base grease Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B at the following points:

annular groove (grease pocket) of release bearing inside diameter

thin coat on inside diameter of release bearing

release bearing retention clips and fingers of clutch release lever

fulcrum point of clutch release lever

Failure situations for release bearing operation:

too little clutch pedal free play may allow contact of clutch fingers 
with bearing and thus result in a continuously running bearing.

riding the clutch pedal has the same effect as above.

misalignment of clutch release lever.

misalignment between engine and the transmission will exhibit symptoms 
such as transmission jumping out of gear, driveshaft vibration, excessive spin 
time resulting in gear clash, and clutch chatter on start-up.

PAGE 3144
================================================================================

Section 08-00: Clutch System, Service

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Release Lever/Shaft

Examine release lever hole or fork end holes for excessive elongation, 
and replace as required.

Make sure that the cross-shaft and fork assembly rotates freely and has 
no play in the clutch housing bushings. If play exists, replace bushings and 
shaft as required.

Check that the release lever fork tips are not excessively worn and 
that the curved portion of the lever is curved with no flat spots. Also, check

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch Adjustment Procedures

Various service tips have been developed to help the heavy truck 
service technician troubleshoot and adjust Spicer stamped angle-spring 
clutches. These include: 

recognizing symptoms of potential concerns

inspecting and checking the affected clutch components 

determining which clutch parts actually require replacement 

adjusting procedures for synchronized and non-synchronized transmissions 

If service is required, use the following service procedure to adjust 
and check the clutch components. 

 330-mm (13-Inch) Clutch with Gasoline Engine 

The 330-mm (13-inch) clutch is adjusted through the clutch linkage. 
Refer to Section 08-02 . If the clutch is not releasing properly, the clutch 
may need to be replaced. Refer to Section 08-01 .

 Stamped Angle-Spring Clutch, Ford Diesel Engines, Spicer 356-mm 
(14-Inch) Single and Double Disc with Adjustment-Free Clutch 

No adjustment is needed for this type of clutch. As the clutch wears, 
the internal self-adjuster will automatically adjust for free play and travel.

If the clutch is not releasing properly, the clutch assembly may need 
to be replaced. Refer to Section 08-01 . After replacement of the clutch, 
actuate the clutch by pushing the pedal all the way to the floor five to ten 
times. This will set the release bearing gap to specification of 12.7-14.2 mm 
(0.500-0.560 inch). Set free play (initially after replacement) by adjusting 
the clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

 Stamped Angle-Spring Clutch, Ford Diesel Engines, Spicer 356-mm 
(14-Inch) Single and Double Disc with Kwik-Adjust Adjustment 

 Non-Synchronized Transmissions 

Adjust the external linkage rod so that the clutch brake squeeze begins 
about 12.7-33 mm (0.5-1.3 inch) from the end of the pedal stroke.

[FIGURE: DC0018A.gif]

Check the adjustment results by placing a business card (or similar 
device) behind the clutch release bearing and depressing the clutch pedal. The 
card should be held tight. 

Release the clutch pedal. See if the card slips out when the pedal is 
approximately 12.7-33 mm (0.5-1.3 inch) from the end of the pedal stroke. 

 Clutch Free Travel 

The linkage should not be adjusted to compensate for clutch face wear. 
Linkage should only be reset to provide proper pedal free play upon 
installation of a new clutch and not every time clutch is adjusted internally. 
If linkage is adjusted for proper pedal free play, it should be done after 
specified bearing release travel is obtained. For proper linkage settings 
refer to Section 08-02 .

 Non-Synchronized Transmission 

Adjust the clutch internally to get about 38.1 mm (1.3 inch) free play 
at the top of the stroke or 3.2 mm (.126 inch) pedal between yoke and wear 
pads and 12.7-14.2 mm (0.500-0.560 inch) release bearing travel as shown below.

[FIGURE: DC0019B.gif]

Adjust the clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until the 
Kwik-Adjust adjustment bolt is exposed. 

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

Hold or block the clutch pedal in the released position. 

Use a 5/8 (6 point) socket. Apply an inward pressure on Kwik-Adjust 
bolt (hex-head). A clockwise adjustment will move release bearing housing 
toward the transmission, a counterclockwise adjustment will move release 
bearing housing toward the flywheel. Rotation will move the release bearing 
approximately 0.51 mm (0.020 inch). 

After final adjustment is made, align the adjustment to the nearest 
edge, allowing the Kwik-Adjust bolt to disengage by returning to an outward 
position. 

Check the distance from the clutch release bearing to the clutch brake. 
There must be 12.7-14.2 mm (0.500-0.560 inch) minimum movement of the release 
bearing for proper clutch release. Adjust the clutch internally to obtain 
this. 

For 

Cummins B5.9 and C8.3 Diesel 12.7-14.2 mm (0.500-0.560 inch)

Whenever clutch pedal free play becomes 12.7 mm (0.5 inch) or less, 
readjustment is recommended. 

 Synchronized Transmissions 

Check measurement with clutch pedal up.

[FIGURE: DC0020B.gif]

Use the Kwik-Adjust bolt to set minimum release travel on clutches. 

 NOTE: The 47.625 mm (1.875 inch) and 19.05 mm (0.75 inch) measurements are 
for reference only. The most accurate measurement for the minimum release 
travel is the 12.7 mm (0.5 inch) measurement between the input shaft cover and 
the release bearing with the clutch release lever tight against wear pads.

To set a 12.7-14.2 mm (0.500-0.560 inch) minimum release travel proceed 
as follows: 

With pedal depressed, turn the Kwik-Adjust bolt to obtain about a 12.7 
mm (0.5 inch) gap minimum between input shaft cover and release bearing (with 
free play removed) as shown for the respective single and two-plate clutches. 

Turn the adjusting ring clockwise to move the release bearing toward 
the transmission. 

Turn the adjusting ring counterclockwise to move the release bearing 
toward the engine. 

To set 3.2 mm (0.126 inch) dimension as shown, proceed as follows: 

Adjust the external linkage by shortening or lengthening to obtain 3.2 
mm (0.126 inch) between the release lever and the wear pads on the release 
bearing housing. Refer to Section 08-02 for adjustments. 

Check to see that this adjustment provides approximately 28-38 mm 
(1.1-1.5 inch) of free travel at the pedal. 

Tighten all lock nuts.

Whenever clutch pedal free play becomes 12.7 mm (0.5 inch) or less, 
readjustment is recommended. 

 Clutch and Driven Disc Check 

If the release of the clutch is still not acceptable after the linkage 
and clutch adjustments have been made, proceed as follows: 

Adjust the clutch so that there is no free travel.

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

[FIGURE: C10319A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not adjust linkage. 

Turn the adjusting bolt counterclockwise to increase release bearing 
travel. 

This will create additional release bearing travel. 

It will increase the internal pressure plate travel. 

Test drive and determine if the release of the clutch has been affected. 

If the release has improved, replace the driven discs only. Refer to 
 Section 08-01 to replace discs.

Readjust the clutch after replacing the discs. 

 Clutch Brake Check (Non-Synchronized Transmissions) 

Clamp the clutch brake, on the outside diameter, in a vise. 

Slide a modified input shaft (a cut input shaft with a nut welded on it 
to accommodate a torque wrench) through the clutch brake.

[FIGURE: C10320A.gif]

Connect the torque wrench to the nut and rotate two half turns. Take 
note of the torque reading. 

The torque should not read lower than 16.3 Nm (12 lb-ft). 

If the reading is higher than 16.3 Nm (12 lb-ft), reuse the 
brake. 

If lower, replace it. 

If the reading is more than 47.5 Nm (35 lb-ft), replace the 
clutch brake to eliminate the possibility of tang breakage. 

 Clutch Release Bearing Adjustment 

Set the gap between the release bearing and the front cover of the 
input shaft (synchronized transmissions) or the clutch brake (non-synchronized 
transmissions) to 13.7-14.2 mm (0.500-0.560 inch).

Rotate the engine flywheel until the Kwik-Adjust bolt is exposed.

Release the clutch by holding the clutch pedal in the depressed position.

Remove the free play from the clutch linkage by holding the release 
lever against the wear pads of the release bearing.

Check the distance as described in Step 1 of this procedure. If 
adjustment is necessary, engage the Kwik-Adjust bolt and adjust until desired 
setting is reached. Counterclockwise rotation of the Kwik-Adjust bolt will 
move the release bearing towards the flywheel. A clockwise rotation will move 
the release bearing away from the flywheel.

Disengage the Kwik-Adjust bolt, engage the clutch and recheck as 
outlined in Step 1 of this procedure.

ADJUSTMENTS

Flywheel Housing Alignment 

Inspection and alignment of the flywheel housing is necessary when 
symptoms exist of excessive transmission gear wear, transmission jumping out 
of gear, driveline vibration, clutch pedal vibration or scrubby feel, pilot 
bearing noise, release bearing noise, or excessive clutch spin time. Common 
complaint areas or obvious misadjustment should always be checked and 
corrected prior to checking alignment, to be sure that the basic system is in 
working order. 

Alignment of the flywheel housing bore and rear face with engine should 
be checked as a possible cause of any of the following troubles: excessive 
transmission gear wear, transmission jumping out of gear, clutch pedal 
vibration or scrubby pedal feel, driveline vibration, excessive pilot bushing 
wear, or excessive clutch spin time. Whenever any of the above concerns are 
identified, the clutch housing should be given a complete inspection. 

The engine and transmission must have a common axis. The following 
checks must be made to locate possible misalignment. Clean all surfaces 
thoroughly before taking readings or checking parts.

When taking the following readings, rotate the engine by hand — 
do not crank the engine with the starter. The engine may be rotated by the 
pulley nut at the front end of the crankshaft, or from the flywheel mounting 
bolts, or starter ring gear on the flywheel. Make sure ignition system is 
disabled, key OFF position. 

Before taking dial indicator measurements of the engine flywheel or 
flywheel housing, make sure the engine crankshaft does not have excessive end 
play. If it does, accurate readings cannot be obtained. Place the dial 
indicator finger against the flywheel. Force the crankshaft back and forth 
with a pry bar. If the end play movement exceeds the maximum, it will have to 
be corrected. 

Inspect for a worn or fretted pilot on both the transmission clutch 
housing and the engine flywheel housing. The 3.2 mm (0.126 inch) pilot lip of 
the transmission clutch housing can wear into the flywheel housing either by 
the transmission loosening up or, after high mileage, from road and engine 
vibration. Any appreciable amount of wear on either part will cause 
misalignment and the part should be replaced. The wear will generally be found 
between the 3 o'clock and 8 o'clock positions.

[FIGURE: C35291A.gif]

[FIGURE: C35301A.gif]

Use Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to measure 
the face of the engine flywheel housing. Secure the dial indicator to the 
engine flywheel with the gauge finger against the housing face. Rotate the 
flywheel by hand and, with chalk or soapstone, mark the high and low points of 
the indicator as it is being rotated.

[FIGURE: C9450C.gif]

The total runout will be the difference between the highest plus and 
minus readings. Maximum total runout of the flywheel housing pilot is 0.203 mm 
(0.008 inch) with No. 2 SAE housings.

[FIGURE: C35321A.gif]

 NOTE: If you have to reposition the flywheel housing, it is necessary to mark 
your high and low runout readings in the clock positions. 

Use dial indicator to measure the bore of the engine flywheel housing. 
With the dial indicator secured to the flywheel, move gauge finger against the 
flywheel housing bore. Mark the high and low points. The SAE maximum total 
runout for the flywheel housing bore is 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) with No. 2 SAE 
housings for wear areas.

[FIGURE: C9449C.gif]

Use dial indicator to measure the flywheel face. Secure the dial 
indicator to the engine flywheel housing with gauge finger against the face of 
the flywheel near the outer edge. Turn the flywheel to obtain readings. A 
runout or face wobble of 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) per inch of flywheel radius is 
allowed. For example, if the vehicle has a 356-mm (14-inch) clutch and 
readings are taken just off the outer edge of the clutch disc, maximum 
tolerance would be 0.178 mm (0.007 inch).

[FIGURE: C35341A.gif]

Use dial indicator to measure the pilot bearing bore of the flywheel. 
With the indicator secured to the flywheel housing, move gauge finger to 
contact pilot bearing bore surface. Turn the flywheel and obtain readings. The 
SAE maximum total runout for the pilot bearing bore is 0.127 mm (0.005 inch).

[FIGURE: C35351A.gif]

The transmission clutch housing face and pilot cannot be checked 
accurately in the field, unless you have a set of case bore plugs and shaft. 
This setup consists of plugs with very close fits that are tapped into the 
front and rear bores of the transmission case. A shaft fits through the 
centers of the plugs and extends to the front far enough to secure the dial 
indicator and obtain a reading on the clutch housing. The SAE maximum runout 
for the transmission clutch housing face and pilot is 0.203 mm (0.008 inch) 
with No. 2 SAE housings. 

 NOTE: Exceeding these limits causes misalignment. If not corrected, 
misalignment causes premature wear of drivetrain components.

Use dial indicator to measure the flywheel crankshaft face. Secure the 
dial indicator to the engine flywheel housing with the gauge finger against 
the crankshaft face near the outer edge. Turn the crankshaft to obtain 
readings. A runout of 0.0381 mm (0.0015 inch) on the crankshaft face is allowed.

[FIGURE: C35361A.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment Correction

Since any change in face alignment will change bore alignment, it may 
be possible to correct bore alignment by changing the face alignment. Face 
alignment can be changed by shimming between the flywheel housing and engine. 
The following illustration shows the type of shim that can be fabricated.

[FIGURE: DC0017A.gif]

The shim required is one half the maximum (minus) indicator reading, 
and should be located at the point of maximum (minus) indicator reading. 

If both the bore and face alignment are out of limits, shim between the 
flywheel housing and engine to bring the face alignment within limits. Check 
the bore alignment. 

If the bore alignment is out of limits and the face alignment is within 
limits, shim the flywheel housing to the limit of face misalignment and check 
the bore alignment. If it is not within limits, replace the housing.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch System

The purpose of the clutch is to transfer power from the engine to the 
drivetrain. It connects and disconnects a manually-operated transmission and 
the remainder of the drivetrain from the engine. This permits starting and 
stopping the vehicle, shifting and changing speeds that correspond to the 
engine speed through gear reductions for both forward and reverse directions.

The clutch consists of a splined driven plate (clutch disc) that is 
held in position by the transmission input shaft and a clutch cover (pressure 
plate) that is bolted to the flywheel. The driven plate is a metal disc, faced 
on both sides with ceramic or organic friction material. The pressure plate is 
a metal member that houses and engages the driven plate. This solid member 
(clutch assembly), when engaged, forms a continuous system through which power 
from the engine is transferred to the transmission and then to the rear wheels 
for forward or reverse rotation. Another internal part is the pilot bearing, 
mounted either in the flywheel or crankshaft. The bearing supports the end of 
the input shaft. It is designed for long life and requires no periodic 
maintenance.

When the clutch is engaged, the pressure springs load the pressure 
plate holding the clutch disc(s) firmly between the flywheel and the pressure 
plate. As the clutch pedal is actuated, movement is transferred through the 
mechanical linkage to the release shaft and clutch release lever. On a 
pull-type design clutch, as the release shaft turns, the release lever pulls 
back on the release bearing, unloading the levers and pressure springs, which 
permits the pressure plate to move away from the clutch disc. On a push-type 
design clutch, a clutch sleeve is mounted over the transmission input shaft. 
The sleeve carries a throw-out bearing that is pressed against the fingers of 
the clutch pressure plate. As the release shaft turns, the release lever 
pushes the release bearing, unloading the levers and diaphragm spring, which 
permits the pressure plate to move away from the clutch disc. On either 
design, the clutch disc is disengaged from the engine flywheel and the 
transmission can be shifted to another gear.

The pull-type design clutch features an adjustable dry pressure plate 
that has centrally located angle pressure springs isolated from the heat of 
the pressure plate. The pressure plate also carries return springs to obtain 
positive pressure plate return at the clutch release. The clutch release 
bearing rotates continuously and only carries a thrust load when the clutch is 
released. The release bearing can be lubricated through the transmission lower 
inspection opening in the clutch housing.

================================================================================
PAGE 3159
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 08-01: Clutch/Pressure Plate

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Brake

The purpose of the clutch brake is to slow down or stop the 
transmission input shaft from rotating. This permits a clean engagement of 
either first or reverse gears when starting the vehicle from a standstill.

Non-synchronized transmissions use a torque limiting clutch brake. The 
brake is a steel hub with two tangs, encased in a cover that has a facing 
material bonded to both sides. The torque limiting feature is provided by an 
internal slip washer, loaded by a wave spring washer that is then driven by 
the hub. The spring washer reacts against the clutch brake cover on the one 
side and the internal slip washer on the other, providing a clamping force, 
creating a breakaway torque within the brake. This feature is called torque 
limiting. The hub and spring washer combination slips with respect to the 
covers after approximately 24 Nm (18 lb-ft) load has been exceeded. 
This protects the outside facings.

When the operator depresses the clutch pedal to the floorboard, beyond 
the normal clutch disengage position, the clutch release bearing comes in 
contact with the clutch brake and the transmission input shaft bearing cover. 
Because the tangs on the brake hub are engaged in the transmission input shaft 
splines, the transmission is slowed down or stopped. The driver can then shift 
from first to reverse or from reverse to first without clashing or putting 
undue strain on the gears.

[FIGURE: C94821A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Preassembly Procedures

 WARNING: DO NOT INHALE THE DUST FROM BRAKES, CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. 
INHALATION OF DUST FROM THESE COMPONENTS COULD BE INJURIOUS TO YOUR HEALTH. 
COMPRESSED AIR OR BRUSHES MUST NOT BE USED TO CLEAN BRAKES, BRAKE DRUMS, 
CLUTCHES OR ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. USE A VACUUM CLEANER SUCH AS ROTUNDA BRAKE, 
CLUTCH, SERVICE VACUUM 164-R3600 OR EQUIVALENT EQUIPPED FOR THIS PURPOSE TO 
REMOVE ANY DUST. ADHERENT DUST SHOULD BE REMOVED WITH A DAMP RAG. ANY DUST 
SHOULD BE CONTAINED IN A SEALED AND LABELED BAG FOR DISPOSAL. WEAR AN APPROVED 
HIGH EFFICIENCY CARTRIDGE OR AIR LINE RESPIRATOR AND USE EXTRA CAUTION TO 
AVOID BREATHING THIS DUST. 

Clean the following components by scraping them and soaking them in a 
suitable solvent:

flywheel housing face and bore

clutch housing face 

transmission input shaft 

front face

Check for any damage or excessive wear and service as necessary. Clean 
the clutch housing interior with a suitable solvent.

Clean the transmission input shaft with a wire brush, then polish the 
shaft and clean with a suitable solvent. Check condition of the transmission 
input shaft. Use a stone to dull sharp edges of the splines. If splines are 
worn excessively or notched, the clutch disc will not slide on the shaft. 
Replace the input shaft as required.

Clean the flywheel face with a suitable solvent.

Clean the clutch release lever with a wire brush. Smooth the clutch 
release lever fingers locating faces with a carborundum stone and then clean 
with a suitable solvent. Apply a light coating of Motorcraft Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to 
the clutch release lever finger tips and locating faces. If clutch release 
lever is worn excessively, replace it.

Apply Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the cross-shaft bushings until clean 
grease appears from all four bushings. Remove the excess grease.

If reinstalling the old clutch, clean the pressure plate with a 
suitable solvent.

If the shaft/fork assembly has not been dismantled, check that the 
shafts do not protrude into the fork locating space and make sure that the 
non-operating shaft end is flush with the outside of the clutch housing. Make 
sure that the assembly turns freely.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Disc and Pressure Plate, 330-mm (13-Inch) Single-Disc, Push-Type Clutch

 Removal 

Disconnect rod assembly at the release lever (fork).

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

Remove the dust cover from the flywheel housing.

Mark the cover assembly and the flywheel, so that the parts can be 
reinstalled in the same relative positions.

 CAUTION: Shipping blocks are required to avoid drive straps being bent and to 
allow clutch to be removed without removal of clutch housing. 

 NOTE: If shipping blocks do not fit under lever tail, push clutch pedal down 
to reduce lever load, then insert shipping blocks. If shipping blocks are 
loose under tail, as mounting bolts are removed, lever will begin to unload, 
holding shipping blocks in place. Shipping blocks may be thicker than shown so 
they are not loose when installed under clutch lever tail.

Install three shipping blocks under lever tail before removing clutch.

[FIGURE: C11444A.gif]

[FIGURE: C11445A.gif]

 CAUTION: If removing clutch through the transmission clutch housing dust cover, 
position a long input shaft or rod 305 mm (12 inches) long and 20-23 mm 
(0.800-0.900 inch) in diameter, through the pilot bearing inner diameter and 
past the transmission clutch housing opening to prevent accidental dropping 
and possible damage to the clutch assembly. 

Install a suitable clutch aligning tool through the driven disc and 
into the pilot bearing.

Loosen the cover attaching bolts evenly and remove the bolts.

Remove the cover assembly and the clutch disc from the flywheel through 
the opening in the bottom of the clutch housing. Remove the pilot bearing only 
for replacement.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: If a new clutch is to be installed, a new pilot bearing must also be 
installed. 

Position the clutch disc on the flywheel so that the truck clutch 
alignment tool can enter the clutch pilot bearing and align the disc. A spare 
spline shaft of compatible size may also be used.

 NOTE: When reinstalling the original cover assembly, align the assembly marks 
made during the removal procedure.

Position the cover assembly on the flywheel, aligning the pressure 
plate and disc with the alignment tool. Install the mounting bolts that fasten 
the assembly to the flywheel. Tighten the bolts to 48-61 Nm (35-45 
lb-ft) in the following sequence.

[FIGURE: C11983A.gif]

Remove the clutch disc alignment tool and shipping blocks. Once the 
clutch is bolted down, move the alignment tool in and out. There should be no 
binding.

With the clutch fully released, apply a light film of Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B on the inside diameter of the release bearing hub. 

Apply a light film of Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the release lever 
fingers and to the lever trunnion or fulcrum. Install the release lever on the 
trunnion in the flywheel housing. Position the clutch release bearing and the 
bearing hub on the release lever.

If the clutch housing has been removed, position it against the engine 
rear cover plate and install the retaining bolts. Tighten clutch housing bolts 
to 68-95 Nm (50-70 lb-ft). If dust cover was removed, install and 
tighten screws to 16-23 Nm (12-17 lb-ft).

Install the transmission assembly on the clutch housing. Refer to the 
appropriate section in Group 07 to finalize transmission installation.

Adjust the clutch pedal free play with linkage trim rod. Refer to 
 Section 08-02 .
