Install Truck Clutch Alignment Shaft D79T-7550-A for 38.1-mm (1.5-inch) 
input shaft or D79T-7550-B for 44.45-mm (1.75-inch) input shaft or equivalents 
into the release bearing, disc and pilot bearing. A spare spline shaft of 
compatible size may also be used.

[FIGURE: DC0027A.gif]

 NOTE: Before removing clutch cover assembly on an adjustment-free clutch, 
four shipping bolts must be installed in the clutch cover to prevent pressure 
plate from moving forward. Refer to illustration of adjustment-free clutch 
assembly.

Install four shipping bolts (adjustment-free clutch only).

 CAUTION: Whenever the clutch is removed, spacer blocks must be installed to 
prevent release bearing from moving forward and bottoming. If the release 
bearing is allowed to move too far forward, the internal levers in the clutch 
cover may partially come out of the groove in the retainer. If the cover is 
reinstalled, internal binding of the clutch or loss of levers can occur. Both 
are detrimental to the performance of the clutch. 

Install two 1/2 x 1 3/4 x 3-inch spacer blocks between the clutch cover 
and the release bearing assembly to relieve the heavy internal spring load in 
the clutch assembly. If there is inadequate clearance to install the spacers, 
use the release fork tool provided in the Spicer Clutch Service Kit (CSKI) to 
evenly pull back the release bearing assembly and then install the spacer 
blocks.

[FIGURE: C9442C.gif]

Remove two top mounting bolts attaching the cover assembly to the 
flywheel and install two 3/8-16 x 2-inch guide studs to help support the 
weight of the clutch.

[FIGURE: C11141A.gif]

[FIGURE: C9443C.gif]

Loosen the remaining clutch cover bolts in a crisscross pattern to 
prevent cocking and bending of the clutch mounting bolts. Remove all of the 
mounting bolts and remove the clutch cover.

Remove the alignment tool and the clutch disc from the flywheel. 

Inspect the engine flywheel housing and flywheel. Refer to Section 08-00 . If flywheel is heat-checked or warped, refer to Section 03-00 for 
flywheel clutch surface machining. To replace flywheel or flywheel housing, 
refer to Section 03A-01 or Section 03B-01 .

Check condition of the transmission input shaft. Use a stone to dull 
sharp edges of the splines. If splines are worn excessively or notched, the 
clutch disc will not slide on the shaft. Replace the input shaft as required.

Inspect the pilot bearing. Refer to Section 08-00 . If required, remove 
pilot bearing using a suitable puller.

Check wear on fingers of the clutch release lever, cross-shaft and 
cross-shaft bushings. Replace any of the components if excessive wear is noted.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: If a new clutch is to be installed, a new pilot bearing must also be 
installed. 

If removed, install the pilot bearing using Pilot Bearing Replacer 
T93T-7025-EH for 44.45-mm (1.75-inch) input shaft and T93T-7025-BH for 38.1-mm 
(1.5-inch) input shaft. Use Driver Handle T80T-4000-W with the Pilot Bearing 
Replacer.

Install two guide studs (3/8-16 x 2-inch) at the 11 and 1 o'clock 
positions of the flywheel.

 CAUTION: Clutch will not function correctly if disc is installed backwards. Make 
sure the side marked PRESSURE PLATE SIDE faces the pressure plate. 

Install the disc by inserting the aligning tool through the splines and 
into the pilot bearing.

With the alignment tool still in place, carefully slide the clutch 
cover assembly over the aligning tool and onto the guide studs. Align the 
Kwik-Adjust bolt with the opening in the clutch housing.

 CAUTION: Use only Ford-approved mounting bolts. 

Install the clutch cover mounting bolts and lockwashers hand-tight. 
Tighten in the following sequence to 48-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C9444B.gif]

Replace the guide studs with the two mounting bolts, and tighten to 
48-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

 NOTE: Whenever an adjustment-free clutch assembly is removed, shipping bolts 
must be installed to prevent pressure plate from moving forward.

For adjustment-free clutch only, remove four shipping bolts from clutch 
cover. Save shipping bolts.

[FIGURE: DC0028A.gif]

For adjustment-free clutch only, check to make sure there is no visible 
gap between the spacer sleeve and the bolt head.

[FIGURE: C12985A.gif]

 NOTE: Save the spacer blocks installed during removal.

Remove the two spacer blocks from between the release bearing housing 
and the clutch cover assembly if they have not fallen out.

Move alignment tool in and out to make sure no binding exists. Remove 
the clutch aligning tool.

Install the clutch brake assembly on the transmission input shaft, if 
so equipped (non-synchronized transmission). Shift the transmission into gear.

Rotate clutch release bearing housing so that flat section is on top.

 NOTE: Clutch release bearings must be lubricated after adjustment and at 
regular maintenance intervals. Lubricate the release bearing with Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. Clutches with a permanently sealed release bearing require no 
lubrication.

Apply a small daub of grease to each of the clutch release lever 
fingers and the release bearing wear pads (both sides).

Install the transmission into the vehicle. Rotate clutch release lever 
so that release lever fingers clear the pads on the release bearing housing, 
as the transmission is moved forward into position.

Make sure the transmission is square to and aligned with the engine 
when it is raised into position. Use a transmission jack to support the 
transmission during installation.

Make sure the release bearing lever clears the bearing and is rotated 
over the wear pads as the clutch housing is moved forward.

Align the splines by turning the transmission output shaft. Do not 
force the transmission onto the clutch or flywheel housing. If it does not 
enter freely, check the installation.

 Engaging Clutch Release Lever 

[FIGURE: C9445B.gif]

Start all transmission retaining bolts and tighten progressively around 
the housing to specifications. Tighten clutch housing bolts to 48-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft). Refer to appropriate transmission section in Group 07 to 
finalize transmission installation. 

Connect clutch release linkage.

Check and adjust clutch.

Remove clutch housing inspection cover.

For adjustment-free clutch, actuate the clutch assembly by depressing 
the clutch pedal five to ten times, releasing the clutch. Check release 
bearing travel. Release bearing travel should be 13-14 Nm (0.500-0.560 
inch). Adjust clutch pedal free play with clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

For Kwik-Adjust clutches, check release bearing travel, clutch brake 
squeeze (non-synchronized transmission) and proper free pedal adjustment. 
Adjust as required according to instructions in the Adjustments portion of 
this section and in Section 08-02 .

Install clutch housing cover.

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch

 Internal Adjustment 

 Clutch, Spicer Disc Pull-Type, Stamped Angle Spring (Single- and 
Double-Disc with Cummins B5.9 Diesel or Cummins C8.3 Diesel) 

The linkage on a 356-mm (14-inch) single- or multiple-disc clutch 
should not be adjusted to compensate for clutch face wear. Linkage should only 
be reset to provide proper pedal free play upon installation of a new clutch 
and not every time you adjust the clutch internally. If linkage is adjusted 
for proper pedal freeplay, it should be done after specified bearing release 
travel is obtained. For proper linkage settings, refer to Section 08-02 . 

To make an internal clutch adjustment, remove the inspection cover from 
the bottom of the clutch housing. 

Remove the pedal free play by placing the clutch release lever against 
the release bearing. Measure the distance between the rear of the release 
bearing and the clutch brake or input shaft cover depending on whether it has 
a synchronized or non-synchronized transmission. On vehicles equipped with 
356-mm (14-inch) Spicer clutches, the dimension between the release bearing 
and the clutch brake or input shaft cover (bearing release travel) should be 
13-14-mm (0.500-0.560-inch) for the Cummins B5.9 and C8.3 diesel engines.

Adjust the clutch assembly by rotating the engine flywheel until the 
Kwik-Adjust bolt is exposed.

[FIGURE: C11140C.gif]

Hold or block the clutch pedal in the released position. 

Use a 5/8 (6-point) socket to turn the Kwik-Adjust bolt. Apply inward 
pressure on the spring and hex-head bolt adjusting ring counterclockwise 
(looking from rear of vehicle) to move the release bearing toward the 
flywheel, or clockwise to move the release bearing away from the flywheel. 
Rotation or movement of one lug position will move the release bearing 
approximately 0.51 mm (0.020 inch). 

Remove the clutch pedal block to engage the clutch. 

Recheck the clearance as outlined in Step 2. Readjust if necessary. 
Check clutch pedal free travel (inches). If it is not within specification, 
then a linkage adjustment should be made. Refer to Section 08-02 . 

Install the inspection cover on the clutch housing.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Control System, Mechanical (All Except UPS Stripped Chassis)

The mechanical clutch linkage is a system of leverage necessary to 
multiply the relatively small force at the clutch pedal to a larger force at 
the clutch pressure plate fingers.

================================================================================
PAGE 3177
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 08-02: Clutch Controls

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Control System, Hydraulic (UPS Stripped Chassis)

The hydraulic clutch control system is comprised of the clutch pedal, 
the clutch master cylinder, a hydraulic line and the clutch slave cylinder.

================================================================================
PAGE 3178
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 08-02: Clutch Controls

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Pedal

The clutch is actuated (disengaged) by pressing the clutch pedal which 
is connected to the clutch master cylinder by means of a push rod. The clutch 
pedal range of motion is controlled by stops installed in the cab bulkhead.

================================================================================
PAGE 3179
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 08-02: Clutch Controls

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Master Cylinder

The clutch master cylinder (UPS stripped chassis only) is located 
behind the hood adjacent to the foot brake control valve.

The clutch master cylinder reservoir supplies the hydraulic fluid for 
the system. The fluid from the reservoir is fed to the area in front of the 
piston in the cylinder housing through the supply orifice. At rest (clutch 
engaged) position there is no pressure in the clutch master cylinder. 

When the clutch pedal is depressed, the piston is forced forward by the 
push rod that is attached to the clutch pedal. As the piston moves forward, 
the seal blocks the supply orifice and the hydraulic force is transmitted 
through the fluid line to actuate the slave cylinder and move the clutch 
release lever.

When the clutch pedal is released, the clutch spring forces the piston 
back to the rest position. Because fluid return is slower than piston return, 
a mild vacuum is formed which forces the fluid that is behind the piston to 
bend the lip of the seal away from the cylinder wall and enter the chamber in 
front of the piston. This flow of liquid prevents the possible entry of air. 
The supply orifice from the reservoir keeps the cylinder filled at all times.

The fluid reservoir is mounted to the clutch master cylinder housing. 
It is made of translucent plastic that permits instant fluid level checking 
without removing the filler cap.

================================================================================
PAGE 3180
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 08-02: Clutch Controls

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Slave Cylinder

The slave cylinder (UPS stripped chassis only) is installed on the 
clutch housing with a mounting bracket.

The slave cylinder is actuated by hydraulic force transmitted from the 
clutch master cylinder through the fluid line. The hydraulic pressure drives 
the piston and push rod forward, actuating the clutch release mechanism.

The clutch levers return the piston to the rest position after the 
clutch pedal is released. The springs inside the slave cylinder preload the 
release bearing, making sure the slave cylinder adjusts automatically.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Pedal and Support

 Removal 

For UPS stripped chassis only, remove the two nuts that retain the 
clutch master cylinder to the passenger compartment bulkhead. Secure the 
cylinder so that the hydraulic line remains attached and the cylinder cannot 
empty.

For UPS stripped chassis only, remove retaining ring from master 
cylinder push rod mounting pin. Remove push rod.

For UPS stripped chassis only, lift the clutch pedal return spring away 
from the clutch pedal, while holding the pedal upward. Push the spring hook 
away from the pedal, and slowly release the spring leg.

For all except UPS stripped chassis, remove retainer and vertical rod 
(adjusting rod) from clutch pedal.

Remove retaining spring and wavy spring washer from the clutch side of 
the brake/clutch shaft and slide the shaft toward the brake pedal to detach 
the clutch pedal from the bracket. For UPS stripped chassis only, the return 
spring and spacer can now be removed by sliding the shaft further outward, and 
pulling the return spring hook from slot in the pedal support bracket.

 Installation 

Apply a light film of Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the clutch and brake 
pedal bushings.

Install the wavy spring washer and retaining spring onto one end of the 
shaft. Insert the end of the shaft into the brake pedal side of the support 
bracket. Align the brake pedal and push the shaft through its bushings, and 
the center support bracket.

Align return spring (UPS stripped chassis only) and spacer and push the 
shaft through. Align clutch pedal and it's bushings, push the shaft through 
bushings and clutch pedal mount, and out the other end of the bracket. Slide 
on a wavy spring washer and insert a retaining spring.

For UPS stripped chassis only, insert master cylinder rod into master 
cylinder and over retaining pin on the clutch pedal. Slide on the retaining 
ring.

For UPS stripped chassis only, hook the clutch pedal return spring into 
bracket and rotate spring to install longer leg around pedal.

For UPS stripped chassis only, secure clutch master cylinder onto 
passenger compartment bulkhead. Check fluid level in reservoir and fill with 
Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 
fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Master Cylinder and Reservoir (UPS Stripped Chassis)

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

 CAUTION: Brake fluid is harmful to painted and plastic surfaces. If brake fluid 
is spilled onto a painted or plastic surface, immediately wash it with water. 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Cap the fluid line to avoid possible fluid contamination. 

Disconnect the fluid line. 

Drain fluid into a suitable container. Pump clutch pedal until all 
fluid is drained from the clutch master cylinder.

Remove the two nuts that retain the clutch master cylinder to the 
bulkhead.

 CAUTION: Use care not to spill any fluid that may remain in the cylinder or 
reservoir. 

Withdraw the clutch master cylinder from the vehicle. 

 Installation 

Position the clutch master cylinder on the bulkhead studs. Make sure 
that the clutch pedal push rod seats in the recessed portion of the cylinder 
piston. Install lock nuts and tighten to 25-28 Nm (18-20 lb-ft).

Install fluid line in clutch master cylinder and tighten to 17-19 
Nm (12-14 lb-ft).

Bleed the system. Refer to Clutch Hydraulic System Bleeding in the 
Adjustments portion of this section.

[FIGURE: C11523A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Hydraulic Line (UPS Stripped Chassis)

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

 CAUTION: Brake fluid is harmful to painted and plastic surfaces. If brake fluid 
is spilled onto a painted or plastic surface, immediately wash it with water. 

 CAUTION: Hydraulic line should always be replaced if inspection reveals cracks 
or other damage. 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Plug the fluid ports to avoid possible contamination and fluid loss. 

Disconnect the line at the clutch master cylinder and slave cylinder.

 CAUTION: Use care not to kink, bend or break any other lines or harnesses. 

Remove side rail tie straps and hydraulic line. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Use care not to kink, break or bend any of the lines or harnesses. 

Position and secure the new fluid line to the side rail with tie straps. 

Install fluid line ends into their respective fluid ports and tighten 
to 17-19 Nm (12-14 lb-ft).

Bleed the system. Refer to Clutch Hydraulic System Bleeding in the 
Adjustments portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Slave Cylinder (UPS Stripped Chassis)

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

 CAUTION: Brake fluid is harmful to painted and plastic surfaces. If brake fluid 
is spilled onto a painted or plastic surface, immediately wash it with water. 

 Removal 

Remove retainer nut from the push rod.

Disconnect and plug fluid line. 

Remove cylinder to bracket retaining nuts.

Remove cylinder from transmission bracket and separate push rod from 
clutch release lever.

Pump push rod several times to drain fluid from cylinder into a 
suitable container.

Plug cylinder port.

 Installation 

Connect push rod to clutch release lever and position cylinder on 
transmission mounting bracket. Install and tighten retaining nuts.

Install push rod retaining nut.

Install fluid line connection in cylinder and tighten to 17-19 
Nm (12-14 lb-ft).

Bleed system. Refer to Clutch Hydraulic System Bleeding in the 
Adjustments portion of this section.

Clutch Master Cylinder

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: Use brass pads to prevent damage.

Remove reservoir cotter pin and clevis.

Remove reservoir and connection between reservoir and cylinder.

Remove reservoir cover and filter.

Remove dust boot retaining ring and then remove dust boot.

Remove cylinder piston retaining ring and then remove piston, seal and 
return spring.

 Assembly 

Clean and lubricate all internal cylinder parts in clean hydraulic 
fluid and assemble in reverse order of disassembly.

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch Pedal

 Height 

Clutch pedal height is controlled by the upper pedal stop which is 
factory-installed and not adjustable.

 Total Travel 

Total travel of the clutch pedal is limited by the upper and lower 
stops which are factory-installed and cannot be adjusted.

 Free Play 

Clutch pedal free play is set by adjusting the clutch trim rod with the 
turnbuckle so the free play is 28-38 mm (1.1-1.5 inches) for 7.0L, B5.9 or 
C8.3 engines.

Measure free play using the following procedure:

 NOTE: The practice of using a ruler to measure free play from the pedal 
straight down to the floorboard is not acceptable. This method does not take 
the arc of pedal travel into account and measures only the straight line 
distance and will always read less than the actual free play distance.

Use a suitable measuring tape and hook the end of the tape to the 
middle of the clutch pedal as shown in the following illustration. Pull the 
tape case back to the middle of the driver seat so that it can be easily held 
in one hand and the initial measurement read.

[FIGURE: DC0041A.gif]

Use the other hand to push on the clutch pedal (following the pedal 
arc) using no more than three pounds of force, and read the distance of free 
play travel on the measuring tape. The difference between the initial and 
final measurement reading is the pedal free play, which should be 27.9-38.1 mm 
(1.1-1.5 inch).

If free play travel is not within specifications, refer to the 
following procedure for linkage adjustment.

================================================================================
PAGE 3193
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 08-02: Clutch Controls

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch Linkage

 NOTE: Clutch facing wear is indicated by loss of clutch pedal free travel. 
The vertical rod assembly adjustment, after being initially set, should not be 
used to compensate for facing wear.

Install rod assembly and retainer spring.

Set clutch adjustment (B5.9 or C8.3). Refer to Section 08-00 .

Adjust vertical rod assembly turnbuckle to provide a clutch pedal free 
travel of 27.9-38.1 mm (1.1-1.5 inch). Tighten turnbuckle jam nuts and check 
that clutch pedal free travel is correct. Readjust if necessary.

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch Hydraulic System Bleeding

The hydraulic clutch uses brake fluid in its hydraulic function. Only 
Ford High Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 
Fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A should be added or used in this 
system.

System bleeding is performed to purge any air that may be in the 
hydraulic system and also to flush the system as it eliminates old fluid.

System bleeding should be carried out as described below whenever 
service is performed which requires disconnecting any hydraulic system part or 
if the clutch pedal feels spongy.

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

 CAUTION: Brake fluid is harmful to painted and plastic surfaces. If brake fluid 
is spilled onto a painted or plastic surface, immediately wash it with water. 

Remove clutch master cylinder reservoir filler cap.

Fill fluid reservoir to specified level.

Remove slave cylinder bleeder dust cover and install a hose over the 
bleeder nipple. Place the other end of the hose in an appropriate container. 
Position the container above the bleeder valve level.

Slowly depress the clutch pedal five times. On the fifth pump, hold the 
pedal to the floor.

With the pedal applied, loosen the bleeder valve to let the fluid flow 
into the container.

 NOTE: Check if fluid flowing into container contains air bubbles (aeration). 
If fluid does show signs of aeration, repeat steps 4 and 5 until fluid runs 
clear with no sign of bubbles.

Close bleeder valve and then release clutch pedal.

 CAUTION: Do not overtighten. 

Tighten bleeder valve to 10-15 Nm (7-11 lb-ft). Remove hose and 
install bleeder dust cover.

Check reservoir fluid level. Fill to specified level with Ford High 
Performance DOT 3 Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AA or equivalent DOT 3 fluid meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A. Do not overfill.

ADJUSTMENTS

Fluid Level

The clutch (reservoir) system works in reverse to a brake system. As 
the clutch wears, the master cylinder reservoir fills up rather than goes 
down. The master cylinder needs to be filled to the MIN. level for a new 
clutch or maintained between the MIN. and MAX. levels.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Exhaust Brake

An exhaust brake is an auxiliary braking system that attaches to the 
engine exhaust system on a vehicle equipped with a diesel engine. The exhaust 
brake functions by partially closing off the turbocharger-to-muffler inlet 
pipe, creating an increase in exhaust back pressure.

During vehicle deceleration the engine must turn against the back 
pressure. This creates a braking effect on the driving wheels. The effect of 
the exhaust brake is to make the engine act as a compressor.

The exhaust brake system is composed of the following components:

dash-mounted control switch

dash-mounted indicator light

idle validation switch

clutch switch

pneumatic solenoid control valve

actuating cylinder

exhaust brake body

The following guidelines must be followed when installing an exhaust 
brake on Cummins diesel engines or the warranty will be voided.

Maximum allowable exhaust back pressure is 310 kPa (45 psi) at 10 
percent above engine rated speed.

Maximum allowable exhaust back pressure while exhaust brake is engaged 
is as follows:

 MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE EXHAUST BACK PRESSURE

Engine

rpm

Maximum Pressure

B5.9

2750

240 kPa (35 psi)

C8.3

2530

240 kPa (35 psi)

The effect of an exhaust brake is not felt as a normal braking force as 
with service brakes, but is more of a gradual decelerating effect, as if the 
service brakes were applied lightly.

The exhaust brake is used to aid the engine and the service brakes in 
slowing the vehicle, reducing service brake wear.

 Exhaust Brake

Elbow

 CAUTION: Never operate the exhaust brake if engine condition is in doubt. Do not 
operate the vehicle if the exhaust brake is stuck in the ON position or engine 
damage can result. 

With the dash-mounted switch on, accelerator pedal released and the 
clutch pedal in the UP (clutch engaged) position, the exhaust brake will be 
activated. The accelerator and clutch switches are closed, and current is 
applied to the control valve. The control valve allows system air pressure to 
be applied to the actuating cylinder, which shifts the brake body butterfly 
valve to the closed position.

When the accelerator or clutch pedal is pressed, the switch will open 
and interrupt current to the control valve. The control valve will stop air 
pressure from going to the actuating cylinder, and will exhaust existing air 
from the cylinder. The return spring in the actuating cylinder will then open 
the exhaust brake butterfly valve.

When the exhaust brake switch is in the ON position, the exhaust brake 
unit will operate whenever the following conditions are met:

The clutch pedal must be in the UP (clutch engaged) position.

The accelerator pedal must be in the idle position.

The vehicle air supply must be up to operating pressure.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Exhaust System

 Inspection and Verification 

Exhaust system performance complaints such as excessive back pressure 
are usually noticeable by their effect on engine performance.

Other inoperative components can have similar effects on engine 
performance and be characterized by the same symptoms or complaints. Refer to 
the engine diagnosis and service procedures in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manualwhen attempting to diagnose engine performance concerns.

For general exhaust system complaints refer to the symptom chart in 
this section.

 Exhaust Leakage or Noise 

Verify customer concern. Inspect entire exhaust system for evidence of 
leakage or damage. Inspect all pipe joints and clamp locations thoroughly. 
Attach a compressed air source to the exhaust outlet pipe. Pressurize exhaust 
system (not to exceed 138 kPa [20 psi]), apply soapy water to all pipe 
joints, clamp locations and any suspected leak points. Replace any damaged or 
deteriorated exhaust system components.

 Exhaust Brake Test 

With the accelerator and clutch pedals released and the transmission in 
gear from a speed of 32-48 km/h (20-30 mph), check for the following conditions:

Road speed should decrease unless descending a steep grade or carrying 
a heavy load.

Slight change in the sound of the engine when the exhaust brake is in 
use.

When descending a grade, the vehicle speed increases slightly if the 
exhaust brake switch is turned to the off position.

Engine exhaust smoke appears normal.

When the accelerator is applied again, the exhaust brake is deactivated 
and the following conditions should exist:

Throttle response is normal.

There is a quick hissing noise from the exhaust brake control valve as 
it releases air pressure.

 Exhaust Brake, Preliminary Inspection 

 CAUTION: Never operate the exhaust brake if engine condition is in doubt. Do not 
operate the vehicle if the exhaust brake is stuck in the ON position or engine 
damage can result. 

Before testing the operation of the exhaust brake:

inspect the exhaust system for leaks.

the engine must be fully warmed up.

the vehicle air system must be up to full operating pressure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Exhaust Brake Assembly

 Removal 

Disconnect the air line from actuating cylinder.

Loosen the two clamps retaining the exhaust brake body to the inlet and 
outlet pipes. Slide the clamps onto the adjoining pipes.

Remove the exhaust brake.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The exhaust brake body must be installed in a specific direction. Make 
sure the arrow on the brake body is pointing in the direction of exhaust flow. 

Position the exhaust brake assembly to the inlet and outlet pipes.

 NOTE: Make sure the slots in the muffler inlet pipe are not directly in line 
with the clamp bolts. Offset the slots to the clamp bolt to ensure there are 
no leaks.

Install the muffler clamp at the pipe inlet.

Connect the air line to the cylinder.

Start the vehicle and check for exhaust leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Actuating Cylinder

 Removal 

Disconnect the air line from the actuating cylinder.

Using a suitable drift, tap the roll pin from the cylinder mounting 
bracket pivot pin bushing. Remove the bushing from the pivot pin.

[FIGURE: U21651A.gif]

Tap the roll pin from the exhaust valve lever pin bushing. Remove the 
bushing from the pin.

 CAUTION: Actuating cylinder is under spring pressure. Use care when removing. 

Remove the actuating cylinder from the mounting bracket.

 Installation 

Position the actuating cylinder on the mounting bracket pivot pin and 
on the exhaust valve lever pin.

Position the bushings on the two pins, lining up the roll pin holes.

Tap the roll pins through the bushings and pins.

Connect the air line.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Actuating Cylinder

 Disassembly 

Mount the air supply end of the cylinder in a vise, using care to 
prevent cylinder damage.

Measure and record the assembled length of the cylinder.

Loosen the jam nut and remove the nut and clevis from the end of the 
cylinder push rod.

Using a pair of slip joint pliers, loosen the center portion of the 
cylinder from the air supply end of the cylinder.

Remove the cylinder from the vise and remove the air supply end of the 
cylinder from the end of the cylinder.

Remove the push rods, springs, spring retainer and push rod locator 
from the cylinder. Remove the O-ring from the air supply end of the cylinder.

 Assembly 

Lubricate seals and O-rings with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A.

Install the push rod, springs, spring retainer and push rod locator in 
the cylinder. Install the O-ring in the air supply end of the cylinder.

Install the air supply end of the cylinder on the cylinder and push rod 
assembly.

 CAUTION: Use care not to overtighten the cylinder and compress the O-ring. 

Position the cylinder in a vise, and tighten the cylinder to the 
cylinder air supply end until it contacts the O-ring. Then tighten the 
cylinder slightly more.

Install the jam nut on the push rod and install the clevis on the push 
rod. Position the clevis and push rod so that the length of the assembled 
actuating cylinder and push rod equals the dimension recorded in Step 2 of the 
disassembly procedure. Tighten the jam nut against the clevis.

Exhaust Brake

exhaust manifold (part of engine)

muffler

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Exhaust System

 Inspection and Verification 

Exhaust system performance complaints such as excessive back pressure 
are usually noticeable by their effect on engine performance. Other worn or 
damaged components can have the same effect on engine performance and be 
characterized by the same symptoms or complaints. For additional information, 
refer to the appropriate engine manufacturer's service literature when 
attempting to diagnose engine performance concerns.

 Exhaust Leakage or Noise 

Noise can be caused by exhaust leaks. Inspect the exhaust system for:

holes, cracks or gaps

loose or missing clamps

black soot residue (indicates leakage) on the exhaust pipes or the 
muffler

1999 F and B-Series

Section 09-00A: Exhaust System, Cummins B5.9 Encore Diesel Engine

1999 F800 Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests

 Exhaust Back Pressure Test — Full Load 

 NOTE: The chassis dynamometer or "full load" test is the preferred method for 
testing exhaust back pressure; however if a chassis dynamometer is not 
available, the "no load" test is the only other authorized method for the 
exhaust back pressure test.

 NOTE: Follow the setup procedures supplied by the dynamometer manufacturer.

Install the pressure gauge onto the test port. The test port is located 
on the muffler inlet pipe either near the turbocharger or the muffler assembly.

Start and run the engine until the temperature gauge indicates normal 
operating temperature.

Select a transmission gear range where acceleration to 
wide-open-throttle (WOT) can be accomplished safely.

Accelerate to WOT and peak engine power.

When the engine reaches maximum RPM and load, record the maximum 
exhaust back pressure reading.

The reading should be less than 20 kPa (6 in-Hg). If the reading is 
higher than the specification, replace the muffler assembly.

If the reading does not exceed the specification, then the muffler 
assembly is not plugged. For additional information, refer to the appropriate 
engine manufacturer's service literature for engine related components.

 Exhaust Back Pressure Test — No Load 

 CAUTION: Make sure the vehicle parking brake is set, the wheels are blocked, the 
transmission is in NEUTRAL and the area around the vehicle is clear before 
performing this test. 

Install the pressure gauge onto the pressure test port.

Start and run the engine until the temperature gauge indicates normal 
operating temperature.

 NOTE: Engine rpm will exceed the rated rpm range by 10 to 17 percent under 
wide-open-throttle no load conditions. This is normal and no cause for concern.

 NOTE: If the engine is unable to reach maximum rpm rating plus 10 percent, it 
will first be necessary to repair this concern before the back pressure test 
can be performed.

Accelerate to wide-open-throttle (WOT). Record the maximum engine rpm 
and the maximum exhaust back pressure reading.

The maximum back pressure reading under a no load condition is 10.2 kPa 
(3 in-Hg).

If the reading exceeds the specification, replace the muffler assembly.

If the reading does not exceed the specification, then the muffler 
assembly is not plugged. For additional information, refer to the appropriate 
engine manufacturer's service literature for engine related components.

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Injected Engines, Gasoline

 WARNING: TANK-TO-INJECTOR FUEL INJECTION SUPPLY MANIFOLD REMAINS UNDER HIGH 
PRESSURE AFTER THE SYSTEM IS SHUT OFF. DEPRESSURIZE THE FUEL INJECTION SUPPLY 
MANIFOLD AT THE SCHRADER VALVE LOCATED ON THE ENGINE FUEL INJECTION SUPPLY 
MANIFOLD BEFORE DISCONNECTING ANY FUEL TUBE. DISCONNECTING FUEL TUBES WITHOUT 
DEPRESSURIZING THE SYSTEM AS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION CAN RESULT IN INJURY 
FROM FUEL BEING SPRAYED UNDER PRESSURE. ALSO, FUEL SPRAYED UNDER PRESSURE IS 
AN OBVIOUS FIRE HAZARD. 

F-Series gasoline-powered vehicles are equipped with multiport fuel 
injection (MFI) engines. Separate electronically controlled fuel injectors are 
mounted in the intake manifold on the runner for each cylinder.

Each fuel injector is mounted so that it sprays fuel into the cylinder 
head intake port of its cylinder. The fuel injectors are supplied fuel under 
high pressure through an engine-mounted fuel injection supply manifold which 
also has a fuel pressure regulator. The fuel pressure regulator controls the 
pressure of fuel going into the fuel injectors and returns excess fuel to the 
fuel tanks.

On all gasoline-powered vehicles, a fuel pump located in a fuel 
delivery module (FDM) in the fuel tank supplies fuel under high pressure to 
the fuel injection supply manifold.

All gasoline-powered vehicles have an in-line fuel filter mounted on 
the frame rail under the vehicle.

================================================================================
PAGE 3214
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 10-01A: Fuel Tank, Filters, Tubes and Fuel Pump, LPG and Gasoline Engines

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank and Fuel Tank Filler Pipe

All gasoline-powered vehicles are equipped with a restricted opening on 
the gasoline fuel tank filler pipes that allows only a non-leaded fuel nozzle 
to be inserted.

The fuel tank filler pipe openings for the fuel tanks on vehicles with 
multiport fuel injection (MFI) engines have been made smaller to prevent 
accidental filling with other than unleaded fuel. Gasoline pumps in the United 
States and Canada dispensing unleaded fuel are equipped with nozzles to 
accommodate the smaller filler opening on the fuel tank filler pipe.

The restrictor in the fuel tank filler pipe consists of a narrow 
opening in the fuel tank filler pipe covered by a spring steel trap door. The 
smaller non-leaded fuel nozzle will fit through the narrow opening and push 
the trap door aside, allowing normal filling. Leaded fuel nozzles will not fit 
through the narrow opening. The trap door being closed causes a fuel backup 
and automatic nozzle shutoff.

The restricted fuel tank filler pipe is manufactured as an assembly, 
and must be serviced by removal and replacement with a new part. Fuel tank 
filler pipes are integral to the fuel tank and are not to be modified in any 
way.

The fill limiting system is designed to permit an approximate 10-12 
percent tank volume air space which provides for thermal expansion of fuel as 
well as being an aid to the in-tank vapor vent system.

Expansion of fuel due to temperature increases or overfilling ("topping 
off") causes fuel overflow at the fuel tank filler cap when the vehicle is 
standing or the fuel tank filler cap is removed. To minimize this condition, 
it is recommended that the amount of fuel put in the fuel tank when filling be 
limited to the automatic pump shutoff. If vehicle has two fuel tanks, use fuel 
from both fuel tanks after fill-up to reduce fuel levels evenly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Filter, In-Line

 NOTE: Change the gasoline fuel filter at 24,000 km (15,000 miles) or 15-month 
intervals, and each time a fuel tank sending unit and pump is replaced. When 
the fuel filter needs to be replaced, proceed to Fuel Filter, In-Line, in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

The in-line fuel filter provides filtration to protect the small 
metering orifices of the fuel injector nozzles. The fuel filter assembly is 
located on the right frame rail on gasoline powered vehicles.

If the fuel tank sending unit and pump is replaced, or the fuel system 
is contaminated with particles, replace the fuel filter. If contamination of 
fuel is suspected, refill tank with clean fuel, not fuel from fuel tanks.

Fuel Filter, In-Tank

An in-tank fuel filter is located on the inlet of the venturi pump. The

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tubes

 WARNING: TANK-TO-INJECTOR FUEL TUBES ON GASOLINE-POWERED VEHICLES WILL REMAIN 
UNDER HIGH PRESSURE AFTER THE SYSTEM IS SHUT OFF. DEPRESSURIZE THE FUEL TUBE 
SYSTEM AT THE SCHRADER VALVE LOCATED ON THE ENGINE FUEL RAIL BEFORE 
DISCONNECTING ANY FUEL TUBES. DISCONNECTING FUEL TUBES WITHOUT DEPRESSURIZING 
THE SYSTEM AS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION CAN RESULT IN INJURY FROM FUEL BEING 
SPRAYED UNDER PRESSURE. ALSO, FUEL SPRAYED UNDER PRESSURE IS AN OBVIOUS FIRE 
HAZARD. 

 CAUTION: Only Ford Motor Company approved fuel tubes and O-rings should be used 
for service or replacement because substitute materials can leak or 
deteriorate rapidly from contact with fuel. Never substitute hose clamps for 
approved fittings on nylon fuel tubes as they can pull loose because of the 
fuel pressure. 

Disconnect vehicle battery.

Keep all flame, burning tobacco products, and sparks from grinders and 
other power tools away from vehicle when servicing fuel system.

Keep the front end of the vehicle higher than the rear when servicing 
fuel tubes. If the fuel tubes are disconnected with the front of the vehicle 
lower than the rear, fuel can syphon out through the tubes.

Steel fuel lines and Teflon® fuel tubes with braided covering 
are used on MFI vehicles. Two types of quick-connect couplings are used on MFI 
vehicles. Some tubes are part of an organizer assembly.

The two types of quick-connect couplings are called push connect 
fittings and metal spring lock couplings.

 Spring Lock Coupling 

Spring lock couplings have a bead formed in one tube which is retained 
by a garter spring inside a cage on the other tube. Sealing is by O-rings on 
the cage side. These couplings are connected by pushing the two sides together 
until the garter spring clicks. They are disconnected by the use of special 
tools. For connecting and disconnecting instructions, refer to Spring Lock 
Coupling, 7.0L MFI Gasoline Engines in the Removal and Installation portion of 
this section. This type of connector is used for fuel tube-to-engine fuel 
manifold connections and sometimes for fuel filter connections.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Pump, Electric

The electric fuel delivery system used on the 7.0L multiport fuel 
injection (MFI) gasoline engine consists of a fuel delivery module (FDM) and 
sending unit. The fuel delivery module includes a high pressure fuel pump, 
venturi jet pump, supply check valve and a shuttle selector valve located 
internally to a reservoir mounted from the fuel tank sender flange.

The following provides a brief description and function of each of the 
FDM internal components.

The high pressure fuel pump is located inside the module.

The supply check valve, which is normally closed, opens when the outlet 
pressure from the energized pump exceeds the opposing check valve spring 
force. When the pump is de-energized (i.e., engine is shut off), the supply 
check valve closes to maintain pump prime and fuel supply tube pressure.

A portion of the high pressure flow from the pump is diverted to 
operate the venturi jet pump. The venturi pump draws fuel from the tank into 
the fuel delivery module reservoir to augment the engine return flow. This 
process ensures an adequate fuel supply to the pump during extreme vehicle 
maneuvers and steep vehicle attitudes with low-tank fill levels.

The inlet of the venturi pump has a nylon filter on it to prevent dirt 
and other particulate matter from entering the system. Water in the fuel tank 
can pass through the filter without restriction.

The in-tank mounted fuel delivery module containing the fuel pump is

pressure relief valve to provide overpressure protection in the event the fuel 
flow becomes restricted. Overpressure is restricted to 850 kPa (123 psi) and 
reduced fuel flow will result. The system pressure is controlled by a fuel 
pressure regulator on the engine.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Inertia Fuel Shutoff Switch (IFS)

 WARNING: IF YOU SEE OR SMELL GASOLINE AT ANY TIME OTHER THAN DURING FUELING, DO 
NOT RESET THE INERTIA FUEL SHUTOFF SWITCH. 

 CAUTION: Do not reset the inertia fuel shutoff switch until the complete fuel 
system has been inspected for leaks. 

In the event of a collision, the electrical contacts in the inertia 
fuel shutoff switch open and the fuel pump automatically shuts off. The fuel 
pump will shut off even if the engine does not stop running. The engine, 
however, will stop a few seconds after the fuel pump stops. It is not possible 
to restart the engine until the inertia fuel shutoff switch is manually reset.

To reset the inertia fuel shutoff switch, depress the button on top of 
the inertia fuel shutoff switch.

The inertia fuel shutoff switch is located on the cowl next to the 
engine control module (ECM), just above the toe board. It may be necessary to 
pull back the floor mat to gain access to it.

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG)

Liquified petroleum gas (LPG) is an engine fuel which is very similar 
to gasoline. Both fuels are a product of crude oil. They differ in that LPG is 
more volatile. It becomes a vapor at ordinary room temperatures. When LPG is 
used in an internal combustion engine, it is converted from a liquid in the 
fuel tank to a vaporous gas before the combustion chamber.

Liquified petroleum gas flows from the fuel tank through a hydrostatic 
relief valve, vacuum-activated Fuelock® and filter, to the converter. 
In the converter the liquid becomes a vapor which flows to the carburetor 
where it is mixed with air in the proper proportions for maximum engine 
performance.

 WARNING: DO NOT PARK OR SERVICE A LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED VEHICLE 
NEAR ANY SOURCE OF FIRE, SUCH AS OPEN FLAME, CIGARETTES OR SMOKING MATERIALS, 
SPARKS, EXCESSIVE HEAT, WELDING OR BODY GRINDING. AVOID PLACING THE VEHICLE 
NEAR ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT THAT DISCHARGES SPARKS THROUGH NORMAL OPERATION, FOR 
EXAMPLE, MOTORS, ELECTRICAL SWITCHES AND RADIO TRANSMISSION EQUIPMENT. AVOID 
STORING OR SERVICING THE VEHICLE OVER SEWER DRAINS, LUBRICATION PITS, SUBFLOOR 
LEVEL ROOMS OR OTHER LOW-LYING AREAS. IF ANY SOURCE OF FIRE OR IGNITION 
CONTACTS LPG VAPOR, A FIRE CAN RESULT. 

 WARNING: DO NOT NEEDLESSLY RELEASE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL DURING 
SERVICE. DO NOT OPEN THE STOP-FILL VALVE WHILE A VEHICLE IS INSIDE A BUILDING. 
WHEN SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM, CLOSE THE FUEL TANK SHUTOFF VALVE(S) AND RUN 
THE ENGINE OUT OF FUEL BEFORE DISCONNECTING FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENTS. IF THE 
FUEL TANK IS BEING SERVICED, HAVE THE FUEL EVACUATED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL AT A 
LOCAL LPG FUEL STATION. LPG FUEL VAPORIZES (AT NORMAL BAROMETRIC PRESSURE) AT 
TEMPERATURES ABOVE -42°C (-44°F), AND CAN EXPAND TO APPROXIMATELY 270 
TIMES ITS VOLUME AS A LIQUID. UNNECESSARY VENTING OF LPG FUEL CAN CREATE FIRES 
AND HEALTH HAZARDS WHICH CAN LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY OR ILLNESS. 

 WARNING: LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL TANKS SHOULD BE DRAINED BY TRAINED 
PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO USE SHOP AIR PRESSURE TO FORCE LPG FUEL FROM 
THE TANKS. NORMAL FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1724 KPA (250 PSI) AT 
ROOM TEMPERATURE. CONNECTING A SHOP AIR HOSE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM CAN RESULT IN 
FUEL FLOWING BACK INTO THE SERVICE AIR SYSTEM, AND CAN RESULT IN FIRE OR 
EXPLOSION. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE PAINT-DRYING OVENS FOR LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED 
VEHICLES. THE HEAT OF PAINT-DRYING OVENS WILL INCREASE PRESSURE IN THE FUEL 
TANKS. THIS CAN CAUSE VENTING OF THE LPG FUEL VAPOR INTO THE OVEN, RESULTING 
IN FIRE FROM HEAT OR SPARK IN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. IF LPG FUEL IS CONFINED IN 
AN OVEN, THERE IS ALSO THE RISK OF EXPLOSION IF THE FUEL IS IGNITED. WHEN 
REFINISHING THE BODY PANELS OF LPG-FUELED VEHICLES, SPOT PAINT THE AFFECTED 
AREA USING SPOT DRYING METHODS. 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY THE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL SYSTEM 
CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS. DO NOT REPLACE COMPONENTS WITH PARTS THAT DO NOT 
MEET FORD SPECIFICATIONS. FORD SPECIFIED PARTS ARE AVAILABLE AT AUTHORIZED 
FORD DEALERS. THE LPG FUEL STORAGE SYSTEM MUST CONFORM TO NATIONAL FIRE 
PROTECTION ASSOCIATION STANDARD #58, AND SIMILAR CANADIAN GAS ASSOCIATION 
STANDARDS. THESE STANDARDS DEFINE THE SPECIALLY APPROVED MATERIALS, COMPONENT 
CONSTRUCTION AND SYSTEM INSTALLATION ON ALL VEHICLES, WHICH IS PRECISELY 
CALIBRATED FOR EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE USE OF DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS 
CAN PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT CAN RESULT IN FIRE HAZARD OR 
OTHERWISE LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: AVOID INHALING LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) OR OCCUPYING CONFINED 
AREAS CONTAINING LPG. LPG IS HEAVIER THAN AIR. THE HEAVIER GAS CAN DISPLACE OR 
"PUSH" FRESH AIR OUT OF AN AREA. IN LARGE QUANTITIES LPG CAN DISPLACE ENOUGH 
OXYGEN TO MAKE THE SURROUNDING AIR UNFIT TO BREATHE, CAUSING HEADACHES, 
DIZZINESS AND POSSIBLE SUFFOCATION DURING PROLONGED EXPOSURE.

IN THE EVENT OF EXPOSURE TO LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG), MOVE THE 
VICTIM IMMEDIATELY TO FRESH AIR AND CONTACT A PHYSICIAN OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY 
PERSONNEL FOR ARTIFICIAL RESPIRATION OR OTHER REQUIRED TREATMENT. 

 WARNING: IF AIR IN A CONFINED AREA, SUCH AS A LUBRICATION PIT, HAS BEEN FOULED 
WITH LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG), THE AREA MUST BE CHECKED FOR ADEQUATE 
OXYGEN LEVELS BY LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL BEFORE BEING USED, TO AVOID 
PERSONAL INJURY OR SUFFOCATION.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Delivery System, 7.0L LPG Engine

The Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) fuel delivery system consists of a 
fuel tank assembly, hose assemblies, relief valve and a Fuelock® 
assembly.

Liquid fuel is supplied to the 7.0L LPG converter assembly under 
pressure from the fuel tanks. It is converted to a vaporous gas at the 
converter, mixed with air and supplied to the engine.

LPG fuel pressure is regulated by a pressure regulator located behind 
the throttle body assembly. 

The LPG fuel tank assembly consists of a manual shutoff valve, 
mechanical gauge, pressure relief valve, excess flow valve, fill valve and an 
80% stop-fill valve. A hydrostatic relief valve is connected in-line between 
the shutoff valve and the Fuelock® assembly. The following provides a 
brief description of the tank and fuel tube component functions.

 Fill valve — is a one-way liquid fuel inlet.

 80% stop-fill valve — vents vapor during 
filling and indicates the 80% liquid fill level (technically referred to as 
"Fixed Liquid Level Gauge").

 Pressure relief valve — vents fuel tank 
pressure when ambient conditions cause pressure increase.

 Manual shutoff valve — stops fuel flow 
during service and storage.

 Excess flow valve — stops fuel flow when 
rate exceeds specification. Resets when shutoff valve is closed. (Located 
inside tank.)

 Hydrostatic relief valve — releases liquid 
fuel pressure in line between a closed fuel lock and closed tank shutoff valve 
when high temperature causes pressure buildup. The valve is not mounted on the 
tank. It is threaded into the bottom of the frame rail T fitting.

 Fuel gauge sending unit — is a mechanical 
float and arm in the tank that operates a gauge on the fuel tank. (No fuel 
gauge sending unit is supplied with the factory installed temporary tank.)

 Fuelock® — is a vacuum-actuated 
valve which will allow fuel flow to the engine-mounted converter/regulator 
when the engine is cranking or running. The fuel flowing through the 
Fuelock® passes through a fine mesh filter and screen.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Filling

The fuel tank filler pipe openings for the fuel tanks on trucks with 
multiport fuel injection (MFI) gasoline-powered engines have been made smaller 
to prevent accidental filling with other than unleaded fuel. Gasoline pumps in 
the United States and Canada dispensing unleaded fuel are equipped with 
nozzles to accommodate the smaller filler opening on the filler neck.

 Fuel Tank Draining and Filling, LPG 

 WARNING: EVACUATE THE FUEL TANK AT A CERTIFIED LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) 
FILLING STATION BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO REMOVE, INSTALL OR DISCONNECT THE LPG 
TANK. FUEL IS UNDER PRESSURE IN THE TANK. ALSO, LPG EVAPORATES AT A LOW 
TEMPERATURE. IF LINES ARE DISCONNECTED, FITTINGS REMOVED OR THE TANK DAMAGED 
WITHOUT BEING PROPERLY DRAINED, FUEL CAN RUSH OUT AND VAPORIZE QUICKLY, 
CREATING A FIRE OR EXPLOSION HAZARD. 

Evacuate the fuel tank at a local LPG fuel station.

Run the engine until the fuel tank is empty.

Place the selector in neutral or the shift lever in reverse (manual 
transmission). Set the parking brake. Block the rear wheels and connect a 
ground strap to the body.

Extinguish all smoking materials and open flames.

 WARNING: DO NOT OVERFILL THE FUEL TANK. THE 80% LIQUID FILL LEVEL PROVIDES SPACE 
FOR NORMAL VARIATIONS OF VAPOR EXPANSION. OVERFILLING CAN CAUSE EXCESS 
PRESSURE IN THE FUEL TANK WHICH CAN UNSEAT THE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE AND 
CREATE A FUEL VAPOR LEAK. IT CAN ALSO CAUSE THE RELEASE OF LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM 
GAS (LPG) FUEL THROUGH THE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE. 

Open the 80% stop-fill valve.

[FIGURE: V9337A.gif]

Open the valve at the end of the fill hose.

Open the main valve at the storage tank.

Start the liquified petroleum gas (LPG) fuel pump. Only LPG designated 
as HD-5 can be used in the system.

Fill the tank until liquid appears as a heavy, dense, white fog out of 
the 80% stop-fill valve.

Immediately close the valve at the end of the fill hose.

Close the 80% stop-fill valve.

Shut off the LPG fuel pump.

Disconnect the fuel fill hose, install the protective cap on the filler 
valve.

Close the main valve at the storage tank.

Remove the ground strap and wheel blocks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tanks

 Fuel Tank, Outside Frame, 7.0L MFI Gasoline Engine 

 Removal 

To avoid electrical sparking, disconnect the battery ground cable, then 
disconnect the fuel lines and the fuel gauge sending unit wire. Disconnect the 
electrical fuel pump wires.

Drain the fuel into a suitable OSHA approved container such as Rotunda 
Fuel Storage Tanker 164-R3201 or equivalent. Either remove the drain plug, if 
so equipped, or siphon through the filler cap opening.

 NOTE: When removing fuel tank straps, make sure the tank is properly 
supported on a suitable jack.

Remove the fuel tank straps. Refer to Fuel Tank Support Straps in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Replace all worn or damaged parts.

If the fuel tank is to be replaced, remove the vent hose, the fuel 
gauge sending unit and gasket from the tank. Also remove the shutoff valve 
assembly, if so equipped, and remove the electric fuel pump. Discard all 
gaskets.

 Installation 

If the fuel tank has been replaced, install the fuel gauge sending unit 
and a new gasket on the tank. Install the shutoff valve assembly and a new 
gasket, if so equipped. Install the electric fuel pump and a new gasket. 
Tighten all screws to 14 Nm (10 lb-ft). Position new insulating strips 
on the fuel tank mounting bracket. Install the drain plug, if so equipped, in 
the fuel tank.

Install the fuel tank on the mounting brackets.

Install the retaining straps, but do not tighten the mounting bolts. 
Align the tank. Make sure the insulators are properly centered under the 
straps and brackets. Tighten the retaining strap mounting nuts to 18-24 
Nm (13-18 lb-ft).

Connect the fuel tubes to the tank. Connect the vent hose. Connect the 
fuel gauge sending unit wire and connect the electric fuel pump wires.

On a vehicle with dual fuel tanks, connect the fuel tube connecting 
the tanks.

Fill the tank with fuel and install the filler cap. Connect the battery 
ground cable. Start the engine and check for leaks.

 Fuel Tank, 7.0L LPG 

 WARNING: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO REPLACE OR SERVICE ANY OF THE COMPONENTS ON THE 
LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY. IN PARTICULAR DO NOT ATTEMPT 
TO WELD OR SOLDER ANY PART OF THE FUEL TANKS. IF ANY PART OF THE FUEL TANK 
SYSTEM IS DAMAGED, THE ENTIRE ASSEMBLY MUST BE REPLACED WITH ONLY FORD 
APPROVED PARTS, OR THEIR FULL EQUIVALENTS. FIELD SERVICE OR USE OF DIFFERENT 
PARTS CAN PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT CAN RESULT IN FIRE HAZARD OR 
OTHERWISE LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE TOOLS TO INSPECT THE FILL VALVE OR OTHER VALVES WITH FUEL IN 
THE TANK. LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL IN THE TANK IS UNDER PRESSURE OF 
ABOUT 1725 KPA (250 PSI). FORCEABLE PROBING WITH A TOOL CAN CAUSE A VALVE TO 
UNSEAT AND UNEXPECTEDLY RELEASE LPG FUEL. THIS CAN LEAD TO POSSIBLE EYE INJURY 
OR CREATE A FIRE HAZARD. ONLY INSPECT THE COMPONENTS VISUALLY. REPLACE THE LPG 
FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY AFTER EXHAUSTING ALL POSSIBILITIES FOR THE CAUSE OF "HARD 
TO FILL" OR "WON'T HOLD FUEL DURING FILLING." 

 WARNING: EVACUATE THE FUEL TANK AT A LOCAL LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL 
STATION BEFORE REMOVING THE FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY. LPG FUEL TANK ASSEMBLIES MUST 
BE STORED OR SHIPPED ACCORDING TO ALL NATIONAL, STATE, AND LOCAL LAWS. IF 
THERE IS ANY DOUBT REGARDING THE APPROVED PROCEDURE FOR LPG FUEL TANK 
HANDLING, CONTACT THE FORD DISTRICT OFFICE FOR INSTRUCTIONS PRIOR TO BEGINNING 
THE SERVICE. FAILURE TO OBSERVE PROPER INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN A FIRE 
HAZARD LEADING TO PERSONAL INJURY AND PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

 WARNING: USE ONLY FORD APPROVED PARTS OR THEIR FULL EQUIVALENTS. USE OF ANY 
OTHER FITTINGS, LINES OR OTHER COMPONENTS CAN PRODUCE AN UNTESTED 
CONFIGURATION, RESULTING IN POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

 WARNING: USE PROPER LIFTING EQUIPMENT AND PERSONAL ASSISTANCE FOR TANK 
REPLACEMENT. THE FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY WEIGHS APPROXIMATELY 55 KG (121 LB) 
WITHOUT FUEL. FAILURE TO PROPERLY SUPPORT THE FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY CAN RESULT IN 
PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: BEFORE LOOSENING ANY FUEL SYSTEM FITTINGS, CLOSE THE FUEL TANK MANUAL 
SHUTOFF VALVE AND RUN THE ENGINE OUT OF FUEL. NORMALLY THIS OCCURS WITHIN 2-3 
MINUTES. FAILURE TO USE UP THE FUEL IN THE LINES WILL CAUSE UNNECESSARY VAPOR 
TO RELEASE WHEN FITTINGS ARE LOOSENED FOR SERVICE. THIS CAN LEAD TO FIRE 
HAZARD AND POSSIBLE HUMAN INJURY. IF THE ENGINE DOES NOT RUN, LOOSEN THE 
REQUIRED FITTING VERY SLOWLY, PREFERABLY OUTSIDE OF THE BUILDINGS, AND ALLOW 
THE FUEL VAPOR PRESSURE TO VENT. 

 WARNING: THE FUEL TANK WEIGHS APPROXIMATELY 54 KG (120 POUNDS) WHEN EMPTY. USE 
PROPER SUPPORT EQUIPMENT AND PERSONAL ASSISTANCE WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING 
THE FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY. FAILURE TO OBSERVE THIS WARNING CAN RESULT IN PERSONAL 
INJURY. 

 NOTE: Liquified petroleum gas (LPG) fuel vapor is heavier than air, and will 
collect in lubrication pits, sewage drains and other low-lying areas.

 NOTE: LPG fuel tank removal, evacuation and replacement must be performed in 
a safe, designated area, such as a local LPG fuel station.

 Removal 

Read and observe all warning notices prior to LPG fuel tank service.

Close the fuel tank manual shutoff valve completely. Close both tank 
manual shutoff valves if vehicle is equipped with dual fuel tanks.

Start and run vehicle engine until all fuel pressure remaining in the 
system is used.

Disconnect the battery ground cable.

Disconnect fuel gauge sending unit if fuel tank is equipped.

Slowly and carefully loosen fuel supply hose fitting to allow any fuel 
vapor to escape safely. Remove and position the hose out of the way.

Position suitable stands and jacking equipment under fuel tank. There 
are many LPG

Fuel Pump, Electric, In-Tank, Gasoline Engines

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES ON VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES WILL 
REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUT-DOWN. THE 
PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM. 

 NOTE: Remove the fuel pump prior to steaming the fuel tank.

An electric fuel pump is located in the fuel tank. The fuel tank must 
be removed to service the fuel pump. Care should be taken during installation 
due to the hose and wire routing on the tank. Make sure all hoses and wires 
are routed properly. Check the fuel tube connections for leaks.

[FIGURE: V8408B.gif]

material.

Position fuel pump and gasket to fuel tank and install retaining screws.

Install the fuel tank in the vehicle.

Connect the battery ground cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tubes, Flexible Hose

Flexible fuel tubes must be serviced with bulk hose and reusable swivel 
 sockets. The appropriate bulk hose and socket replacements must satisfy SAE 
J1402 requirements. Ford Trucks use Aeroquip hose and sockets. Refer to the 
following conversion chart.

 BULK HOSE PART NUMBERS

Hose Assembly Base

Bulk Hose No. a 

Socket Part No. a 

-2C037-

FC350-06

401-6S

-2C038-

FC350-08

401-8S

-2C039-

FC350-10

401-10S

 a Aeroquip part numbers.

 Removal 

Disconnect fuel tubes at both ends. If removing crossover tube, shut 
off valves. Remove units from holding clips and remove from the vehicle.

Slide looms, if used, off tubes. Replace all worn or damaged parts.

 Installation 

Use bulk hose, according to above chart, as determined from hose 
assembly base numbers shown in service manual.

Cut hose square with either a cut-off wheel or fine-toothed hacksaw.

Put socket in vise. Screw hose counterclockwise into socket until tight 
and then back off one-quarter turn. For long hose lengths it may be preferred 
to place the hose in the vise and screw socket until tight. Again, back off 
one-quarter turn. Thoroughly lubricate nipple threads and inside of hose with 
heavy oil or hose assembly lubrication.

Screw nipple clockwise into socket and hose, being careful to leave 
1/32-inch to 1/16-inch clearance between nipple hex and socket.

Clean hose assembly by blowing out with clean compressed air. Then 
rinse inside of hose assembly with diesel fuel.

Install connecting hoses and clamps, if required, on fuel tubes. 
Position tubes in clips on vehicle. Tighten connecting hose clamps, if so 
equipped.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tubes, LPG

 WARNING: BEFORE LOOSENING ANY FUEL SYSTEM FITTINGS, CLOSE THE FUEL TANK MANUAL 
SHUTOFF VALVE AND RUN THE ENGINE OUT OF FUEL. NORMALLY THIS OCCURS WITHIN 2-3 
MINUTES. FAILURE TO USE UP THE FUEL IN THE TUBES WILL CAUSE UNNECESSARY VAPOR 
TO RELEASE WHEN FITTINGS ARE LOOSENED FOR SERVICE. THIS CAN LEAD TO FIRE 
HAZARD AND POSSIBLE HUMAN INJURY. IF THE ENGINE DOES NOT RUN, LOOSEN THE 
REQUIRED FITTING VERY SLOWLY, PREFERABLY OUTSIDE OF THE BUILDING, AND ALLOW 
THE FUEL VAPOR PRESSURE TO VENT. 

 Removal 

Close the fuel tank manual shutoff valve and run the engine out of fuel 
(approximately 2-3 minutes).

Slowly loosen each connector end of the fuel tube.

Disconnect each end.

Remove the fuel tube routing clamps.

 Installation 

Replace the tube and carefully align the fittings and hose before 
tightening.

Slowly crack open the fuel tank manual shutoff valve to full open and 
check the system for leaks.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Tanks

Inspect the fuel tank mounting brackets and straps to be sure the fuel 
tanks are securely attached to the vehicle. Inspect the fuel tube(s) at the 
tank(s) to make sure they do not leak.

 Fuel Tank, Gasoline 

 CAUTION: Do not apply steam to the thermal relief plug or the fuel filler cap. 

Fuel tanks do not require special service procedures and can be 
steam-cleaned or serviced using standard procedures. After steaming, allow 
time to thoroughly air dry. Remove the fuel vapor valve and fuel tank sending 
unit and pump prior to steaming.

 Fuel Tank, LPG 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE TOOLS TO INSPECT THE FILL VALVE OR OTHER VALVES WITH FUEL IN 
THE TANK. LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL IN THE TANK IS UNDER PRESSURE OF 
ABOUT 1725 KPA (160 PSI). FORCIBLE PROBING WITH A TOOL CAN CAUSE A VALVE TO 
UNSEAT AND UNEXPECTEDLY RELEASE LPG FUEL. THIS CAN LEAD TO POSSIBLE EYE INJURY 
OR CREATE A FIRE HAZARD. ONLY INSPECT THE COMPONENTS VISUALLY. REPLACE THE 
FUEL TANK ASSEMBLY AFTER EXHAUSTING ALL POSSIBILITIES FOR THE CAUSE OF "HARD 
TO FILL" OR "WON'T HOLD FUEL DURING FILLING." 

The LPG fuel tank and components are not serviceable. Inspect the 
entire fuel tank and each fitting, valve, and line for indications of 
restriction to fuel entry or fuel leaks. If any of the following items appear 
damaged or inoperative, the entire fuel tank assembly must be replaced.

fuel tank

manual shutoff valve

pressure relief valve

excess flow valve

fill valve

80% stop-fill valve, hose and connections

fuel tank sending unit or gauge

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fuel System Pressure Relief

 CAUTION: Fuel supply tubes on 7.0L MFI gasoline-powered engines will remain 
pressurized for some period of time after the engine is shut off. This 
pressure must be relieved before servicing the fuel system. 

Before opening the fuel system on vehicles with MFI engines, relieve 
fuel pressure as follows:

Locate and disconnect the electrical connection to either the fuel pump 
relay, the inertia fuel shutoff switch or the in-line high fuel pump.

Crank engine for approximately ten seconds. Engine may start and run 
for a short time. If so, crank engine an additional five seconds after engine 
stalls.

Connect the electrical connector that was disconnected in Step 1.

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Fuel System Pressure Relief, MFI Gasoline Engines

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Fuel Pressure Gauge

T80L-9974-B

 CAUTION: Fuel supply tubes on 7.0L MFI gasoline-powered engines will remain 
pressurized for some period of time after the engine is shut off. This 
pressure must be relieved before servicing the fuel system. 

Before opening the fuel system on vehicles with MFI gasoline engines, 
relieve fuel pressure as follows:

Remove the fuel cap to relieve fuel tank pressure.

Connect Fuel Pressure Gauge T80L-9974-B to the pressure relief valve 
located on the right bank of the fuel injection supply manifold.

Place the other end of the gauge hose in a jar to collect any drained 
fuel.

Open the valve on the gauge to evacuate any fuel pressure in the system.

Remove the gauge from the manifold.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank Sending Unit, Diesel

The fuel level sending unit consists of a variable resistor 
(potentiometer) which is attached to a float in the fuel tank and varies 
according to fluid level in the tank. When the fuel level is low, resistance 
in the sending unit is high and allows only a low current to flow through the 
indicator gauge windings, causing the pointer to move a short distance. When 
the fuel level is high, the resistance in the sending unit is low and allows a 
higher current flow and a greater heating effect, causing the pointer to move 
a greater distance.

1999 P800, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tank(s)

Typical fuel tank installations are shown in the following illustrations.

 Removal 

Drain the fuel into an OSHA-approved container by either removing the 
drain plug, if so equipped, or use Rotunda Fuel Storage Tanker 164-R3201 or 
equivalent.

To avoid electrical sparking, disconnect the battery ground cable, 
then disconnect the fuel line and the fuel gauge sending unit wire.

Disconnect the fuel return lines.

On a vehicle with dual fuel tanks, disconnect the fuel line connecting 
the tanks.

 CAUTION: Use a suitable jack to support and lower the tank. 

Remove the fuel tank strap retaining bolts and remove the straps. 
Remove the tank. 

If the fuel tank is to be replaced, remove the fuel gauge sending unit 
and gasket from the tank. Remove the shutoff valve assembly, if so equipped. 
Remove the vent valve.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Use a suitable jack to support and raise the tank. 

If the fuel tank has been replaced, install the fuel gauge sending unit 
and a new gasket on the tank. Install the vent valve. Replace the vent valve 
gasket, if so equipped. Install the transfer valve assembly, if so equipped. 
Position new insulating strips on the fuel tank mounting bracket. Install the 
drain plug (if it was removed) in the fuel tank.

Install the fuel tank on the mounting bracket.

Install the retaining straps, but do not tighten the mounting bolts. 
Align the tank. Make sure insulators are properly centered under the straps 
and brackets. Tighten the retaining strap mounting bolts to 17-25 Nm 
(13-18 lb-ft).

Connect the fuel line to the tank. Connect the fuel gauge sending unit 
wire.

Connect the fuel return line.

On a vehicle with dual fuel tanks, connect the fuel line connecting the 
tanks.

Fill the tank with fuel and install the filler cap. Connect the battery 
ground cable. Start the engine and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tank Support Straps

 Removal 

Support the fuel tank, using a suitable jack, before removing one or 
both fuel tank straps.

Remove the lower fuel tank retaining strap nut.

[FIGURE: V8443C.gif]

 NOTE: When removing upper fuel tank strap, use caution not to let holding 
bolt fall out of frame hole. If fuel tank strap bolt falls out of frame hole, 
use a length of wire to pull strap bolt back into position.

Remove the upper fuel tank retaining strap nut.

[FIGURE: V8445C.gif]

Remove the strap from the fuel tank.

If a new strap is being installed, the rubber insulator must be removed 
from the tank strap for installation of the new strap.

 Installation 

If a new strap is being installed, position rubber insulator to strap.

Position fuel tank strap to fuel tank.

Install upper strap stud retaining nut and hand-tighten.

Install lower strap stud retaining nut and hand-tighten.

Make sure strap is properly positioned and tighten upper and lower 
strap stud nuts to 17-25 Nm (13-18 lb-ft).

1999 P800, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Sending Unit, Fuel Tank 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Disconnect the wiring from the fuel sending unit.

Remove and discard the mounting screws.

Remove the fuel sending unit and mounting gasket from the fuel tank 
opening and discard the gasket.

[FIGURE: V9817A.gif]

 Installation 

Clean the fuel sending unit mounting surface of the fuel tank. Do not 
allow foreign material to enter the tank opening.

Position the new mounting gasket at the fuel tank opening and carefully 
align holes in gasket to screw holes in tank.

Position the fuel sending unit in the tank and carefully align holes in 
sending unit flange-to-gasket holes with screw holes in tank.

Install the new mounting screws and tighten to 2.0-2.7 Nm (18-24 
lb-in). Then check all mounting screw torques.

Connect the wiring to the fuel sending unit.

Connect battery ground cable.

Check for proper fuel gauge operation and for leaks while refilling.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Tubes

If fuel tubes are suspected of contamination or leaks, inspect tubes 
for cracks and fittings for leaks. Replace any tubes that are damaged. If fuel 
tube contains contaminated fuel, flush with clean diesel fuel, drain fuel 
filter and inspect filter element.

1999 P800, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Tanks

Fuel tanks do not require special service procedures and can be 
steam-cleaned or serviced using standard procedures. After steaming, allow 
them to thoroughly air dry. Replace dual tank strap bolts. Remove fuel tank 
sending unit before cleaning tank.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

The throttle is controlled by an accelerator rod or cable linkage and a 
pedal assembly. The accelerator pedal must travel smoothly from idle to the 
wide-open throttle position. Hesitation on return or prevention of return to 
the idle position must not occur. Surrounding components, such as wiring, 
hoses, sound insulator and floor covering, must not contact any moving member 
of the linkage or the accelerator pedal assembly.

================================================================================
PAGE 3265
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 10-02: Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

1999 P800, F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

 Inspection and Verification 

 WARNING: SURROUNDING ENGINE COMPARTMENT COMPONENTS, SUCH AS WIRING OR HOSES, 
MUST NOT CONTACT ANY MOVING MEMBER OF THE ACCELERATOR CONTROLS. CHECK ALL 
VEHICLES FOR RETURN TO IDLE. PERCEPTIBLE HESITATION OR PREVENTION OF RETURN TO 
IDLE POSITION MUST NOT OCCUR DURING SLOW REMOVAL OF THE FOOT FROM THE 
ACCELERATOR PEDAL AND SHAFT, STARTING AT THE FULLY DEPRESSED, WIDE-OPEN 
THROTTLE (WOT) POSITION. 

Verify the customer's concerns by inspecting the condition. Check for 
any resistance in accelerator pedal action. Inspect the accelerator pedal and 
linkage if a high engine idle speed condition exists. After inspection and 
verification, refer to the symptom chart for the condition, and perform the 
appropriate action to correct the condition.

Operate the accelerator pedal and linkage by hand, observing and 
feeling that the full range of travel is not restricted by wiring, hoses, dash 
panel insulation, carpet mat, padding or any other components.

 Symptom Chart — Accelerator Pedal To Throttle
Body 

 ACCELERATOR PEDAL TO THROTTLE BODY 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Accelerator Pedal Is Hard to Push Down or Has a Rough/Raspy or Sticky 
Feel

 NOTE: Accelerator cable should not be lubricated and it is not serviceable.

Accelerator cable and spring contact surrounding parts.

DISCONNECT accelerator cable end from ball stud at throttle body, 
making sure the disconnected end of the accelerator cable or its spring does 
not come into contact with any of the surrounding parts.

Insulation or trim interferes with pedal travel.

OPERATE the accelerator pedal by hand, observing and feeling that the 
full pedal range of travel is not restricted by the dash panel insulator or 
carpet/mat/padding. If full pedal travel to WOT is restricted, ADJUST 
insulator or trim items as required.

Shaft not moving.

OPERATE the accelerator pedal and shaft by foot.

Internal components other than cable not working properly.

If accelerator cable operation is smooth, REFER to the throttle body 
diagnosis procedures in the appropriate section in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

Cable is worn.

If the condition recurs (making sure disconnected end of accelerator 
cable has not come into contact with anything), CHECK the accelerator pedal 
for free operation. If the pedal operation is free, REPLACE accelerator cable.

High Engine Idle Speed

Cable ball socket extends beyond the throttle lever ball stud.

REFER to the throttle body diagnosis procedure in the appropriate 
section of the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.(Can 
be purchased as a separate item.)

Restricted foot pedal operation.

ADJUST carpet, mat or wiring as required.

Internal components interacting improperly.

If the accelerator cable ball socket extends beyond the throttle lever 
ball stud, REFER to the throttle body diagnosis procedures in the appropriate 
section in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.(Can 
be purchased as a separate item.)

Component, trim or insulation interference.

If the socket does not extend beyond the stud, CHECK the accelerator 
pedal for free operation (no contact with carpet, mats, wiring, etc.). If the 
pedal operation is free, REPLACE the accelerator cable.
