SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant System

 Refrigerant System Identification 

Several refrigerants are used in today's air conditioning systems. The 
refrigerants are not compatible. While system operations and procedures are 
the same, the equipment is unique and cannot be used interchangeably.

The label stating A/C refrigerant use in the vehicle is attached in the 
engine compartment so the proper service procedure and equipment can be 
referenced in the service manual. An R-134a refrigerant system will have gold 
R-134a NON-CFC tags in addition to the refrigerant charge tag.

[FIGURE: M4526A.gif]

If a component has been used with R-12, it cannot be used again in an 
R-134a system. If used in an R-134a system, it cannot be put into an R-12 
system. Contamination can occur and performance can be adversely affected 
because each system uses a different refrigerant oil designed for that system.

 Special Service Equipment 

The refrigerant used in this refrigerant system is HFC-134a 
(tetrafluoroethane-CF 3 CH 2 F) which is a 
hydrofluorocarbon refrigerant. HFC-134a, also known as R-134a, is 
non-corrosive, non-explosive, non-flammable and has a slight ether-type odor. 
R-134a is heavier than air. Although it is classified as a safe refrigerant, 
certain precautions must be observed to protect the parts involved and the 
person working on the unit.

Use only R-134a refrigerant and R-134a compatible refrigerant oil. Due 
to environmental concerns, when the air conditioning system is drained, the 
refrigerant must be collected using refrigerant recovery/recycling equipment 
meeting SAE J1990 and J2210. R-134a must never be removed without the 
appropriate equipment or released into the atmosphere. Use of a recovery 
machine dedicated for R-134a is necessary to reduce the possibility of oil and 
refrigerant incompatibility concerns. Refer to the instructions provided by 
the equipment manufacturer when removing refrigerant from or charging the air 
conditioning system.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant Recovery

 CAUTION: Use extreme care and observe all safety and service precautions related 
to the use of refrigerants. 

Refrigerant recovery systems and recycling stations are in use in most 
automotive A/C service facilities. The use of such equipment makes possible 
the recovery and reuse of A/C system refrigerant after contaminants and 
moisture have been removed.

[FIGURE: L9811A.gif]

If a refrigerant recovery or recycling station is used, the following 
general procedures must be observed, in addition to the operating instructions 
provided by the equipment manufacturer.

 NOTE: Hoses must have shutoff devices or check valves within 305 mm (12 
inches) of the hose end to minimize the introduction of non-condensable gases 
(air) into the recycling station and to minimize the amount of refrigerant 
released when the hose(s) is disconnected.

Connect the refrigerant recycling station hose(s) to vehicle A/C 
service ports and recovery station inlet fitting.

Turn power to the recycling station on to start the recovery process. 
Allow recycling station to pump refrigerant from the system until the station 
pressure goes into a vacuum. On some stations, the pump will be shut off 
automatically by a low-pressure switch in the electrical system. On other 
units it may be necessary to manually turn off the pump.

Once the recycling station has evacuated vehicle A/C system, close the 
station inlet valve (if so equipped). Then, switch off the electrical power.

Allow vehicle A/C system to remain closed for about two minutes. 
Observe system pressure level as shown on the gauge. If pressure does not 
rise, disconnect recycling station hose(s).

If system pressure rises, repeat Steps 2, 3 and 4 until the vacuum 
level remains stable for two minutes.

Perform required service operations, evacuate and recharge the A/C 
system.

 Refrigerant Reclaiming/Recovery/Recycling Equipment 

 CAUTION: The A/C refrigerant of all vehicles must be identified and analyzed 
prior to refrigerant charging. Failure to do so can contaminate the shop bulk 
refrigerant and other vehicles. 

Ford Motor Co. supports the efficient usage, recovery, and recycling of 
R-134a used in car and truck air conditioners. Ford Motor Co. recommends the 
use of an U.L. approved recovery/recycling device such as Rotunda R-134a A/C 
Service Center 023-00150 or equivalent during any air conditioning system 
repair and recharge procedure which requires the air conditioning system to be 
discharged.

Refrigerant recovery systems and recycling stations are in use in an 
increasing number of automotive air conditioning service facilities. The use 
of such equipment makes possible the recovery and use of air conditioning 
system refrigerant after contaminants and moisture have been removed.

If a refrigerant recovery or recycling station is used, the following 
general procedures must be observed, in addition to the operating instructions 
provided by the equipment manufacturer.

 CAUTION: Use extreme care and observe all safety and service precautions related 
to the use of refrigerants.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant Identification and Analysis

Use the A/C refrigerant analyzer 198-0001, or equivalent to identify 
the refrigerant type and purity. Refer to the manufacturer's operating 
instructions.

If the purity percentage of the R-134a or R-12 is 98% or greater by 
weight, a green "PASS" LED will light. Proceed with the refrigerant recovery. 
Refer to System Discharging and Recovery in the Service Procedures portion of 
this section.

If the R-134a or R-12 does not meet 98% purity, a red "FAIL" LED will 
light. Proceed with the refrigerant recovery. Refer to System Discharging and 
Recovery in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Levels of R-22 and flammable hydrocarbons above 2% will light the red 
"FAIL" LED. Refer to Recovery of Contaminated A/C Systems in the Service 
Procedures portion of this section.

If a flammable hydrocarbon is detected above 5%, both the "FAIL" and 
"HYDROCARBON" LEDs will light and a horn will sound. Refer to Recovery of 
Contaminated A/C Systems in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

System Evacuating

 NOTE: Ford Motor Company supports the efficient usage, recovery, and 
recycling of R-134a used in car and truck air conditioners. Ford Motor Company 
recommends the use of a U.L.-approved recovery/recycling device such as 
Rotunda R-134a Service Center 023-00150, or equivalent, which meets SAE 
Standard J1991 during any A/C system service and recharge procedure which 
requires the A/C system to be discharged.

 NOTE: Some R-134a service centers require the use of an A/C manifold gauge 
set. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Connect the A/C service center hoses to the service gauge access ports.

 NOTE: The vacuum should be as close as 101 kPa (30 in-Hg) as possible.

Evacuate the system until the low-pressure gauge is between 84-101 kPa 
(25-30 in-Hg). Refer to the equipment manufacturer's operating instructions.

Operate the vacuum pump for an additional 45 minutes if a part of the 
A/C system has been replaced.

Turn the vacuum pump off.

Observe the low-pressure side gauge to make sure that it will hold a 
vacuum for five minutes.

If the A/C system holds a vacuum, then proceed with A/C system charging.

If the A/C system leaks, then leak test the system, service any 
leak(s), and evacuate the system.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

System Charging Setup 

Ford Motor Company recommends using a charging station to perform 
evacuation and charging of the refrigerant system. Follow the instructions 
provided with the charging station. 

If a charging station is not available, system charging can be 
accomplished using a separate vacuum pump, charging cylinder and manifold 
gauge set. 

If the charging cylinder method is used, the center port of the 
manifold gauge set should have two refrigerant hoses with integral shutoff 
valves built into the gauge set manifold. If the gauge set is the type that 
does not have shutoff valves and two hoses at the center port, a tee fitting 
and two hoses must be installed at the center port. In addition, the hoses 
attached to the center port must have shutoff valves at the other ends of the 
two center hoses to prevent air from entering the hoses when not connected to 
the vacuum pump and charging cylinder.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

System Charging

 Charging with a Charging Cylinder 

 CAUTION: The A/C refrigerant of all vehicles must be identified and analyzed 
prior to refrigerant charging. Failure to do so can contaminate the shop bulk 
refrigerant and other vehicles. 

Ford Motor Company supports the efficient use, recovery, and recycling 
of R-134a used in modern air conditioners. Ford Motor Company recommends the 
use of a U.L. approved recovery/recycling device such as Rotunda R-134a A/C 
Service Center 023-00150 or equivalent during any air conditioning system 
service and recharge procedure which requires the air conditioning system to 
be discharged.

 CAUTION: Do not liquid-charge into the vehicle A/C system. Refrigerant tanks 
must be in an upright position only when charging the A/C system. Refrigerant 
tanks in an upside down or side laying position will allow liquid refrigerant 
to enter the vehicle's A/C system, which can result in A/C compressor damage. 

Connect the manifold gauge set. Refer to the A/C Manifold Gauge Set 
Connection procedure in Service Procedures in this section.

Discharge the refrigerant system. Refer to System Discharging and 
Recovery procedure in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Evacuate the refrigerant system. Refer to System Evacuating procedure 
in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Connect the center hose of the manifold gauge set to a refrigerant 
cylinder. If a charging station is used, follow the instructions of the 
manufacturer.

 NOTE: Keep the refrigerant cylinder in the upright position.

Open the low-pressure valve on the manifold gauge set to allow 
refrigerant to enter the system. Continue to add refrigerant until 
approximately 1.3 kg (3.0 lb) is drawn into the system.

Close the low-pressure valve.

 CAUTION: Do not open the high-pressure valve while the engine is running. 

Start the engine and turn on the air conditioning.

Open the low-pressure valve on the manifold gauge set to allow 
refrigerant to enter the system. Continue to add refrigerant until the 
recommended amount of refrigerant is drawn into the system.

Close the low-pressure valve.

Check the air conditioning system for proper operation.

Stop the engine.

Disconnect the manifold gauge set.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

System Flushing

 WARNING: R134A IS CLASSIFIED AS A SAFE REFRIGERANT, BUT MISUSE CAN MAKE IT 
DANGEROUS. THE FOLLOWING PRECAUTIONS MUST BE OBSERVED:

ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GOGGLES WHEN SERVICING AN AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM.

AVOID CONTACT WITH LIQUID REFRIGERANT R-134A. R-134A VAPORIZES AT 
APPROXIMATELY -20°F UNDER ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE AND IT WILL FREEZE SKIN 
TISSUE.

NEVER ALLOW REFRIGERANT R-134A GAS TO ESCAPE IN QUANTITY IN AN OCCUPIED 
SPACE. R-134A IS NON-TOXIC, BUT IT WILL NOT FURNISH THE OXYGEN NEEDED TO 
SUPPORT LIFE.

NEVER USE A TORCH IN AN ATMOSPHERE CONTAINING R-134A GAS. R-134A IS 
NON-TOXIC UNDER ALL NORMAL CONDITIONS, BUT WHEN IT IS EXPOSED TO HIGH 
TEMPERATURES, SUCH AS A TORCH FLAME, IT DECOMPOSES. ONE OF THE PRODUCTS OF THE 
CHEMICAL BREAKDOWN IS A PHOSGENE GAS WHICH IS HIGHLY TOXIC.

CARE SHOULD BE EXERCISED SO AS NOT TO OVERHEAT ANY PORTION OF THE 
CHARGED AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM. THE PRESSURE IN AN AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM 
RISES AS THE TEMPERATURE RISES AND TEMPERATURES OF APPROXIMATELY 200°F CAN 
BE DANGEROUS. 

 CAUTION: Only an A/C flushing kit which includes the A/C flusher, A/C flusher 
fitting kit, and Ford A/C system flushing solvent such as Rotunda A/C Flusher 
Kit 014-00991 and Rotunda A/C Flushing Fitting Kit 014-00992 or equivalent, is 
approved for use on Ford vehicles. No other flushing device or solvent is 
approved for flushing heat exchangers. Use of any other flusher or solvent can 
cause damage to the A/C system and the flushing unit. 

 CAUTION: Do not flush the A/C evaporator core orifice or hoses. The internal 
plumbing and material make-up of these items make it impossible to properly 
remove the debris and residual flushing fluid which can cause premature system 
failure. 

 CAUTION: The flushing solvent and flushing unit filter are intended for one 
vehicle use only. They can be used to flush one or all of the heat exchangers 
in the A/C system. Failure to change the flushing solvent and filter can 
spread A/C system contamination. 

 NOTE: The A/C system filtering, as described in this section, is optional if 
A/C system flushing is performed. However, filter kit use after flushing is 
recommended if the A/C system contamination is extensive.

Recover the refrigerant. Refer to System Discharging and Recovery in 
the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Disconnect the refrigerant lines from the heat exchanger(s) to be 
flushed. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Connect Rotunda A/C Flusher Kit 014-00991 and A/C Flushing Fitting Kit 
014-00992 or equivalents to the heat exchanger to be flushed. Refer to the 
equipment manufacturer's procedures and instructions for use of the R-134a 
service center.

Flush the heat exchanger, using 4 liters (1 gallon) of Ford A/C 
Flushing Solvent F4AZ-19597-A. Back-flush for a minimum of 15 minutes.

 CAUTION: The failure to successfully remove all of the residual solvent within 
the component can result in A/C system damage when it is reconnected and 
operated. 

 NOTE: Dispose of the flushing solvent and filter in accordance with all 
Federal, State, and Local laws.

Purge the heat exchanger. Apply 621-862 kPa (90-125 psi) of pressurized 
air for 30 minutes.

Replace the suction accumulator/drier and A/C evaporator core orifice 
on any vehicle being serviced for A/C compressor or desiccant failure. Refer 
to Section 12-03A .

Replace any refrigerant hoses that are clogged with debris. Refer to 
 Section 12-03A .

Reconnect the heat exchanger being serviced. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Add additional refrigerant oil as required. Refer to Refrigerant Oil 
Addition in the Service Procedures portion of this section.

Evacuate, charge, and leak test the A/C system. Refer to the Service 
Procedures portion of this section.

Check the A/C system for proper operation.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant System Filtering After A/C Compressor Replacement

 CAUTION: Follow all refrigerant system safety and service precautions as outlined. 

An A/C service kit has been released to provide the necessary equipment 
and information to perform the new, mandatory A/C system filtering procedure. 
The filter kit with the service part number suffix "A" is to be used on 
vehicles that have a nylon-lined evaporator-to-compressor suction line between 
the suction accumulator/drier and the A/C compressor.

[FIGURE: M4546A.gif]

To determine that the A/C compressor has failed and must be replaced, 
remove the A/C evaporator core orifice and condenser to evaporator tube, if 
necessary. Look for a dirty A/C evaporator core orifice or a condenser to 
evaporator tube containing black refrigerant oil and particles.

Remove the damaged A/C compressor and drain the oil into a calibrated 
container.

 NOTE: The proper amount of refrigerant oil must be added to the new A/C 
compressor before it can be installed.

If the amount of oil drained from the removed A/C compressor is between 
30 and 142 ml (3 oz to 5 oz), pour the same amount of clean oil into the new 
A/C compressor. If the amount of oil drained from the old A/C compressor is 
greater than 142 ml (5 oz), pour only 142 ml (5 oz) of clean refrigerant oil 
into the new A/C compressor. If the amount of refrigerant oil drained from the 
old A/C compressor is less than 85 ml (3 oz), pour 85 ml (3 oz) of clean 
refrigerant oil into the new A/C compressor.

 NOTE: It will be necessary to transfer the A/C clutch from the old A/C 
compressor to the new A/C compressor.

Install the new A/C compressor. Make sure the compressor mounting bolts 
are tightened to the proper specification. Check the tension of the drive 
belt. Adjust, if necessary.

Remove the suction accumulator/drier assembly and drain the oil into a 
calibrated container.

Add clean refrigerant oil to the new suction accumulator/drier in the 
same amount that was removed from the old unit, plus an additional 60 ml (2 
oz) of new refrigerant oil.

Install the suction accumulator/drier in the vehicle.

Obtain the proper service kit for the vehicle on which you are working. 
Filter kits with the service part number suffix "A" are to be used on vehicles 
with a nylon-lined evaporator to compressor suction line. The label on the 
filter shows which evaporator to compressor suction line it is to be used with.

[FIGURE: M3730A.gif]

Remove a length of evaporator-to-compressor suction line to accommodate 
the suction filter and install the filter using the clamps provided with the 
kit. Be sure filter is correctly oriented for refrigerant system flow. Check 
the label on the filter. On the filter for nylon-lined 
evaporator-to-compressor suction line, install O-rings (two on each filter 
tube, making sure they are properly seated in the grooves on the tube). 
Tighten the clamps securely.

Install a new A/C evaporator core orifice. The A/C evaporator core 
orifice is located in the condenser to evaporator tube between the A/C 
condenser core and the A/C evaporator core. Reinstall the condenser to 
evaporator tube. Refer to Section 12-03A .

Install a pancake filter in the condenser to evaporator tube between 
the A/C condenser core and the A/C evaporator core orifice. Be sure the filter 
inlet is toward the A/C condenser core. Connections can be made using the A/C 
Test Fitting Set D93L-19703-B or equivalent and flexible refrigerant hose of 
17237.5 kPa (2500 psi) burst rating. Individual fittings are also available.

 Pancake Filter 

[FIGURE: M3878A.gif]

Evacuate, charge and leak test the system.

Check all refrigerant system hoses, lines and the positioning of the 
newly installed filters to be sure they do not interfere with other engine 
compartment components. If necessary, use tie straps to make adjustments.

Provide adequate airflow to the front of the vehicle (with a fan, if 
necessary), and set the air conditioner control at MAX A/C. Set the A/C blower 
motor speed control on HI and temperature control at full COOL. Start the 
engine and let it idle briefly. Make sure the A/C system is operating properly.

Gradually bring the engine up to 1200 rpm by running it at lower rpms 
for short periods (first at 800 rpm, then at 1000 rpm). Set the engine at 1200 
rpm and run it for an hour with the A/C system operating.

Stop the engine.

Allow the engine to cool sufficiently to remove the fittings, flexible 
hoses and pancake filter from the condenser to evaporator tube. (It will be 
necessary to discharge and recover the refrigerant in the system first.)

Discard the pancake filter. It can be used ONE TIME ONLY.

Reconnect the condenser to evaporator tube back into the system.

Evacuate, charge and leak test the system. Observe all safety 
precautions. Make any necessary adjustments.

Check the operation of the system in all modes.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

A/C Evaporator Core Orifice Replacement Kit Installation

The fixed orifice tube is constructed with a plastic body, two screens 
and a small brass tube down the center of the orifice body. Two O-rings are 
installed around the orifice tube body to seal against leakage.

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to remove the fixed orifice tube with pliers or by 
twisting the tube. To do so will break the fixed orifice tube body in the 
evaporator core tube. Use only the recommended tool and follow the recommended 
service procedures. 

 Removal 

Discharge and recover the refrigerant from the air conditioning system. 
Observe all safety precautions.

Disconnect the liquid line from the evaporator core. Cap the liquid 
line to prevent the entry of dirt and excessive moisture.

Squirt a small amount of clean refrigerant oil into the evaporator core 
inlet tube to lubricate the tube and orifice O-rings during removal of the 
fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

Engage the Fixed Orifice Tube Tool D80L-19990-A or equivalent with the 
two tangs on the fixed orifice tube. Extract the orifice tube from the 
evaporator core tube.

If the orifice tube should break, hold the T-handle of Broken Orifice 
Tube Tool D80L-19990-B or equivalent to keep the orifice tube from turning.

Run the nut on the tool down against the evaporator core tube until the 
orifice is pulled from the tube.

To remove a broken segment of an orifice tube, insert the screw end of 
the extractor into the evaporator core tube and thread the screw end of the 
tool into the brass tube in the center of the fixed orifice tube. Then, pull 
the fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

If only the brass center is removed during Step 7, insert the screw end 
of the extractor tool into the evaporator core tube and turn it into the end 
of the fixed orifice tube body. Then, pull the fixed orifice tube body from 
the evaporator core tube.

 Installation 

Lubricate the O-rings on the fixed orifice tube body liberally with 
clean refrigerant oil.

Place the fixed orifice tube in the Fixed Orifice Tube Tool 
D80L-19990-A or equivalent, and insert the fixed orifice tube into the 
evaporator core tube until the orifice is seated at the stop.

Remove the tool from the fixed orifice tube.

Connect the liquid line to the evaporator core. Use only specified 
green O-ring seals.

Leak test, evacuate and charge the system. Observe all safety 
precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Suction Accumulator/Drier Replacement Guidelines

Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is necessary anytime a 
major component of the refrigerant system is replaced. A major component 
includes A/C condenser core, compressor or the A/C evaporator core. An A/C 
hose is not considered a major component. However, the suction 
accumulator/drier should be replaced if a refrigerant hose is replaced due to 
bursting. An evaporator core orifice or O-ring is not considered a major 
component, but the A/C evaporator core orifice must be replaced whenever the 
A/C compressor is replaced for lack of performance.

In addition to the preceding condition, the accumulator/drier must also 
be replaced if one of the following conditions exist.

The suction accumulator/drier is perforated.

The refrigerant system has been opened to the atmosphere for a period 
of time longer than required for minor service.

There is evidence of moisture in the system, such as internal corrosion 
of metal refrigerant lines or the refrigerant oil is thick and dark.

 NOTE: When replacing the suction accumulator/drier, the procedure given here 
must be followed to make sure that the total oil charge in the system is 
correct after the new suction accumulator/drier is installed.

Drain the oil from the removed suction accumulator/drier into a 
suitable measuring container. If necessary, drill one or two 12.7-mm 
(1/2-inch) holes in the bottom of the old accumulator/drier to make sure that 
all the oil has drained out. Add the same amount of clean new refrigerant oil 
plus 60 ml (2 oz) to the new suction accumulator/drier. Use only the oil 
specified for the specific vehicle being serviced.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Refrigerant Oil Addition

The compressor uses a unique high-quality polyalkalylene glycol (PAG) 
refrigerant oil meeting Ford specification WSH-M1C231-B. An oil charge of 310 
ml (10 oz) is used in a new system. It is extremely important that only the 
specified type and quantity of refrigerant oil be used in the compressor. If 
there is a surplus of oil in the system, it will circulate with the 
refrigerant, reducing the cooling capacity of the system. Using too little oil 
or oil not meeting the Ford specification will result in poor lubrication of 
the compressor.

When replacing a component of the refrigerant system, the procedures in 
this section must be followed to make sure that the total oil charge in the 
system is correct after the new part is installed.

When the compressor is operated, oil gradually leaves the compressor 
and is circulated through the system with the refrigerant. Eventually, a 
balanced condition is reached in which a certain amount of oil is retained in 
the compressor and a certain amount is continually circulated. If a component 
of the system is removed after the system has been operated, some oil will go 
with it. To maintain the original total oil charge, add oil as required to the 
new replacement part.

The procedures for replacing oil are as follows:

 During A/C Compressor Replacement 

 NOTE: The suction accumulator/drier and orifice tube must also be replaced 
when the compressor is replaced.

A new service replacement compressor may or may not contain refrigerant 
oil. Prior to installing the replacement compressor, drain the refrigerant oil 
from the removed compressor into a calibrated container. Then, drain the 
refrigerant oil from the new compressor into a clean calibrated container. 
Rotate the shaft about six to eight revolutions while pouring the oil from the 
ports. This effectively empties the compressor of oil.

Obtain a clean container that can also be used as a measuring device.

Place the disc and hub assembly on the compressor shaft so the shaft 
can be rotated.

Rotate the shaft by hand six to eight revolutions, collecting the oil 
in a clean measuring device.

If the amount of oil drained from the old compressor was between 85 and 
142 ml (3 and 5 oz), pour the same amount of clean Motorcraft YN-12B 
refrigerant oil into the new compressor.

If the amount of oil that was removed from the old compressor is 
greater than 142 ml (5 oz), pour 142 ml (5 oz) of clean Motorcraft YN-12B 
refrigerant oil into the new compressor.

If the amount of refrigerant oil that was removed from the old 
compressor is less than 85 ml (3 oz), pour 85 ml (3 oz) of clean Motorcraft 
YN-12B refrigerant oil into the new compressor.

 R-134a Refrigerant Oil 

The refrigerant oil required for R-134a A/C systems is a polyalkalylene 
glycol (PAG) oil, Ford specification WSH-M1C231-B or equivalent. This type of 
refrigerant oil is made specifically for R-134a systems and is not suitable 
for use in R-12 systems. Never use an R-134a refrigerant oil in R-12 systems 
or R-12 refrigerant oil in R-134a systems.

 During Component Replacement 

When replacing other components of the air conditioning system, 
measured quantities of the specified refrigerant oil must be added to the 
component to make sure that the total oil charge in the system is correct 
before the system is operated.

Clean refrigerant oil should be poured directly into the replacement 
components as follows:

A/C evaporator core: add 90 ml (3 oz).

A/C condenser core: add 30 ml (1 oz).

Accumulator: drain oil from removed accumulator/drier. Add same amount 
plus 60 ml (2 oz) of clean refrigerant oil to new accumulator.

 Other Refrigerant System Components 

Replacement of other refrigerant system components such as hoses, A/C 
compressor valves, and pressure switches does not require the addition of 
refrigerant oil.

Inspection and Assembly Requirements

 NOTE: Any time a hose or component connection leak is observed, to correctly

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Mini-Tube Vacuum Hose Service

Measure the length of the damaged area of the mini-tube vacuum hose.

Cut a piece of standard 3-mm (1/8-inch) ID vacuum hose approximately 
25.4 mm (1 inch) longer than the damaged area of the mini-tube vacuum hose.

Cut off the mini-tube vacuum hose on each side of the damaged area.

Dip the mini-tube hose ends in tetra hydro furan (THF) or methyl ethyl 
ketone (MEK). This will act as a solvent and seal the mini-tube in the vacuum 
hose.

Insert the ends of the mini-tube vacuum hose approximately 9 mm (3/8 
inch) into the ends of the standard 3-mm (1/8-inch) service vacuum hose section.

Shake service joint after assembly to make sure solvent is dispersed 
and vacuum line is not plugged.

Test system for a vacuum leak in the serviced area.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ventilation, Fresh Air 

The ventilation system consists of two air inlets which, when open, 
allow outside air to enter the vehicle cab. One inlet is located in the left 
side cowl. The other inlet is located in the right side cowl or is integral 
with the heater or air conditioner, depending on vehicle and heater or air 
conditioner applications. For information on the integral ventilation system, 
refer to Section 12-02 or Section 12-03A .

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Climate Control Assembly

With all Ford heating systems, outside air comes through an opening at 
the upper cowl and into the right duct of the heater assembly. All heater 
assemblies contain a heater core and a blower. The air (forced by blower or 
ram effect) passes through and around the heater core and discharges through 
various outlets. 

Several valves or doors determine the amount of air that goes through 
the heater core and the particular outlet(s) through which it discharges. The 
number of doors differs according to the particular heating system. 

The Comfort Vent Heater is a blend-air heating system similar in design 
to the manual heater-air conditioner. It features a power ventilation system 
through the instrument panel registers in addition to the two side cowl vents 
used with the other heater systems.

The heater case and air inlet duct are located in the engine 
compartment. The plenum, containing the heater core and the necessary air 
ducts, is located in the passenger compartment behind the instrument panel.

During system operation, outside air is drawn into the system by the 
blower motor from the cowl air intake in all function selector lever positions 
except OFF. In the OFF position, the outside air door is closed. In all other 
positions, air is forced by the blower into the plenum and through or around 
the heater core, depending on the setting of the temperature control lever. 
Air is then directed to the floor, defroster nozzles or the instrument panel 
registers depending on the position of the function selector lever.

Airflow volume through the system is controlled by a four-position 
blower switch. The blower switch, used with a resistor assembly, provides four 
blower speeds to control airflow through the system. The blower can be shut 
off only by moving the function selector lever to OFF.

Three vacuum motors are used with the Deluxe Heater system. The 
locations and operations of the motors are as follows:

Outside air door vacuum motor — this motor operates the outside 
air door and is located on top of the air inlet duct. The outside air door is 
open when there is no vacuum applied to this motor.

Panel door vacuum motor — this is the lower motor on the 
passenger side of the plenum to the left of the right register duct. It is 
connected to the panel door inside the plenum and closes the door to the panel 
register ducts with no vacuum.

Floor defrost door vacuum motor — this dual diaphragm vacuum 
motor is located on the passenger side of the plenum above the panel door 
vacuum motor. Vacuum must exist at both diaphragm ports for full travel of the 
motor arm. Vacuum at the top or end port of the motor will give about half 
travel of the motor arm. If vacuum is applied to the side port only, motor 
operation is minimal. If the vacuum hoses to this motor are reversed, the 
motor will not operate properly when the function selector lever is between 
FLOOR and DEFROST.

 Airflow Control 

The climate control assembly is installed in the lower center of the 
instrument panel. It consists of the control head, a nine-port vacuum selector 
valve, cable-controlled temperature selection lever, and the fan (blower) 
speed switch. F-Series vehicles may have an optional fuel tank selector switch 
in the same location.

The temperature control lever controls system temperatures with a cable 
connected between the temperature control lever and the temperature blend door.

The function selector lever actuates a nine-port vacuum selector valve 
which directs vacuum to the various vacuum motors within the system to control 
air discharge from the system. The function selector lever also controls the 
blower motor on-off switch which is part of the nine-port vacuum selector 
valve. Refer to the following Comfort Vent Heater System Airflow illustration, 
which shows the vacuum diagram and the function selector test.

Distribution of air inside the vehicle is controlled by the function 
selector lever. Air can be distributed through the floor outlets, through the 
instrument panel registers, through the defroster outlets, or through the 
floor and defroster outlets.

When the function selector lever is in the OFF position, no air flows 
through the system because the blower is off and the outside air door is 
closed. When the function selector lever is in the PANEL position, air 
distribution is primarily through the instrument panel registers with a small 
amount of air through the floor outlets. When the function selector lever is 
in the FLOOR position, airflow is from the floor outlets. Moving the function 
selector lever to DEF and FLR distributes airflow between the defroster and 
floor outlets. With the function selector lever in DEFROST, airflow is from 
the defroster outlets.

 Temperature Control 

Temperature is controlled by a cable-operated air blend door in the 
plenum assembly. When the temperature control lever is in the COOL (extreme 
left) position, all air bypasses the heater core. When the temperature control 
lever is moved to the extreme right position (warm), all air passes through 
the heater core. When the temperature control lever is between cool and warm 
(extreme left and extreme right), air is directed through and around the 
heater core in proportion to the position of the temperature control lever 
between the extremes of its travel.

 Blower Motor Control 

Blower speeds are controlled by a four-position blower switch and a 
resistor assembly located in the heater case next to the blower wheel. The 
switch is used to select low (LO), two intermediate or high (HI) blower speed. 
The blower is turned off by the function selector lever when it is in the OFF 
position.

With the switch at OFF, the ground circuit of the blower motor is open 
to stop blower operation.

With the switch at LO (lowest dot), current flow in the motor ground 
circuit is through two resistor coils to obtain the lowest motor operating 
speed.

With the switch at MED, current flow in the motor ground circuit is 
through one resistor coil to obtain an intermediate motor operating speed.

 Recirculation/Fresh Air Control 

The outside air door is controlled by the use of a vacuum-controlled 
motor located on top of the air inlet duct. This vacuum-controlled motor opens 
the outside air door in all positions except OFF on the climate control 
assembly. In the OFF position on the climate control assembly, when the engine 
is running, vacuum is applied to the outside air vacuum control motor, which 
closes the outside air door and airflow is stopped from entering the heating 
system. When the function control lever is in any position except OFF, no 
vacuum is applied to the outside air door motor and airflow passing over the 
cowl inlet is allowed to enter the heater system.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor

The heating and defrosting system blower motor is located in the heater 
case in the engine compartment on the right side of the dash panel. The volume 
of air entering the plenum is determined by blower motor speed. As outside air 
enters the opening in the upper cowl, it passes through the blower motor. When 
the ignition switch is in the ON or RUN position the blower motor operates at 
whatever speed is selected at the blower motor switch on the climate control 
assembly. Blower motor operation is interrupted only when the ignition switch 
is OFF or the function selector switch is in the OFF position.

================================================================================
PAGE 3409
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Resistor 

The blower motor resistor is located on the heater case in the engine 
compartment. This resistor contains three resistor coils and a thermal 
limiter. Blower motor speed is determined by the amount of resistor coils 
electrical current must pass through.

When LOW blower motor speed is selected at the climate control 
assembly, electrical current must pass through all three resistor coils and 
the blower motor before reaching the ground circuit.

When MED/LOW speed is selected, electrical current is directed through 
two resistor coils.

When MED/HIGH speed is selected, electrical current is directed through 
only one resistor coil.

In HIGH blower motor speed, electrical current bypasses the blower 
motor resistor and is directed through the blower motor only.

The blower motor resistor is serviced as a complete unit only.

================================================================================
PAGE 3410
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Thermal Limiter 

The resistor assembly also contains a thermal limiter, which is used as 
a temperature protection fuse. The thermal limiter is located a preset 
distance from the resistor coils. If the temperature of the thermal limiter 
reaches 149°C (300°F), the limiter contacts will open interrupting the 
blower motor circuit for all blower speeds except high speed. The thermal 
limiter will not reset and the resistor assembly must be replaced if the 
thermal limiter opens.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Panel Registers

The register ducts consist of two pieces, right and left. The right 
duct is attached to the instrument panel with three screws and is held against 
the plenum to complete the air passage. The left duct connects to the right 
duct and is attached to the instrument panel with four screws at the register 
openings.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Heater Core

The heater core consists of a number of fins and tubes positioned to 
extract available heat from the engine coolant and transfer that heat to the 
air that passes through the core. The heater core is located in the plenum, 
which is installed on the dash panel inside the passenger compartment.

================================================================================
PAGE 3413
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

System Airflow

The Comfort Vent Heater system airflow and vacuum control chart is 
shown in the following illustration. This chart shows the possible airflow 
routes and door positions. Outside air is drawn into the blower housing 
through an opening located under the cowl top grille by the blower motor and 
wheel assembly. From there, the blower wheel forces the outside air through 
and around the heater core. The heated and unheated air then blends together 
as it enters the plenum for distribution to the floor outlets and defroster 
outlets. When the temperature control lever is in an extreme position, COOL or 
WARM, all outside air bypasses or passes through the heater core and no 
blending of air occurs. The vacuum motor chart gives the vacuum applications 
of each vacuum motor for each position of the function selector lever.

 OFF 

When the function control knob is in the OFF position: 

The outside-recirc door is at full vacuum. As a result, outside air is 
closed off and the recirc air is admitted to the system. 

The defrost door and the floor door are both at full vacuum, closing 
off the passages to the defrosters. 

The blend door position may be anywhere within the range of its A/C 
temperature cable travel from FULL HEAT to FULL COLD. 

The heater blower motor is off. 

The panel door is in the no vacuum position. 

 PANEL 

Ventilation is delivered through the instrument panel registers when 
the function control lever in the climate control assembly is set in the PANEL 
position. In the PANEL position, no vacuum is applied to the door motor and 
the outside/recirc door is open to the outside. The air coming in through the 
cowl is discharged through the panel registers.

 FLOOR 

When the function control knob is in the FLOOR position: 

The outside-recirc door is in the no vacuum position to block recirc 
air and admit outside air. 

The floor door is in the vacuum position which closes off all but a 
minimum of airflow to the defroster. 

The blend air door position will channel airflow so that a desired 
temperature level will be achieved. 

The panel door is in the no vacuum position to block air circulation to 
the A/C registers.

The heater blower motor is on. 

The defrost door is at full vacuum, closing off airflow to the 
defroster. 

 DEF and FLR 

When the function control lever is in the DEF and FLR position:

The outside-recirc door is in the no vacuum position to block recirc 
air and admit outside air.

The floor door is in the partial vacuum position, which allows air to 
be distributed equally to the floor and defrost registers.

The panel door is in the no vacuum position to block air circulation to 
the panel registers.

The blend door position will channel airflow so that a desired 
temperature will be achieved.

The heater blower motor is on.

 DEFROST 

When the function control knob is in the DEF position: 

The outside-recirc air door is in the no vacuum position to block 
recirc air and to admit outside air. 

Both the floor and the defrost doors are in the no vacuum position so 
that most of the incoming air is directed to the defroster nozzles. There is a 
slight air bleed to the floor registers. 

The A/C temperature control knob setting will determine the amount of 
heat being introduced into the airflow. 

The heater blower motor is on.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Vacuum Hose Harnesses

Five hoses (black, red, yellow, blue and black/white) extend from the 
climate control assembly to the vacuum control motors and vacuum supply. The 
solid black hose goes to the vacuum supply through a tee-shaped vacuum check 
valve, which attaches the vacuum tank and vacuum source. The red and the 
yellow hoses actuate the three-position vacuum control motor which operates 
the flow-defrost air door. The blue hose connects to the panel door vacuum 
control motor, which controls the airflow to the panel vents. The black/white 
hose connects to the outside air door to control outside airflow into the 
vehicle. The end of each hose slides on to the nipple of the vacuum port to 
which it attaches.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Precautions 

 WARNING: CARBON MONOXIDE IS COLORLESS, ODORLESS AND DANGEROUS. IF NECESSARY TO 
OPERATE THE ENGINE WITH THE VEHICLE IN A CLOSED AREA SUCH AS A GARAGE, ALWAYS 
USE AN EXHAUST COLLECTOR TO VENT THE EXHAUST GAS OUTSIDE THE CLOSED AREA. 

Whenever components in the engine compartment or instrument panel areas 
are being serviced, the battery ground cable must be disconnected to eliminate 
the possibility of electrical shorts. Extreme care must be exercised when 
performing electrical tests where the battery must be connected to operate the 
system.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Assembly

 Removal 

Remove two screws attaching the top of the instrument panel center 
finish panel to the instrument panel pad and remove the finish panel. 

Disconnect the wiring harness connectors from the warning lights and 
switches at top of the panel. 

Remove the knobs from the control assembly by placing a small 
screwdriver between the knob spring retainer and the control assembly. Pull on 
the screwdriver, applying pressure on the spring retainer and pull the knob 
from the control assembly. Repeat this procedure for each knob.

Remove the ash receptacle, the ash receptacle bracket and the floor 
register duct. 

Remove the four control assembly attaching screws. 

Disconnect the wire harness connectors from the blower switch, the 
illumination lamp, the vacuum selector switch and the auxiliary fuel tank 
switch (if so equipped). 

Disconnect the vacuum harness connector from the vacuum selector switch. 

Release bullet connector that attaches the temperature control cable to 
the climate control assembly.

Disconnect the cable from the control assembly. Remove the control 
assembly. 

 Installation 

Transfer the vacuum selector valve, illumination lamp socket and bulb, 
blower switch and the auxiliary fuel tank switch to the new control assembly. 

Install the temperature cable on the temperature lever arm and install 
a new spring nut (Part No. 385129-S2) to retain the cable wire on the lever 
arm. 

Position the temperature cable housing to the control assembly and 
install the attaching screw. 

Connect the vacuum harness to the vacuum selector valve. 

Connect the wire harness connectors to the vacuum selector valve, 
blower switch, illumination lamp socket and the auxiliary fuel tank switch (if 
so equipped). 

Position the control assembly to the instrument panel opening and 
install the four attaching screws. 

Install the floor register duct, the ash receptacle bracket and the ash 
receptacle. 

Connect the wiring harness connectors to the warning lights and 
switches at the top of the panel. 

Position the center finish panel to the instrument panel and install 
the two attaching screws. 

Install the knobs on the control assembly. 

Adjust the temperature control cable. Refer to Temperature Control 
Cable in the Adjustments portion of this section. 

Check the system for proper operation.

Climate Control Cables

 Airflow Control Cable — Standard Heater 

 Removal 

Disengage the function control cable from the cable bracket on the 
passenger side of the plenum. Then disconnect the self-adjusting clip from the 
heat-defrost door crank arm. 

Remove two screws attaching the top of the instrument panel center 
finish panel to the instrument panel pad and remove the finish panel.

Move the control assembly away from the instrument panel.

lever arm and disengage the function control cable from the arm.

 Installation 

Follow the removal procedure in reverse order.

 Temperature Control Cable 

 Removal 

Remove the glove compartment liner. 

Working through the glove compartment opening, remove one screw 
attaching the temperature cable to the cable bracket on top of the plenum. 

Remove the spring nut retaining the temperature cable to the 
temperature door crank arm and disengage the cable from the crank arm. 

Remove two screws attaching the top of the center finish panel to the 
instrument panel pad and remove the finish panel. 

Disconnect the wiring harness connectors from the warning lights and 
switches at the top of the panel. 

Remove the ash receptacle and ash receptacle bracket. 

Remove four control assembly attaching screws. 

Move the control assembly away from the instrument panel and remove the 
screw attaching the temperature cable housing to the control assembly. It may 
be necessary to disconnect the vacuum and wire harnesses from the control 
assembly to remove the cable attaching screw. 

Disengage the temperature control cable from the arm. 

 Installation 

Connect the temperature control cable to the temperature lever arm of 
the control assembly. 

Position the cable housing bullet connector to the control assembly and 
install the attaching screw. 

Position the control assembly to the instrument panel opening and 
install the four attaching screws. Connect the vacuum and wire harnesses to 
the control assembly if it was necessary to disconnect them during removal. 

Install the ash receptacle bracket and ash receptacle. 

Connect the wiring harness connectors to the warning lights and 
switches at the top of the panel. 

Position the center finish panel to the instrument panel and install 
the two attaching screws. 

Route the temperature control cable as shown in the illustration, and 
connect the pigtail to the temperature door crank arm with the pigtail 
pointing up away from the bend in the crank arm. Install the spring nut to 
retain the cable on the door crank arm. 

Position the cable housing mounting tab to the mounting bracket and 
install the attaching screw. 

Adjust the temperature control cable. Refer to Temperature Control 
Cable in the Adjustments portion of this section. 

Install the glove compartment liner and check the system for proper 
operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Instrument Panel Registers

 Register Louver Assembly 

 Removal 

Insert a thin blade under the retaining tab and pry the retaining tab 
toward the louvers until the retaining tab pivot clears the hole in the 
register opening. 

Pull the register louver assembly end out from the housing only enough 
to prevent the pivot from going back into the pivot hole. 

Repeat Step 1 for the other retaining tab and pull the register louver 
assembly from the register opening. 

[FIGURE: L3409B.gif]

 Installation 

The pivots on each end of the register louver assembly are different 
diameters and therefore determine the installed position of the register 
louver assembly. 

Position the register louver assembly into the opening with the largest 
diameter pivot near the largest pivot hole. 

Depress the retaining tabs, push the register louver assembly into the 
register opening and engage the retainer tab pivots in the pivot holes.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Heater Case

 Removal 

Disconnect the blower motor wires and the blower motor resistor wires. 

Disconnect the vacuum supply hose at the vacuum reservoir and the small 
vacuum hose at the check valve. Reposition the check valve away from the 
heater case. 

Disconnect the heater hoses from the heater core and plug the hoses 
with suitable 16-mm (5/8-inch) plugs.

Working in the passenger compartment, remove two screws attaching the

edge of the plenum to the dash panel.

of the plenum and tuck the harness coming from the air duct opening back into 
the opening. 

Remove two screws attaching the right side of the air duct to the dash 
panel. 

Remove two retaining nuts attaching the heater case and the air duct to 
the dash panel. 

Pull the heater case and air duct forward and remove from the vehicle. 

Remove five screws attaching the air duct to the heater case and remove 
duct.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Heater Core 

 Removal 

Disconnect the heater hoses from the heater core tubes and plug the 
hoses with suitable 16-mm (5/8-inch) plugs. 

Remove the glove compartment liner.

from the core. 

 Installation 

Install the heater core in the plenum. 

Install the heater core cover (seven screws along the top edge of the 
cover). 

Install the glove compartment liner.

2.3-2.8 Nm (20-25 lb-in).

 Section 03-03 . 

Check the system for proper operation and for coolant leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Plenum Chamber and Duct 

 Removal 

Disconnect the ground cable from the battery negative terminal.

Remove the instrument panel pad. Refer to Section 01-12 . 

Remove the right and left cowl side trim panels (if so equipped). 

Remove the parking brake release and the hood latch release handles 
from the lower edge of the instrument panel. 

Remove the lower trim cover from the steering column opening of the 
instrument panel. 

Remove four screws attaching the steering column seal and seal retainer 
to the dash panel. 

Remove two nuts attaching the steering column clamp to the brake pedal 
support and allow the steering column to be lowered down toward the seat. 

Disconnect the speedometer cable connector from the speedometer. 

Disconnect the heater hoses from the heater core tubes and plug the 
hoses with suitable 5/8-inch plugs. 

Remove one screw attaching the left end of the plenum to the dash panel. 

Remove one screw attaching the lower center of the plenum to the dash 
panel. 

Remove two nuts attaching the heater case and plenum to the dash panel. 

Remove one screw attaching each lower end of the instrument panel to 
the side cowl. 

Disconnect the two instrument panel support center braces from the 
lower edge of the instrument panel (one screw each).

Remove one screw attaching the instrument panel to the brake pedal 
support at the steering column opening. 

Remove the defroster nozzle. Refer to Defroster Ducts in the Removal 
and Installation portion of this section. 

Place a protective cover over the steering column and support the 
instrument panel. 

Disconnect the wires from the right door courtesy lamp switch (if so 
equipped). 

Disconnect the antenna lead-in cable from the radio (if so equipped). 
Refer to Section 15-01 . 

Remove one screw attaching the upper right and left corners of the 
instrument panel to the cowl at the windshield lower corners. 

Position the instrument panel right end rearward as necessary to 
provide clearance to remove the plenum. If necessary, disconnect any wires, 
cables or vacuum hoses to prevent the instrument panel from moving to the rear.

Disconnect the temperature door cable and vacuum harnesses from the 
plenum and remove the plenum from the vehicle.

Blower Motor and Blower Motor Wheel Assembly

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Temperature Control Door 

 Removal 

Remove the heater case from the vehicle. Refer to Heater Case in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Remove nine screws and one bolt and nut attaching the heater housing 
plate to the heater case, and remove the heater housing plate. 

Remove three screws attaching the heater core frame to the heater case 
and remove the frame. 

Remove the heater core and seal from the heater case. 

Remove four screws attaching the temperature door frame to the heater 
case and remove the frame. 

Remove one screw retaining the temperature door on the door shaft. Then 
open the clamp on the door with a screwdriver and remove the door from the 
shaft. 

Remove the temperature door shaft from the heater case. 

 Installation 

Place the flatwasher on the door end of the temperature door shaft so 
that the washer rides against the shoulder on the shaft. 

Insert the temperature door shaft into the heater case from the top of 
the case. 

Position the temperature blend door to the shaft and install the 
retaining screw. 

Position the temperature door frame in the heater case and install the 
four attaching screws. 

Place Caulking Cord D6AZ-19560-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M4G32-A around the temperature door frame to seal against 
air leakage. DO NOT put sealer on the door side of the temperature door frame. 

Position the heater core and seal in the heater case. 

Install the heater core frame (three screws). 

Position the heater housing plate on the heater case and install the 
nine screws and one bolt and nut. 

Install the heater case in the vehicle. Refer to Heater Case in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Inlet Duct Door 

 Removal 

Remove the outside air duct. 

Remove the spring nut retaining the vacuum motor arm to the air door 
shaft crank arm. Disconnect the motor arm from the shaft crank arm. 

Remove one screw attaching the air door to the door shaft and remove 
the door. 

Remove the spring nut from the bottom of the door shaft and remove the 
shaft from the air duct. 

 Installation 

Insert the door shaft into the air duct and install the spring nut on 
the bottom of the shaft. 

Position the door on the door shaft and install the door attaching 
screw from the grille side. 

Connect the vacuum motor arm to the shaft crank arm with the flatwasher 
below the arm and the spring nut above to retain the motor arm on the shaft 
crank arm. The offset of the motor arm must be up. 

Install the outside air duct in the vehicle and check the system for 
proper operation.

================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Windshield Defroster Door 

 Removal 

Remove the plenum from the vehicle. Refer to Air Plenum Chamber and 
Duct in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Remove the spring nut retaining the floor-defrost door vacuum motor arm 
on the door shaft crank arm. Disengage the motor arm from the door shaft crank 
arm. 

Remove the heater core cover (seven screws). 

Remove the heater core and seal from the plenum. 

Remove two screws attaching the panel door hinge to the case top half. 

Peel back the dash panel seal and drill out three rivets attaching the 
case top half to the temperature door frame. 

Peel the heater core seal away from the sealing flange of the case top 
half inside the heater core cavity. 

Remove one screw and drill out six rivets attaching the case top to the 
case bottom and separate the case. 

Remove one screw retaining the floor-defrost door on the door shaft and 
remove the door from the shaft. 

Remove the door shaft from the lower case. 

 Installation 

Position the door shaft in the lower case and install the door on the 
shaft. Install one screw to retain the door on the shaft. 

Assemble the case halves and install one screw and six 5-mm (3/16-inch) 
pop rivets around the case flange to attach the halves together using Rotunda 
Blind Fastener Installation Tool 107-R0600 or equivalent.

Install two screws to attach the panel door hinge to the top half of 
the case. 

Install three 5-mm (3/16-inch) pop rivets behind the dash panel seal to 
attach the top half of the case to the temperature door housing using Rotunda 
Blind Fastener Installation Tool 107-R0600 or equivalent.

Cement the dash panel seal to the plenum with Liquid Butyl Sealer 
C9AZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G162-A. 

Cement the heater core seal to the cavity flange of the case top half. 

Install the heater core and top seal in the plenum and install the 
heater core cover (seven screws along the top edge of the cover). 

Install the heater core tube seal on the heater core tubes. 

Install the plenum in the vehicle. 

Check the system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Panel-Defrost Door 

 Removal 

Remove the plenum from the vehicle. Refer to Air Plenum Chamber and 
Duct in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Remove the spring nut retaining the floor-defrost door vacuum motor arm 
on the door shaft crank arm. 

Remove the heater core cover (seven screws). 

Remove the heater core and seal from the plenum. 

Remove two screws attaching the panel door hinge to the case top half. 

Peel back the dash panel seal and drill out three rivets attaching the 
case top half to the temperature door frame. 

Peel the heater core seal away from the sealing flange of the case top 
half inside the heater core cavity. 

Remove one screw and six rivets attaching the case top to the case 
bottom and separate the case. 

Remove the sleeve nut attaching the vacuum motor arm to the panel door 
hinge. 

 CAUTION: DO NOT grind the heads from the rivets as they will overheat and damage 
the case lower half. 

Drill out the two rivets attaching the panel door hinge to the case 
lower half and remove the door and hinge assembly.

 Installation 

Position the panel door and hinge to the case lower half and rivet the 
hinge in place with two 5-mm (3/16-inch) diameter pop rivets, using Rotunda 
Blind Fastener Installation Tool 107-R0600 or equivalent.

Position the vacuum motor arm to the door hinge and install the sleeve 
nut.

Assemble the plenum case halves and install six 5-mm (3/16-inch) pop 
rivets, using Rotunda Blind Fastener Installation Tool 107-R0600 or 
equivalent, and one screw around the case flange to attach the halves 
together. 

Install two 5-mm (3/16-inch) pop rivets to attach the panel door hinge 
to the top half of the case, using Rotunda Blind Fastener Installation Tool 
107-R0600 or equivalent. 

Install three 5-mm (3/16-inch) pop rivets behind the dash panel seal to 
attach the top half of the case to the temperature door housing, using Rotunda 
Blind Fastener Installation Tool 107-R0600 or equivalent.

Cement the dash panel seal to the plenum with Liquid Butyl Sealer 
C9AZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G162-A. 

Cement the heater core seal to the cavity flange of the case top half. 

Install the heater core and top seal in the plenum and install the 
heater core cover (seven screws along the top edge of the cover). 

Install the tube seal on the heater core tubes. 

Install the plenum in the vehicle and check the system for proper 
operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Vacuum Control Motors

 Air Inlet Duct Door 

 Removal 

Disconnect the vacuum hose from the vacuum motor. 

Remove the spring nut retaining the vacuum motor arm on the outside air 
door crank arm. 

Loosen the two motor retaining nuts and lift the motor from the 
mounting bracket. 

 Installation 

Position the vacuum motor to the mounting bracket and the vacuum motor 
arm to the outside air door crank arm and follow the removal procedure in 
reverse order. Check for proper operation. 

 Windshield Defroster Door 

 Removal 

Remove the spring nut retaining the vacuum motor arm on the door shaft 
crank arm. 

Remove two nuts retaining the vacuum motor on the mounting bracket. 

Disengage the vacuum motor from the crank arm and the mounting bracket. 
Disconnect the vacuum hoses from the motor. 

 Installation 

Connect the vacuum hoses to the motor. The yellow hose connects to the 
end port and the red hose to the side port. 

Position the vacuum motor to the mounting bracket and the door crank 
arm. Be sure the flatwasher is installed on the door crank arm before 
installing the motor on the crank arm. 

Install two nuts to attach the vacuum motor to the mounting bracket. 

Install a new spring nut (Part No. 383358-S) to retain the motor arm on 
the door crank arm. 

Check the system for proper operation. 

 Floor Duct Door 

 Removal 

Remove the glove compartment door, hinge and liner. 

Remove the heater core cover (eight screws). 

Remove the floor duct from the plenum (two screws). 

Working through the floor duct and heater core cover openings, remove 
the sleeve nut retaining the vacuum motor arm to the floor duct door hinge. 
This sleeve nut has two barbs on the bottom which must be squeezed together to 
facilitate removal. 

Disconnect the vacuum hose from the vacuum motor. 

Remove two screws attaching the vacuum motor to the mounting bracket 
and remove the vacuum motor.

 Installation 

Follow the removal procedure in reverse order, using a new sleeve nut 
(Part No. 385024-S2) on the vacuum motor arm. Check the system for proper 
operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Heater Water Hoses 

 Removal

 Installation

Route the heater hose(s) as shown in the following illustrations, 
depending on vehicle/engine application. 

Connect the heater hose to the fittings and tighten the clamps to 
2.3-2.8 Nm (20-25 lb-in). DO NOT overtighten the hose clamps. 

Fill and bleed the cooling system to the specified level. Refer to 
 Section 03-03 .

Check for coolant leaks and for proper operation of the system.

ADJUSTMENTS

Airflow Selector Cable

The airflow control cable is self-adjusting with the movement of the 
control lever to the right end of the slot (DEFROST). To prevent kinking of 
the control cable wire, a preset adjustment should be made before attempting 
to perform the self-adjustment operation. The preset adjustment can be 
performed either in the vehicle with the cable installed or before 
installation of the cable.

ADJUSTMENTS

Temperature Control Cable 

Remove the glove compartment liner. 

Loosen the temperature control cable attaching screw at the cable 
bracket located on top of the plenum. 

Position the temperature control lever 1.59 mm (1/16 inch) from the 
left (blue) end of the lever slot of the control assembly. 

Rotate the temperature door crank arm to the extreme left and tighten 
the cable attaching screw. 

Move the temperature control lever from left to right and check to make 
sure the lever bounces back slightly at both ends of the slot. If bounce-back 
does not occur at both ends of the slot, readjust the cable to obtain 
bounce-back of the lever at each end of the slot. 

Install the glove compartment liner.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

R-134a Refrigerant System

All Ford Truck A/C systems use R-134a refrigerant. The system operation 
is similar to the old R-12 refrigerant system except it requires its own 
refrigerant oil and the R-134a system does not harm the environment when used 
properly. R-134a and R-12 should not be used in the same system, as these two 
refrigerant systems are not compatible. If a component has been used in an 
R-12 system, it should not be used in an R-134a system. If R-12 and R-134a 
components are used within the same system, internal damage and system failure 
will occur.

================================================================================
PAGE 3447
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 12-03A: Air Conditioning System, Manual A/C-Heater, F-Series

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C-Heater System, Manual

The manual air conditioner-heater system uses a plate-fin evaporator 
core with an accumulator/drier, a fixed orifice tube for refrigerant flow 
control replacing the expansion valve, and a pressure cycling switch to 
control clutch cycling in place of the de-icing switch.

During system operation, outside air is drawn into the system by the 
blower motor and wheel from the cowl air intake in all function selector lever 
settings except OFF and MAX A/C. In the MAX A/C position, airflow is drawn 
from inside the vehicle through the recirculating air duct. The air is then 
forced by the blower through the evaporator core and, depending on the setting 
of the temperature lever, is forced through and around the heater core into 
the plenum. Air is then directed to the floor, defrost nozzles or the 
instrument panel registers depending on the position of the function selector 
lever.

Airflow volume through the system is controlled by a four-position 
blower switch. The blower switch, used with a resistor assembly, provides four 
blower speeds to control airflow through the system. The blower can be shut 
off only by moving the function selector lever to OFF.

 Manual Air Conditioner, Heater System Air Distribution

To test the air conditioner-heater control system, start the engine and 
move the function selector lever slowly from one position to another. A 
momentary hiss should be heard as the function selector lever is moved from 
one position to another indicating that vacuum is available at the control 
assembly. A continuous hiss at the control assembly indicates a major leak 
somewhere in the system. It does not necessarily indicate that the leak is at 
the control assembly.

If a momentary hiss cannot be heard when the function selector lever is 
moved from one position to another, check for a kinked, pinched or 
disconnected vacuum supply hose. Also inspect the check valve in the supply 
line (located above the evaporator assembly) to make sure it is working 
properly.

Vacuum is supplied by the vacuum manifold on gasoline engine-powered 
vehicles, by the vacuum generator on diesel engine-powered vehicles equipped 
with air brakes, and by the vacuum compressor on diesel engine-powered 
vehicles without air brakes.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ventilation System

Distribution of air inside the vehicle is controlled by the function 
selector lever. Air can be distributed through the floor outlets, through the 
instrument panel registers, through the defroster outlets, or through the 
floor and defroster outlets.

When the function selector lever is in the OFF position, no air flows 
through the system because the fan is off and the outside-recirc. door is 
closed to outside air. When the function selector lever is in PANEL, MAX A/C 
or A/C, air distribution is through the instrument panel registers. When the 
function selector lever is in the FLOOR position, airflow is from the floor 
outlets. Moving the function selector lever to the DEF & FLR position, 
airflow is distributed between the defroster and floor outlets. With the 
function selector lever in the DEFROST position, airflow is from the defroster 
outlets.

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Climate Control Assembly

The climate control assembly is installed in the lower center of the 
instrument panel. It consists of the control head, a nine-port vacuum selector 
valve and the blower speed switch. Some vehicles have an optional fuel tank 
selector switch on the right side of the control.

The temperature control lever controls system temperatures with a cable 
connected between the temperature control lever and the temperature blend 
door. The function selector lever operates the nine-port vacuum selector valve 
to control the system's three vacuum motors and the compressor clutch and 
blower motor electrical circuits.

 Airflow Control 

The function selector lever actuates a nine-port vacuum selector valve 
which directs vacuum to vacuum motors within the system to control air source 
intake and air discharge from the system. The function selector lever also 
operates the blower on-off switch and the air conditioner compressor clutch 
operating circuit. However, the actual cycling of the clutch is dependent on 
the position of the function selector lever and the pressure switch in the 
refrigerant system. Both switches must be closed to energize the clutch for 
compressor operation.

 Temperature Control 

Temperature is controlled by a cable-operated air blend door in the 
plenum assembly. When the temperature control lever is in the extreme left 
(COOL) position, all air is directed around the heater core. When the 
temperature control lever is moved to the extreme right (WARM) position, all 
air is directed through the heater core. When the temperature control lever is 
between COOL and WARM (between extreme left and extreme right), air is 
directed through and around the heater core in proportion to the position of 
the temperature control lever between the extremes of its travel.

 Blower Motor Control 

Blower speeds are controlled by a four-position blower switch and a 
resistor assembly located in the evaporator case upstream from the evaporator 
core. The switch is used to select low, two intermediate or high blower 
speeds. The blower is turned off by the function selector lever when it is in 
the OFF position. This is accomplished by a switch integral with the nine-port 
vacuum selector attached to the control assembly.

The blower motor is installed in the blower housing which is part of 
the evaporator case. The motor is connected to the electrical circuit with two 
hardshell connectors located near the motor.

The blower speed switch is installed on the control assembly and, with 
the blower resistor, provides the selection of four blower operating speeds. 
This switch does not turn the blower off.

 A/C Switch 

The air conditioning system is turned on and off by the function 
selector lever. When the lever is set in A/C (MAX, A/C, DEF & FLR, or DEF) 
positions, electrical current flows through the A/C cycling switch to the A/C 
compressor clutch field coil; the A/C clutch engages and the air conditioning 
system is on when the knob is in the DEF & FLR, or DEF modes. Current also 
flows through the A/C cycling switch to the A/C compressor clutch field coil. 
This allows the operator to select fully cool air, if needed, for defogging 
the windshield. When the lever is moved to other functions, current is stopped 
to the A/C compressor clutch field coil and the air conditioning system is off.

 Vacuum Hoses 

Airflow direction is controlled through vacuum being applied to one of 
three vacuum controlled motors within the A/C system. Vacuum is directed to 
the various motors through a vacuum hose harness which is made up of five 
color-coded vacuum hoses: black, white, blue, red and yellow. Each of these 
hoses serves a different function within the A/C system.

The black hose is the vacuum source hose. It delivers source vacuum to 
the nine-port function selector valve. At the valve, vacuum is directed to the 
port which corresponds with the function selector lever.

When the function selector lever is set in the OFF position, vacuum is 
delivered through the white vacuum hose to the recirc/fresh air door vacuum 
controlled motor to prevent outside air from entering the system.

When the function selector lever is set in the MAX A/C position, vacuum 
is delivered through the white vacuum hose to the recirc/fresh air door vacuum 
controlled motor to prevent outside air from entering the system. Vacuum is 
also delivered through the blue vacuum hose to the panel door vacuum 
controlled motor to direct airflow through the panel registers.

When the function selector lever is set in the A/C or PANEL position, 
no vacuum is directed to the recirc/fresh air door vacuum-controlled motor 
through the white vacuum hose to allow outside air to enter the system. The 
function selector valve does direct vacuum through the blue vacuum hose to the 
panel door vacuum-controlled motor to allow airflow to discharge through the 
panel registers.

When the function control lever is placed in the FLOOR position, no 
vacuum is delivered through the white vacuum hose to allow outside air to 
enter the system. Vacuum is delivered through the red and yellow vacuum hoses 
to allow the three-position defrost/floor vacuum-controlled motor to direct 
airflow to the floor air duct.

When the function control lever is set in the DEF & FLR position, 
no vacuum is delivered to the white vacuum hose to allow outside air to enter 
the system. Vacuum is delivered to the yellow vacuum hose, which operates the 
def/flr vacuum-controlled motor and sets the def/flr door in a mid-position 
allowing airflow to be directed to both the floor and defrost outlets.

When the function selector lever is set in the DEF position, no vacuum 
is delivered to the white vacuum hose to allow outside air to enter the 
system, and no vacuum is applied to any of the three vacuum-controlled motors. 
This directs all airflow to the defrost registers.
