DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Resistor

The blower motor resistor is installed in the evaporator case between 
the blower motor and the evaporator core. The resistor is used with the blower 
speed switch to provide four blower speeds.

 Blower Motor Thermal Limiter 

The resistor assembly also contains a thermal limiter which is used as 
a temperature protecting fuse. The thermal limiter is located a preset 
distance from the resistor coils. If the temperature of the thermal limiter 
reaches approximately 149°C (300°F), the limiter contacts will open 
interrupting the blower motor circuit for all blower speeds except high speed. 
The thermal limiter will not reset and the resistor assembly must be replaced 
if the thermal limiter opens.

[FIGURE: L32451A.gif]

The clutch, thermal protection switch and the pressure switches are 
connected in series to control compressor operation. The clutch switch is an 
integral part of the nine-port vacuum valve and is closed when the function 
selector lever is in MAX A/C, A/C, DEF, DEF & FLR (between FLOOR and DEF).

The pressure switch is located on the side of the suction accumulator 
and controls the compressor clutch cycling. When the evaporator pressure 
increases to approximately 295 kPa (42.5 psi), the switch closes. When the 
pressure drops to approximately 175 kPa (25.5 psi), the switch opens to stop 
compressor operation. In ambient temperatures below approximately 7°C 
(45°F), the pressure switch will not allow compressor operation because of 
low system pressures.

The thermal protection switch is located in the rear head of the 
compressor and will automatically shut down operation by interrupting the 
electrical power to the compressor clutch when the compressor temperature 
exceeds approximately 116°C (240°F). The compressor will automatically 
restart when it has cooled to approximately 99°C (210°F). A CHECK A/C 
warning light is mounted on the instrument panel. Illumination of the CHECK 
A/C warning light is an indication the thermal protection system has been 
activated and air conditioning system service is required.

To service the thermal protection switch, refer to Section 12-03B .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Vacuum Control Motors

Three vacuum control motors are used with the manual air 
conditioner-heater system. The locations and operations of the motors are as 
follows:

Heater and A/C air inlet-recirculating door vacuum motor — This 
motor is used to operate the outside-recirc. door and is located on top of the 
air inlet duct in the engine compartment. It opens the outside-recirc. door to 
outside air with no vacuum.

Panel door vacuum motor — This is the lower motor on the 
passenger side of the plenum to the left of the right register duct. It is 
connected to the panel door inside the plenum and closes the door to the panel 
register ducts with no vacuum.

Floor-windshield defroster door vacuum motor — A dual diaphragm 
vacuum motor located on the passenger side of the plenum above the panel door 
vacuum motor. Vacuum must exist at both diaphragm ports for full travel of the 
motor arm. Vacuum at the top or end port of the motor will give about half 
travel of the motor arm. If vacuum is applied to the side port only, motor 
operation is minimal. If the vacuum hoses to this motor are reversed, the 
motor will not operate properly when the function selector lever is between 
the FLOOR and DEF positions.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

System Airflow Description

System airflow is controlled by a nine-port vacuum selector valve 
attached to the control assembly. This valve controls vacuum to operate the 
vacuum motors and also contains the on-off switches for the blower motor and 
the clutch circuit. System air temperature is regulated by a temperature blend 
door controlled by cable from the temperature control lever.

 OFF 

Function control lever in the OFF position turns off the entire climate 
control system, including the blower motor.

 MAX A/C 

Move the temperature control lever to far left, the function control 
lever to MAX A/C, and the fan switch to HI. This will recirculate air in the 
vehicle for maximum cooling (recommended for extremely hot or humid weather).

 A/C 

For outside air operation, set the function control lever to A/C. After 
the vehicle is cool, adjust the temperature control and fan switch lever to 
maintain the desired temperature. A/C operation is recommended whenever 
climate or traffic conditions permit and maximum cooling is not required.

The cooled air is directed through the instrument panel registers. The 
registers can be adjusted to direct the air as desired. These registers can 
also be closed to block most of the airflow. However, closing more than two 
registers at once is not recommended.

 PANEL 

To ventilate your vehicle, move the function control lever to PANEL. 
When the lever is moved from OFF, the fan automatically starts. Set the fan 
switch to the desired speed. The outside air is directed to the instrument 
panel registers. Adjust the air temperature as desired using the temperature 
control lever.

The side and rear windows can be defrosted by directing warm air at 
them from the instrument panel registers with the function control lever at 
PANEL.

The air conditioning system can be used to defog the side windows in 
mild weather. Set the function control lever to A/C, and the fan switch to a 
high speed, then adjust the temperature lever for comfort. Adjust the 
instrument panel registers to direct air onto the windows.

 FLOOR 

For maximum heating with outside air, move the temperature lever to far 
right, the function control lever to FLOOR, and the fan switch to HI. Air is 
directed through the floor ducts. As the vehicle warms up, adjust the fan 
switch and temperature control lever to the desired position.

 DEF & FLR 

Airflow can be split between the floor ducts and the defroster by 
setting the function control lever at the DEF & FLR position.

 DEF 

To defrost the windshield, move the temperature control lever to the 
far right, the function control lever to DEF, and the fan switch to HI.

1999 F700, F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Refrigerant System

The manual air conditioner-heater refrigerant system uses a compressor, 
a condenser, an evaporator core with a fixed orifice in the liquid line tube, 
a suction accumulator with an integral drier, a pressure switch, service 
access gauge port valves and the necessary refrigerant lines. Some vehicles 
will also have manual valves at the compressor and a self-sealing coupling in 
the liquid line at the condenser.

During established (air conditioning system shutdown) conditions, 
refrigerant system pressures are equalized on both the high and low sides of 
the refrigerant system.

When the function control lever is moved to DEF or any A/C position, 
the air conditioner compressor magnetic clutch field coil is energized and the 
clutch plate is pulled into contact with the belt-driven compressor clutch 
pulley. The clutch plate and hub assembly then rotate the compressor shaft.

When the compressor shaft is rotated, the pistons are alternately 
pulled out and forced into their respective cylinder bores. As each piston is 
pulled from its cylinder bore, the pressure in the cylinder suddenly reduces 
to a pressure (or vacuum) considerably lower than the refrigerant vapor 
pressure on the suction side of the refrigerant system. The higher refrigerant 
system vapor pressure overcomes the suction reed valve spring pressure, 
forcing itself through the reed valve and into the lower pressure (or vacuum) 
area inside the compressor cylinder. The spring pressure on the reed valve 
closes the valve when the refrigerant system suction vapor pressure and the 
compressor cylinder vapor pressure are equalized.

As each piston is forced into its respective cylinder bore, the 
refrigerant vapors from the suction side of the refrigerant system are 
compressed into a decreasingly smaller area, thus increasing the refrigerant 
vapor pressure and also raising the refrigerant vapor temperature. The higher 
refrigerant vapor pressure now assists in sealing the suction reed valve 
closed and also opens the discharge (high-pressure) reed valve as the cylinder 
pressure exceeds the higher pressure side of the refrigerant system. When the 
compressed higher pressure and temperature refrigerant vapor is discharged 
into the high-pressure side of the refrigerant system, the discharge reed 
valve spring pressure and the high side refrigerant pressure closes and seals 
the reed valve, thus preventing the discharge pressure from re-entering the 
compressor cylinder. The compressor's refrigerant vapor compression cycle 
begins again as the pistons are again pulled from their respective compressor 
cylinder bores by the rotating compressor shaft.

The high-pressure and high-temperature compressor discharge refrigerant 
vapor is released into the top of the condenser assembly, via the compressor 
discharge hose. The condenser, being close to ambient temperature, causes the 
refrigerant vapor to condense into a liquid when heat is removed from the 
refrigerant vapor by ambient air passing over the condenser fins and tubing.

Liquid refrigerant from the bottom of the condenser passes through a 
filter in the condenser liquid line and enters the high-pressure liquid line 
and then the inlet side of the fixed orifice tube located in the evaporator 
inlet tube. The inlet filter screen of the fixed orifice tube assembly removes 
coarse contaminant particulates, which may be present in the liquid 
refrigerant, before the liquid refrigerant enters the calibrated opening of 
the fixed orifice tube. The outlet end of the orifice tube assembly has a fine 
mesh filter with four open side slots in the body of the tube assembly, 
upstream from the filter. This filter removes fine contaminants and allows 
some of the refrigerant to exit through the non-filtered side slots. The side 
slots and filter act as a refrigerant flow suppressor.

Evaporator pressure is reduced as a result of air conditioner 
compressor suction. As the evaporator pressure is lowered and the liquid line 
pressure increases, the liquid refrigerant passes through the fixed orifice 
tube and enters the evaporator at a low pressure and as a cold liquid. As 
airflow passes over the plate-fin sections of the evaporator core, the 
refrigerant inside absorbs the heat and changes into a vapor.

Compressor suction draws the vaporized refrigerant and oil mixture into 
the suction accumulator/drier where the heavier oil-laden vapors fall to the 
bottom and the lighter vapors and oil mixture continue their path to the 
compressor via the top of the vapor return tube. A desiccant bag, located 
inside the suction accumulator/drier, absorbs and retains moisture which may 
be circulating in the refrigerant system. The heavier oil-laden refrigerant 
also returns to the compressor through a small liquid bleed hole near the 
bottom of the vapor return tube. The liquid bleed hole provides a controlled 
second opportunity for the accumulated refrigerant and oil mixture to 
revaporize as it passes through the opening to re-enter into the main vapor 
flow path to the suction side of the compressor.

 Service Access Gauge Port Valves 

The high-pressure valve is located near the compressor in the discharge 
line between the A/C compressor and A/C condenser core and has a 
quick-disconnect type valve body. This requires a special high-pressure 
service access valve adapter to connect a manifold gauge set or a charging 
station to the valve. The other service access gauge port valve is located on 
the inlet of the suction accumulator and is used to measure evaporator 
pressure. In addition, some vehicles have valves at the compressor. However, 
these valves do not have service ports and can be used only to service the 
compressor.

Some vehicles are equipped with manual valves at the compressor similar 
to manual service valves. These valves do not have service ports and are used 
to isolate the compressor. DO NOT mistake these manual valves for manual 
service valves.

The compressor discharge line has a service access gauge port valve 
located near the compressor. This is the high pressure service port. Use of a 
suitable high side adapter set is necessary to connect a manifold gauge set or 
a charging station to this service port.

 A/C Evaporator Core 

The evaporator core is a flooded type (plate/fin) core. The liquid line 
connects to the bottom of the core and the suction (low pressure) line 
connects to the top of the core. A liquid bleed line is not used in this 
system. The liquid line tube is fitted with a fixed orifice tube to control 
refrigerant flow. This orifice tube can be removed from the evaporator core 
tube for replacement if necessary. However, Fixed Orifice Tube Tool 
D80L-19990-A or equivalent is required to prevent breaking the orifice tube.

 A/C Evaporator Core Orifice 

The fixed orifice tube meters the flow of liquid refrigerant during 
cool-down (while the vehicle interior and evaporator core are cooling down). 
After initial system start-up, compressor suction pressure drops, the 
evaporator core pressure reduces toward 179 kPa (26.0 psi), and the evaporator 
fin temperature approaches freezing, the clutch cycling pressure switch then 
opens the compressor clutch coil circuit to disengage the compressor clutch 
and prevent evaporator icing.

The fixed orifice tube is located in the evaporator inlet tube and has 
filter screens located on the inlet and outlet ends of the tube body. The 
filter screens act as a strainer for the liquid refrigerant flowing through 
the fixed orifice opening. O-rings, on the tube body, prevent the 
high-pressure liquid refrigerant from bypassing the orifice. Adjustment or 
repairs cannot be made to fixed orifice tube assembly and it must be replaced 
as a unit.

 Suction Accumulator/Drier 

The suction accumulator/drier is mounted on the side of the evaporator 
core and attaches directly to the evaporator outlet tube. A suction service 
access gauge port valve is mounted on the inlet fitting of the suction 
accumulator/drier.

Its purpose is to provide service access to the suction side of the 
refrigerant system for pressure readings and system diagnosis.

An inverted liquid diverter cup is internally mounted on top of the 
refrigerant vapor return tube, in the center of the suction accumulator/drier 
to prevent the heavier oil-laden liquid refrigerant from going directly into 
the compressor suction line.

Upon entering the inlet of the suction accumulator/drier, heavier 
oil-laden refrigerant contacts the liquid diverter cup, which serves as an 
umbrella, and drips down onto the bottom of the housing. A small-diameter oil 
bleed hole, approximately 8 mm (3/10 inch) above the bottom of the housing, 
allows the accumulated heavier liquid refrigerant and oil mixture to re-enter 
the compressor suction line at a controlled rate.

As the heavier liquid refrigerant and oil mixture pass through the 
small-diameter liquid bleed hole, it has a second opportunity to revaporize 
and recirculate through the compressor without causing compressor damage due 
to slugging.

A fine mesh-screened filter fits tightly around the bottom of the vapor 
return tube to filter out refrigerant system contaminant particles and prevent 
them from plugging the oil bleed hole.

A desiccant bag is mounted inside the suction accumulator/drier tank 
assembly to absorb any moisture which may be in the refrigerant system.

Another fitting, on the side and close to the top of the suction 
accumulator/drier, is used to mount the A/C cycling switch. It has a long 
travel valve stem core installed in the fitting opening to prevent refrigerant 
loss when the A/C cycling switch is removed.

 NOTE: A good practice is to replace the accumulator/drier any time the 
refrigeration system is opened. This is because an opened system should have a 
fresh desiccant bag, and the desiccant is serviced only in the accumulator 
assembly. Replacement of the accumulator is essential if any of the following 
conditions exist:

Evidence of moisture in the system.

Evaporator replacement due to internal corrosion.

Suction accumulator/drier housing punctured.

The accumulator contains more than 148 ml (5 oz) of compressor oil, 
indicating that the bleed hole is clogged. Be sure to make this check if the 
compressor is replaced for lack of performance.

 A/C Cycling Switch 

The A/C cycling switch is mounted on a valve fitting on the side of the 
suction accumulator/drier assembly. A valve depressor, located inside the 
threaded end of the pressure switch, presses in on the valve stem as the 
switch is mounted and allows the suction pressure inside the accumulator/drier 
housing to activate the switch.

The electrical switch contacts are normally open when the suction 
pressure is at or below 179 kPa (26 psi). They will close when the suction 
pressure rises to approximately 310 kPa (45 psi) or above. Lower ambient 
temperatures (below approximately 9°C or 48°F), during cold weather 
seasons, will also open the clutch cycling pressure switch contacts due to the 
pressure/temperature relationship of the refrigerant in the system.

The electrical switch contacts control the electrical circuit to the 
compressor's magnetic clutch coil. When the switch contacts are closed, the 
clutch coil is energized and the air conditioner clutch is engaged to drive 
the compressor. When the switch contacts are open, the compressor's magnet 
clutch coil is de-energized, the air conditioner clutch is disengaged and the 
compressor does not operate.

The A/C cycling switch, when functioning properly, will control the 
evaporator core pressure at a point where the plate/fin surface temperature 
will be maintained slightly above freezing, which prevents evaporator icing 
and the blockage of airflow.

 A/C Condenser Core 

The A/C condenser core is attached to the radiator support in front of 
the radiator with two mounting brackets at the top and bottom of the 
condenser. The top mounting brackets attach to the rear side of the radiator 
support and the lower brackets attach to the front side of the radiator support.

Vehicles with manual valves at the compressor have a self-sealing 
coupling at the condenser liquid line connection. Vehicles without manual 
valves do not have a self-sealing coupling.

 A/C Compressor 

The Sanden compressor is a five-cylinder type, and is installed on the 
top left side of 7.0L gasoline engines. The seven-cylinder type compressor is 
used on the Cummins B5.9 and the Cummins C8.3 diesel engines. It is installed 
on the right side of these engines.

To adjust drive belt tension, a sliding compressor mounting bracket is 
used.

An integral clutch is used to drive the compressor shaft. When voltage 
is applied to the clutch field coil, the clutch plate and hub assembly (which 
is solidly coupled to the compressor shaft) is drawn by magnetic force toward 
the pulley which rotates freely on the compressor front head casting. The 
magnetic force locks the clutch plate and hub assembly and the pulley together 
as one unit. The compressor shaft then turns with the pulley. When voltage is 
removed from the clutch field coil, a rubber bushing in the clutch plate and 
hub assembly move the clutch plate away from the pulley and the clutch plate

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Refrigerant Oil Addition

The compressor uses a unique high-quality refrigerant oil, Sanden SP-20 
or an equivalent refrigerant oil meeting Ford specification WST-M1C231-B2. An 
oil charge is required in a new system and capacities are different for the 
different types of compressors. The SD-5 requires 310 ml (10 oz) oil charge 
(gasoline engines), and the SD-7 requires 240 ml (8 oz) oil charge (Cummins 
B5.9 and Cummins C8.3 diesel engines) in new systems. It is extremely 
important that only the specified type and quantity of refrigerant oil be used 
in the compressor. If there is a surplus of oil in the system, it will 
circulate with the refrigerant, reducing the cooling capacity of the system. 
Using too little oil or oil not meeting the Ford specification will result in 
poor lubrication of the compressor.

When replacing a component of the refrigerant system, the procedures in 
this section must be followed to ensure that the total oil charge in the 
system is correct after the new part is installed.

When the compressor is operated, oil gradually leaves the compressor 
and is circulated through the system with the refrigerant. Eventually, a 
balanced condition is reached in which a certain amount of oil is retained in 
the compressor and a certain amount is continually circulated. If a component 
of the system is removed after the system has been operated, some oil will go 
with it. To maintain the original total oil charge, add oil as required to the 
new replacement part.

 During A/C Compressor Replacement 

 NOTE: The suction accumulator/drier and orifice tube must also be replaced 
when the compressor is replaced.

A new service replacement compressor may or may not contain refrigerant 
oil. Prior to installing the replacement compressor, drain the refrigerant oil 
from the removed compressor into a calibrated container. Drain the refrigerant 
oil from the new compressor into a clean calibrated container. Rotate the 
shaft about six to eight revolutions while pouring the oil from the ports. 
This effectively empties the compressor of oil.

Obtain a clean container that can also be used as a measuring device.

Place the disc and hub assembly on the compressor shaft of the new 
compressor so the shaft can be rotated.

Rotate the shaft by hand (six to eight revolutions), collecting the oil 
in a clean measuring device.

If the amount of oil drained from the old compressor was between 85 and 
142 ml (3 and 5 oz), pour the same amount of clean specified refrigerant oil 
into the new compressor.

If the amount of oil that was removed from the old compressor is 
greater than 142 ml (5 oz), pour 142 ml (5 oz) of clean specified refrigerant 
oil into the new compressor.

If the amount of refrigerant oil that was removed from the old 
compressor is less than 85 ml (3 oz), pour 85 ml (3 oz) of clean specified 
refrigerant oil into the new compressor.

 During Component Replacement 

When replacing other components of the air conditioning system, 
measured quantities of the specified refrigerant oil should be added to the 
component to ensure that the total oil charge in the system is correct before 
the system is operated.

Clean refrigerant oil should be poured directly into the replacement 
components as follows:

A/C evaporator core: add 90 ml (3 oz).

A/C condenser core: add 30 ml (1 oz).

Accumulator: drain oil from removed accumulator/drier. Add same amount 
plus 60 ml (2 oz) of clean refrigerant oil to new accumulator.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Assembly

 Removal 

Disconnect negative battery cable.

Remove two screws attaching the top of the instrument panel center 
finish panel to the instrument panel pad and remove the finish panel.

Remove the knobs from the climate control assembly by placing a small 
screwdriver between the knob spring retainer and the climate control assembly. 
Pull on the screwdriver, applying pressure on the spring retainer and pull the 
knob from the function control assembly. Repeat this procedure for each knob.

Remove the ashtray, the ashtray bracket, and the floor register duct.

Remove the four climate control assembly attaching screws.

Disconnect the wire harness connectors from the blower motor switch, 
the illumination light, the vacuum selector switch and the auxiliary fuel tank 
selector switch, if so equipped.

 Illumination Bulbs 

 Removal 

Disconnect negative battery cable.

Remove two screws attaching the top of the instrument panel center 
finish trim panel to the instrument panel pad, and remove the center finish 
trim panel.

Remove the ashtray, the ashtray bracket and floor register duct.

Remove the four climate control assembly attaching screws.

Gently pull the climate control assembly away from the instrument panel 
far enough to gain access to the backside of the assembly.

Disconnect the illumination bulb socket by rotating it one-quarter turn 
and releasing the socket from the climate control assembly.

 WARNING: USE CAUTION WHEN REMOVING THE MINIATURE BULB. GRASPING THE BULB TOO 
HARD WITH YOUR FINGERS MAY RESULT IN BULB BREAKAGE, RESULTING IN INJURY TO THE 
TECHNICIAN. 

Remove the miniature bulb from the socket by grasping it in your 
fingers and pulling the bulb from the socket. 

 Installation 

Install new miniature bulb by aligning the bulb contacts with the 
illumination bulb socket, and gently push into place.

Reconnect the illumination bulb socket in the climate control assembly 
by aligning the locating tabs on the socket and climate control assembly and 
rotating one-quarter turn.

Reinstall the climate control assembly in the instrument panel and 
secure with four attaching screws.

Reinstall the floor register duct, ashtray bracket and ashtray.

Install the instrument panel center finish trim panel and secure with 
two retaining screws.

Connect the battery ground cable.

 A/C Switch 

 Removal 

Disconnect the negative battery cable.

Remove two screws attaching the top of the instrument panel center 
finish trim panel to the instrument panel pad, and remove the center finish 
trim panel.

Remove the ashtray, the ashtray bracket and the floor register duct.

Remove the four climate control assembly attaching screws.

Disconnect the wire harness connectors from the blower motor switch, 
the illumination light, the vacuum selector switch and the auxiliary fuel tank 
selector switch, if so equipped.

Disconnect the vacuum harness connector from the vacuum selector switch.

Disconnect the temperature control cable from the climate control 
assembly.

Remove the climate control assembly.

Remove the two screws retaining the A/C switch/vacuum selector valve 
assembly, and remove the switch/valve assembly from the climate control 
assembly.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Check system for proper operation.

 Switch Knobs 

 Removal 

Place a small, flat-bladed screwdriver between the knob spring retainer 
and the climate control assembly.

Gently pull on the screwdriver, applying pressure to the knob spring 
retainer while pulling the knob off the climate control assembly shaft.

Repeat this procedure for each switch knob.

 Installation 

Align the spring retainer and knob with the climate control assembly 
shaft and gently push the knob onto the shaft until the knob bottoms against 
the shaft.

Repeat this procedure for each knob.

 Blower Motor Switch 

 Removal 

Remove two screws attaching the top of the instrument panel center 
finish panel to the instrument panel pad. Remove the finish panel.

Remove the knob from the blower motor switch by placing a small 
screwdriver between the knob spring retainer and the A/C-heater function 
control assembly. Pull on the screwdriver, applying pressure on the spring 
retainer and pull the knob from the switch.

Remove the ashtray, the ashtray bracket and the floor register duct.

Remove four A/C-heater function control assembly attaching screws.

Move the control assembly away from the instrument panel opening and 
disconnect the wire connector from the switch.

Remove one screw attaching the blower motor switch to the bottom of the 
control assembly and remove the blower motor switch.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Evaporator Core Housing

 Removal 

Discharge the refrigerant system, following the recommended service 
procedures. Observe all safety precautions. Refer to Section 12-00 .

Disconnect the blower motor wires, the blower motor resistor wires and 
the wires connected to the A/C cycling switch.

Disconnect the vacuum supply hose at the vacuum reservoir and the small 
vacuum hose at the check valve. Reposition the check valve away from the 
evaporator case.

Disconnect the liquid line from the evaporator core and the suction 
line from the accumulator. Cap all open refrigerant lines to prevent 
contamination.

Disconnect the heater hoses from the heater core and plug the hoses 
with suitable 16-mm (5/8-inch) plugs.

Working in the passenger compartment, remove two screws attaching the 
bottom of the evaporator core housing to the dash panel. One screw also 
attaches the lower edge of the plenum to the dash panel.

Unplug the vacuum harness at the connector located near the right end 
of the plenum and tuck the harness coming from the recirculating duct opening 
back into the opening.

Remove two screws attaching the right side of the recirculating duct to 
the dash panel.

Remove two retaining nuts attaching the evaporator core housing and the 
recirculating duct to the dash panel.

Pull the evaporator core housing and recirculating duct forward and 
remove from the vehicle.

Remove five screws attaching the recirculating duct to the evaporator 
core housing and remove the recirculating duct.

 Installation 

Position the recirculating duct and gasket to the evaporator case and 
install the five attaching screws.

Position the recirculating duct and evaporator core housing to the dash 
panel and install the two retaining nuts along the top edge of the assembly.

Install two screws along the right side of the recirculating duct.

Working in the passenger compartment, install two screws to attach the 
bottom of the evaporator core housing to the dash panel.

Connect the vacuum harness from the recirculating duct opening to the 
connector at the right end of the plenum.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
liquid line to the evaporator core. Tighten the connection to 21-27 Nm 
(15-20 lb-ft) using two wrenches.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
suction line to the accumulator. Tighten the connection to 38-44 Nm 
(28-33 lb-ft) using two wrenches.

Connect the heater hoses to the heater core. Tighten the clamps only to 
2.3-2.8 Nm (20-25 lb-in).

Connect the two vacuum hoses to the reservoir and to the vacuum check 
valve.

Connect the wires to the blower motor, blower motor resistor and the 
A/C cycling switch.

Fill and bleed cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Leak test, evacuate and charge the system following the recommended 
procedures. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

 Installation 

Transfer the suction accumulator bracket and spring nuts to the new 
evaporator core.

Apply a bead of Ford Caulking Cord D6AZ-19560-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESB-M4G32-A to the flange of the evaporator core housing. 
Use only the specified rope sealer.

Position the evaporator core to the evaporator core housing. Apply a 
strip of rope sealer on the suction accumulator/drier mounting bracket and 
around the evaporator core tubes at the housing flange area.

Position the left evaporator housing to the right evaporator case. 
Install six screws to attach the housing to the right evaporator housing along 
the flange.

Install the two spring clips to retain the housing cover plate to the 
left edge of the left evaporator housing.

Install one nut to retain the upper left corner of the housing to the 
dash panel.

In the passenger compartment, install one screw to attach the lower 
edge of the plenum and the bottom of the evaporator housing to the dash panel.

Remove the cap from the evaporator core liquid line connection and 
install a new fixed orifice tube in the evaporator core tube. Refer to A/C 
Evaporator Core Orifice in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
liquid line to the evaporator core. Tighten the connection to 21-27 Nm 
(15-20 lb-ft) using two wrenches.

Add three ounces of clean refrigerant oil to a new suction 
accumulator/drier to compensate for oil lost in the evaporator core replacement.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
suction accumulator/drier to the evaporator core. Tighten the connection to 
28-37 Nm (21-27 lb-ft) using two wrenches.

Install the suction accumulator/drier support straps (two screws). Then 
tighten the suction accumulator/drier to evaporator core fitting to 
specification. Use a backup wrench on the suction accumulator/drier to prevent 
component damage.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
suction hose to the suction accumulator/drier. Use a backup wrench to prevent 
component damage.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, install the 
A/C cycling switch on the suction accumulator/drier nipple.

Connect the electrical connector to the A/C cycling switch.

Evacuate, leak test and charge the system following the recommended 
procedures. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

 Louvers 

 Removal 

Insert a thin blade under the retaining tab and pry the retaining tab 
toward the louvers until the retaining tab pivot clears the hole in the 
register opening.

[FIGURE: L3409B.gif]

Pull the louver assembly end out from the housing only enough to 
prevent the pivot from going back into the pivot hole.

Repeat Step 1 for the other retaining tab and pull the register louver 
assembly from the register opening.

 Installation 

 NOTE: The pivots on each end of the louver assembly are different diameters 
and therefore determine the installed position of the assembly.

Position the louver assembly into the opening with the largest diameter 
pivot near the largest pivot hole.

Depress the retaining tabs. Push the louver assembly into the register 
opening and engage the retainer tab pivots in the pivot holes.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Suction Accumulator/Drier

 Removal 

Discharge the refrigerant from the air conditioner system, following 
the recommended service procedures. Observe all safety precautions. Refer to 
 Section 12-00 .

Disconnect the electrical connector from the A/C cycling switch.

Remove the cycling switch by unscrewing it from the suction 
accumulator/drier.

Disconnect the suction hose from the suction accumulator/drier. Use two 
wrenches to prevent component damage. Cap the suction hose to prevent the 
entrance of dirt and moisture.

Loosen the fitting connecting the suction accumulator/drier to the 
evaporator core. Use two wrenches to prevent component damage.

Remove two screws attaching the two suction accumulator/drier straps to 
the mounting bracket.

Disconnect the suction accumulator/drier from the evaporator core and 
remove the two straps from the suction accumulator/drier.

 Installation 

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
suction accumulator/drier to the evaporator core tube. Tighten the connection 
finger-tight.

Position the two straps on the suction accumulator/drier. Align the 
straps with the mounting bracket and install the two attaching screws. Loosen 
the connection of the suction accumulator/drier to the evaporator core if it 
is necessary to position the suction accumulator/drier to install the two 
strap attaching screws.

Tighten the suction accumulator/drier to evaporator core fitting to 
28-37 Nm (21-27 lb-ft), using two wrenches.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
suction hose to the suction accumulator/drier. Use two wrenches and tighten 
the connection to 38-44 Nm (28-33 lb-ft).

Install a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil on the A/C 
cycling switch nipple of the suction accumulator/drier. Then, install the 
switch and tighten to 7-13 Nm (62-115 lb-in) if switch has a steel 
base, and only hand-tight if switch has a plastic base.

Connect the electrical connector to the A/C cycling switch.

Leak test, evacuate and charge the system, following the recommended 
service procedures. Observe all safety precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Evaporator Core Orifice

The fixed orifice tube is constructed with a plastic body, two screens 
and a small brass tube down the center of the orifice body. Two O-rings are 
around the orifice tube body to seal against leakage around the body.

[FIGURE: L3413H.gif]

 Removal 

Discharge the refrigerant from the air conditioning system, following 
the recommended service procedures. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety 
precautions.

Disconnect the liquid line from the evaporator core. Cap the liquid 
line to prevent the entrance of dirt and excessive moisture.

Pour a small amount of clean refrigerant oil into the evaporator core 
inlet tube to lubricate the tube and orifice O-rings during removal of the 
fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

 CAUTION: DO NOT attempt to remove the fixed orifice tube with pliers or to twist 
or rotate the orifice tube in the evaporator core tube. To do so will break 
the fixed orifice tube body in the evaporator core tube. Use only the 
recommended tool, following the recommended service procedures. 

Engage Fixed Orifice Tube Tool D80L-19990-A or equivalent with the two 
tangs on the fixed orifice tube.

Hold the T-handle of Fixed Orifice Tube Tool D80L-19990-A or equivalent 
to keep it from turning, and run the nut on the tool down against the 
evaporator core tube until the orifice is pulled from the tube.

If the fixed orifice tube breaks in the evaporator core tube, it must 
be removed from the tube with Broken Orifice Tube Extractor D80L-19990-B or 
equivalent.

To remove a broken orifice tube, insert the screw end of extractor 
D80L-19990-B or equivalent into the evaporator core tube and thread the screw 
end of the tool into the brass tube in the center of the fixed orifice tube. 
Pull the fixed orifice tube from the evaporator core tube.

If only the brass center tube is removed during the previous steps, 
insert the screw end of Broken Orifice Tube Extractor D80L-19990-B or 
equivalent into the evaporator core tube and screw the end of the tool into 
the fixed orifice tube body. Pull the fixed orifice tube body from the 
evaporator core tube.

 Installation 

Lubricate the O-rings on the fixed orifice tube body liberally with 
clean refrigerant oil.

 NOTE: The fixed orifice tube is color-coded. Be sure to use same color fixed 
orifice tube when replacing.

Place the fixed orifice tube in Fixed Orifice Tube Tool D80L-19990-A or 
equivalent and insert the fixed orifice tube into the evaporator core tube 
until the orifice is seated at the stop.

Remove the remover tool from the fixed orifice tube.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
liquid line to the evaporator core tube. Tighten the fitting to 21-27 
Nm (15-20 lb-ft), using a backup wrench.

Leak test, evacuate and charge the system following the recommended 
service procedures. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions. 

Check the system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Condenser Core

 Removal 

Discharge the refrigerant from the system following the recommended 
service procedures. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions.

Disconnect the liquid line from the condenser. Cap the liquid line to 
prevent the entrance of dirt and moisture.

Disconnect the compressor discharge line from the condenser and cap the 
discharge line to prevent the entrance of dirt and moisture.

Partially drain the radiator and disconnect the upper hose from the 
radiator.

Working under the vehicle, remove two screws attaching the two 
condenser lower mounting brackets to the front of the radiator support.

Remove the two radiator upper retaining brackets (two screws each).

Tilt the top of the radiator rearward and remove two screws attaching 
the two condenser upper mounting brackets to the rear side of the radiator 
support.

Lift the condenser from the vehicle.

 Installation 

Position the condenser to the vehicle with the lower mounting brackets 
on the front side of the radiator support and the upper brackets on the rear 
side.

Install the four screws to attach the four mounting brackets to the 
radiator support. Tighten the screws to 14-19 Nm (11-14 lb-ft).

Move the radiator into the correct installed position and install the 
two upper retaining brackets (two screws each).

Connect the radiator upper hose to the radiator and fill the cooling 
system to the specified level.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
compressor discharge line to the condenser. Tighten the connection to 21-27 
Nm (15-20 lb-ft).

Make sure the condenser outlet filter is installed in the condenser 
outlet tube.

Connect the liquid line to the condenser using a new O-ring lubricated 
with clean refrigerant oil. Tighten the connection to 21-27 Nm (15-20 
lb-ft).

Fill and bleed cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Leak test, evacuate and charge the system, following the recommended 
service procedures. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Condenser Core Filter

 Removal 

Discharge the refrigerant from the system, following the recommended 
procedures. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all safety precautions.

Disconnect the self-sealing coupling from the condenser outlet tube. If 
a self-sealing coupling is not used, disconnect the liquid line from the 
condenser outlet tube.

Pull the filter from the condenser outlet tube. 

 Installation 

Insert a new condenser outlet filter into the condenser outlet tube, 
small end first. Make sure the filter is inserted into the tube until the 
filter end is against the end of the condenser outlet tube.

Using a new O-ring lubricated with clean refrigerant oil, connect the 
self-sealing coupling (if used) or the liquid line to the condenser outlet 
tube. Tighten the connection to 11-21 Nm (8-16 lb-ft) with 
self-sealing, or 21-27 Nm (15-20 lb-ft) without self-sealing, using a 
backup wrench to prevent component damage.

Evacuate, leak test and charge A/C system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 
Observe all safety precautions.

Check the system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Compressor

All compressor replacement operations except belt replacement can be 
performed only after the unit has been relieved of its refrigerant charge. 
Discharge the entire refrigerant system. Refer to Section 12-00 . Observe all 
safety precautions.

 Removal 

 NOTE: Refer to Refrigerant Oil Addition in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section when replacing an A/C compressor.

Refer to the following illustrations for component location and 
orientation.

Discharge the system and disconnect the two hoses from the compressor.

Disconnect electrical connectors from A/C compressor.

Loosen the idler pulley or generator and remove the drive belt and the 
clutch and then remove the mounting bolts and the compressor. Refer to the 
following illustration.

 Installation 

Place the compressor on the mounting bracket and install the mounting 
bolts. Tighten to 40-55 Nm (30-40 lb-ft).

Install the belt and adjust and tighten the idler pulley.

Connect the two hoses to the compressor. Evacuate, charge and leak test 
the system.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C System Filtering

 CAUTION: Follow all refrigerant system safety and service precautions. Refer to 
 Section 12-00 . 

An A/C service kit has been released to provide the necessary equipment 
and information to perform the new, mandatory A/C system filtering 
procedure.The filter kit with the service part number suffix A is to be used 
on vehicles that have a nylon-lined evaporator-to-compressor suction line 
between the suction accumulator/drier and the A/C compressor.

To determine if the compressor has failed and must be replaced, remove 
the A/C evaporator core orifice and the condenser-to-evaporator tube, if 
necessary. Look for a dirty A/C evaporator core orifice or a 
condenser-to-evaporator tube containing black refrigerant oil and particles.

Remove the damaged compressor and drain the oil into a calibrated 
container.

 NOTE: The proper amount of refrigerant oil must be added to the new 
compressor before it can be installed. Refer to Adding Refrigerant Oil in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 NOTE: It will be necessary to transfer the A/C clutch from the old A/C 
compressor to the new A/C compressor.

Install the new A/C compressor. Make sure the compressor mounting bolts 
are tightened to the correct specification. Check the tension of the drive 
belt. Adjust if necessary.

Remove the suction accumulator/drier assembly and drain the refrigerant 
oil contained in it into a calibrated container.

Add clean refrigerant oil to the new suction accumulator/drier in the 
same amount that was removed from the old suction accumulator/drier plus an 
additional 60ml of new refrigerant oil.

Install the suction accumulator/drier in the vehicle.

Get the proper service kit for the vehicle on which you are working. 
The filter kit with the service part number suffix A is used on vehicles with 
a nylon-lined evaporator-to-compressor suction line.

[FIGURE: M4546A.gif]

Remove a length of evaporator-to-compressor suction line to accommodate 
the suction filter, and install the filter using the clamps provided with the 
kit. Make sure filter is correctly oriented for refrigerant flow. Check the 
label on the filter. On the filter for nylon-lined evaporator-to-compressor 
suction line, install O-rings (two on each filter tube), making sure they are 
properly seated in the grooves on the tube. Tighten the clamps securely.

[FIGURE: M3730A.gif]

Install a new A/C evaporator core orifice.

Install a pancake filter in the condenser-to-evaporator tube between 
the A/C condenser core and the A/C evaporator core orifice. Make sure the 
filter inlet is toward the A/C condenser core. Connections can be made using 
A/C Test Fitting Set 014-00333 or equivalent and flexible refrigerant hose of 
17,238 kPa (2500 psi) burst rating. Individual fittings are also available.

 Condenser-to-Evaporator Line Connections 

[FIGURE: M3729B.gif]

Evacuate, leak test and charge the system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 
Observe all safety precautions.

Check all refrigerant system hoses, lines and the positioning of the 
newly installed filters to make sure they do not interfere with other engine 
compartment components. If necessary, use tie straps to make adjustments.

Provide adequate airflow to the front of the vehicle (with a fan if 
necessary), and set the function selector lever to MAX A/C. Set the blower 
motor switch on HIGH and temperature control to full COOL. Start the engine 
and let it idle briefly. Make sure the A/C system is operating.

Gradually bring the engine up to 1200 rpm by running it at lower rpms 
for short periods (first at 800 rpm, then at 1000 rpm). Set the engine at 1200 
rpm and run it for an hour with the A/C system operating.

Stop the engine.

Allow the engine to cool sufficiently to remove the fittings, flexible 
hoses and the pancake filter from the condenser to evaporator tube. (It will 
be necessary to discharge the system first. Refer to Section 12-00 .) 

Discard the pancake filter. It can be used one time only.

Reconnect the condenser-to-evaporator tube.

Evacuate, leak test and charge the system. Refer to Section 12-00 . 
Observe all safety precautions. Make all necessary adjustments.

Check the operation of the system in all modes.

ADJUSTMENTS

Cables

 Temperature Control Cable 

Remove the glove compartment liner.

Loosen the temperature control cable attaching screw at the cable 
bracket located on top of the plenum.

Position the temperature control lever 1/8 inch from the left (blue) 
end of the lever slot of the control assembly.

Rotate the temperature door crank arm to the extreme left and tighten 
the cable attaching screw.

Move the temperature lever from left to right and make sure the lever 
bounces back slightly at both ends of the slot. If bounce-back does not occur 
at both ends of the slot, adjust the cable to obtain bounce-back of the lever 
at each end of the slot.

Install the glove compartment liner.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Compressor

The SD-7H15 compressor is an axial compressor with mounting brackets 
for tangential mounting. The compressor shaft is belt-driven from the engine 
accessory drive. The pistons, positioned axially around the compressor shaft, 
are actuated by a swash plate that is pressed on the compressor shaft. The 
swash plate uses the rotating action of the shaft to provide a reciprocating 
driving force to each of the pistons. 

The SD-7H15 has seven cylinders. 

Reed-type suction and discharge valve plates are located between the 
cylinder assembly and the head. 

An integral clutch is used to drive the compressor shaft. When voltage 
is applied to the clutch field coil, the clutch plate and hub assembly (which 
is solidly coupled to the compressor shaft) is drawn by magnetic force toward 
the pulley, which rotates freely on the compressor front head casting. The 
magnetic force locks the clutch plate and hub assembly and the pulley together 
as one unit. The compressor shaft then turns with the pulley. When voltage is 
removed from the clutch field coil, a rubber bushing in the clutch plate and 
hub assembly moves the clutch plate away from the pulley and the compressor 
shaft ceases to rotate.

[FIGURE: K16826C.gif]

The A/C compressor is equipped with a thermal protection switch to 
automatically shut down operation by interrupting the electrical power to the 
compressor clutch when the compressor temperature exceeds approximately 
116°C (240°F). The compressor will automatically restart when it has 
cooled to approximately 99°C (210°F). A CHECK A/C warning light is 
mounted on the instrument panel. Illumination of the CHECK A/C warning light 
is an indication the thermal protection system has been activated and air 
conditioning system service is required. 

This warning is provided to indicate that the system needs service 
(such as low on refrigerant, etc.) and with immediate attention the potential 
for system damage will be reduced. Continued use of the air conditioning 
system with the warning light indication cycling periodically, can result in 
compressor damage.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

A/C Clutch

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spanner Wrench

T70P-4067-A

Steering Wheel Puller

T67L-3600-A

 A/C Clutch and A/C Clutch Pulley 

 Removal 

Install Spanner Wrench T70P-4067-A into two threaded holes in the 
clutch front plate. 

Hold clutch plate stationary and remove hex nut.

[FIGURE: M5200A.gif]

Using Steering Wheel Puller T67L-3600-A, align puller center bolt to 
compressor shaft. Tighten three puller bolts into the threaded holes, then 
screw puller center bolt down against A/C compressor center shaft until A/C 
clutch releases from the A/C compressor shaft.

[FIGURE: M5301A.gif]

Remove bearing dust cover, using a screwdriver.

[FIGURE: K138161A.gif]

Remove shaft key by lightly tapping it loose with a slotted screwdriver 
and hammer.

[FIGURE: K138171A.gif]

Remove the internal bearing snap ring.

[FIGURE: K138181A.gif]

Remove the external front housing snap ring.

[FIGURE: K13819B.gif]

Insert puller jaws into the snap ring groove. 

Place rotor puller shaft protector over exposed shaft.

[FIGURE: K138201A.gif]

Align thumb head bolts to puller jaws and finger-tighten. 

Tighten center bolt until A/C clutch pulley is removed.

[FIGURE: K13821B.gif]

 Installation 

Support the compressor on the four mounting ears on the rear of the 
compressor. If using a vise, clamp only on mounting ears, not on compressor 
body. 

Align A/C clutch pulley squarely on the front housing hub.

[FIGURE: K13822B.gif]

Using rotor installer ring set, place rotor installer ring into bearing 
cavity. Make certain the outer edge rests firmly on the A/C clutch pulley 
bearing outer race. 

Place rotor installer driver into rotor installer ring.

[FIGURE: K138231A.gif]

Tap driver with a hammer while guiding the A/C clutch pulley to prevent 
binding. Tap until the A/C clutch pulley bottoms against the compressor front 
housing hub. 

Install internal bearing snap ring. 

Install external front housing snap ring. 

Install front plate assembly. 

Install compressor shaft key. 

Align front plate keyway to compressor shaft key. 

Using shaft protector, tap front plate to shaft until it bottoms out on 
the shims.

[FIGURE: K138241A.gif]

Install shaft hex nut. Tighten to 34-40 Nm (25-30 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: K138251A.gif]

Check air gap, using a.016- to.031-inch feeler gauge between hub and 
mating pulley surface in three locations equally spaced around pulley. Record 
air gap readings. 

Rotate compressor pulley one-half turn (180 degrees) and again check 
air gap in three equally spaced locations. Smallest air gap must be within 
specified limits for air gap. Add or remove shims between hub and compressor 
shaft end as necessary until smallest air gap is within specification. 

 A/C Clutch Field Coil 

 Removal 

Remove A/C clutch hub and pulley.

Loosen coil lead wire clip from compressor front housing.

[FIGURE: K138261B.gif]

Remove snap ring and field coil.

[FIGURE: K138271A.gif]

 Installation 

Install field coil and snap ring.

Tighten clip on field coil lead wire.

Install pulley and hub on compressor.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermal Protection Switch 

 Removal 

Remove the screw securing the thermal protection switch retainer plate 
and lead wire clamp. 

 NOTE: Switch removal may be difficult due to the silicone RTV used in switch 
installation. NEVER reinstall old thermal protection switch. ALWAYS replace 
with new switch unit, when required. 

Using a small-bladed screwdriver, insert blade between switch and 
switch socket and remove switch.

 Installation 

Remove all the old silicone RTV and thoroughly clean the thermal 
protection switch socket. 

Position the thermal protection switch so that the flat copper surface 
faces upward. Apply a small amount of silicone RTV to the flat copper switch 
surface to make sure outside air temperatures do not affect switch thermal 
sensing ability. 

Install the switch in the mounting socket. Position wire clamp, 
retainer and install retaining screw. Tighten to 5.4-8.1 Nm (48-72 
lb-in).

ADJUSTMENTS

A/C Clutch Air Gap

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spanner Wrench

T70P-4067-A

Steering Wheel Puller

T67L-3600-A

 NOTE: Before disassembling an A/C compressor for repair, it is important to 
check the A/C clutch air gap. This will help determine if the A/C clutch is 
not engaging, or if the A/C compressor is failing internally.

Check the A/C clutch air gap between the A/C clutch hub and the A/C 
clutch pulley mating surfaces with a feeler gauge. The air gap should be 
between 0.41 and 0.79 mm (0.016-0.031 in.). Check at three locations equally 
spaced around the A/C clutch pulley.

 NOTE: If a desired gap is not attainable with the available shims, the A/C 
clutch hub and A/C clutch pulley should be inspected for wear or damage. 
Replace as required.

If the A/C clutch air gap is not within specification, use the 
following steps to adjust air gap.

Use Spanner Wrench T70P-4067-A to hold the A/C clutch in position while 
removing the A/C clutch retaining hex nut.

Pull the A/C clutch and shims from the A/C compressor shaft. If the A/C 
clutch cannot be removed, install Steering Wheel Puller T67L-3600-A on the A/C 
compressor clutch, and use puller center bolt to force the A/C clutch off the 
A/C compressor shaft.

Start by placing the smallest nominal thickness shim inside the A/C 
clutch spline opening, and slide the A/C clutch onto the end of the A/C 
compressor shaft.

 CAUTION: Do not use air tools to tighten the bolt. 

Install the clutch hex nut into the end of the A/C compressor shaft. 
Use Spanner Wrench T70P-4067-A to hold the A/C clutch and hub in position 
while tightening the A/C clutch hex nut. Tighten to 34-40 Nm (25-30 
lb-ft).

Recheck the A/C clutch air gap between the A/C clutch hub and pulley 
mating surfaces with a feeler gauge. The air gap should be between 0.41 and 
0.79 mm (0.016 and 0.031 in.). Check at three locations spaced equally around 
the pulley.

If the A/C clutch air gap is not within specification, repeat Steps 3 
through 7. Install the correct shim(s) to achieve the desired air gap.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Cluster and Panel Lighting

The instrument cluster and panel lighting is controlled by the headlamp 
switch. When the headlamp switch is in the HEAD or PARK position, battery 
voltage is supplied to the illumination lights through the headlamp dimmer 
switch. The lights can be dimmed manually with the headlamp dimmer switch, 
which is contained within the headlamp switch.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Cluster (IC)

On F-Series Cab vehicles, the instrument cluster warning lights are 
arranged across the top of the cluster and in the center. On F-Cowl and 
B-Series, the cluster warning lights are grouped together to the left of the 
steering wheel, next to the tachometer.

 Printed Circuit 

The instrument cluster printed circuit, which supplies current to the 
instrument panel indicators, gauges, and some clocks, is made of copper foil 
which is bonded to a polyester base film (usually referred to as 
Mylar®).

The instrument cluster printed circuit is mounted to the cluster 
housing and, due to its location, cannot be easily inspected or tested in the 
vehicle. This makes the instrument cluster printed circuit vulnerable to 
damage when a probe is used for in-vehicle testing as the probe can pierce the 
instrument cluster printed circuit or, in some cases, burn the copper conductor.

Since there is no approved procedure for in-vehicle testing of the 
instrument cluster printed circuit, it must be removed for visual inspection. 
If no visual damage is evident, each circuit should be tested with an 
ohmmeter. If an open circuit or short is detected, the instrument cluster 
printed circuit must be replaced.

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1999 F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Level Indication System

The fuel level indicating system on F-Cowl and B-Series vehicles is a 
magnetic gauge system. It consists of a magnetic fuel gauge mounted in the 
instrument cluster and a fuel level sensor located in the fuel tank. The fuel 
level indicating system on F-Series Cab vehicles is a bimetal resistance-type 
system. It consists of an instrument voltage regulator, a fuel indicator gauge 
mounted in the instrument cluster and a fuel level sensor located in the fuel 
tank. 

 Fuel Gauge 

The magnetic gauge movement consists of three primary coils, one of 
which is wound at a 90-degree angle to the other two. The coils form a 
magnetic field which varies in direction according to the variable resistance 
of the sending unit which is connected between two of them. A primary magnet, 
to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to align to this primary 
field, resulting in pointer position. 

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for this 
gauge. 

The bimetal fuel indicator gauge pointer is attached to a wire-wound 
bimetal strip which, when heated by the flow of electrical current controlled 
by the sending unit, produces the appropriate level indication. 

 Instrument Cluster Gauge Amplifier 

The instrument voltage regulator (IVR) used with the fuel indicator 
gauge controls and maintains an average pulsating voltage of 5.0 volts at the 
gauge terminals. 

 Fuel Level Sensor 

The fuel level sensor consists of a variable screened resistor made up 
of a ceramic substrate. It is controlled by the action of an attached float in 
the fuel tank. When the fuel level is low, resistance in the sensor is low. 
When the fuel level is high, resistance in the sensor is high.

1999 F and B-Series

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1999 F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Temperature Indication System

The temperature indicating system on F-Series Cab vehicles consists of 
the instrument voltage regulator (IVR), a sending unit mounted in the 
thermostat housing and a temperature gauge mounted on the instrument panel. 
When the engine temperature is low, the resistance of the sending unit is 
high. The high resistance restricts current through the gauge which moves the 
pointer only a short distance.

The temperature indicating system on F-Cowl and B-Series consists of a 
sending unit mounted in the thermostat housing and a temperature gauge mounted 
on the instrument panel. When the engine temperature is low, the resistance of 
the sending unit is high, thus restricting the flow of current through the 
gauge which moves the pointer only a short distance.

 Instrument Cluster Temperature Gauge 

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for this 
gauge.

The magnetic gauge movement consists of two primary coils, one of which 
is wound at a 90-degree angle to the other one. The coils form a magnetic 
field which varies in direction according to the variable resistance of the 
sender unit which is connected between them. A primary magnet, to which a 
shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to align to this primary field, 
resulting in pointer position. The bobbin/coil assembly is pressed into a 
metal housing which has two holes for dial mounting. 

 High Coolant Temperature Warning 

This red light will illuminate to indicate a high engine coolant 
temperature.

 Water Temperature Indicator Sender Unit 

As the temperature of the engine increases, the resistance of the 
sending unit decreases, causing a proportionately increased flow of current 
and movement of the pointer.

1999 F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Pressure Indication System

The oil pressure gauge indicating system consists of the instrument 
voltage regulator (IVR), an oil pressure indicating gauge and an oil pressure 
sending unit, all connected in series.

 Oil Pressure Gauge 

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for this 
gauge.

The magnetic gauge movement consists of three primary coils, one of 
which is wound at a 90-degree angle to the other two. The coils form a 
magnetic field which varies in direction according to the variable resistance 
of the sending unit which is connected between two of them. A primary magnet, 
to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to align to this primary 
field, resulting in pointer position.

The bimetal oil pressure indicator gauge pointer is attached to a 
wire-wound bimetal strip which, when heated by the flow of electrical current 
controlled by the sending unit, produces the appropriate level indication.

 Low Oil Pressure Warning 

On F-Series Cab vehicles, a red indicator lamp glows when the oil 
pressure is below a safe value. The lamp should come on when the key is first 
turned to the RUN position. The indicator lamp should go out after the engine 
is started, indicating that the oil pressure has reached a safe value.

The lamp is connected between the oil pressure sensor (mounted on the 
engine) and the coil terminal of the ignition switch.

 Oil Pressure Sensor 

The sending unit consists of a diaphragm, a contact and a variable 
resistor. The oil pressure causes the diaphragm to move the contact on the 
variable resistor, thus controlling the flow of current through the gauge.

When the oil pressure is low, the resistance of the sensor is high, 
thus restricting the flow of current through the gauge which moves the pointer 
only a short distance. As the oil pressure increases, the resistance of the 
sensor decreases, causing a proportionately increased flow of current and 
movement of the pointer.

PAGE 3508
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1999 F700, F800, FT900, B800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charge Indication System

The battery, generator, and electronic voltage regulator make up the 
charging system. 

 Battery Voltage Gauge 

The voltmeter is a gauge which measures the voltage potential at the 
battery to indicate the battery state of charge. The voltmeter is not 
adjustable and should be replaced if inoperative. 

 Charging System Warning 

With the key in START or RUN, battery current flows through the 
generator warning indicator lamp into the regulator at terminal I, and to 
ground through the solid-state indicator switch. The electronic control 
measures a low voltage at regulator terminal A, and closes the field switch. 
This applies battery voltage to the field through generator terminal F. 

With current in the field and the rotor turning, the generator stator 
produces a DC voltage at terminal BAT (to battery) and terminal STA. Voltage 
at STA is one-half voltage at BAT. 

A preset voltage at regulator terminal STA operates the electronic 
control to open the indicator switch, which removes ground from the generator 
warning indicator lamp. 

The generator output is controlled by the current in the field. The 
average voltage on the field depends on the percentage of time the field 
switch is closed. The electronic control closes the field switch when the 
voltage at A+ is low, and opens the switch when the voltage at A+ is 
high. 

The voltage regulator holds the system voltage at approximately 14 
volts. The average generator output is then any required value between zero 
and full current, depending on conditions sensed by the voltage regulator.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Pressure Gauge

The air pressure gauge indicates the amount of air pressure in the 
brake system (pounds per square inch). The air pressure is too low for brake 
system to operate properly when the indicator reads less than 414 kPa (60 
psi). All vehicles are equipped with a dual-pointer air pressure gauge to 
indicate pressure in each of the two brake circuits.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ammeter Gauge

The ammeter is a gauge which senses the direction and rate of flow of 
electrical current to or from the battery to indicate whether the battery is 
being charged or discharged. A shunt-type ammeter is used.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Odometer

The odometer indicates the total distance the vehicle has been driven.

 Odometer Replacement 

The mileage on replacement speedometer/odometers cannot be reset. If a 
replacement speedometer/odometer is installed, a label recording the vehicle's 
mileage and date at the time of the speedometer/odometer replacement must be 
attached to the driver door jamb.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Programmable Speedometer/Odometer Module

The programmable electronic speedometer/odometer is standard on all 
Ford F- and B-Series vehicles. This instrument features an analog air-core 
meter movement for speed indication and a digital stepper motor to drive the 
odometer. Both mechanisms are inherently rugged with improved accuracy because 
of the digital technology and relatively few moving mechanical parts. 

An odometer that displays an incorrect mileage reading may be caused by 
the stepper motor inside the speedometer. The stepper motor may not produce 
enough torque to advance the odometer. 

Install a new speedometer assembly with a stepper motor that produces 
more torque. Refer to Speedometer/Odometer in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section.

The instrument receives electrical pulses from a variable reluctance 
magnetic (VRM) sensor. This sensor detects the teeth of a 16-tooth interrupter 
mounted in most transmissions or a signal generator mounted at the rear of 
some automatic transmissions. These electrical pulses are converted to an 
analog speedometer/odometer display. The speedometer is designed so that the 
pointer will not return to zero with the key off. This should never be 
interpreted as a damaged unit. 

The instrument is identical in size to a cable-driven mechanical 
speedometer/odometer unit and mounts interchangeably in the instrument panel. 
Only one external adjustment, a DIP rocker switch, is necessary to calibrate 
both the speedometer and odometer.

PAGE 3514
================================================================================

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Tachometer 

The electric tachometer features an analog air core meter movement 
indicating engine speed in revolutions per minute (rpm). The tachometer has 
few moving mechanical parts. 

The tachometer receives electrical pulses from the ignition coil (gas 
engines), or a variable reluctance magnetic (VRM) sensor (diesel engines). The 
VRM sensor is mounted in the flywheel housing. It reads engine rpm. The 
electrical pulses are converted to an analog tachometer display.

 NOTE: The tachometer pointer will not return to zero with the key off. This 
should never be interpreted as an inoperative condition. 

On F-Cowl and B-Series vehicles a DIP switch is necessary for engine 
calibration. DIP switch settings are shown on the tachometer case 
identification label. 

On F-Cab vehicles with diesel engines, a rotary switch is employed for 
calibration. The switch has the numbers 1 through 4 embossed on the case.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators

 Brake System 

The brake system warning light should glow when the ignition lock 
cylinder is in the START position. With hydraulic brakes, a dual circuit 
(split) system is used. In case of a loss of hydraulic pressure in either 
brake circuit, the other will provide reduced braking capability. If this 
occurs, the BRAKE warning light will illuminate upon the first application of 
the brakes and remain on until hydraulic pressure is restored. The brake 
warning light will also illuminate if there is damage in the engine driven 
hydraulic pump system (in combination with BRK ELEC MTR light and chime).

 WARNING: ANY INDICATED DAMAGE IN THE BRAKE SYSTEM MUST RECEIVE IMMEDIATE 
ATTENTION TO AVOID THE POSSIBILITY OF LOSS OF BRAKING AND PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: REPAIRS MUST BE MADE IMMEDIATELY TO AN INOPERATIVE BRAKE SYSTEM CIRCUIT. 

 Check Engine 

This light is used on vehicles with 7.0L engines to indicate when 
maintenance of emission control devices is required.

The light will glow amber for 2-3 seconds with the key in the RUN 
position to indicate that the light and wiring are functioning. If the light 
does not glow, the vehicle's electrical circuitry is inoperative.

When the light stays on continuously with the key in the RUN position, 
it indicates that maintenance of emission control devices is required. Refer 
to the vehicle maintenance schedule for specific information on the 
maintenance required.

 Charging System 

This light, shown as a battery symbol on your cluster, indicates that 
your battery is not being charged and that you need to have the electrical 
system checked.

The charging system warning light glows red when the key is in the RUN 
position until the engine starts and the alternator charges.

If the light stays on or comes on when the engine is running, have the 
electrical system checked as soon as possible.

 Low Oil Pressure 

This red light will come on to indicate low engine oil pressure. If the 
light comes on while the engine is running, pull off the road as soon as it is 
safely possible, wait at least 5 minutes after turning the engine off to check 
oil level when vehicle is on level ground. If level is low, add oil, but do 
not overfill.

 Low Coolant 

All vehicles equipped with diesel engines have a low coolant warning 
system with a red indicator light mounted to the instrument panel. If this 
light comes on, correct the low coolant condition immediately.

 High Beam 

This blue indicator light will glow when the headlamps are operating on 
high beam. To change headlamps from low to high beam or high to low beam, 
press the foot-operated dimmer switch located on the floor.

 LH/RH Turn 

The green indicator will flash for left turn when the turn signal lever 
is pulled down, and will flash for right turn when the turn signal lever is 
pushed up.

 Inertia Fuel Shutoff Switch 

The fuel switch warning light will glow when the fuel pump shutoff 
switch has been triggered, preventing the engine from running by shutting off 
the fuel pump.

 Water Temperature 

This red light will come on to indicate a high engine coolant 
temperature. If the light comes on, operate the engine at a low rpm 
(approximately 1000 rpm) for five minutes, then low idle for 30-60 seconds. 
Stop the engine and let it cool. This procedure allows a hot engine to cool 
gradually. Check the coolant level, following the instructions about care in 
removing the filler cap. If the engine coolant is low, add coolant gradually, 
with the engine running.

 Transmission Temperature/Check Transmission 

This light comes on to indicate maximum transmission-to-cooler oil 
temperature of 149°C (300°F). Should the light come on, stop the 
vehicle and shift the transmission to neutral. Accelerate the engine to 
1200-1500 rpm to allow the transmission to return to normal temperature, 
71-104°C (160-220°F) before resuming operation. Check transmission oil 
level.

 Check A/C 

This warning light is used on vehicles equipped with air conditioning 
systems, to monitor and evaluate the air conditioner compressor operating 
temperatures and to shut the air conditioning system off if the temperature 
gets too high. If the in-cab warning light comes on when you are driving, it 
indicates a possible need for service. The air conditioner compressor will 
restart when the operating temperature returns to within the normal range.

 Exhaust Brake 

This light will illuminate when the engine exhaust brake is in the ON 
position.

 Brake Electric Motor 

The brake electric motor light and chime indicate operation of the 
reserve pump motor during braking. They also may indicate that the reserve 
pump motor system is inoperative.

 WARNING: IF THE BRAKE ELECTRIC MOTOR LIGHT AND CHIME REMAIN LIT AFTER THE ENGINE 
STARTS, THE VEHICLE HAS AN INOPERATIVE RESERVE PUMP SYSTEM. DO NOT OPERATE THE 
VEHICLE. 

 Low Air 

Vehicles with air brakes are equipped with a low air pressure warning 
light. The air brake systems are split or dual systems. If there is a loss of 
air pressure in either system (to a level below 414 kPa [60 psi]), the 
red warning light will illuminate and the chime will sound. The remaining 
brake system is capable of stopping the vehicle. However, the stopping 
distance will be greater.

 WARNING: IF THE LOW AIR PRESSURE WARNING LIGHT COMES ON WHEN YOU ARE DRIVING, IT 
IS AN INDICATION OF DAMAGE IN THE BRAKE SYSTEM. IMMEDIATE ATTENTION IS 
NECESSARY. DO NOT DRIVE THE VEHICLE. 

 WARNING: ANY INDICATED DAMAGE IN THE BRAKE SYSTEM MUST RECEIVE IMMEDIATE 
ATTENTION TO AVOID THE POSSIBILITY OF LOSS OF BRAKING AND PERSONAL INJURY. 

 Differential Lock 

This red indicator light will come on when the differential lockout 
control and wheel-to-wheel lock is in the LOCK position to indicate that the 
lockout mechanism in the tandem rear axle is engaged to provide extra 
traction, or if the single axle wheel lock is engaged.

 Parking Brake Warning Light/Chime 

On vehicles with a hydraulic brake system, the brake parking light will 
illuminate when the parking brakes are applied and momentarily when the key is 
placed in the START position. Upon actuation of the parking brake hand control 
to apply the brake, a chime will sound until brakes are fully applied.

 Daytime Running Lamps 

If this amber warning light is on, it indicates the headlights are 
illuminated at reduced intensity for daytime driving.
