1999 F800, FT900 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element, air cleaner housing or turbocharger inlet 
tube is removed, use a clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering 
the engine. 

Remove the fasteners that retain the cover assembly and remove the cover.

Release the seal gently. The air cleaner element fits tightly over the 
outlet tube, creating the critical seal on the inside diameter of the element 
end cap. Remove the element gently to reduce the amount of dust dislodged. 
There will be some initial resistance, similar to breaking the seal on a jar. 
Gently move the end of the element up and down and side to side or twist to 
break the seal.

[FIGURE: V8451A.gif]

Avoid dislodging dust from the air cleaner element. Gently pull the 
filter element off the outlet tube and out of the housing. Avoid knocking the 
element against the housing.

[FIGURE: V8452A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use care to avoid damage to the outlet tube to minimize air leaks. 

With a clean shop cloth, carefully clean the outlet tube where it 
extends into the housing. Inspect for possible air leaks in housing, inlet or 
outlet pipes.

[FIGURE: V8453A.gif]

Clean the inside of the outlet tube carefully. Dirt accidentally 
transferred to the inside of the outlet tube will reach the engine and cause 
wear. Use care not to damage the air cleaner element sealing area on the tube.

[FIGURE: V8454A.gif]

Check the old air cleaner element. Inspect for foreign material on the 
sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of dust on the clean air 
side of the air cleaner element seal is the tell-tale sign. If dust exists, 
make sure the cause is removed before installing a new air cleaner element.

 Installation 

Inspect the new air cleaner element for damage. Always look for 
possible shipping or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside 
of the open end (the sealing area). Check for cuts, etc. Do not use a damaged 
air cleaner element.

Insert the new air cleaner element properly. The radial seal area is on 
the inside of the open end of the air cleaner element. This critical sealing 
area will stretch slightly, adjust itself and distribute the sealing pressure 
evenly as the air cleaner element is forced onto the outlet tube. Apply firm 
pressure to complete a tight seal. Apply pressure at the outer rim of the air 
cleaner element, not the flexible center. Cover pressure is not necessary to 
make the air cleaner element seal.

[FIGURE: V8457A.gif]

Position the cover assembly on the housing and install the fasteners 
that retain the cover assembly. Cover pressure is not necessary to make the 
air cleaner element seal.

Press air restriction indicator reset button, located on the air 
restriction indicator.

[FIGURE: DV0675A.gif]

Check connections and ducts for air-tight fit. Make sure all clamps, 
flange connections and cleaner mounting bolts are tight. Seal any leaks in the 
clean air ducting before returning to service — they permit dirt to 
enter the engine directly. All connection seals from air cleaner to engine 
must be tight.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Inlet Restriction Check 

The best method for determining dry-type air cleaner maintenance 
periods is by checking the air restriction indicator. A visual inspection of 
the air cleaner element will not ascertain the need for service. The air 
cleaner should be serviced at regular scheduled maintenance intervals. 
Overservicing is not recommended.

Resetting the air restriction indicator each time the indicator is 
checked is recommended to verify the correct air restriction reading at the 
next check.

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine

The 7.0L (429 CID) V-8 engine incorporates one of two fuel systems. 
Fuel (gasoline) is supplied by electric fuel pumps located in the fuel tanks 
for the 7.0L MFI (multiport fuel injection) engine. Fuel system pressure is 
regulated by a fuel pressure regulator located on the fuel charging manifold. 
Liquid fuel is supplied to the 7.0L LPG (liquid propane gas) converter 
assembly under pressure from the fuel tanks. It is converted to a vaporous gas 
at the converter, mixed with air and supplied to the engine. Liquid LPG fuel 
pressure is regulated by a pressure regulator located behind the 
mixer/throttle body assembly. Refer to Section 03D-04A for a more detailed 
description of the LPG fuel system. 

The cylinder block is gray iron with extended cylinder bores. The 
crankshaft has five main bearings and is made of nodular iron alloy or forged 
steel. The pistons are hyper-eutectic, cast aluminum alloy, tin plated.

The exhaust valve seats are made of hi-nickel alloy. All valve stems 
are chrome plated with sodium cooled exhaust valves. Refer to the 
Specifications portion of this section for complete specifications. 

 WARNING: DO NOT PARK OR SERVICE A LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED VEHICLE 
NEAR ANY SOURCE OF FIRE, SUCH AS OPEN FLAME, CIGARETTES OR SMOKING MATERIALS, 
SPARKS, EXCESSIVE HEAT, WELDING, OR BODY GRINDING. AVOID PLACING THE VEHICLE 
NEAR ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT THAT DISCHARGES SPARKS THROUGH NORMAL OPERATION; FOR 
EXAMPLE, MOTORS, ELECTRICAL SWITCHES, AND RADIO TRANSMISSION EQUIPMENT. AVOID 
STORING OR SERVICING A VEHICLE OVER SEWER DRAINS, LUBRICATION PITS, SUB-FLOOR 
LEVEL ROOMS, OR OTHER LOW-LYING AREAS. IF ANY SOURCE OF FIRE OR IGNITION 
CONTACTS LPG VAPOR, A FIRE COULD RESULT. 

 WARNING: DO NOT NEEDLESSLY RELEASE LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL DURING 
SERVICE, AND DO NOT OPEN THE STOP-FILL VALVE WHILE A VEHICLE IS INSIDE A 
BUILDING. WHEN SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM, CLOSE THE FUEL TANK SHUTOFF VALVES 
(TWO VALVES IF EQUIPPED WITH TWO FUEL TANKS) AND RUN THE ENGINE OUT OF FUEL 
BEFORE DISCONNECTING FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENTS. IF THE FUEL TANK IS BEING 
SERVICED, HAVE THE FUEL EVACUATED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL AT A LOCAL LPG FUEL 
STATION. LPG FUEL VAPORIZES AT NORMAL BAROMETRIC PRESSURE AT TEMPERATURES 
ABOVE -42°C (-44°F), AND CAN EXPAND TO APPROXIMATELY 270 TIMES ITS 
VOLUME AS A LIQUID. UNNECESSARY VENTING OF LPG CAN CREATE FIRES AND HEALTH 
HAZARDS WHICH CAN LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY OR ILLNESS. 

 WARNING: FUEL TANKS SHOULD BE DRAINED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT ATTEMPT 
TO USE SHOP AIR PRESSURE TO FORCE LPG FROM THE TANKS. NORMAL FUEL SYSTEM 
PRESSURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1724 KPA (160 PSI) AT ROOM TEMPERATURE. CONNECTING 
A SHOP AIR HOSE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM CAN RESULT IN FUEL FLOWING BACK INTO THE 
SERVICE AIR SYSTEM, AND RESULT IN FIRE OR EXPLOSION. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE PAINT DRYING OVENS FOR LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED 
VEHICLES. THE HEAT OF PAINT DRYING OVENS WILL INCREASE PRESSURE IN THE FUEL 
TANKS. THIS CAN CAUSE VENTING OF THE LPG FUEL VAPOR INTO THE OVEN RESULTING IN 
FIRE FROM HEAT OR SPARK IN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. IF FUEL IS CONFINED IN AN 
OVEN, THERE IS ALSO THE RISK OF EXPLOSION IF THE FUEL IS IGNITED. WHEN 
REFINISHING THE BODY PANELS OF LPG-FUELED VEHICLES, SPOT PAINT THE AFFECTED 
AREA AND USE SPOT DRYING METHODS. 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY THE ENGINE FUEL SYSTEM CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS, OR 
REPLACE COMPONENTS WITH PARTS THAT DO NOT MEET FORD SPECIFICATIONS. FORD 
SPECIFIED PARTS ARE AVAILABLE AT AUTHORIZED FORD DEALERS. THE LIQUID PETROLEUM 
GAS (LPG) FUEL STORAGE SYSTEM MUST CONFORM TO NATIONAL FIRE PROTECTION 
ASSOCIATION STANDARD NO. 58, AND SIMILAR CANADIAN GAS ASSOCIATION STANDARDS. 
THESE STANDARDS DEFINE THE SPECIALLY-APPROVED MATERIALS, COMPONENT 
CONSTRUCTION, AND THE SYSTEM INSTALLED ON ALL VEHICLES, WHICH IS PRECISELY 
CALIBRATED FOR EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE USE OF DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS 
CAN PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT COULD RESULT IN FIRE, EXPLOSION AND 
PERSONAL INJURY, ENGINE DAMAGE, OR NONCOMPLIANCE TO CURRENT EMISSION 
STANDARDS. 

 WARNING: AVOID INHALING LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) OR OCCUPYING CONFINED AREAS 
CONTAINING LPG. LPG IS HEAVIER THAN AIR. THE HEAVIER GAS CAN DISPLACE OR 
"PUSH" FRESH AIR OUT OF AN AREA. IN LARGE QUANTITIES LPG CAN DISPLACE ENOUGH 
OXYGEN TO MAKE THE SURROUNDING AIR UNFIT TO BREATHE, AND POSSIBLY CAUSE 
ILLNESS. IF A PERSON BREATHES LPG OR AIR WHICH LACKS OXYGEN DUE TO THE 
PRESENCE OF LPG, HEADACHE, DIZZINESS, AND WEAKNESS IN THE EXTREMITIES CAN 
RESULT. IN SEVERE CASES, PROLONGED EXPOSURE TO LPG-FUELED AIR CAN BE LETHAL. 

IN THE EVENT OF EXPOSURE TO LPG, MOVE THE VICTIM IMMEDIATELY TO FRESH 
AIR AND CONTACT A PHYSICIAN OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY PERSONNEL FOR ARTIFICIAL 
RESPIRATION OR OTHER REQUIRED TREATMENT. 

 CAUTION: If a confined area, such as a lubrication pit, has been exposed to 
liquid petroleum gas (LPG), the area must be checked for adequate oxygen 
levels by local health department personnel before being entered. Otherwise, 
illness or suffocation can result. 

Refer to Section 03D-04A for a more detailed description of the LPG 
fuel system.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Identification

For quick engine identification, refer to the Safety Certification Decal.

The decal is mounted on the LH front door lock face panel.

Find the engine code (letter or number) on the decal, then refer to the 
engine identification chart to determine the engine type and size.

An engine identification label is also attached to the engine.

The symbol code on the identification tag identifies each engine for 
determining parts usage; for instance, engine cubic inch displacement and 
model year.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Exhaust Emission Control System 

Description and operation and required maintenance of the exhaust 
control devices used on these engines are covered in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

All models have EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) valves. The 7.0L MFI 
High Output engine has dual secondary air injection pumps. The 7.0L LPG and 
7.0L MFI Economy engines have a single (RH) secondary air injection pump.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Induction System, 7.0 Gasoline Engine

The multiport fuel injection system (MFI) is a multi-point, pulse time, 
speed density fuel injection system. Fuel is metered into the intake air 
stream (in accordance with engine demand) through eight injectors mounted on 
the intake manifold.

================================================================================
PAGE 4142
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Induction System, 7.0 LPG Engine

Liquid propane gas flows from the fuel tank through a hydrostatic 
relief valve, vacuum-activated fuel lock and filter, to the converter. In the 
converter the liquid becomes a vapor which flows to the carburetor where it is 
mixed with air in the proper proportions for maximum engine performance.

================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Crankshaft

The crankshaft is supported by five crankshaft bearings and bearing 
caps. The crankshaft thrust main bearing (No. 3 bearing insert) limits 
crankshaft end play and absorbs thrust loads applied to the crankshaft ends. 
The camshaft sprocket, crankshaft sprocket and timing chain connect the 
crankshaft with the camshaft and provide a 2:1 drive ratio.

================================================================================
PAGE 4144
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Camshaft

The camshaft is installed in the cylinder block and is supported by 
five camshaft bearings pressed into the cylinder block bores. Thrust loads and 
end play are limited by a camshaft thrust plate installed at the front of the 
camshaft.

================================================================================
PAGE 4145
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve Train

A hydraulic valve tappet, providing automatic lash adjustment, rides on 
a camshaft lobe and transfers its up-and-down motion to the rocker arm through 
a push rod. The rocker arms are pedestal-mounted and pivot on rocker arm seats 
bolted to the cylinder head. The intake valves and exhaust valves are arranged 
alternately in the cylinder head.

================================================================================

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Positive Crankcase Ventilation System 

These engines are equipped with a positive, closed-type crankcase 
ventilation system that directs crankcase vapors to the intake manifold for 
combustion.

================================================================================
PAGE 4147
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Lubrication System 

The heart of the lubrication system is a full-pressure cast-iron pump. 
The high-capacity gerotor design pump is driven by a hex shaft from the 
distributor. Lubrication system pressure is controlled by a relief valve.

[FIGURE: A5502D.gif]

Oil is directed through drilled passages directly to the full-flow oil 
filter. Oil is directed from the filter to the main oil galleries, which 
intersect the valve tappet bores. A drilled gallery (crossover) at the rear of 
the tappet chamber routes oil to the left bank. The crankshaft main bearings, 
connecting rod bearings and camshaft bearings are supplied with oil from the 
right oil gallery. 

Oil flows to the camshaft sprocket and timing chain through an annulus 
and drilled passage at the front of the No. 1 camshaft bearing. Oil flow to 
the rocker arms is through the valve tappets and up the push rods to the 
rocker arms.

================================================================================
PAGE 4148
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Cooling System 

The cooling system employed is a series-parallel flow. Coolant flow is 
from the water pump through passages in the engine front cover (both sides) to 
the cylinder block. Flow continues through the cylinder block to the rear and 
up through the deck or head faces, out through the cylinder head to the water 
crossover at the front of the intake manifold, through the water outlet 
connection (thermostat housing) and to the top of the radiator. A portion of 
the coolant flows from the cylinder block to the cylinder head by way of 
transfer holes to eliminate stagnant pockets and prevent steam buildup.

[FIGURE: A5503C.gif]

Valve Cover and Gasket

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spark Plug Wire Remover

T74P-6666-A

 Removal 

Remove the air cleaner assembly and hoses. Refer to Section 03D-12 for 
7.0L LPG engine, or Section 03C-12 for 7.0L MFI engine for service procedures.

If the right valve cover (6582)
 is to be 
removed, remove the secondary air injection bypass diverter valves, hoses and 
bracket as an assembly. Disconnect the crankcase ventilation hose at the crankcase vent filter (6A768)
.

If the left valve cover
 is to be 
removed, disconnect and remove the ignition coil (12029)
, AIR 
and EVR solenoids. Refer to Section 03C-07 for service procedures. Also remove 
the crankcase ventilation tube (6758)
 from the positive crankcase ventilation valve (PCV valve) (6A666)
. 

Disconnect the spark plug wires at the spark plugs (12405)
using 
Spark Plug Wire Remover T74P-6666-A. Remove the spark plug wires from the 
retainers on the valve covers
and 
position them out of the way. 

Remove the bolts that hold the valve covers
in place. 

Remove the valve covers
. If the valve cover
is tight 
on the cylinder head (6049), 
tap it lightly with a plastic or rubber mallet to loosen. 

 Installation 

Clean the valve cover(s) and cylinder head mating surfaces. 

Install a new valve cover gasket.

Position the valve cover
 on the cylinder head
. 

On the right valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the front and working 
rearward.

On the left valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the back and working 
forward. 

 Valve Cover and Filter 

[FIGURE: A15272D.gif]

 NOTE: Whenever an ignition wire is removed from a spark plug, ignition coil 
or distributor cap terminal, silicone compound must be applied to the spark 
plug wire boot before it is reconnected. Using a small, clean tool, lightly 
coat the entire inner surface of the boot with Silicone Dielectric Compound 
D7AZ-19A331-A (Motorcraft WA-10) or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESE-M1C171-A.

Connect the spark plug wires to the spark plugs
and 
connect them to the wire retainers on the valve covers
. 

If the left valve cover
 was 
removed, install the ignition coil, AIR and EVR solenoids. Refer to Section 03C-07 . Also install the crankcase ventilation tube
 and positive crankcase ventilation valve
 at this time. 

If the right valve cover
 was 
removed, install the secondary air injection bypass diverter valves, hoses and 
bracket assembly. Connect the crankcase ventilation hose to the crankcase vent filter
.

Install the air cleaner assembly and hoses as outlined in Section 03C-12 for 7.0L MFI engine or 03D-12 for 7.0L LPG engine. 

Start the engine and check for leaks.

Rocker Arm 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spark Plug Wire Remover

T74P-6666-A

 Removal 

Remove valve cover (6582)
. Refer to 
Valve Cover and Gasket in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

Remove the rocker arm seat bolt, rocker arm seat (6A528)
 and 
the rocker arm (6564).

[FIGURE: A21991A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not mix rocker arm seats and rocker arms. They must stay together as 
a set. 

Apply Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-B to the top of the valve stems, rocker arms
 and the rocker arm seats
. 
Make sure the rocker arm seat base is inserted in its slot on the cylinder head (6049)
 before 
tightening the rocker arm seat bolts.

Position the No. 1 piston on TDC at the end of the compression stroke 
(firing) POSITION 1 and install the rocker arm
, rocker arm seat
 and 
rocker arm seat bolt onto the following valves:

No. 1 Intake and No. 1 Exhaust 

No. 3 Intake and No. 4 and 5 Exhaust 

No. 7 Intake and No. 8 Intake and Exhaust 

Rotate the crankshaft (6303)
 one 
complete revolution clockwise from position No. 1 and install the rocker arm
, rocker arm seat
 and 
rocker arm seat bolt onto the following valves: 

No. 2 Intake and Exhaust 

No. 3 Exhaust and No. 4 and 5 Intake 

No. 6 Intake and Exhaust 

No. 7 Exhaust 

Tighten the rocker arm seat bolts to 25-33 Nm (18-24 lb-ft). 
Check the valve clearance following the procedures under Adjustments, Valve 
Clearance in this section. 

Install valve cover
. Refer to 
Valve Cover and Gasket in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Valve Spring, Retainer and Valve Stem Seal 

Broken valve springs (6513)
 or worn 
or damaged valve stem seals (6571)
 or 
retainers may be replaced without removing the cylinder head (6049)
 if 
valve or valve seat is not damaged. 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Compressor

T70P-6049-A

 Removal 

Remove the valve cover (6582)
 on the 
side of the engine that has the worn or damaged part. Refer to In-Vehicle 
Service, Valve Cover and Gasket removal procedure in this section.

Remove the spark plug (12405)
 from the 
affected cylinder. 

Crank engine until the piston is at TDC at the end of the compression 
stroke on the cylinder being repaired. 

Remove rocker arm bolts, rocker arm seats (6A528)
, rocker arms (6564)
, and push rods (6565)
 from 
affected cylinder(s). 

Using a suitable adapter, install air line in spark plug hole. Turn on 
air supply to hold valves closed. 

Install Valve Spring Compressor T70P-6049-A, and compress valve spring
.

[FIGURE: A10098B.gif]

 Remove valve spring retainer keys (6518)
, valve spring retainer (6514)
, and valve spring. 
Remove and discard valve stem seal
. If 
air pressure fails to hold valve in closed position, valve damage affecting 
sealing is indicated. Remove and inspect cylinder head
.

[FIGURE: A103891A.gif]

Wrap rubber band, tape or string around end of valve stem to prevent 
valve from dropping into cylinder when air pressure in cylinder is shut off or 
if piston, pin and ring (6102)
 is at bottom of cylinder. Shut off air pressure. 

Inspect valve stem for damage. Rotate valve, checking tip for eccentric 
movement. Move valve up and down through normal travel in valve guide and 
check for binding. If valve is damaged, cylinder head
 must be 
removed for repairs.

 Installation 

If valve proves satisfactory, hold valve closed and turn on air 
pressure in cylinder. 

Lubricate the valve stems with heavy engine oil. Install new valve stem seal
. Set valve spring
 and valve spring retainer

over valve stem. Compress valve spring
 and 
install valve spring retainer keys
. Release valve spring
 and remove tool.

[FIGURE: A10098B.gif]

Shut off air pressure and remove air line and adapter. Install spark plug
. 

Apply Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-B to tip of valve stem and each end 
of push rod. Install push rod
. Make sure 
lower end of push rod 
is seated in valve tappet (6500)
.

Lubricate rocker arm seats

and sockets with Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-B. 

Lubricate the push rod socket, fulcrum seat and the valve pad of the rocker arm
 with 
specified engine oil.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Valve Tappet, Hydraulic

The following procedure is applicable for removing one or all of the valve tappets (6500)
. Before 
replacing a hydraulic valve tappet
 for 
noisy operation, verify the noise is not caused by improper valve clearance or 
by worn valve tappet 
or push rods (6565). 

 Removal 

Remove upper and lower intake manifolds (9424)
 as 
an assembly. Refer to Intake Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of 
this section.

Remove the valve covers (6582)
. Loosen 
the rocker arm seat bolts and turn rocker arms (6564)
 to one 
side.

[FIGURE: A15758A.gif]

Remove the push rods
 in 
sequence. 

 NOTE: If the valve tappets
 are to 
be reused, they must be returned to the same bore.

Remove the valve tappets
 with a 
magnet. Place them in a rack in sequence. If the valve tappets
 are 
stuck in bores, use a Hydraulic Tappet Puller to remove them. Rotate valve tappets
 back 
and forth to loosen them from gum or varnish deposits.

[FIGURE: A10372D.gif]

Refer to Section 03-00 , for inspection and cleaning procedures. If it 
becomes necessary to disassemble valve tappet
, refer 
to Valve Tappet, Hydraulic under Subassemblies in the Disassembly and Assembly 
portion of this section. 

 Installation 

Clean the outside of valve tappets
. Valve tappet
and bores 
are to be lubricated with specified engine oil before installation. Install 
the valve tappetsin 
their original bores. Check any new valve tappet
 for free 
fit in bore to which it is to be installed.

Prior to installation of a valve tappet
, make 
sure valve tappet is 
full of oil by working the valve tappet plunger up and down until it fills 
with fluid and all traces of air bubbles have disappeared. 

Install push rods
 in original 
positions. Apply Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-MIC159-A and ESB-M1C93-B to valve stem tips and push rod 
ends. 

Install the rocker arms
. Refer to 
Rocker Arm in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section. Adjust valve 
clearance. 

Clean the valve cover(s) and cylinder head mating surfaces.

Position the valve cover
 on the cylinder head (6049)
.

On the right valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the front and working 
rearward.

On the left valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the back and working forward.

Install upper and lower intake manifolds
. 
Refer to Intake Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

Section 03C-01: Engine, 7.0L Gasoline and LPG

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Intake Manifold 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spark Plug Wire Remover

T74P-6666-A

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT PARK OR SERVICE A LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED VEHICLE NEAR 
ANY SOURCE OF FIRE, SUCH AS OPEN FLAME, CIGARETTES OR SMOKING MATERIALS, 
SPARKS, EXCESSIVE HEAT, WELDING, OR BODY GRINDING. AVOID PLACING THE VEHICLE 
NEAR ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT THAT DISCHARGES SPARKS THROUGH NORMAL OPERATION, FOR 
EXAMPLE, MOTORS, ELECTRICAL SWITCHES, AND RADIO TRANSMISSION EQUIPMENT. AVOID 
STORING OR SERVICING A VEHICLE OVER SEWER DRAINS, LUBRICATION PITS, SUB-FLOOR 
LEVEL ROOMS, OR OTHER LOW-LYING AREAS. IF ANY SOURCE OF FIRE OR IGNITION 
CONTACTS LPG VAPOR, A FIRE CAN RESULT. 

 WARNING: DO NOT NEEDLESSLY RELEASE LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) DURING SERVICE, 
AND DO NOT OPEN THE STOP-FILL VALVE WHILE A VEHICLE IS INSIDE A BUILDING. WHEN 
SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM, CLOSE THE FUEL TANK SHUTOFF VALVES (TWO VALVES IF 
EQUIPPED WITH TWO FUEL TANKS) AND RUN THE ENGINE OUT OF FUEL BEFORE 
DISCONNECTING FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENTS. IF THE FUEL TANK IS BEING SERVICED, HAVE 
THE FUEL EVACUATED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL AT A LOCAL LPG FUEL STATION. LIQUID 
PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) VAPORIZES AT NORMAL BAROMETRIC PRESSURE AT TEMPERATURES 
ABOVE -42°C (-44°F), AND CAN EXPAND TO APPROXIMATELY 270 TIMES ITS 
VOLUME AS A LIQUID. UNNECESSARY VENTING OF LPG CAN CREATE FIRES AND HEALTH 
HAZARDS WHICH CAN LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY OR ILLNESS. 

 WARNING: FUEL TANKS SHOULD BE DRAINED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT ATTEMPT 
TO USE SHOP AIR PRESSURE TO FORCE LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FROM THE TANKS. 
NORMAL FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1724 KPA (160 PSI) AT ROOM 
TEMPERATURE. CONNECTING A SHOP AIR HOSE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM CAN RESULT IN FUEL 
FLOWING BACK INTO THE SERVICE AIR SYSTEM, AND RESULT IN FIRE OR EXPLOSION. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE PAINT DRYING OVENS FOR LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED 
VEHICLES. THE HEAT OF PAINT DRYING OVENS WILL INCREASE PRESSURE IN THE FUEL 
TANKS. THIS CAN CAUSE VENTING OF THE LPG VAPOR INTO THE OVEN RESULTING IN FIRE 
FROM HEAT OR SPARK IN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. IF FUEL IS CONFINED IN AN OVEN, 
THERE IS ALSO THE RISK OF EXPLOSION IF THE FUEL IS IGNITED. WHEN REFINISHING 
THE BODY PANELS OF LPG-FUELED VEHICLES, SPOT PAINT THE AFFECTED AREA AND USE 
SPOT DRYING METHODS. 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY THE ENGINE FUEL SYSTEM CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS, OR 
REPLACE COMPONENTS WITH PARTS THAT DO NOT MEET FORD SPECIFICATIONS. FORD 
SPECIFIED PARTS ARE AVAILABLE AT AUTHORIZED FORD DEALERS. THE LIQUID PETROLEUM 
GAS (LPG) FUEL STORAGE SYSTEM MUST CONFORM TO NATIONAL FIRE PROTECTION 
ASSOCIATION STANDARD NO. 58, AND SIMILAR CANADIAN GAS ASSOCIATION STANDARDS. 
THESE STANDARDS DEFINE THE SPECIALLY-APPROVED MATERIALS, COMPONENT 
CONSTRUCTION, AND THE SYSTEM INSTALLED ON ALL VEHICLES, WHICH IS PRECISELY 
CALIBRATED FOR EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE USE OF DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS 
CAN PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT COULD RESULT IN FIRE, EXPLOSION AND 
PERSONAL INJURY, ENGINE DAMAGE, OR NONCOMPLIANCE TO CURRENT EMISSION 
STANDARDS. 

 WARNING: AVOID INHALING LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) OR OCCUPYING CONFINED AREAS 
CONTAINING LPG. LPG IS HEAVIER THAN AIR. THE HEAVIER GAS CAN DISPLACE OR 
"PUSH" FRESH AIR OUT OF AN AREA. IN LARGE QUANTITIES LPG CAN DISPLACE ENOUGH 
OXYGEN TO MAKE THE SURROUNDING AIR UNFIT TO BREATHE, AND POSSIBLY CAUSE 
ILLNESS. IF A PERSON BREATHES LPG OR AIR WHICH LACKS OXYGEN DUE TO THE 
PRESENCE OF LPG, HEADACHE, DIZZINESS, AND WEAKNESS IN THE EXTREMITIES CAN 
RESULT. IN SEVERE CASES, PROLONGED EXPOSURE TO LPG-FUELED AIR CAN BE LETHAL. 

IN THE EVENT OF EXPOSURE TO LPG, MOVE THE VICTIM IMMEDIATELY TO FRESH 
AIR AND CONTACT A PHYSICIAN OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY PERSONNEL FOR ARTIFICIAL 
RESPIRATION OR OTHER REQUIRED TREATMENT. 

Relieve fuel system pressure. Refer to service procedures in Section or 
03C-04 for 7.0L MFI engine, or Section 03D-04A for 7.0L LPG engine. 

Drain cooling system. Remove the engine air cleaner (ACL) (9600)

and all hose assemblies including the H-fitting at the MFI engine throttle body (9E926)
 or 
T-fitting at LPG carburetor. 

Disconnect upper radiator hose (8260)

at the engine.

position them out of the way. Loosen the water pump bypass hose clamp at the water hose connection (8592)

Remove the fuel line redundant clips from the fuel line connectors at 
the fuel injection supply manifold (9F792)
 (7.0L MFI engine). 

 CAUTION: If a confined area, such as a lubrication pit, has been exposed to 
liquid petroleum gas (LPG), the area must be checked for adequate oxygen 
levels by local health department personnel before being entered. Otherwise, 
illness or suffocation can result. 

Using Disconnect Tool D87L-9280-A or -B or equivalent, disconnect the 
supply and return fuel hoses at the fuel injection supply manifold
for 7.0L MFI engine. Disconnect fuel supply line at the fuelock for 7.0L LPG

Note all cautions and warnings.

Cylinder Head(s)

 Removal 

Remove upper and lower intake manifolds (9424)
 as 
an assembly. Refer to Intake Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of 
this section. 

Disconnect muffler inlet pipe at exhaust manifolds (9430)
. 

Some applications may require removal of exhaust manifold
 at 
the cylinder heads (6049). 

Loosen generator and secondary air injection pump bracket attaching 
bolts and remove brackets. 

If equipped with air conditioning, shut off compressor at service 
valves and remove valves and hoses from compressor. Remove nuts attaching 
compressor support bracket to water pump (8501)
. Remove 
bolts attaching compressor to upper mounting bracket and position compressor 
out of the way. Remove compressor upper mounting bracket from cylinder head
. Remove 
bolts attaching power steering pump bracket to water pump
. Position 
reservoir and bracket out of the way. Remove air brake and secondary air 
injection brackets as necessary. 

Remove valve covers (6582)
. Remove 
rocker arm seat bolts, rocker arms (6564)
, rocker arm seats (6A528)
and push rods (6565)
 in sequence 
so they can be installed in their original positions.

[FIGURE: A15758A.gif]

Remove cylinder head attaching bolts. Lift cylinder heads
and exhaust manifolds
 as 
assemblies from cylinder block with a hoist. If necessary to loosen cylinder 
head gasket seal, pry at forward corners of cylinder heads

against casting bosses provided on cylinder block. Do not damage machined 
surfaces of cylinder head
 or 
cylinder block. Discard head gasket (6051)
.

If disassembly or machining of cylinder head
 is 
required, remove exhaust manifold
. 

 Installation 

Clean cylinder head
, lower intake manifold
, valve cover
, and 
cylinder block gasket surfaces. If cylinder head
 was 
removed for cylinder head gasket replacement, check flatness of cylinder head
 and 
cylinder block gasket surfaces. 

 NOTE: A gasket tab should protrude at the front lower corner when properly 
installed. 

Position new head gasket
 on 
cylinder block over dowels.

 NOTE: When this procedure is used, it is not necessary to retighten bolts 
after extended operation.

Do not apply sealer to cylinder head gasket surfaces. Place cylinder heads
 on 
cylinder block, and install remaining attaching bolts (longer bolts in lower 
row of bolt holes). Tighten all cylinder head attaching bolts in sequence, in 
three steps: 

95-108 Nm (70-80 lb-ft) 

136-149 Nm (100-110 lb-ft) 

177-189 Nm (130-140 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A103931A.gif]

Clean and inspect push rods
, one at a 
time. Clean the oil passage in the push rods
 with a 
suitable solvent, and blow out with compressed air. 

Install push rods
 in original 
positions. Apply Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford

ends. 

Lubricate and install the rocker arms
. Refer to 
Rocker Arm in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section. Make sure lower 
ends of push rods 
remain seated in valve tappets (6500)
. Adjust 
valve clearance.

Clean the valve cover(s) and cylinder head mating surfaces. 

Position the valve cover
 on the cylinder head
. 

On the right valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the front and working 
rearward.

On the left valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the back and working 
forward. 

Install exhaust inlet pipes to the exhaust manifold
. 

Install upper and lower intake manifold assembly. Refer to Intake 
Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

If equipped with air conditioning, install compressor upper mounting 
bracket to cylinder head. Attach compressor to upper mounting bracket. Attach 
power steering reservoir (left side) and compressor mounting bracket (right 
side) to water pump. 
Connect service valves and hoses to compressor. Install air compressor 
(brake), secondary air injection pump and brackets, if so equipped. Attach 
power steering reservoir bracket to left cylinder head
. 

Install generator bracket and secondary air injection pump brackets to 
right cylinder head. 
Tighten retaining bolts to 41-61 Nm (30-45 lb-ft). Adjust generator 
drive belt tension to specifications and tighten attaching bolts to 33-46 
Nm (24-34 lb-ft). Refer to Specifications for belt tension. 

Fill radiator (8005) 
and power steering reservoir, as necessary. 

Start engine and check for leaks. 

Check curb idle speed. Refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual for 
service procedure. Refer to the engine decal for specifications. 

If equipped with air conditioning, evacuate compressor and partially 
charge system. Refer to Section 12-00 .

[FIGURE: A15763C.gif]

 and

.

.

.

Position compressor onto the mounting bracket. Install attaching bolts.

 and fan shroud
. Refer to 
 Section 03C-05 .

Install the engine air cleaner

as outlined in Section 03C-12 (7.0L MFI engine) or Section 03D-12 (7.0L LPG 
engine).

If the engine front cover (6019)
 is 
being removed to replace the engine front cover gasket (6020)
, it is not necessary to check the timing chain deflection. For engine timing 
cover gasket replacement, it is not necessary to remove the timing chain camshaft sprocket (6256)
 and crankshaft sprocket (6306)
. 

Drain the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . Remove the engine air cleaner (ACL) (9600)
. Disconnect the battery ground cable. 

Disconnect the upper radiator hose (8260)

at the water hose connection (8592)
. Disconnect the lower radiator hose (8286)

at the water pump (8501). 

Disconnect the transmission fluid cooler lines, if so equipped. Remove 
the radiator (8005) and 
support as an assembly. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

Disconnect the heater hose at the water pump
. Remove 
the water pump bypass hose. 

Remove the power steering pump and position it to one side, leaving 
the hoses attached. 

If equipped with an air compressor, remove the attaching bolts and 
position the compressor on the frame rail. 

Remove the generator adjusting arm bolt at the generator (GEN) (10346)
. 
Remove the drive belts. Disconnect the wires and remove the generator
 from 
the support bracket. Remove the water pump
and cooling 
fan drive belts. Remove the water pump
 and fan blade (8600)
as an 
assembly. 

Remove the crankshaft damper bolt and washer from the end of the crankshaft (6303)
. Install 
Damper Remover/Replacer Tool T79T-6316-A on the crankshaft damper assembly and 
remove the crankshaft damper assembly. Remove bolts on crankshaft pulley (6312)
.

[FIGURE: A4777D.gif]

 NOTE: Front engine support bracket (6028) has 6 bolts common with engine front cover
. 

 NOTE: Oil pan gasket (6710) 
must be replaced following the procedure described under Oil Pan/Pump Screen 
Cover and Tube in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

Raise engine slightly. Remove the bolts attaching the engine front cover

and front engine support bracket
 to the cylinder block and the oil pan (6675)
. Remove the engine front cover
, 
and the front engine support bracket
. 

[FIGURE: A21992A.gif]

Discard the engine front cover gasket

Check the timing chain deflection. Refer to Specifications in this 
section for allowable tolerance. 

Check the camshaft end play. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

 Installation 

Clean the crankshaft damper assembly. 

Clean all oil pan, cylinder block, and engine front cover gasket 
surfaces. Remove old crankshaft front seal (6700)
. Refer to Section 03-00 for cleaning and inspection procedures. 

Coat the gasket surfaces of the cylinder block and engine front cover

with Perfect Seal Sealing Compound B5A-19554-A or F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A and position a new engine front cover gasket
 on the cylinder block. 

 CAUTION: Use care when installing the engine front cover
 to 
avoid sealer damage or possible engine front cover gasket
 mislocation. 

Position the engine front cover

onto the cylinder block. 

Install suitable engine front cover aligner and, while pushing in on 
the tool, align the oil pan gasket surfaces with the engine front cover
and 
cylinder block. Tighten the upper engine front cover-to-cylinder block 
attaching bolts to 21-28 Nm (15-21 lb-ft).

Position the front engine support bracket
, generator mounting bracket, and adjusting arm bracket on the engine front cover
. 
Install the remaining bolts. Tighten engine support 5/16-inch bolts to 17-24 
Nm (13-18 lb-ft) and 7/16-inch bolts to 62-74 Nm (46-55 lb-ft). 
Tighten generator mount bracket to 41-61 Nm (30-45 lb-ft) and adjusting 
arm bracket to 33-46 Nm (24-34 lb-ft). 

Thread the forcing screw adapter of the Damper Remover/Replacer Tool 
T79T-6316-A into the crankshaft
. 

Position the crankshaft front seal

under the Front Cover Aligner T79T-6019-A. Position the tool and crankshaft 
front seal assembly in the engine front cover
. 

Slide the Damper Remover/Replacer Sleeve T79T-6316-A4 over the Damper 
Remover/Replacer Forcing Screw T79T-6316-A1 and thread the forcing screw into 
the forcing nut. Make sure the installation sleeve seats in the groove in the 
seal replacer disc.

[FIGURE: DA1347A.gif]

Turn the forcing nut while holding the forcing screw to properly seat 
the crankshaft front seal
. 

Remove the tools.

Replace oil pan gasket
. Refer

Lubricate the crankshaft damper assembly hub and line up the crankshaft 
 damper assembly keyway with the key on the crankshaft
. Position

Install the Damper Remover/Replacer Tool T79T-6316-A into the crankshaft
. 

Slide the Damper Remover/Replacer Sleeve T79T-6316-A4 over the Damper 
Remover/Replacer Forcing Screw T79T-6316-A1 and thread the forcing screw into 
the forcing screw adapter tool.

[FIGURE: A48431C.gif]

Turn the forcing screw nut with a wrench while holding the forcing 
screw to properly seat the crankshaft damper assembly on the crankshaft

Remove the tools.

Clean the water pump gasket surfaces. Coat new water pump gasket and engine front cover gasket
 with Perfect Seal Sealing Compound B5A-19554-A or F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent

sealer and position the gaskets on the engine front cover
 or water pump
. Install 
the water pump and fan assembly. Tighten the attaching bolts to 17-24 
Nm (13-18 lb-ft). 

Install the generator
 and 
electrical connector. Install generator
 and water pump
drive 
belt(s). Install the power steering pump and drive belt. If equipped with an

in this section for belt tension.

Connect the heater hose to the water pump

the water pump bypass hose and tighten the hose clamps.

 and radiator 
support as an assembly. Refer to Section 03C-03 . Connect the lower radiator hose

at the water pump and 
the upper radiator hose
 at the water hose connection
. Connect transmission fluid cooler lines, if so equipped. 

If any of the coolant has entered the oil pan
 when 
separating the engine front cover

from the cylinder block, the crankcase should be drained and flushed. 

Fill the crankcase with the correct type and quantity of oil. 

Fill and bleed the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . Check and 
adjust automatic transmission fluid as required, if so equipped.

Connect battery ground cable.

Install the engine air cleaner

and operate the engine at fast idle to check for coolant and oil leaks. Adjust 
the ignition timing to specifications on engine decal.

Camshaft 

If the camshaft (6250)
 and distributor drive gear are being replaced because of wear, the following 
steps must be followed to prevent a repeat failure: 

Remove the oil pan (6675)
 and clean the 
oil pan sump. 

Inspect the front face of the cylinder block (oil pan area) and clean 
any debris or shavings that might be present. 

Inspect the oil pump (6600)
 and replace 
if worn or damaged. 

Replace the oil pump screen, tube and cover assembly if necessary. 

Change the engine oil and oil bypass filter (6714)
. 

The camshaft 
and related parts are shown in the following illustration.

[FIGURE: A10396C.gif]

 Removal 

Crank engine until No. 1 piston is at TDC at the end of the compression 
stroke.

Remove engine front cover (6019)
. 
Refer to Engine Front Cover in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

Remove timing chain and sprockets. Refer to Timing Chain and Sprockets 
in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

Remove the upper and lower intake manifold (9424)
 as 
an assembly. Refer to Intake Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of 
this section.

Remove valve covers (6582)
. Back 
off all rocker arm seat bolts, turn rocker arms (6564)
 sideways, 
and remove the push rods (6565)
 in 
sequence. 

Remove the valve tappets (6500)
 with a 
magnet and place them in a rack in sequence. If the valve tappets
 are 
stuck in bores, use a hydraulic lifter puller tool to remove them. Rotate the valve tappet
 back and 
forth to loosen it from gum or varnish deposits. 

Remove the bolts attaching the air conditioning condenser to the 
chassis, if so equipped, and carefully move the condenser to rest on the left 
fender. Secure it in this position. 

Remove the grille. 

 CAUTION: Do not damage the camshaft bearings (6261)
. 

Remove the camshaft thrust plate bolts. Carefully remove the camshaft
 from the 
front of engine. Refer to Section 03-00 for cleaning and inspection 
procedures. Repair if required. 

 Installation 

Oil the camshaft journals and apply Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A to the 
camshaft lobes. Carefully slide camshaft
 into 
position. Use a long stud threaded into the bolt hole for a hand hold when 
installing camshaft. 

Install camshaft thrust plate (6269)
. Tighten camshaft thrust plate bolts to 13-16 Nm (10-12 lb-ft). (The camshaft sprocket (6256)

must be installed to check end play.) Check camshaft end play. Refer to 
 Section 03-00 for service procedures. If end play is excessive, replace the camshaft thrust plate
. 

Install timing chain and sprockets. Refer to Timing Chain and Sprockets 
in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section. Install engine front cover
. 
Refer to Engine Front Cover in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

Install the grille, center support and air conditioning condenser, if 
so equipped. Refer to Section 12-03A for service procedures. 

Clean the valve tappets

externally. Lubricate the valve tappets
 and 
valve tappet bores with specified engine oil before installing them. Lubricate 
the push rod ends with Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-B and ESB-M1C93-B. Install the valve tappets
 and push rods
in their 
original positions. 

Install rocker arms
. Refer to 
Rocker Arm in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section. Adjust valve 
clearance.

Clean the valve cover(s) and cylinder head mating surfaces. 

Position the valve cover
 on the cylinder head (6049)
. 

On the right valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the front and working 
rearward.

On the left valve cover
, tighten 
bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) starting at the back and working 
forward. 

Install upper and lower intake manifold
 as 
an assembly. Refer to Intake Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of 
this section.

Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen Cover and Tube

 Removal 

Drain the crankcase and remove the oil level indicator and tube 
assembly. 

Remove the air brake compressor oil drain back hose, if so equipped. 

Remove the oil pan attaching bolts. Lower the oil pan (6675)
 and let it 
rest on the axle. Position the crankshaft (6303)
 so that 
the counterweights will clear the oil pan
. 

Remove the oil pump attaching bolts and the oil pump screen, tube and 
cover assembly attaching nut. Allow the oil pump (6600)
, oil pump 
screen, tube and cover assembly and the oil pump intermediate shaft (6A618)
to rest in the oil pan
. 

Remove cotter pin and attaching nut from one end of the steering 
connecting rod. Reinstall the attaching nut upside down on the stud and tap it 
with a hammer to loosen the connecting rod. Remove the rod and swing it out of 
the way. 

Remove the oil pan
 from vehicle. 
Refer to Section 03-00 for cleaning and inspection procedures. 

 Installation 

Clean the oil pan and cylinder block gasket surfaces. 

Apply Silicone Gasket Adhesive E6AZ-19562-A or equivalent to cylinder 
block rails and engine front cover (6019)
. 

 NOTE: Refer to the illustration after Step No. 6 to see Areas B and C. 

Apply a bead of Silicone Rubber F4AZ-19562-B or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications WSE-M4G323-A1 and ESE-M4G195-A (two places, Area C) to the 
parting line between the engine front cover

and cylinder block. Also (four places, Area B) to the parting line between the 
cylinder block and front and rear main bearing caps. Immediately install the oil pan gasket (6710)
 on the 
cylinder block to facilitate oil pan installation. Apply a bead of Silicone 
Rubber F4AZ-19562-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSE-M4G323-A1 
and ESE-M4G195-A (4 places, Area B) to the oil pan gasket
 in the 
area of the parting line between the cylinder block and front and rear main 
bearing caps. 

Prime the oil pump
 by filling 
the inlet port with engine oil. Rotate the oil pump shaft to distribute the 
oil within the oil pump body. 

Place the oil pump
 in the oil pan
. Position the oil pan
 on the 
crossmember. Insert the oil pump intermediate shaft
 into the oil pump housing and install the oil pump
 and oil pump intermediate shaft
 as an assembly. Do not attempt to force the oil pump
 into 
position if it will not seal. The oil pump intermediate shaft hex may be 
misaligned with the distributor shaft. To align, rotate the oil pump intermediate shaft
 into a new position. Tighten the oil pump attaching bolt to 30-43 Nm 
(22-32 lb-ft) and oil pump, screen, tube and cover assembly attaching nut to 
30-43 Nm (22-32 lb-ft).

Crankshaft Main Bearings 

Upper and lower main bearing and connecting rod bearing inserts are 
selective fits. 

 Removal 

Remove oil pan (6675) 
and oil pump (6600). Refer 
to Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen and Tube in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this 
section.

Replace one crankshaft main bearing at a time, leaving other crankshaft 
main bearings securely fastened. Remove the main bearing cap to which new 
crankshaft main bearings are to be installed. 

Insert Main Bearing Insert Tool TOOL-6331-E or equivalent in oil hole in crankshaft (6303)
.

[FIGURE: A10363B.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft
 in the 
direction of engine rotation to force upper main bearing out of block. 

Clean the crankshaft journals. Inspect journals and thrust faces 
(thrust bearing) for nicks, burrs or crankshaft main bearing pickup that cause 
premature crankshaft main bearing wear. 

 Installation 

To install upper main bearing, place the plain end of upper main 
bearing over crankshaft
 on locking tang side of cylinder block and partially install upper main 
bearing so Main Bearing Insert Tool TOOL-6331-E or equivalent can be inserted 
in oil hole in crankshaft
. With Main 
Bearing Insert Tool TOOL-6331-E or equivalent in oil hole, rotate the crankshaft
 in the 
opposite direction of engine rotation until the upper main bearing seats 
itself. Remove the tool.

Fit the main bearings. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

After the main bearing has been fitted, apply a light coat of engine 
oil to crankshaft journal and crankshaft main bearings. Install the main 
bearing cap. Tighten the crankshaft main bearing cap bolts to 129-142 
Nm (95-105 lb-ft). 

Repeat the procedure for remaining crankshaft main bearings requiring 
replacement. 

If the rear crankshaft main bearing is to be replaced, remove and 
discard the crankshaft rear oil seal (6701)
. Refer to Crankshaft Rear Oil Seal in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this 
section.

If main bearing cap for crankshaft main thrust bearing (No. 3 
crankshaft main bearing) has been removed, install as follows:

Install the main thrust bearing cap with cap bolts finger-tight. Pry the crankshaft
 forward 
against the thrust surface of the upper main thrust bearing. Hold the crankshaft
 forward 
and pry the main bearing cap to the rear. This aligns the thrust surfaces of 
both upper and lower main thrust bearings. Retain forward pressure on the crankshaft
. Tighten 
the crankshaft main thrust bearing cap bolts to 129-142 Nm (95-105 
lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: A24972A.gif]

Install oil pump and oil pan. Refer to Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen and Tube 
in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Pistons and Connecting Rods 

 Removal 

Remove the upper and lower intake manifold assembly. Refer to Intake 
Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section. 

Remove cylinder heads (6049)
. Refer 
to Cylinder Head(s) in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section. 

Remove oil pan (6675) 
and oil pump (6600). Refer 
to Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen and Tube in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this 
section. 

 CAUTION: Never cut into piston ring travel area in excess of 0.793 mm (1/32 
inch) when removing ridges. 

Remove any ridge or deposits from upper end of cylinder bores as 
follows: 

Turn the crankshaft (6303)
 until the 
piston to be removed is at bottom of its travel. Place a cloth on top of the 
piston to collect cuttings. Remove any ridge or deposits from the upper end of 
the cylinder bore. Remove the cylinder ridge with a ridge cutter. Follow 
instructions furnished by tool manufacturer. Repeat the procedure at the 
remaining cylinders. 

Make sure all connecting rod caps are marked so they can be installed 
in their original positions. 

Turn the crankshaft
 until the connecting rod (6200)
 being 
removed is down. 

Remove the connecting rod nuts (6212)

and connecting rod cap. 

 CAUTION: Avoid damage to the crankshaft journal and cylinder wall when removing 
the piston and connecting rod assembly. 

Push the connecting rod and piston assembly out through the top of the 
cylinder with the handle end of a hammer. Be certain to note from which bore 
and from which direction the piston and connecting rod assembly was removed.

Remove the connecting rod bearing inserts from the connecting rod
 and 
connecting rod cap. 

Install the connecting rod cap on the connecting rod
 from 
which it was removed. 

 Installation 

If new piston rings are to be installed, remove the cylinder wall 
glaze. Refer to Section 03-00 . Clean cylinder bores with soap and water after 
honing or deglazing. Dry and oil immediately after cleaning. 

Install piston rings with a proper size piston ring installer tool. 

Oil the piston, pin and rings (6102)

and cylinder walls with light engine oil. Always install piston, pin and rings

in the same cylinders from which they were removed or to which they were 
fitted. Connecting rod
 and connecting rod caps are numbered from 1 to 4 in the right bank, and 5 to 
8 in the left bank, beginning at the front of engine. Numbers on the connecting rod
 and 
connecting rod cap must be on the same side when installed in the cylinder 
bore. If a connecting rod
 is 
ever transposed from one cylinder block or cylinder to another, new connecting rod bearings (6211)
 should be fitted and the connecting rod
 should 
be numbered to correspond with the new cylinder number.

 CAUTION: Failure to install the piston and connecting rod assembly in their 
proper relationship can cause damage to the engine. 

Locate the large chamfer at the crankshaft end of the connecting rod
and the 
dome identification mark on top of the piston, pin and ring

as follows:

For right-hand piston assemblies (cylinders 1 to 4), the identification 
mark must be on the same side as the large chamfer of the connecting rod large 
end bearing.

For left-hand piston assemblies (cylinders 5 to 8), the identification 
mark must be 180 degrees away from the large chamfer on the connecting rod 
large end bearing.

Confirm that the piston is in its proper relationship to the connecting rod
.

[FIGURE: A21994A.gif]

[FIGURE: A23062A.gif]

Make sure piston ring gaps (A-oil ring, B-compression rings) are spaced 
around circumference of piston.

[FIGURE: A71251A.gif]

Install Piston Ring Compressor D81L-6002-C or equivalent onto piston 
and push in with hammer handle until it is slightly below top of cylinder. 
Make sure to guide connecting rods
while 
tapping them into position to avoid damaging crankshaft journals. Install 
piston with notch or dimple in piston head toward the front of the engine.

[FIGURE: A103981A.gif]

Turn the crankshaft
 until the 
crankshaft journal is at the bottom of the stroke. Push the piston all the way 
down until the connecting rod bearings
 seat on the crankshaft journal. Guide the connecting rod
 to 
prevent damage to the crankshaft journals. 

Install the connecting rod cap. Make sure connecting rod bolt heads are 
properly seated in the connecting rod
. 
Tighten the connecting rod nuts

to 62-67 Nm (46-49 lb-ft). 

Check clearance of each connecting rod bearing
. Refer to Section 03-00 to service connecting rod bearings
. 

After the connecting rod bearings
 have been fitted, apply a light coat of engine oil to the crankshaft journals 
and connecting rod bearings
. 

After the piston and connecting rod assemblies have been installed, 
check the side clearance between the connecting rods
 on 
each crankshaft journal. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

Install oil pump
 and oil pan. Refer 
to Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen and Tube in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this 
section.

Install cylinder heads
. Refer 
to Cylinder Head(s) in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

Install intake manifold (9424)
. 
Refer to Intake Manifold in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this section.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Connecting Rod Bearings

 Removal 

Remove oil pan (6675) 
and oil pump (6600). Refer 
to Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen and Tube in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this 
section.

Turn the crankshaft (6303)
 until connecting rod (6200)
 to 
which new connecting rod bearings (6211)
 are to be fitted is down. Remove the connecting rod cap. Remove the 
connecting rod bearing inserts from connecting rod and connecting rod cap. 

Make sure connecting rod bearing inserts and bearing bore in connecting rod
 and 
connecting rod cap are clean. Foreign material under connecting rod bearing 
inserts will distort connecting rod bearing
 and cause a failure. 

Clean the crankshaft journal. When replacing standard connecting rod bearings
 with new connecting rod bearings
, it is good practice to fit the connecting rod bearing
 to minimum specified clearance. 

 Installation 

Fit connecting rod bearings
. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

Install the connecting rod bearing inserts in the connecting rod
 and 
connecting rod cap with tangs in the slots provided. 

Pull the connecting rod assembly down firmly on the crankshaft journal. 

Apply a light coat of engine oil to the crankshaft journal and connecting rod bearings
. Install the connecting rod cap. Make sure connecting rod bolt heads are 
properly seated in the connecting rod
. 
Tighten the connecting rod nuts (6212)

to 62-67 Nm (46-49 lb-ft). 

Repeat the procedure for the remaining connecting rods
 that 
require new connecting rod bearings
. 

Install oil pump
 andoil pan. Refer to 
Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen and Tube in the In-Vehicle Service portion of this 
section.

Crankshaft Rear Oil Seal 

 Removal 

Remove oil pan (6675) 
and oil pump (6600). Refer 
to Oil Pan/Oil Pump Screen Cover and Tube in the In-Vehicle Service portion of 
this section.

Remove rear main bearing cap. 

Using a long, narrow punch, tap one end of the crankshaft rear oil seal 
upper half until the other end protrudes past the cylinder block surface. Grab 
the protruding end of the crankshaft rear oil seal (6701)
 with small pliers or side cutters and pull the crankshaft rear oil seal
 from around the crankshaft (6303)
. 

Remove the crankshaft rear oil seal lower half from the rear main 
bearing cap. 

 Installation 

Install crankshaft rear oil seal lower half into the rear main bearing 
cap with locating tab side of crankshaft rear oil seal
 directed toward rear face of cylinder block. 

Install the crankshaft rear oil seal upper half into the cylinder block 
groove by dipping crankshaft rear oil seal half in oil and sliding it up 
around the crankshaft. 

Apply light finger pressure to slightly compress crankshaft rear oil 
seal ends. 

Clean oil from both cylinder block assembly and rear main bearing cap 
mating surfaces with a rag soaked with cleaning solvent.

 NOTE: Rear main bearing cap must be installed within five minutes of sealer 
application, or sealer will begin to cure. If more than five minutes elapse, 
sealer must be cleaned off and reapplied. 

Apply a 1/16-inch bead of Silicone Rubber F4AZ-19562-B or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSE-M4G323-A1 and ESE-M4G195-A on the cylinder 
block mating surface in two places as shown.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Oil Bypass Filter/Adapter

 Removal 

The oil bypass filter (6714)
 and oil filter adapter (6881)

is shown in the following illustration.

[FIGURE: A5763F.gif]

Place a drip pan under the oil bypass filter
. 
Unscrew the oil bypass filter

from the oil filter adapter assembly fitting and clean the adapter recess. 
Clean the oil bypass filter gasket surface. 

Remove oil filter adapter mounting bolt, oil filter adapter assembly 
and gasket from engine. Discard gasket.

 Installation 

Install a new gasket on oil filter adapter assembly. Coat gasket with 
clean engine oil.

Install oil filter adapter assembly on engine with oil filter adapter 
assembly mounting bolt. Tighten mounting bolt to 54-88 Nm (40-65 lb-ft).

Coat the gasket on a new oil bypass filter

with oil. Place the new oil bypass filter
 on 
the oil filter adapter assembly fitting. Hand-tighten the oil bypass filter

until the gasket contacts the sealing surface, then tighten one-half turn 
more. DO NOT over-tighten oil bypass filter
. 

Check the oil level and fill the crankcase to the correct level. 
Operate the engine at fast idle and check for oil leaks. If oil leaks are 
evident, perform the necessary repairs to correct the leakage.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Engine

 WARNING: TO AVOID THE POSSIBILITY OF PERSONAL INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE, 
DO NOT OPERATE THE ENGINE WITH THE HOOD OPEN UNTIL THE FAN HAS BEEN FIRST 
EXAMINED FOR POSSIBLE CRACKS AND SEPARATION. 

When installing nuts or bolts that must be tightened (refer to torque 
specifications in the Specifications portion of this section), oil the threads 
with lightweight engine oil. Do not oil threads that require oil-resistant or 
water-resistant sealer.

Refer to Section 03-00 for engine cleaning, inspection and test 
procedures. 

The camshaft bearing removal and installation is to be done with the 
engine removed from the vehicle. Always lubricate all bearing surfaces with 
recommended quality engine oil. 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Engine Lifting Brackets

T70P-6000

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT PARK OR SERVICE A LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED VEHICLE NEAR 
ANY SOURCE OF FIRE, SUCH AS OPEN FLAME, CIGARETTES OR SMOKING MATERIALS, 
SPARKS, EXCESSIVE HEAT, WELDING, OR BODY GRINDING. AVOID PLACING THE VEHICLE 
NEAR ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT THAT DISCHARGES SPARKS THROUGH NORMAL OPERATION, FOR 
EXAMPLE, MOTORS, ELECTRICAL SWITCHES, AND RADIO TRANSMISSION EQUIPMENT. AVOID 
STORING OR SERVICING A VEHICLE OVER SEWER DRAINS, LUBRICATION PITS, SUB-FLOOR 
LEVEL ROOMS, OR OTHER LOW-LYING AREAS. IF ANY SOURCE OF FIRE OR IGNITION 
CONTACTS LPG VAPOR, A FIRE CAN RESULT. 

 WARNING: DO NOT NEEDLESSLY RELEASE LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL DURING 
SERVICE, AND DO NOT OPEN THE STOP-FILL VALVE WHILE A VEHICLE IS INSIDE A 
BUILDING. WHEN SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM, CLOSE THE FUEL TANK SHUTOFF VALVES 
(TWO VALVES IF EQUIPPED WITH TWO FUEL TANKS) AND RUN THE ENGINE OUT OF FUEL 
BEFORE DISCONNECTING FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENTS. IF THE FUEL TANK IS BEING 
SERVICED, HAVE THE FUEL EVACUATED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL AT A LOCAL LPG FUEL 
STATION. LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) VAPORIZES AT NORMAL BAROMETRIC PRESSURE AT 
TEMPERATURES ABOVE -42°C (-44°F), AND CAN EXPAND TO APPROXIMATELY 270 
TIMES ITS VOLUME AS A LIQUID. UNNECESSARY VENTING OF LPG FUEL CAN CREATE FIRES 
AND HEALTH HAZARDS WHICH CAN LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY OR ILLNESS. 

 WARNING: FUEL TANKS SHOULD BE DRAINED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT ATTEMPT 
TO USE SHOP AIR PRESSURE TO FORCE LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL FROM THE 
TANKS. NORMAL FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1724 KPA (160 PSI) AT ROOM 
TEMPERATURE. CONNECTING A SHOP AIR HOSE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM CAN RESULT IN FUEL 
FLOWING BACK INTO THE SERVICE AIR SYSTEM, AND RESULT IN FIRE OR EXPLOSION. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE PAINT DRYING OVENS FOR LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED 
VEHICLES. THE HEAT OF PAINT DRYING OVENS WILL INCREASE PRESSURE IN THE FUEL 
TANKS. THIS CAN CAUSE VENTING OF THE LPG VAPOR INTO THE OVEN RESULTING IN FIRE 
FROM HEAT OR SPARK IN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. IF FUEL IS CONFINED IN AN OVEN, 
THERE IS ALSO A RISK OF EXPLOSION IF THE FUEL IS IGNITED. WHEN REFINISHING THE 
BODY PANELS OF LPG-FUELED VEHICLES, SPOT PAINT THE AFFECTED AREA AND USE SPOT 
DRYING METHODS. 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY THE ENGINE FUEL SYSTEM CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS, OR 
REPLACE COMPONENTS WITH PARTS THAT DO NOT MEET FORD SPECIFICATIONS. FORD 
SPECIFIED PARTS ARE AVAILABLE AT AUTHORIZED FORD DEALERS. THE LIQUID PETROLEUM 
GAS (LPG) STORAGE SYSTEM MUST CONFORM TO NATIONAL FIRE PROTECTION ASSOCIATION 
STANDARD NO. 58, AND SIMILAR CANADIAN GAS ASSOCIATION STANDARDS. THESE 
STANDARDS DEFINE THE SPECIALLY-APPROVED MATERIALS, COMPONENT CONSTRUCTION, AND 
THE SYSTEM INSTALLED ON ALL VEHICLES, WHICH IS PRECISELY CALIBRATED FOR 
EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE USE OF DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS CAN PRODUCE AN 
UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT COULD RESULT IN FIRE, EXPLOSION AND PERSONAL 
INJURY, ENGINE DAMAGE, OR NONCOMPLIANCE TO CURRENT EMISSION STANDARDS. 

 WARNING: AVOID INHALING LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) OR OCCUPYING CONFINED AREAS 
CONTAINING LPG. LPG IS HEAVIER THAN AIR. THE HEAVIER GAS CAN DISPLACE OR 
"PUSH" FRESH AIR OUT OF AN AREA. IN LARGE QUANTITIES LPG CAN DISPLACE ENOUGH 
OXYGEN TO MAKE THE SURROUNDING AIR UNFIT TO BREATHE, AND POSSIBLY CAUSE 
ILLNESS. IF A PERSON BREATHES LPG OR AIR WHICH LACKS OXYGEN DUE TO THE 
PRESENCE OF LPG, HEADACHE, DIZZINESS, AND WEAKNESS IN THE EXTREMITIES CAN 
RESULT. IN SEVERE CASES, PROLONGED EXPOSURE TO LPG-FUELED AIR CAN BE LETHAL. 

IN THE EVENT OF EXPOSURE TO LPG, MOVE THE VICTIM IMMEDIATELY TO FRESH 
AIR AND CONTACT A PHYSICIAN OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY PERSONNEL FOR ARTIFICIAL 
RESPIRATION OR OTHER REQUIRED TREATMENT. 

Drain the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301)
. 

On non-tilt hood vehicles, hood must be removed from vehicle. On tilt 
hood vehicles, hood must be tilted forward and supported. Remove hood 
retaining cables. 

Disconnect the upper radiator hose (8260)

from the engine, and the lower radiator hose (8286)

from the water pump (8501). 

Remove the fan blade assembly attaching bolts and remove the fan blade (8600)
. Refer to 
 Section 03C-05 or Section 03D-05 .

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Subassemblies

When installing nuts or bolts that must be tightened, oil the threads 
with light engine oil. Do not oil threads that require oil-resistant or 
water-resistant sealer. Refer to Torque Specifications under the 
Specifications portion of this section. 

 Cylinder Head 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Compressor

T70P-6049-A

 Disassembly 

With cylinder head (6049)
 removed 
from engine, remove rocker arm seat bolts, rocker arm seats (6A528)
, 
and rocker arms (6564). 
Remove exhaust manifolds (9430)
 and spark plugs (12405)
.

[FIGURE: A21991A.gif]

Clean carbon from combustion chambers before removing valves. 

Compress valve springs (6513)
 using 
Valve Spring Compressor T70P-6049-A. Remove valve spring retainer keys (6518)
 and release valve springs
. Remove valve spring retainers (6514)
, valve springs, valve stem seals (6571)
, 
and intake valves (6507) and exhaust valves (6505)
. 
Discard valve stem seals
. 

Clean and inspect cylinder head
(s) and 
related components. Repair if necessary. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

 Assembly 

Lubricate all valves, valve stems and valve guides with specified 
engine oil. Apply Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-B to the valve tips. The 
lubricant is to be applied before installation. 

Install each valve in port from which it was removed. Install new valve stem seal
 on 
each valve. 

Set valve spring
 and valve spring retainer

over valve stem. Compress valve spring
 and 
install valve spring retainer keys
. 

 CAUTION: Reducing assembled height below specifications can cause valve spring 
breakage and rapid wear of camshaft lobe. 

With dividers, measure assembled height of valve spring
 from 
surface of spring pad on cylinder head
 to 
underside of valve spring retainer
. Check dividers with accurate scale. If assembled height exceeds 
specifications, install spacer(s) below valve spring
 to 
reduce height to recommended dimension. 

[FIGURE: A10401B.gif]

Coat the rocker arm seat
 and 
sockets with Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-B. Make sure rocker arm seat bolts 
are in a serviceable condition before installing them. Install rocker arms
, rocker arm seats
, 
and rocker arm seat bolts. Refer to In-Vehicle Service, Cylinder Head(s) 
installation in this section.

Install exhaust manifolds
 and spark plugs
.

 Assembly

.

 and

the connecting rod 
with the cylinder number side of the connecting rod
 and

[FIGURE: A21994A.gif]

Start the piston pin
 in the

.

End gap must be within specifications. Follow the instructions contained on 
piston ring set and install the piston rings. Use a proper size piston ring 
installation tool. 

Check the ring-side clearance of compression rings with a feeler gauge 
inserted into the groove between the ring and the lower land. Feeler gauge 
should slide freely around the ring circumference without binding. Any wear 
may form a step at the outer groove edge near the inner portion of the lower 
land. If the lower lands have high steps, replace the piston, pin and ring
.

Make sure connecting rod bearing inserts and bearing bore in the connecting rod
 and 
connecting rod cap are clean. Foreign material under the connecting rod 
bearing inserts will distort the connecting rod bearing (6211)
 and cause failure. Install connecting rod bearing inserts in connecting rod
 and 
connecting rod cap with tangs fitting in slots provided. 

 Valve Tappet, Hydraulic 

Each valve tappet (6500)
 is a 
matched assembly. If parts of one are mixed with those of another, improper 
valve operation may result. Disassemble and assemble each valve tappet

separately. Valve tappets
 should 
be tested after assembly. Refer to Section 03-00 . Keep the valve tappets
 in 
proper sequence so they can be installed in their original bores. 

 Disassembly 

Grasp the lock ring with needlenose pliers to release it from the 
groove. It may be necessary to depress the plunger to fully release lock ring. 

Remove the push rod cup and metering valve (disc). 

Remove the plunger assembly and the plunger spring. Carefully remove 
the check valve retainer, check valve spring and check valve disc from the 
plunger. 

Refer to Section 03-00 for cleaning and inspection procedures.

 Assembly 

Place the plunger upside down on a clean work bench. 

Place the check valve (disc or ball check) in position over the oil 
hole on the bottom of the plunger. Set the check valve spring on top of the 
check valve (disc or ball check). 

Position the check valve retainer over the check valve and spring, then 
push the retainer down into place on the plunger. 

Place the plunger spring and the plunger (open end up) into lifter body. 

Position the metering valve (disc) in the plunger, and place push rod 
cup in the plunger. 

Depress the plunger and position the closed end of lock ring in the 
groove of the valve lifter body. With the plunger still depressed, position 
the open ends of lock ring in the groove. Release the plunger, and then 
depress it again to fully seat the lock ring. 

Use a hydraulic valve tappet leak-down tester to fill the valve tappet
 with 
test fluid. 

 Cylinder Block Assembly 

 Disassembly 

Mount the engine in a work stand and remove all engine dress components 
and any base engine components not furnished with the new engine short block (6009)

following procedures described in this section. 

Make sure that cylinder bores are ridge-reamed before removing piston 
and connecting rod assemblies. 

Remove the four cylinder head locating dowels and the cylinder block 
drain plugs. 

Remove the old engine short block

from the work stand. 

 Assembly 

Clean the gasket and seal surfaces of all serviceable parts and 
assemblies.

Position the new engine short block
 in 
a work stand. Install cylinder head locating dowels and cylinder block drain 
plugs. 

Transfer all serviceable parts removed from the old cylinder assembly, 
following procedures described in this section. 

Check all assembly clearances and correct as necessary. 

 Cylinder Block, Bare 

Before replacing a cylinder block, determine if it is repairable. Refer 
to Section 03-00 . If cylinder block replacement is necessary, refer to 
procedures in that section.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Tappet Bleed Down Wrench

T71P-6513-B

Refer to the Specifications portion of this section for bolt torque 
values and other engine specifications. 

The valve arrangement on the left bank is E-I-E-I-E-I-E-I and on the 
right bank is I-E-I-E-I-E-I-E. 

A 1.53 mm (0.060 inch) shorter push rod (6565)
 or a 1.53 mm 
(0.060 inch) longer push rod
 is available 
for service. Both push rods
provide a 
means of compensating for dimensional changes in the valve mechanism. Refer to 
the Master Parts Catalog for the applicable color code. 

Valve stem-to-rocker arm clearance should be within specifications 
listed at the end of this section with the hydraulic valve tappet (6500)

completely collapsed. Repeated valve reconditioning operations (valve and 
valve seat refacing) will decrease the clearance to the point that, if not 
compensated for, the hydraulic valve tappet
 will 
cease to function and the valve will be held closed. 

To determine whether a shorter or a longer push rod
 is 
necessary, make the following check: 

Install an auxiliary starter switch. Crank the engine with the ignition 
switch in OFF position until the No. 1 piston is on TDC (Top Dead Center) at 
the end of the compression stroke. 

With the crankshaft (6303)
 in the 
positions designated in Steps 3 and 4, position the hydraulic tappet 
compressor tool on the rocker arm (6564)
. Slowly 
apply pressure to bleed down the valve tappet
until the 
plunger is completely bottomed using Tappet Bleed Down Wrench T71P-6513-B. 
Hold the valve tappet 
in this position and check the available clearance between the rocker arm
 and the 
valve stem tip with a feeler gauge. If the clearance is less than 
specifications at the end of this section, install a shorter push rod
. If the 
clearance is greater than specifications, install a longer push rod
.

(firing), position No. 1, check the following valves: 

No. 1 Intake and No. 1 Exhaust

No. 7 Intake and No. 8 Intake and Exhaust

valves: 

No. 2 Intake and Exhaust 

No. 3 Exhaust and No. 4 and 5 Intake 

No. 6 Intake and Exhaust 

No. 7 Exhaust

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES WHILE THE ENGINE 
IS OPERATING. SWITCH OFF THE ENGINE AND WAIT UNTIL IT HAS COOLED. EVEN THEN, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM THE RADIATOR SUPPLY TANK. WRAP A 
THICK CLOTH AROUND THE CAP AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK 
WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL 
THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP — STILL WITH A 
CLOTH, TURN AND REMOVE IT. STAND CLEAR OF THE RADIATOR SUPPLY TANK OPENING. 
HOT COOLANT CAN SPLASH OUT. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN 
SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY FROM HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT AND DAMAGE TO THE 
COOLING SYSTEM OR ENGINE. 

Refer to Section 03-03 .

PAGE 4181
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-03: Engine Cooling, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Block Heater

The engine block heater consists of an electrical heating element 
installed in one or more of the core plug openings in the engine block and an 
electrical cable that plugs into a standard A/C electrical outlet. It is 
designed to keep the engine coolant warm during cold weather to aid in cold 
weather starting.

================================================================================
PAGE 4182
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-03: Engine Cooling, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Recovery System

The coolant recovery system consists of a sealed plastic bottle 
connected to the radiator with a rubber hose. The recovery bottle receives and 
stores surplus (expanded) coolant when hot and supplies coolant back to the 
radiator during cool-down.
