REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermostat, Water

The poppet-type thermostat used in production is a higher temperature 
thermostat for use with a mixture of water and permanent type antifreeze. A 
low-temperature thermostat should be installed if a non-permanent type 
antifreeze and water coolant solution is used (except on vehicles with 
automatic radiator shutters).

 NOTE: Do not attempt to service the thermostat. It must be replaced if not 
operating properly.

Check the thermostat before installing it. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

 Removal 

Drain the radiator so the coolant level is below the thermostat. 

Disconnect the bypass hoses at the water pump and intake manifold. 
Remove the bypass tube. 

Remove the upper water outlet housing retaining bolts. Position the 
radiator upper hose upward and remove the thermostat(s) and gasket. 

 Installation 

Completely remove all old gasket material from water outlet housing 
gasket surfaces. Coat a new water outlet housing gasket with Perfect Seal 
Sealing Compound B5A-19554-A or equivalent. Position the water outlet housing 
gasket on the intake manifold opening. 

Install the thermostat(s) in the intake manifold opening with the 
copper pellet or element toward the engine and the thermostat flange 
positioned in the recess. If the thermostat is improperly installed, it will 
restrict coolant flow. 

Position the water outlet housing against the intake manifold. Install 
and tighten the attaching bolts to specifications. Install the water bypass 
line and tighten hose connections. 

Fill and bleed the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . Install 
pressure cap. Operate the engine until normal operating temperature is 
reached; then check the coolant level and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator, Tilt Hood 

The disconnect and reconnect points for radiators are shown in the 
radiator installation illustrations.

 Removal 

 NOTE: Tilt hood must be supported during radiator removal and installation.

Tilt hood forward and place on supports.

Disconnect hood support cables from hood.

Drain cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Loosen clamp retaining coolant bypass hose to surge tank. Remove bypass 
hose from surge tank.

Loosen clamps retaining two vent hoses to surge tank. Remove vent hoses 
from surge tank.

Disconnect coolant overflow hose from radiator. Remove four screws 
retaining coolant reservoir to radiator support. Remove coolant reservoir from 
vehicle.

Loosen clamp retaining upper radiator hose to radiator. Remove hose 
from radiator.

Loosen clamp retaining lower radiator hose to radiator. Remove hose 
from radiator.

Remove four screws and fan and clutch assembly from water pump pulley.

Remove six screws retaining fan shroud to radiator. Remove fan shroud 
and fan and clutch assembly from vehicle.

Remove two bolts securing radiator support cross brace. Remove brace.

Remove four bolts retaining radiator support braces to radiator.

Remove four screws retaining radiator support braces to engine 
compartment bulkhead. Remove support braces.

Remove six bolts retaining radiator support.

 NOTE: An assistant and a lifting device are needed to remove the radiator.

Attach the lifting device to the radiator, raise and remove radiator 
from vehicle.

Refer to Section 03-03 for radiator service procedures.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten radiator mounting bolts.

Tighten fan shroud mounting bolts.

Tighten fan and clutch mounting bolts to 34-40 Nm (25-30 lb-ft).

Tighten radiator hose clamps to 14-16 Nm (10-12 lb-ft).

Tighten coolant bypass hose clamp to 4-5 Nm (35-44 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Coolant Supply Tank 

 Removal 

Drain the radiator until the coolant is out of the supply tank. 
Disconnect the radiator supply tank hose at the supply tank. Disconnect the 
radiator vent tubes at the supply tank. 

Remove the overflow tube from the supply tank. Remove the supply tank 
strap or bracket retaining bolt(s) and remove the supply tank. 

 Installation 

Position the supply tank in the chassis and install the strap or 
bracket retaining bolt(s). 

Connect the radiator hose, overflow tube and vent tubes to the supply 
tank. 

Fill and bleed the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . Check for 
coolant leaks and proper coolant level after the engine reaches normal 
operating temperatures.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel System

The multiport fuel injection system (MFI) is a multi-point, pulse time, 
speed density fuel injection system. Fuel is metered into the intake air 
stream (in accordance with engine demand) through eight injectors mounted on 
the lower intake manifold. 

An on-board vehicle engine control module (ECM) accepts inputs from 
various engine sensors to compute the required fuel flow rate necessary to 
maintain a prescribed air/fuel ratio throughout the entire engine operational 
range. The ECM then outputs a command to the fuel injectors to meter the 
appropriate quantity of fuel. The electronic engine control system also 
determines and compensates for the age of the vehicle and its uniqueness. The 
system will automatically sense and compensate for changes in altitudes (i.e., 
from sea level to mountains) and also permits push-starting vehicles equipped 
with manual transmissions, should it become necessary. 

The fuel delivery subsystem consists of an in-tank mounted reservoir 
and a high-pressure electric fuel pump. These components deliver fuel from the 
tank through a chassis-mounted, 20-micron fuel filter to the fuel injection 
supply manifold. 

 MFI System Components 

[FIGURE: V8349C.gif]

Sensor, Throttle Position 

The fuel injection supply manifold has electrically actuated fuel 
injectors directly above each of the engine's eight intake ports. The 
injectors, when energized, spray a metered quantity of fuel into the intake 
air stream. 

A constant fuel pressure drop is maintained across the injectors by a 
pressure regulator. The regulator is connected in series with the fuel 
injectors and is positioned downstream from them. Excess fuel supplied by the 
pump, but not required by the engine, passes through the regulator reservoir 
input and returns to the fuel tank through a fuel return line.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Injection Timing

One group of four injectors is energized simultaneously, once every 
crankshaft revolution, followed by the second group of injectors in the next 
crankshaft revolution. The period of time that the injectors are energized 
(injector on-time or pulse width) is controlled by the ECM.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Throttle Body 

The throttle body controls airflow to the engine through a double 
butterfly-type valve. The throttle position is controlled by four-bar link

The throttle body for this vehicle is a sludge-resistant design. Do not

Features of the throttle body include:

a preset stop to locate the closed throttle position. 

a throttle body-mounted throttle position sensor.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Intake Manifold 

The intake manifold assembly is a two-piece (upper and lower intake 
manifold) aluminum casting. Runner lengths are tuned to optimize engine torque 
and power output. The intake manifold assembly provides mounting flanges for 
the throttle body, fuel injection supply manifold and accelerator control 
bracketry, idle air control valve, and the EGR valve. Vacuum taps are provided 
to support various engine accessories. The pockets in which the injectors are 
mounted are placed to direct the injector fuel spray immediately in front of 
each engine intake valve.

================================================================================
PAGE 4207
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-04: Fuel Charging and Controls, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Injectors 

The fuel injectors are electromechanical devices that both meter and 
atomize fuel delivered to the engine. The MFI injectors are mounted in the 
lower intake manifold and are positioned so that their tips direct fuel just 
ahead of the engine intake valves. 

The fuel injectors consist of:

solenoid actuated needle valve 

fixed-size orifice

integral filter

coil and armature

director/metering plate

spacer and O-rings

end cap

Fuel flow to the engine is regulated by how long the solenoid is 
energized. An electrical signal from the ECM activates the solenoid, causing 
the valve to move inward off the seat, allowing fuel to flow through the 
orifice. Atomization of the fuel is obtained by a director/metering plate at 
the point where the fuel passes through. 

The 7.0L MFI engine uses deposit-resistant fuel injectors, and 
therefore must not be cleaned. These deposit-resistant fuel injectors prevent 
tip deposit formation, which is a major cause of customer driveability 
complaints in vehicles that use electronic fuel injection systems. 
Deposit-resistant fuel injectors operate the same as standard fuel injectors, 
but use a director/metering plate with four metering holes directly below the 
metering valve assembly. 

 NOTE: Do not clean deposit-resistant fuel injectors.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Pressure Regulator 

The fuel pressure regulator is attached to the fuel injection supply 
manifold downstream of the fuel injectors. It regulates the fuel pressure 
supplied to the injectors. The regulator is a diaphragm-operated relief valve 
in which one side of the diaphragm senses fuel pressure and the other side is 
subjected to intake manifold vacuum. The nominal fuel pressure is established 
by a spring preload applied to the diaphragm. Balancing one side of the 
diaphragm with manifold pressure maintains a constant fuel pressure drop 
across the injectors. Fuel in excess of that used by the engine is bypassed 
through the regulator and returns to the fuel tank.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Charging Wiring

The fuel charging wiring connects the engine wire harness to each fuel 
injector and other electronic engine controls such as throttle position sensor 
and idle air control valve. The fuel charging wiring receives fuel injector 
signals from the ECM and transfers the signals to the fuel injectors. The 
signals from the ECM determine the fuel injection sequence and duration each 
fuel injector will stay open to allow fuel into the combustion chambers.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Charging System 

 WARNING: ALWAYS PERFORM THE PRE-SERVICE PROCEDURES BEFORE SERVICING ANY PART OF 
THE FUEL CHARGING ASSEMBLY. 

 Pre-Service Procedures 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Fuel Pressure Gauge

T80L-9974-B

Adapter Hose (Part of T80L-9974-B)

T85L-9974-A

The fuel charging system consists of the throttle body, upper and lower 
intake manifolds, fuel injection supply manifold, fuel pressure regulator and 
fuel injectors. Prior to any service or removal of the charging system, the 
following steps must be taken: 

Open the hood and install protective covers. 

Disconnect the battery negative cable. 

Relieve fuel system pressure as follows: 

Remove fuel cap to relieve fuel tank pressure. 

Connect Fuel Pressure Gauge T80L-9974-B, including Adapter Hose 
T85L-9974-A (Part of T80L-9974-A), to the pressure relief valve located on the 
right bank of the fuel injection supply manifold. 

Place the other end of the gauge hose in a jar to collect any drained 
fuel. 

Open the valve on the gauge to evacuate any pressure in the system. 

Remove the gauge assembly from the fuel injection supply manifold. 

 Post-Service Procedures 

After the service is completed and the fuel charging system component 
is installed, the following steps must be taken: 

Connect the battery negative cable. 

Add coolant, if it was removed. 

Check all connections at the fuel rails, push connect fittings, etc. 

 CAUTION: The fuel system is normally pressurized to 270 kPa (40 psi). 

Turn ignition switch on and off several times without starting the 
engine to check for fuel leaks. 

Start the engine and warm to operating temperature. Check for coolant 
leak if coolant was removed. 

Perform self test to check systems function. Refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.(Can be purchased as a 
separate item.)

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring Lock Coupling

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spring Lock Coupling Disconnect Tool (3/8-Inch)

T81P-19623-G1

Spring Lock Coupling Disconnect Tool (1/2-Inch)

T81P-19623-G2

The spring lock coupling is a fuel line coupling held together by a 
garter spring inside a circular cage. When the coupling is connected, the 
flared end of the female fitting slips behind the garter spring inside the 
cage of the male fitting. The garter spring and cage then prevent the flared 
end of the female fitting from pulling out of the cage. As a redundant locking 
feature, a horseshoe shaped retaining clip is incorporated to improve the 
retaining reliability of the spring lock coupling.

[FIGURE: V7329A.gif]

 Removal 

Relieve fuel system pressure. Refer to Pre-Service Procedures under 
Fuel Charging System in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Remove retaining clip from spring lock coupling by hand only. Do not 
use any sharp tool or screwdriver as it may damage the spring lock coupling.

Twist fitting to free it from any adhesion at the O-ring seals.

Using Spring Lock Coupling Disconnect Tool T81P-19623-G1 (3/8-inch) or 
Spring Lock Coupling Disconnect Tool T81P-19623-G2 (1/2-inch), disconnect fuel 
hoses at the fuel rail supply tube and fuel rail return tube.

Fit tool to coupling so tool can enter cage to release garter spring.

Push the tool into the cage opening to release female fitting from 
garter spring.

Pull the coupling male and female fittings apart.

Remove the tool from the disconnected coupling.

[FIGURE: V4803D.gif]

 Installation 

 WARNING: USE ONLY THE SPECIFIED O-RINGS. THEY ARE MADE OF A SPECIAL MATERIAL. 
THE USE OF ANY O-RING OTHER THAN THE SPECIFIED O-RING MAY ALLOW THE CONNECTION 
TO LEAK INTERMITTENTLY DURING VEHICLE OPERATION. 

Make sure the garter spring is in cage of male fitting. If garter 
spring is missing, install a new spring by pushing it into cage opening. If 
garter spring is damaged, remove it from cage with a small wire hook (do not 
use a screwdriver) and install a new spring.

Clean all dirt or foreign material from both pieces of coupling.

Replace missing or damaged O-rings. Use only specified O-rings.

[FIGURE: V5908D.gif]

Lubricate male fitting and O-rings and inside of female fitting with 
clean engine oil XO-10W30-QSP or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESE-M2C153-E.

Fit female fitting to male fitting and push until garter spring snaps 
over flared end of female fitting.

Check coupling engagement by pulling on fitting and visually checking 
to make sure garter spring is over flared end of female fitting.

 NOTE: All vehicles require the large black clip to be installed on the supply 
side fuel line and the small gray clip to be installed on the return side fuel 
line.

Position retaining clip over metal portion of spring lock coupling. 
Firmly push retaining clip onto spring lock coupling. Make sure horseshoe 
portion of clip is over the coupling. Do not install retaining clip over 
rubber fuel line.

Perform the Post-Service Procedures under Fuel Charging System in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

PAGE 4216
================================================================================

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Upper Intake Manifold and Throttle Body 

 Removal 

Relieve fuel system pressure. Refer to Pre-Service Procedures under 
Fuel Charging System in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Remove air cleaner assembly. Refer to Section 03C-12 . Also remove the 
air cleaner-to-throttle body hoses. 

Disconnect the following components: 

idle air control (IAC) valve connector 

EGR position sensor connector 

EGR vacuum line 

MAP sensor vacuum line 

idle air control (IAC) valve air inlet hose 

PCV hose at the rear of the upper intake manifold 

canister purge solenoid vacuum line 

Remove the EGR tube flare nut. 

Remove the upper intake manifold retainer studs and nuts. Remove the 
upper intake manifold and throttle body as an assembly. 

If the upper intake manifold is being replaced, place the assembly on a 
work bench and transfer the following components onto the new intake manifold: 

throttle body using a new gasket 

idle air control (IAC) valve using a new gasket 

vacuum connector 

MAP line vacuum tee 

pipe plug at rear of intake manifold

 Installation 

Clean the gasket surfaces on the upper and lower intake manifold 
mounting surfaces. 

Position a new gasket on the lower intake manifold. 

Install the upper intake manifold and throttle body assembly, making 
sure the gasket is properly aligned. 

Install the retaining nuts and studs and tighten to specifications. 

Connect the following components: 

PCV hose at the rear of the intake manifold 

MAP sensor vacuum line 

canister purge solenoid vacuum line 

EGR position sensor connector 

idle air control valve air inlet hose 

EGR vacuum line

Connect the EGR tube flare nut. 

Install the air cleaner assembly and the air cleaner-to-throttle body 
hoses. Refer to Section 03C-12 . 

Perform the Post-Service Procedures under Fuel Charging System in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Throttle Body 

 NOTE: The throttle body is sludge-tolerant and therefore should not be 
cleaned. 

 Removal 

Remove air cleaner assembly. Refer to Section 03C-12 . Also remove the 
air cleaner-to-throttle body hoses. 

Disconnect the electrical connector at the throttle position sensor. 

Disconnect throttle cable.

Remove the four throttle body bolts and studs. Carefully separate the 
throttle body from the upper intake manifold.

 Installation 

 NOTE: If scraping is necessary, be careful not to damage the surfaces of the 
throttle body and upper intake manifold, or allow material to fall into the 
manifold. 

Make sure that both the throttle body and upper intake manifold gasket 
surfaces are clean. 

Install the throttle body gasket between the upper intake manifold and 
throttle body. Make sure the gasket stays in place if alignment studs are not 
used. 

Install the throttle body to the upper intake manifold. 

Secure the throttle body to the upper intake manifold with the four 
retaining bolts and studs. Tighten to 8-11 Nm (70-97 lb-in). 

Connect throttle linkage.

Connect the throttle position sensor electrical connector.

Fuel Pressure Regulator 

 Removal

Fuel Charging System in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

gasket and the O-ring.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Belts, Accessory 

F700 vehicles are equipped with vee type accessory drive belts. The 
belt type is selected for each engine based on performance requirements. To 
ensure maximum life, replacement belts must be of the same type as originally 
installed. These belts must be properly adjusted at all times. Loose belt(s) 
will result in slippage, which can cause a noise complaint or improper 
accessory operation (generator will not charge, etc.). Overly tight belts will 
place severe loads on accessory bearings.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Drive Belts, Accessory

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the original concern by operating the engine to duplicate the 
condition.

Inspect to determine if any of the following mechanical concerns apply.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Drive belt cracking/chunking/wear

Drive belt noise or squeal

Pulley misaligned or excessive pulley runout

If the concern(s) remain after the inspection, determine the symptoms 
and proceed to the following symptom chart.

 Symptom Chart — Accessory Drive Belts 

 ACCESSORY DRIVE BELTS 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Excessive Noise, Belt Squeal

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE accessory if 
necessary. REPLACE belt.

Loose belt.

CHECK condition and tension of all belts. REPLACE belts or ADJUST 
tension of manually tensioned belts as necessary.

Rattle

Loose pulley or accessory.

CHECK for looseness and tighten.

Belt Chirp

Misaligned power steering pulley.

ALIGN power steering per power steering pulley alignment procedure.

Severe Belt Flutter

Loose belt.

CHECK belt tension and ADJUST (manually tensioned belts only) if 
necessary. CHECK condition of belt and REPLACE if necessary.

Frayed Belt

Belt not seated correctly (poly-V belt).

REPLACE belt and VERIFY correct belt seating.

Severely misaligned pulley.

USE a straightedge to CHECK for severe angular misalignment between 
adjacent pulleys. CORRECT as necessary.

Belt too tight.

REPLACE belt.

Belt worn out.

REPLACE belt.

Severely Glazed Belt

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE if necessary.

Loose belt.

REPLACE belt.

Improper Accessory Operation (Power Steering or Air Conditioning 
Doesn't Work, Engine Overheats or Battery Doesn't Charge)

Loose belt.

CHECK belt for looseness or glazing and REPLACE or ADJUST tension of 
manually tensioned belts if necessary.

Belt Jumps Off Pulley

Greatly misaligned pulleys.

CHECK for misalignment between adjacent pulleys.

Belt not seated correctly (poly-V belt).

REPLACE belt and VERIFY correct seating.

Pulley wobble.

VERIFY that no pulley wobbles during engine operation. Conditions 
causing wobble are: bent pulley, bent accessory shaft, rear face of pulley not 
seated flat against mating surface.

Excessive crankshaft end play.

Engine rebuild.

 Component Test 

 Drive Belt Tension 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Belt Tension Gauge

T63L-8620-A

Install Belt Tension Gauge T63L-8620-A on the drive belt(s). Check the 
tension following the tool manufacturer's instructions.

If tension is not within specification, service components as required.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Replacement

 Air Conditioner Compressor 

 Removal 

Remove power take-off drive belts (if so equipped).

Loosen nut on air conditioner compressor mounting bracket.

Loosen jam nut on belt tensioner. Turn bolt on tensioner 
counterclockwise until drive belt is loose enough to remove from A/C compressor.

Remove drive belt from idler pulley and crankshaft pulley. Discard old 
belt.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Adjust belt tension.

Tighten jam nut on belt tensioner to 40 Nm (30 lb-ft).

Tighten nut on A/C compressor pivot bolt to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft).

 Brake Compressor/Pump/Air Injection Pump (Right Side) 

 Removal 

Remove power take-off drive belts, if so equipped, as outlined.

Remove A/C compressor drive belt, if so equipped.

Loosen pivot bolt on secondary air injection pump (right side).

Loosen jam nut on air injector pump belt tensioner. Turn bolt on 
tensioner counterclockwise until drive belt is loose enough to remove from 
vehicle.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten jam nut and pivot bolt.

 Power Steering/Alternator/Air Injection Pump (Left Side) 

 Removal 

Remove power take-off (if so equipped), air conditioner compressor, 
and brake pump belts.

Loosen pivot bolt on the secondary air injection pump (right side). 
Loosen jam nut on tensioner assembly.

Loosen jam nut on air injector pump belt tensioner. Turn bolt on 
tensioner counterclockwise until drive belt is loose enough to remove from 
vehicle.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Adjust belt tension.

Tighten pivot bolt.

 Power Take-Off (PTO) 

 Removal 

Loosen mounting bolts on power take-off (PTO).

Loosen jam nut on PTO tensioner bracket.

Turn adjustment nut on tensioner counterclockwise to loosen drive 
belts. Remove drive belts.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Power take-off (PTO) uses two matched v-belts; both drive belts must be 
replaced at the same time.

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten jam nut. 

Tighten mounting bolts to 90-112 Nm (66-83 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fan and Clutch, High Mount

 Removal 

Partially drain the cooling system. (Refer to Section 03C-03 .)

Loosen clamp and remove upper radiator hose from radiator.

Remove six screws retaining radiator shroud to radiator.

 CAUTION: Clutch assembly has a left-hand thread and must be rotated clockwise to 
remove it. 

Remove fan and clutch assembly by turning clutch assembly shaft bolt 
and removing from power take-off pulley. Remove fan and clutch assembly and 
shroud from vehicle.

Remove four bolts and washers retaining fan blade to clutch assembly. 
Separate fan blade and clutch assembly.

 Installation 

Install fan blade on clutch assembly with four washers and bolts. 
Tighten bolts to 34-40 Nm (25-30 lb-ft).

Position radiator shroud, fan and clutch assembly in vehicle.

 CAUTION: Clutch assembly has a left-hand thread and must be rotated 
counterclockwise to tighten it. 

Install fan and clutch assembly on power take-off pulley by turning 
clutch assembly shaft until tight.

Install radiator shroud on radiator with six screws. Tighten screws.

Install upper radiator hose on radiator. Position and tighten clamp.

Refill cooling system. Refer to Section 03C-03 .

Fan and Clutch, Water Pump-Mounted, Non-Tilt Hood

 Removal

lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fan Pulley and Bearing

 Power Take-Off (PTO) Pulley 

 Removal 

Remove high mount fan and clutch assembly.

Remove power take-off (PTO) drive belts.

Remove adjustment nut and mounting bolts from PTO pulley and bearing 
assembly. Remove PTO pulley and bearing assembly from vehicle.

ADJUSTMENTS

Drive Belt Adjustment

 Power Take-Off (PTO) (If So Equipped) 

Loosen three mounting bolts and jam nut on PTO pulley and bearing 
assembly.

Turn adjustment nut clockwise or counterclockwise to achieve correct 
belt tension.

Tighten jam nut and mounting bolts.

 A/C Compressor 

Loosen nut on A/C compressor mounting bracket.

Loosen jam nut on A/C compressor belt tensioner. Turn bolt clockwise 
or counterclockwise to achieve correct belt tension.

Tighten jam nut and nut on A/C compressor mounting bracket.

 Secondary Air Injection (Right Side) and Brake Compressor/Pump 

Loosen nut on secondary air injection pump pivot mounting bolt.

Loosen jam nut on air injection pump drive belt tensioner. Turn bolt on 
tensioner clockwise to add tension or counterclockwise to decrease tension. 
Tighten jam nut on air injection pump tensioner and nut on pivot mounting bolt.

 Secondary Air Injection (Left Side), Alternator and Power Steering Pump 

Loosen pivot mounting bolt and jam nut.

Turn bolt on belt tensioner clockwise or counterclockwise to achieve 
correct belt tension.

Tighten jam nut and pivot mounting bolt.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Motor 

 WARNING: WHEN SERVICING STARTER MOTOR OR PERFORMING ANY MAINTENANCE IN THE AREA 
OF THE STARTER MOTOR, NOTE THE HEAVY GAUGE INPUT LEAD CONNECTED TO THE STARTER 
SOLENOID IS HOT AT ALL TIMES. 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Raise vehicle on a hoist. 

Remove retaining bolts and starter motor shield.

 CAUTION: When disconnecting hardshell connector at starter motor solenoid 
S-terminal, grasp the plastic shell and pull off. Do not pull on wire. Be 
careful to pull straight off to prevent damage to connector and S-terminal. If 
any part of connection is damaged, replace damaged components. 

Disconnect battery cable and push-on connector from starter solenoid.

Remove starter motor retaining bolts and starter. 

 Installation 

Position starter motor on engine and install upper retaining bolt. 

Position ground cable and install lower retaining bolt.

Tighten retaining bolts to 21-27 Nm (15-20 lb-ft). 

Connect starter solenoid S-terminal wire. Be careful to push straight 
on and make sure connector locks in position with a notable click or detent. 

Install battery cable and retaining nut on solenoid B-terminal. Tighten 
nut to 9-13 Nm (80-120 lb-in). 

Position starter motor shield and install retaining bolts.

Lower vehicle. 

Connect battery ground cable.

 Disassembly 

Remove positive brush connector from solenoid M-terminal. 

Remove retaining screws and starter solenoid. 

Remove through-bolts and separate drive end housing from starter frame. 
Remove housing seal assembly from drive end housing. Remove drive and gear 
assembly from drive end housing. 

Remove drive lever from drive assembly. Remove stop ring and stop ring 
retainer from output shaft, then remove drive assembly from output shaft. Push 
Truarc® E-ring off output shaft, and separate stationary gear assembly 
from output shaft. 

Remove brush plate screws and brush end plate from starter frame. 
Remove brush assembly and push armature assembly out of starter frame. 

 Assembly 

Install armature assembly in starter frame.

Apply a thin coating of Ford Teflon® Lubricant D2AZ-19590-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C111-A on both ends of armature 
shaft and spline.

Install brush assembly. Make sure brushes fit over armature commutator.

Apply grease to bushing bore in brush end plate.

Push back grommet onto starter frame and attach brush end plate with 
brush plate screws. Tighten to 2.3-3.4 Nm (20-30 lb-in). 

Apply grease to shaft assembly spline and place stationary gear 
assembly over output shaft.

Install armature thrust washer and push Truarc® E-ring onto 
output shaft.

Place drive assembly onto output shaft and install stop ring and stop 
ring retainer.

Attach drive lever to drive assembly. 

Grease and install planet gears. 

Apply grease to drive end housing bushing bearing bore (approximately 
one-quarter full).

Install drive gear assembly into drive end housing, making sure to line 
up bolt holes in drive gear assembly and drive end housing.

 Place gear retainer over drive gear assembly.

Install housing seal assembly into drive end housing. 

Position starter frame to drive end housing and install through-bolts. 
Tighten to 5.0-9.5 Nm (45-84 lb-in). 

Correctly position starter solenoid to drive end housing. Make sure 
that solenoid plunger is attached through drive lever (bottom solenoid 
M-terminal should have a metal strip attached to it). Tighten starter solenoid 
bolts to 5.1-9.6 Nm (45-85 lb-in). 

Attach positive brush connector to starter solenoid (bottom terminal). 
Tighten nut to 9-13 Nm (80-120 lb-in). 

Check that starter motor no-load current draw is within specification. 
Refer to Section 03-06 for testing procedures.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Drive Replacement 

Remove positive brush connector from solenoid M-terminal. Remove 
retaining screws and remove starter solenoid. 

Remove through-bolts and separate drive end housing from starter frame. 

Remove housing seal assembly from drive end housing.

Remove drive gear assembly from drive end housing and detach drive

remove drive assembly.

(approximately one-quarter full). Install drive gear assembly in drive end 
housing, making sure to line up bolt holes in drive gear assembly and drive 
end housing. 

Install housing seal assembly in drive end housing. 

Position starter frame to drive end housing and install through-bolts. 
Tighten to 5.0-9.5 Nm (45-84 lb-in). 

Install starter solenoid.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Starter System

The function of the starting system is to crank the engine at a speed 
fast enough to permit the engine to start. Heavy cables, connectors and 
switches are used in the starting system because of the large current required 
by the starter motor while it is cranking the engine. The amount of resistance 
in the starting circuit must be kept to an absolute minimum to provide maximum 
current for starter motor operation. A discharged or damaged battery, loose or 
corroded connections, or partially broken cables will result in slower than 
normal cranking speeds, and may even prevent the starter from cranking the 
engine.

================================================================================
PAGE 4250
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-06B: Starting System, UPS Vehicles

1999 P800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Starter Motor

The starting system includes the gear-reduction starter motor with a 
solenoid-actuated drive, the battery, a remote-control starter switch (part of 
the ignition switch), clutch switch (manual transmission), the starter relay 
and the heavy circuit wiring.

Vehicles equipped with a manual transmission have a clutch switch in 
the starter circuit that prevents operation of the starter motor unless the 
clutch pedal is depressed.

================================================================================
PAGE 4251
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-06B: Starting System, UPS Vehicles

1999 P800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Starter Relay

The starter relay consists of a pull-in coil, a contact disc, and two 
terminal contacts. Battery voltage is always present at the relay positive 
terminal. When the key is in the START position, the pull-in coil is activated 
and pulls the contact disc into contact with both terminal contacts. This 
allows battery current to pass through the starter relay to the starter 
solenoid. The starter solenoid is deactivated when the ignition is in the RUN 
or OFF position.

================================================================================
PAGE 4252
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-06B: Starting System, UPS Vehicles

1999 P800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Sequence of Operation

The field windings are connected in series with the armature windings, 
through brushes and commutator segments.

 Starter Motor Diagram 

[FIGURE: J5999B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

11083

(Part of 11390)

10655

11390

8

Plunger Return Spring
(Part of 11390)

9

11350

Starter Drive

10

—

Pinion (Part of 11350)

When the ignition switch is closed, battery current flows through the 
ignition switch and into two circuits, as follows:

the pull-in coil in the solenoid to field coil to the armature then out 
to ground

the hold-in coil in the solenoid then out to ground

This permits the plunger to be pulled by the magnetic force produced by 
pull-in and hold-in coils.

[FIGURE: J6000A.gif]

When the main switch is closed, the pull-in coil is shorted by 
bypassing the main terminal to connecting terminal. Then battery current flows 
through two circuits: 1) the ignition switch to the hold-in coil, 2) the main 
terminal to the main switch to the field winding to the armature, and the 
starter begins to crank the engine.

At this time the plunger is maintained in a pull-in position only by 
the hold-in coil magnetic force because of the minimum air gap between the 
magnet core and plunger.

[FIGURE: J6001A.gif]

When the ignition switch is opened and the main switch closed, the 
current flows through the main switch from the battery. From the main switch, 
the current flows to the pull-in coil, then to the hold-in coil and to ground.

The current flows through both pull-in and hold-in coils in the same 
direction, causing the hold-in coil magnetic force and pull-in coil magnetic 
force to be cancelled.

The main switch is opened and the plunger is pulled back toward its 
original position by the force of the return spring.

[FIGURE: J6002A.gif]

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Starter System

 Inspection and Verification 

 WARNING: WHEN SERVICING STARTER OR PERFORMING OTHER UNDERHOOD WORK IN THE 
VICINITY OF THE STARTER, BE AWARE THAT THE HEAVY GAUGE BATTERY INPUT LEAD AT 
THE STARTER SOLENOID IS ELECTRICALLY HOT AT ALL TIMES. BE SURE TO DISCONNECT 
BATTERY NEGATIVE CABLE BEFORE SERVICING STARTER. 

 WARNING: WHEN WORKING IN AREA OF THE STARTER, BE CAREFUL TO AVOID TOUCHING HOT 
EXHAUST COMPONENTS. 

Inspect starting system for loose connections.

If system does not operate properly, note condition and continue 
diagnosis using the symptom chart.

 Symptom Chart — Starter System Diagnosis 

 CAUTION: Do not operate the starter longer than 30 seconds. Do not disconnect or 
short any lead wire while starter is operating.

 Component Tests 

 Armature, Open Circuit Test 

Using a circuit tester, touch probes to two segments. There should be 
continuity at any point. If there is no continuity, the winding is 
open-circuited. Replace the armature if open-circuited.

[FIGURE: J6012A.gif]

 Armature Grounded Circuit Test 

Using a circuit tester, touch one probe to a commutator segment and the 
other to the armature core.

There should be no continuity. If there is continuity, the armature is 
grounded. Replace the armature if grounded.

[FIGURE: J6011A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Motor

 Removal 

Open battery box and disconnect battery ground cable.

Remove starter motor upper mounting bolt.

Disconnect starter and starter solenoid wires. Tag wires to facilitate 
connection at proper terminals during starter installation.

Remove remaining starter motor mounting bolt. Remove starter.

 Installation 

Position starter on engine. Install two bolts. Tighten to 150-200 
Nm (110-148 lb-ft).

Connect solenoid wire to starter 50-terminal. This is a blade terminal.

Connect remaining starter wires to starter M-terminal and tighten nut 
to 6-11 Nm (53-97 lb-in).

Connect battery ground cable and close battery box. Check operation of 
starter.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Starting System

 CAUTION: Do not clean or immerse cranking motor parts in grease dissolving 
solvents. Solvents will dissolve grease packed in drive assembly and can 
damage armature or field coil insulation. 

Clean all cranking motor parts with a soft cloth prior to inspection.

Inspect all parts for cracks, distortion or other structural damage. 
Replace parts or assemblies that are cracked bent or otherwise damaged.

Inspect threaded parts for stripped, crossed or otherwise damaged 
threads. Replace parts with thread damage that cannot be cleaned up using a 
suitable tap or die. Replace any hardware items that have damaged threads.

Inspect solenoid assembly for cut or torn boot. If boot is damaged, 
replace solenoid assembly.

Using a suitable ohmmeter, check windings of solenoid assembly for 
continuity as follows:

Check resistance of solenoid pull-in and hold-in windings in series by 
measuring resistance between starter motor terminal and solenoid case. 
Resistance should be approximately 1.2 ohms for 12-volt cranking motors.

An extremely high resistance reading indicates a break or fault in 
winding continuity. A very low resistance reading indicates a short or ground 
in the winding circuit. Either condition is cause for replacement of the 
solenoid assembly.

================================================================================
PAGE 4259
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-06B: Starting System, UPS Vehicles

1999 P800 Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Armature Coil, Starter Motor

Inspect armature assembly for the following:

Gear teeth that are broken, or that show evidence of step wear or root 
interference.

Rough commutator surface. Polish with No. 400 grit polishing cloth if 
necessary. Thoroughly clean metal dust from between commutator bars. If 
commutator surface cannot be serviced in this manner, replace armature 
assembly. Do not turn commutator in a lathe.

Worn commutator. Replace armature assembly if commutator OD is less 
than 34 mm (1.339 inch) or if undercut depth at any point is less than 0.2 mm 
(0.008 inch).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition System

The DI system features a camshaft-driven distributor without 
centrifugal or vacuum advance. The distributor has a diecast base that 
incorporates a Hall effect stator assembly. 

Initial timing adjustments are not required unless the base of the 
distributor has been moved or removed from the engine. Ignition timing 
procedures and diagnostics are found in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

 NOTE: Do not change timing by use of different octane rods without first 
having the proper authorization; federal emission requirements will be 
affected. 

The 7.0L MFI engine has computer controlled dwell, which features 
engine control module (ECM) controlled ignition coil charge times.

================================================================================
PAGE 4268
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-07: Ignition, Distributor, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition Coil

The ignition coil produces high voltage pulses that are routed through 
the distributor to the spark plugs.

================================================================================
PAGE 4269
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-07: Ignition, Distributor, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition Control Module

The ignition module receives timing signals from the ECM and controls 
the high voltage of the ignition coil. Based on input signals, the ECM will 
signal the ignition control module to make ignition timing corrections. The 
computed ignition timing is determined by the engine speed, intake manifold 
vacuum (calculated by the intake air amount and engine speed) and EGR flow rate.

================================================================================
PAGE 4270
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-07: Ignition, Distributor, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Universal Distributor

The universal distributor operates with a Hall effect vane switch 
assembly, causing the ignition coil to be switched off and on by the engine 
control module (ECM) and the ignition control module (ICM). The vane switch is 
an encapsulated package consisting of a Hall sensor on one side and a 
permanent magnet on the other side. 

[FIGURE: B4144A.gif]

A rotary vane cup is used to trigger the signal off and on. 

[FIGURE: B4145A.gif]

When the window of the vane cup is between the magnet and the Hall 
effect device, a magnetic flux field is completed from the magnet through the 
Hall effect device and back to the magnet. 

[FIGURE: B4146A.gif]

As the vane passes through this opening, the flux lines are shunted 
through the vane and back to the magnet. 

During this time, a voltage is produced as the vane passes through the 
opening. When the vane clears the opening, the window edge causes the signal 
to go to zero volts. The signal is then used by the ECM for crankshaft 
position sensing and the computation of the desired spark advance based on 
engine demand and calibration. The conditioned spark advance and voltage 
distribution is accomplished through a conventional rotor, cap and ignition 
wires. 

[FIGURE: B4147A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Distributor Cap 

 Removal 

Unsnap retaining springs from distributor cap with a screwdriver. 

Lift cap straight off distributor to prevent damage to rotor blade and 
spring. 

 Installation 

Position distributor cap on distributor base, noting the alignment 
locator. 

Snap retaining springs onto locating bosses on the cap.

 NOTE: Whenever a high-tension wire is removed from a spark plug, coil or 
distributor cap, or a new high-tension wire is installed, Silicone Dielectric 
Compound D7AZ-19A331-A (Motorcraft WA-10) or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESE-M1C171-A must be applied to boot before it is reconnected.

Reinstall any ignition wires that were removed, noting their correct 
locations on the distributor cap.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Distributor Rotor 

 Removal 

With distributor cap removed, pull rotor upward to remove it from 
distributor shaft and armature. 

 Installation 

Align locating boss on rotor with hole on armature. Fully seat rotor on 
distributor shaft. Replace distributor cap.

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Distributor 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Remove air intake tubes from air cleaner assembly to throttle body. 

Disconnect distributor from engine wiring harness. 

Mark position of No. 1 cylinder wire tower on distributor base for 
reference when installing distributor. 

Unsnap distributor cap retaining springs. Remove cap straight off 
distributor to prevent damage to rotor blade and spring. Position cap and 
attached wires aside so as not to interfere with distributor removal. 

Remove rotor by pulling it upward from the distributor shaft and 
armature. 

Remove distributor hold-down bolt and clamp. Remove distributor by 
pulling upward. 

Cover distributor opening in the cylinder block with a clean shop towel 
to prevent the entry of foreign material or dirt into the engine. 

 Installation 

Before reinstalling distributor, visually inspect distributor. Inspect 
O-ring. It must fit tightly and be free of cuts. The drive gear must be free 
of nicks, cracks and excessive wear. Rotate distributor drive shaft. It should 
rotate freely, without binding. 

To install distributor properly, No. 1 piston must be at top dead 
center (TDC) of compression stroke. Remove No. 1 cylinder spark plug and 
rotate engine clockwise until No. 1 piston is on the compression stroke. 

With No. 1 piston on compression stroke, align timing pointer with TDC 
on the crankshaft damper. 

Align locating boss on rotor with hole on armature. Fully seat rotor on 
distributor shaft. 

Rotate distributor shaft so blade on rotor is pointing toward mark on 
distributor base that was marked in Step 4 of the removal procedure. 

While installing distributor, continue rotating rotor slightly so 
leading edge of the vane is centered in vane switch stator assembly. 

Rotate distributor in block to align leading edge of vane and vane 
switch stator assembly. Verify rotor is pointing at No. 1 mark on distributor 
base. 

If vane and vane switch stator cannot be aligned by rotating 
distributor in cylinder block, remove distributor just enough to disengage 
distributor gear from camshaft gear. Rotate rotor enough to engage distributor 
gear on another tooth of camshaft gear. Repeat Step 1 if necessary. 

Install distributor hold-down clamp and bolt. Tighten bolt enough to 
rotate distributor. 

Install distributor cap, No. 1 spark plug and ignition wires. Check 
that ignition wires are securely connected to the cap and spark plugs. 

Reconnect distributor to engine wiring harness. 

Reconnect battery ground cable.

Set initial timing according to procedures found in the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.

After timing is set, tighten distributor hold-down bolt to 23-34 
Nm (17-25 lb-ft). 

Recheck initial timing. Adjust if necessary. 

Install air intake tubes to air cleaner and throttle body.

 Removal 

 CAUTION: The distributor drive gear is not released for service. If any nicks or 
cracks occur during the disassembly or assembly procedure, a new distributor 
must be installed. The distributor drive gear is matched to the distributor at 
assembly and should never be replaced. Although some of the drive gears for 
other distributors may physically fit the distributor, they must not be used. 
Whenever damage or excessive wear is noted on the drive gear, a new 
distributor must be installed.

Remove distributor assembly. 

Loosen the armature retaining screws. While loosening screws, use a

distributor armature.

when reinstalling distributor gear.

Remove and discard roll pin from thrust collar.

Invert distributor and place in Axle Bearing/Seal Plate T75L-1165-B. 
Press off the gear, using Bearing Pulling Attachment D79L-4621-A or equivalent.

on shaft.

Remove shaft assembly.

concentration. Replace complete distributor if damaged.

 Installation 

Position stator and press downward to seat in distributor base.

Position wiring grommet in distributor base notch so that eyelets align 
with screw holes.

Position distributor stator connector wires away from any moving parts.

Install distributor stator assembly retaining screw and retainer.

1.7-4.0 Nm (15-35 lb-in).

Lubricate shaft assembly with a light coating of Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent fresh motor oil meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A.

Place a 1/2-inch deep well socket over end of shaft assembly.

Invert distributor on an arbor press.

Install collar and roll pin.

 CAUTION: The distributor drive gear is not released for service. If any nicks or 
cracks occur during the disassembly or reassembly procedure, a new distributor 
must be installed. The distributor drive gear is matched to the distributor at 
assembly and should never be replaced. 

 NOTE: The hole in the drive gear and shaft assembly must be aligned as 
accurately as possible to allow for ease of roll pin insertion. If the hole in 
the drive gear and shaft assembly will not align, the gear must be removed and 
installation attempted again. The gear cannot be turned for alignment.

Install distributor gear on shaft assembly and align distributor gear 
with felt tip reference mark made at disassembly.

Place a 5/8-inch deep well socket centered around gear hole and press 
distributor gear onto shaft assembly.

Install new roll pin through distributor gear.

Install distributor armature.

 NOTE: While tightening screws, use a 5/16-inch Allen wrench to hold 
distributor shaft stationary. Do not hold distributor armature.

Install armature retaining screws and tighten to 2.8-4.0 Nm 
(25-35 lb-in).

 NOTE: If the distributor armature contacts the stator, the entire distributor 
must be replaced.

Rotate distributor shaft. Shaft should rotate freely, without any 
binding.

Install distributor assembly and reset initial timing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Ignition Wires 

The ignition wires include the spark plug wires connecting the 
distributor cap to the spark plugs and the ignition coil wire connecting the 
distributor cap to the ignition coil high voltage terminal. 

These wires are designed to reduce radio interference created by high 
voltage discharges in the ignition system. 

For testing procedures, refer to the Ignition section of the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.(Can be purchased as a 
separate item.) Do not puncture an ignition wire with any type of 
probing device. 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spark Plug Wire Remover

T74P-6666-A

 Removal 

Remove the air cleaner tube to gain access to the spark plug wires on 
the right side of the engine. 

When removing spark plug wires from spark plugs, use Spark Plug Wire 
Remover T74P-6666-A. With the special tool, twist the boot back and forth on 
plug insulator to free boot. Do not pull on wire directly; the spark plug wire 
can become separated from connector inside the boot. 

[FIGURE: A6626C.gif]

When removing spark plug wires from distributor cap or ignition coil, 
grasp boot by hand and remove with twisting and pulling motion. Do not pull on 
wire.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Whenever a high-tension wire is removed from a spark plug, coil or 
distributor cap, or a new high-tension wire is installed, Silicone Dielectric 
Compound D7AZ-19A331-A (Motorcraft WA-10) or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESE-M1C171-A must be applied to boot before it is reconnected.

Using a small clean tool, coat entire interior surface of boot with 
Silicone Dielectric Compound D7AZ-19A331-A (Motorcraft WA-10) or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESE-M1C171-A. 

Insert each spark plug wire on proper terminal of distributor cap. Make 
sure spark plug wires are fully seated on their terminals. The No. 1 terminal 
is identified on cap. Install spark plug wires starting with No. 1 terminal. 

Remove wire retaining brackets from the high tension wire set and 
install them on new set in same relative position. Install spark plug wires in 
brackets on valve rocker arm covers. 

Connect spark plug wires to proper spark plugs. 

Install ignition coil wire. 

Install air cleaner inlet tube.

 Removal 

Remove spark plug wire from spark plug, using Spark Plug Wire Remover 
T74P-6666-A, with a twisting-pulling motion. Do not pull directly on spark

 Spark Plug Hole Taperset Installation 

 WARNING: USE PROTECTIVE EYE GLASSES AT ALL TIMES. 

 NOTE: Use of power tools is not approved for installation of tapersets. 

 NOTE: Cylinder head must be removed from vehicle to prevent metal shavings 
from entering engine. 

Refer to Section 03C-01 for cylinder head removal and installation. 

 Tap 

Thoroughly clean spark plug counterbore walls and seat of all foreign 
material. 

Lubricate cutting threads of tap with cutting oil. 

Install tap pilot into spark plug port threads. 

Using ratchet wrench and keeping tap aligned, rotate tap until depth 
stop collar bottoms on face of port and tightens against retaining ring. 

Using an air hose, clean out as many shavings as possible. 

If stop collar is loose, tap has not penetrated to full depth. 

Remove tap from spark plug port. 

Clear shavings from spark plug port and cylinder with air hose. 

Inspect spark plug threads in cylinder head. Damaged spark plug threads 
in the cylinder head can be serviced using Rotunda Spark Plug Repair Kit 
107-R0921 or equivalent.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Repeat Steps 1 through 8 of tap procedure above to ensure a clean bore. 

Lubricate mandrel threads and taperset with aluminum cutting coil. Then 
thread taperset onto mandrel with larger counterbore end toward 18-mm 
(11/16-inch) hex body until one thread of mandrel shows beyond tip of taperset.

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Induction System

The air induction system supplies clean air to the throttle body 
assembly. Outside air enters the tube assembly mounted to the radiator 
support, and flows through the engine air cleaner intake duct and into the 
engine air cleaner. From there, the air is filtered through the air filter 
element and then travels through the outlet tube and into the throttle body 
assembly.

================================================================================
PAGE 4293
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-12: Air Intake System, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Cleaner Element

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a 
clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering the engine. 

The air cleaner element is a dry-type, chemically treated and pleated 
paper air filtering element that permits airflow through the air induction 
system while filtering out unwanted dust, dirt and debris.

Air Restriction Indicator

Some air intake systems are equipped with direct mounted air 
restriction indicators (mounted to the cover of the air cleaner) that 
indicate when the air cleaner needs servicing. When the yellow diaphragm 
reaches the red marker of the air restriction indicator, the air cleaner 
needs servicing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a 
clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering the engine. 

Loosen latches or remove wing nut.

Remove air cleaner housing cover.

Remove wing nut retaining air cleaner element to stud (if so equipped).

Release the seal gently. Remove the air cleaner element gently to 
reduce the amount of dust dislodged. There will be some initial resistance, 
similar to breaking the seal on a jar. Gently move the end of the air cleaner 
element up and down and side to side or twist to break the seal.

[FIGURE: V8451A.gif]

Avoid dislodging dust from the air cleaner element. Gently pull the air 
cleaner element out of the housing. Avoid knocking the air cleaner element 
against the air cleaner housing.

[FIGURE: V8452A.gif]

 Installation

make sure the following conditions exist:

gasket surfaces clean and undamaged

air cleaner housing outlet tube clean and undamaged

air cleaner element dry and free of holes, ruptures, damaged gaskets or 
dents in end covers and liners

air cleaner element retaining nut gasket washer attached and in good 
condition

Install the air cleaner element into the air cleaner housing and 
tighten the wing nut. Make sure the rubber face of the washer seals against 
the air cleaner element.

Install air cleaner housing cover.

Tighten wing nut or secure latches.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Cleaner Element

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a

Inspect the air cleaner element for indications of air leaks that can

air cleaner element. Do not attempt to clean air cleaner element.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Engine Air Cleaner Housing

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a 
clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering the engine. 

Always clean the sealing surface of the air cleaner housing outlet 
tube. Dust on the outer diameter of the housing outlet tube can hinder an 
effective seal and cause leakage. Make sure all contaminants are removed 
before the new air cleaner element is inserted.

[FIGURE: V8453A.gif]

Always clean the inside of the air cleaner housing outlet tube 
carefully. Dirt accidentally transferred to the inside of the air cleaner 
housing outlet tube will etch the engine and cause wear. Use care not to 
damage the air cleaner element sealing area on the housing outlet tube.

[FIGURE: V8454A.gif]

Check the old air cleaner element. It can help in the detection of 
foreign material on the sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of 
dust on the clean air side of the air cleaner element seal is the tell-tale 
sign. If dust exists, make sure the cause is removed before installing a new 
air cleaner element.

[FIGURE: V8455A.gif]

Inspect the new air cleaner element for damage. Always look for 
possible shipping or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside 
of the open end (the sealing area). Check for cuts, etc. Do not use a damaged 
air cleaner element.

[FIGURE: V8456A.gif]

After the air cleaner element and other parts are found to be in good 
condition, assemble the parts. Install the air cleaner element and tighten the 
wing nut. Make sure the rubber face of washer seals against the air cleaner 
element. Install the air cleaner cover. Tighten wing nut or secure latches.

Check connections and ducts for air-tight fit. Make sure all clamps, 
flange connections and mounting bolts are tight. Seal any leaks in the clean 
air duct immediately — they permit dirt to enter the engine directly. 
All ducts, from air cleaner housing to engine, must be tight.

Section 03C-13: Evaporative Emission, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Evaporative Emission Control System

All gasoline-fueled engines are equipped with a fuel evaporative 
emission system. The evaporative emission system limits the amount of fuel 
vapor a vehicle releases to the atmosphere in accordance with current federal 
and state requirements for fuel evaporation. Fuel vapors are vented through an 
evaporative emission hose or tube from the top of the fuel tank to the 
evaporative emission canister. A hose or tube directs evaporative emissions 
from the evaporative emission canister to the engine permitting evaporative 
emission canister purging, and vapor consumption by the engine.

The 7.0L MFI engines have an additional valve in the tube or hose 
between the evaporative emission canister and engine. This evaporative 
emission canister regulator valve provides control over quantity and duration 
of emission delivery to the engine. Refer to Evaporative Emission Canister 
Purge Regulator Valve in the Description and Operation portion of this 
section. 

The evaporative emission system, regardless of application, establishes 
a path between the fuel vapor source (fuel tank) and a fuel vapor storage area 
(evaporative emission canister). Additionally, a path is established between 
the evaporative emission canister and engine air intake stream to provide 
canister purging and vapor consumption by the engine.

================================================================================
PAGE 4304
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-13: Evaporative Emission, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fill Control/Vapor Vent System 

Fill limiting is accomplished through fill pipe configuration or 
external vent lines within the fuel tank filler pipe and fuel tank. The vent 
system is designed to permit at least 10 percent fuel tank volume air space 
when the fuel tank is filled to capacity. This air space provides for thermal 
expansion of fuel as well as being an aid to the in-tank vapor vent system.

This system provides a vapor space above the gasoline surface in the 
fuel tank. This area is sufficient to permit adequate breathing space for the 
evaporative emission valve under static and most dynamic conditions. This is 
accomplished by the evaporative emission valve that is located on the upper 
surface of the fuel tank.

All evaporative emission valves make use of a small orifice that tends 
to allow only vapor and not fuel to pass into the tube running forward to the 
evaporative emission canister. The evaporative emission valve mounts directly 
to the top of the fuel tank using a fuel vapor separator seal.

Fuel vapors trapped in the sealed fuel tank are vented through the 
orificed evaporative emission valve in the top of the fuel tank. The vapors 
leave the evaporative emission valve through a single tube and continue to the 
evaporative emission canister for storage, until they are purged to the engine.

================================================================================
PAGE 4305
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-13: Evaporative Emission, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

System Components 

 Fuel Tank Evaporative Emission System 

This system consists of the following components:

sealed fuel tank and fuel tank filler pipe

evaporative emission valve 

activated carbon evaporative emission canister 

evaporative emission canister regulatory valve 

associated tubes, hoses, clamps and fittings 

The 7.0L MFI evaporative emission system incorporates a purge control 
solenoid in the tube/hose between the evaporative emission canister and 
throttle body vacuum fitting. The purge control solenoid is operated by the 
engine control module (ECM) and regulates the quantity and duration of vapor 
delivery to the throttle body. 

The system functions as follows: fuel vapors are continuously generated 
in the fuel tank due to the evaporation of fuel. Fuel vapors are directed to 
the evaporative emission canister where they are stored until conditions are 
favorable for the vapors to be introduced into the engine air intake stream. 
With the engine running and in an off idle (any rpm except idle) condition, 
fuel vapors are introduced into the engine through the evaporative emission 
canister output tube/hose. The evaporative emission canister output tube/hose 
connects the evaporative emission canister to the throttle body vacuum 
fitting. 

Evaporative emission canister purging occurs as fresh air is introduced 
into the system and passes through the carbon canister, into the engine air 
intake stream. Fresh air enters the evaporative emission system through the 
evaporative emission valve/orifice rollover valve assembly. The fresh air is 
directed to the evaporative emission canister where it passes over the 
activated carbon bed and releases stored fuel vapors. The fresh air/fuel vapor 
mixture is vented from the evaporative emission canister to the throttle body 
vacuum fitting where it is introduced into the engine air intake stream. Thus, 
the evaporative emission canister is purged and prepared for future fuel vapor 
storage. 

 Engine Evaporative Emission System 

This system consists of the following components:

evaporative emission canister valve

evaporative emission regulatory valve

secondary air bypass valve

System control and operation are accomplished through five separate 
basic functions in the system:

Fill control venting

Tank vapor venting and storage system

Fuel vapor return system

Fuel vapor purge system

Pressure and vacuum relief valve

================================================================================
PAGE 4306
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-13: Evaporative Emission, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Evaporative Emission Canister 

All vehicles use two engine compartment-mounted 1400-ml evaporative 
emission canisters. Contained within the evaporative emission canister is 1400 
ml (1.48 qt) of activated carbon, referred to as the carbon bed. Activated 
carbon has the ability to store fuel vapors when exposed to them. Activated 
carbon also has the ability to purge (release) stored fuel vapors when exposed 
to fresh airflow. The carbon bed experiences almost no loss of vapor 
absorption or purgation capacity over time. Thus, the evaporative emission 
canister provides storage of fuel vapors until conditions are acceptable for 
the vapors to be introduced into the engine intake air stream. 

[FIGURE: V5351B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4307
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-13: Evaporative Emission, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Evaporative Emission Hose

The evaporative emission hose transmits vapor from the evaporative 
emission canister purge regulatory valve and evaporative emission return tube 
to the evaporative emission canister.

================================================================================
PAGE 4308
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03C-13: Evaporative Emission, 7.0L Gasoline Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Evaporative Emission Canister Purge Regulator Valve 

The evaporative emission canister purge regulator valve is a normally 
closed valve in the evaporative emission system. The evaporative emission 
canister purge regulator valve is connected in-line between the evaporative 
emission canister and the intake manifold. 

[FIGURE: V47291B.gif]

The operation of the evaporative emission canister purge regulator 
valve is controlled by the engine control module (ECM). When engine is off, 
the evaporative emission canister regulator valve is not energized and is in a 
closed, non-flowing condition. When the engine is running the ECM reads engine 
rpm, engine load, engine temperature and other variables and decides the 
proper time for the engine to accept fuel vapors. When this occurs, the ECM 
energizes the evaporative emission canister regulator valve to open, allowing 
flow from the evaporative emission canister into the intake manifold through 
the throttle body vacuum fitting. The vapors are then consumed in the engine. 
This action "purges" the evaporative emission canister of fuel vapors, and 
occurs as fresh air is sucked into the evaporative emission canister under the 
fresh air inlet cap of the canister. This fresh air passes through the 
activated carbon bed of the canister and releases the stored fuel vapors to 
pass from the canister through the evaporative emission return tube, to the 
canister purge solenoid, and into the engine for consumption.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Evaporative Emission Valve 

The hydraulic mechanical evaporative emission valve is located 
centrally on top of the fuel tank. It is attached to the tank by six fasteners 
and sealed by a compression O-ring. Air or vapor passes through the 
evaporative emission and is metered by an orifice when tank pressure is at 
0-10.3 kPa (0-1.5 psi). All vapors passing through the orifice must flow 
through the internal rollover valve. The rollover valve prevents liquid fuel 
from entering the vapor tube. Over-pressurization of the fuel tank is 
prevented by the pressure relief valve, which is activated at 10.3 kPa (1.5 
psi) ±3.44 kPa (0.5 psi). 

[FIGURE: V5345C.gif]

Fuel vapors trapped in the sealed fuel tank are vented through the 
orificed evaporative emission valve assembly in the top of the tank. The 
vapors leave the valve assembly through a single vapor tube and a purge valve 
which also controls vapor flow. They continue to the evaporative emission 
canister in the engine compartment for storage. The vapors are stored until 
the evaporative emission canister regulatory valve is actuated and then the 
vapors are drawn into the engine. 

The evaporative emission valve has a float system that eliminates the 
chance of liquid fuel from passing into the vent tube system on vehicle 
rollover.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Evaporative Emission System

 Inspection and Verification

diagnosis of evaporative emission system complaints. Fill cap damage or 
contamination that renders the pressure-vacuum valve inoperative may result in 
deformation of the tank. Care should always be exercised to ensure that a 
proper fill cap (in working order) is used. Refer to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual for individual components. Typical evaporative emission system is

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Evaporative Emission Canister 

 WARNING: THE EVAPORATIVE EMISSION SYSTEM CONTAINS FUEL VAPOR AND CONDENSED FUEL 
VAPOR. ALTHOUGH NOT PRESENT IN LARGE QUANTITIES, IT STILL PRESENTS THE DANGER 
OF EXPLOSION OR FIRE. DISCONNECT THE BATTERY GROUND CABLE FROM THE BATTERY TO 
MINIMIZE THE POSSIBILITY OF AN ELECTRICAL SPARK OCCURRING, POSSIBLY CAUSING A 
FIRE OR EXPLOSION IF FUEL VAPOR OR LIQUID FUEL IS PRESENT IN THE AREA. 

Evaporative emission components have been designed and tested to exceed 
193,116 km (120,000 miles) or 10 years of vehicle use. No maintenance or 
servicing should be required. However, if components have been damaged and are 
to be replaced, or if disconnection or removal is required for diagnosis, use 
the following techniques to aid servicing the system.

 Removal 

To disconnect a hose from any component, perform the following steps. 

Grip component securely with one hand and the hose with the other hand, 
as close as possible to connection.

 WARNING: MOST CONNECTIONS IN THE EVAPORATIVE EMISSION SYSTEM ARE VERY SECURE. A 
STRONG PULLING AND SIMULTANEOUS TWISTING ACTION IS REQUIRED TO DISCONNECT. 
WHEN DISCONNECTION OCCURS, BOTH HANDS CAN SHARPLY AND UNCONTROLLABLY MOVE IN 
THE DIRECTION OF EACH HAND'S PULLING. BE CAREFUL THAT NO SHARP OR DAMAGING 
OBJECTS ARE IN LINE WITH THE DIRECTION OF PULL TO PREVENT PHYSICAL INJURY AND 
DAMAGE TO THE OBJECTS THAT WILL BE IMPACTED BY THE HANDS WHEN DISCONNECTION 
OCCURS. 

 NOTE: It is important to break the hose free at its connection point. If the 
joint is stubborn and a sharp twist does not work, grip the hose with a pair 
of pliers directly over the joint and twist again.

Sharply twist hose along its axis to break the temporary bond between 
hose and component. (No adhesive is used to make hose connections during 
vehicle assembly, but natural aging of the connections causes a temporary bond 
to exist.)

Once the hose/component joint has been broken, disconnect by gripping 
the component securely with with one hand and hose with the other. Twist hose 
and, at the same time, pull apart. Use Ford-approved vacuum hoses for 
replacement of damaged hoses. Original equipment hoses are designed to resist 
most environmental conditions encountered in the evaporative emission system.

Disconnect the hoses from the canister. 

Remove the screw securing the canister to the bracket or fender apron. 

Lift up on the canister to disengage the tab on the back side and 
remove the canister. 

 Installation 

Insert the tab at the back of the canister into the slot in the bracket 
or fender apron. 

Align the screw hole and install the screw. 

Tighten the screw to 5-9 Nm (44-80 lb-in). 

Connect hose(s) by wetting the hose and pushing it onto component. 

On a vehicle with dual fuel tanks, connect the evaporative emission 
tube connecting the tanks. 

Fill the tank with fuel and install the filler cap. Connect the battery 
ground cables. Start the engine and check for leaks.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Control Systems, Electronic

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE OR CARRY LIGHTED TOBACCO OR OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND CAN BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY. 

The multiport fuel injection (MFI) system is classified as a 
multi-point, pulse time, speed density fuel injection system.

To maintain the required exhaust emission levels, the fuel metering 
system must be in proper operating condition and adjusted to the 
specifications listed in or on the following sources:

the applicable section of the 1996 Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual

the applicable section in Group 03 of this manual

the Vehicle Emission Control Information (VECI) decal

Additional engine performance checks are required to keep the exhaust 
emissions at the specified minimum pollutant level.

Always refer to the Master Parts List for parts usage and 
interchangeability before replacing a throttle body or any component part of a 
throttle body.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Control Module (ECM)

The engine control module (ECM) receives inputs from various engine 
sensors to compute the required fuel flow rate necessary to maintain a proper 
air/fuel ratio throughout the entire engine operational range. The ECM outputs 
a command to the fuel injector to meter the appropriate quantity of fuel.

The ECM is very sensitive to static electricity and can be easily 
damaged by the voltage induced by a common static discharge. Refer to 
safeguards in the Removal and Installation portion of this section before 
handling an ECM. 

[FIGURE: DA1336A.gif]

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Throttle Position (TP) Sensor

The throttle position (TP) sensor is a potentiometer that provides a 
signal to the engine control module proportional to the throttle plate 
position. The throttle position sensor connects to the throttle plate shaft.

[FIGURE: A20790C.gif]

Section 03C-14: Engine Controls, Electronic

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Sensor

The intake air temperature (IAT) sensor changes resistance in response 
to changing intake air temperature. The IAT sensor resistance decreases as the 
air temperature increases providing a signal to the engine control module 
(ECM) indicating the temperature of incoming intake air. The IAT sensor is 
installed in the lower intake manifold.

[FIGURE: A20792A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Idle Air Control (IAC) Valve

 CAUTION: Use of solvents can damage the IAC valve. 

The idle air control (IAC) valve is used to control engine idle speed 
and dashpot functions. The idle air control valve is mounted on the lower 
portion of the upper intake manifold and allows air to bypass the throttle 
plate. The amount of air allowed to bypass the throttle plate is determined by 
the engine control module (ECM) and controlled by a duty cycle signal.

[FIGURE: DA0851A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) Sensor

The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor changes resistance in 
response to changing temperature of the engine coolant. The engine coolant 
temperature sensor resistance decreases as the engine coolant temperature 
increases, providing a signal to the engine control module (ECM) indicating 
the temperature of the engine coolant.

[FIGURE: A20793B.gif]
