DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) Sensor

The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor measures the pressure in 
the intake manifold and provides this information as a variable frequency 
signal to the engine control module (ECM). With the ignition switch in the KEY 
ON/ENGINE OFF position, the manifold absolute pressure sensor will indicate 
the barometric pressure in the intake manifold. 

[FIGURE: A20794A.gif]

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Heated Oxygen Sensor (HO2S)

The heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) reacts with the oxygen in the exhaust 
gases and will generate a voltage. A low voltage indicates too much oxygen or 
a lean condition. A high voltage indicates not enough oxygen or a rich 
condition. 

[FIGURE: A20795B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Safeguards 

Use the following safeguards to avoid static electrical damage. 

Always disconnect the battery ground cable prior to service or 
replacement of emission system electronic engine controls.

Follow diagnostic procedures in the 1996 Powertrain Control/Emissions 
Diagnosis Manual.

Disconnect electronic engine controls from wire harness before 
measuring for continuity or resistance or energizing with a B+ source.

Never measure voltage or resistance directly at the engine control 
module (ECM).

Leave the electronic modules in their original packaging until ready to 
install in vehicles. 

Avoid touching module connector pins. 

Avoid laying modules on nonconductive surfaces. 

As an added safeguard, use a 3M Static Protection Kit (3M part number 
18293). This kit contains special wrist straps, a 15-inch x 24-inch flexible 
conductive mat, grounding cords and full instructions. It is available through 
local 3M suppliers.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Engine Control Module (ECM)

The ECM is located under the glove compartment and is mounted to the 
dash panel inside the vehicle. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable. 

Remove the ECM holding box cover screws. 

[FIGURE: B5098C.gif]

Position floor matting out of the way to gain access to the ECM. 

Remove module box cover retaining nut and ground screw. 

Remove the module from its retaining mounts.

[FIGURE: DA1337A.gif]

Remove the bolt that retains the electrical connector to the ECM and 
remove the connector from the module. 

Remove the module from engine control housing cover.

 Installation 

Connect the electrical connector to the ECM and install the retaining 
bolt.

Install the module in the engine control housing cover.

Position ground wire on cowl panel stud and install module and housing 
onto cowl panel stud using retaining nut. 

Install module box cover and tighten retaining screws. 

Position floor matting. 

Connect battery ground cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Idle Air Control (IAC) Valve

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Idle Air Control (IAC) Valve

 Recommended Cleaning Procedure 

 CAUTION: Use only specified cleaner. Do not spray directly on throttle plate or 
use any type of scrubbing method. 

Make sure bypass actuator is operating properly. Refer to the 1996 
Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual.(Can be purchased as a 
separate item.)

Remove air cleaner outlet tube.

Disconnect idle air control (IAC) valve connector.

Connect Rotunda Fuel Injector Tester/Cleaner 164-R3750 and Air Bypass 
Valve Actuator 164-R3756 or equivalents.

Start the actuator and then start the vehicle. Do not start engine if 
vehicle is equipped with mass airflow sensor.

Spray Carburetor Tune Up Cleaner D9AZ-19579-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M14P9-A into IAC valve port for five seconds while 
actuator is operating. Avoid direct spraying on throttle plate bore area.

Turn off the actuator and stop engine (if running). Allow solvent to 
soak for 15 minutes.

Turn on actuator and start engine.

Spray carburetor cleaner into idle air bypass passage for one minute.

Operate the actuator and make sure the solvent is purged from the IAC 
valve.

Turn off actuator and stop engine (if running).

Install air cleaner outlet tube. Start actuator and engine and run 
engine for one minute to dry out solvent residue.

Disconnect actuator from IAC valve. Connect IAC valve electrical 
connector.

Start engine and check for normal operation.

 Alternate Cleaning Procedure 

This method should be used only when Rotunda Fuel Injector 
Tester/Cleaner 164-R3750 and Air Bypass Valve Actuator 164-R3756 or 
equivalents are not available.

Remove the idle air control (IAC) valve from the upper manifold 
assembly. Remove the electrical solenoid assembly from the mechanical portion 
of the IAC valve by removing the two screws, then sliding the mechanical 
portion away from the solenoid.

 CAUTION: Do not exceed three minutes soak time, and do not use choke cleaner; an 
internal O-ring may begin to deteriorate. 

Soak the mechanical portion in Carburetor Tune-Up Cleaner D9AZ-19579-BA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P9-A for three minutes maximum.

With the mechanical portion completely submerged, shake in all 
directions: up, down, right, and left. Then push in on the rod that mates with 
the solenoid assembly, and again shake in all directions with the unit 
submerged and the rod held in as far as possible.

Remove the unit from the cleaner and dry out thoroughly using 
compressed air.

Section 03D-04A: Fuel Vaporization and Carburetion, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Special Handling

 WARNING: DO NOT PARK OR SERVICE A LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED VEHICLE 
NEAR ANY SOURCE OF FIRE, SUCH AS OPEN FLAME, CIGARETTES OR SMOKING MATERIALS, 
SPARKS, EXCESSIVE HEAT, WELDING OR GRINDING. AVOID PLACING THE VEHICLE NEAR 
ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT THAT DISCHARGES SPARKS THROUGH NORMAL OPERATION, FOR 
EXAMPLE, MOTORS, ELECTRICAL SWITCHES, AND RADIO TRANSMISSION EQUIPMENT. AVOID 
STORING OR SERVICING THE VEHICLE OVER SEWER DRAINS, LUBRICATION PITS, 
SUB-FLOOR LEVEL ROOMS, OR OTHER LOW-LYING AREAS. IF ANY SOURCE OF FIRE OR 
IGNITION CONTACTS LPG VAPOR, A FIRE COULD RESULT. 

 WARNING: DO NOT NEEDLESSLY RELEASE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL DURING 
SERVICE, AND DO NOT OPEN THE STOP-FILL VALVE WHILE A VEHICLE IS INSIDE A 
BUILDING. WHEN SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM, CLOSE THE LPG FUEL TANK SHUTOFF 
VALVES (TWO VALVES IF EQUIPPED WITH TWO FUEL TANKS) AND RUN THE ENGINE OUT OF 
FUEL BEFORE DISCONNECTING FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENTS. IF THE FUEL TANK IS BEING 
SERVICED, HAVE THE FUEL EVACUATED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL AT A LOCAL LPG FUEL 
STATION. LPG FUEL VAPORIZES (AT NORMAL BAROMETRIC PRESSURE) AT TEMPERATURES 
ABOVE -42°C (-44°F), AND CAN EXPAND TO APPROXIMATELY 270 TIMES ITS 
LIQUID VOLUME. UNNECESSARY VENTING OF LPG CAN CREATE FIRES AND HEALTH HAZARDS 
WHICH CAN LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY OR ILLNESS. 

 WARNING: LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL TANKS SHOULD BE DRAINED BY TRAINED 
PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO USE SHOP AIR PRESSURE TO FORCE LPG FUEL FROM 
THE TANKS. NORMAL FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1724 KPA (250 PSI) AT 
ROOM TEMPERATURE. CONNECTING A SHOP AIR HOSE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM CAN RESULT IN 
FUEL FLOWING BACK INTO THE SERVICE AIR SYSTEM, AND RESULT IN FIRE OR 
EXPLOSION. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE PAINT DRYING OVENS FOR LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED 
VEHICLES. THE HEAT OF PAINT DRYING OVENS WILL INCREASE PRESSURE IN THE FUEL 
TANKS. THIS CAN CAUSE VENTING OF THE LPG FUEL VAPOR INTO THE OVEN RESULTING IN 
FIRE FROM HEAT OR SPARK IN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. IF LPG FUEL IS CONFINED IN AN 
OVEN, THERE IS ALSO THE RISK OF EXPLOSION IF THE FUEL IS IGNITED. WHEN 
REFINISHING THE BODY PANELS OF LPG-FUELED VEHICLES, SPOT PAINT THE AFFECTED 
AREA USING SPOT DRYING METHODS. 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY THE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) ENGINE FUEL SYSTEM 
CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS. DO NOT REPLACE COMPONENTS WITH PARTS THAT DO NOT 
MEET FORD SPECIFICATIONS. FORD SPECIFIED PARTS ARE AVAILABLE AT AUTHORIZED 
FORD DEALERS. THE LPG FUEL STORAGE SYSTEM MUST CONFORM TO NATIONAL FIRE 
PROTECTION ASSOCIATION STANDARD NO. 58, AND SIMILAR CANADIAN GAS ASSOCIATION 
STANDARDS. THESE STANDARDS DEFINE THE SPECIALLY-APPROVED MATERIALS, COMPONENT 
CONSTRUCTION, AND SYSTEM INSTALLATION ON ALL LPG-POWERED VEHICLES. THE USE OF 
DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS CAN PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT CAN 
RESULT IN FIRE HAZARD OR OTHERWISE LEAD TO HUMAN INJURY. 

 WARNING: AVOID INHALING LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) OR OCCUPYING CONFINED 
AREAS CONTAINING LPG. LPG IS HEAVIER THAN AIR. THE HEAVIER GAS CAN DISPLACE OR 
"PUSH" FRESH AIR OUT OF AN AREA. IN LARGE QUANTITIES LPG CAN DISPLACE ENOUGH 
OXYGEN TO MAKE THE SURROUNDING AIR UNFIT TO BREATHE, CAUSING HEADACHES, 
DIZZINESS AND POSSIBLE SUFFOCATION DURING PROLONGED EXPOSURE. 

IN THE EVENT OF EXPOSURE TO LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG), MOVE THE 
VICTIM IMMEDIATELY TO FRESH AIR AND CONTACT A PHYSICIAN OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY 
PERSONNEL FOR ARTIFICIAL RESPIRATION OR OTHER REQUIRED TREATMENT. 

 WARNING: IF AIR IN A CONFINED AREA, SUCH AS A LUBRICATION PIT, HAS BEEN FOULED 
WITH LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG), THE AREA SHOULD BE CHECKED FOR ADEQUATE 
OXYGEN LEVELS BY LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL BEFORE BEING USED, TO AVOID 
PERSONAL INJURY OR SUFFOCATION.

PAGE 4340
================================================================================

Section 03D-04A: Fuel Vaporization and Carburetion, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

LPG System

Liquified petroleum gas (LPG) is an engine fuel very similar to 
gasoline. Both fuels are a product of crude oil. They differ in that LPG is 
more volatile and becomes a vapor at ordinary temperatures. When LPG is used 
in an internal combustion engine it is converted from a liquid in the fuel 
tank to a vaporous gas before entering the combustion chamber. 

LPG flows from the fuel tank through a hydrostatic relief valve, 
vacuum-activated fuel lock and filter, to the converter. In the converter the 
liquid becomes a vapor, which flows to the carburetor where it is mixed with 
air in the proper proportions for maximum engine performance.

================================================================================
PAGE 4341
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-04A: Fuel Vaporization and Carburetion, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuelock®

The main function of the Fuelock® is to supply filtered fuel 
only when the engine is operating. The Fuelock® is a vacuum-operated 
switch that only allows fuel to enter the engine when the engine creates a 
vacuum while cranking or running.

================================================================================
PAGE 4342
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-04A: Fuel Vaporization and Carburetion, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Converter 

This convertor is a water-heated, two stage vaporizer regulator. The 
fuel enters at tank pressure as a liquid and is reduced to approximately 10.3 
kPa (1.5 psi) within the vaporizing chamber where the fuel is converted from a 
liquid to a vapor. The heat for vaporization is supplied from the engine 
cooling system, which circulates coolant through the chambers within the heat 
exchange portion of the converter. 

The fuel, now a vapor, passes through the secondary valve (controlled 
by the secondary diaphragm) into the secondary chamber or regulator, where the 
fuel is drawn off through the fuel outlet to the carburetor. The start-assist 
valve provides enrichment of fuel during cranking for fast starts and seals 
off the fuel when the engine is not cranking. The converter also seals the 
fuel from escaping into the environment.

================================================================================
PAGE 4343
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-04A: Fuel Vaporization and Carburetion, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

LPG Carburetor 

The LPG carburetor consists of two components. The first is the mixer 
assembly, the second is the throttle body assembly.

================================================================================
PAGE 4344
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-04A: Fuel Vaporization and Carburetion, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mixer 

The function of the mixer is to accurately meter the correct proportion 
of air and fuel to satisfy the full range of load demands of the engine. The 
fuel flow through the carburetor is controlled by an air-fuel valve. The fuel 
metering valve is connected directly to the air-fuel valve so that accurate 
air-fuel proportions are ensured. A vacuum circuit opens and closes the 
air-fuel valve assembly by directing vacuum from the throat of the carburetor 
body to a diaphragm above the air-fuel valve assembly. During engine cranking, 
the air-fuel valve assembly will pulsate with the changing vacuum signal. When 
the engine is operating at low speeds the lower vacuum signal will hold the 
air-fuel valve assembly open a small amount. As the speed of the engine 
increases, the higher manifold vacuum creates a stronger force on the 
diaphragm allowing more LPG fuel and air to flow into the carburetor. When the 
engine is not running the air-fuel valve assembly closes off the opening 
trapping the LPG fuel within the mixer assembly. 

The mixer contains two adjustments, one for the idle and one for the 
power mixture. These are preset and sealed at the factory. The idle mixture 
circuit consists of a bypass port, diaphragm and cover. A passage within the 
carburetor body provides a bypass port. At idle, the engine vacuum lifts the 
seal off the port allowing LPG fuel to enter the engine. As engine demands 
increase, the air-fuel valve lifts, which overrides the idle circuit. The 
power circuit is only an adjustment to the maximum fuel delivery.

================================================================================
PAGE 4345
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-04A: Fuel Vaporization and Carburetion, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Throttle Body 

The throttle body is a Holley® four-barrel carburetor base. 
This supplies the vacuum sources for positive crankcase ventilation, 
distributor vacuum advance, and accessory vacuum. The throttle body also 
provides mounting for the governor assembly and curb idle adjustments, and 
provisions for the throttle and fast idle linkage.

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

LPG Fuel Charging Assembly 

 WARNING: ALWAYS PERFORM THE PRE-SERVICE PROCEDURES BEFORE SERVICING ANY PART OF 
THE LPG FUEL CHARGING SYSTEM. 

 NOTE: Some components cannot be removed while the carburetor assembly remains 
installed on the intake manifold. If removal is required, a new throttle body 
gasket must be used when reinstalling the carburetor. 

 Pre-Service Procedures 

The fuel charging assembly consists of the Fuelock®, converter, 
air horn, start assist valve, and carburetor assembly. The carburetor assembly 
consists of the mixer, throttle body, and governor. Prior to any service or 
removal of the components from the LPG fuel charging system, the following 
steps must be taken: 

Close the fuel valve at the fuel supply. 

To exhaust residual fuel, start and run the engine until it stalls.

Disconnect the battery negative cable. 

 Post-Service Procedure 

After the service is complete and the LPG fuel charging system is 
completely installed, the following steps must be taken: 

Pressurize the fuel system and check for leaks with a solution of 
liquid soap and water. Coat fuel fittings and seals. If bubbling occurs, 
repair or replace as necessary. 

Connect the battery negative cable. 

Add coolant as needed. 

Start the engine and allow it to reach operating temperature. Check for 
coolant leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Carburetor Assembly 

 WARNING: ALWAYS PERFORM THE PRE-SERVICE PROCEDURES BEFORE SERVICING ANY PART OF 
THE LPG FUEL CHARGING SYSTEM. 

 Removal 

Close LPG fuel manual valve at the fuel tank (both valves on vehicles 
equipped with two fuel tanks). 

Start and run vehicle engine until it stalls and all residual LPG in 
the system is used. Make sure to ventilate the exhaust properly. 

Make sure radiator is cool. Position a suitable container under the 
radiator. Open petcock and drain radiator, so the coolant level is low enough 
to avoid leaks from coolant lines disconnected at the converter.

Remove air cleaner assembly. Refer to Section 03D-12 .

Disconnect throttle linkages at the carburetor assembly. 

Disconnect PCV hose, vacuum lines, and all electrical connectors from 
governor and converter assemblies.

Slowly and carefully unscrew the LPG fuel supply line and allow any 
residual LPG pressure to escape. Follow all safety warnings and use adequate 
ventilation during this step. When all residual fuel pressure is exhausted, 
disconnect fuel supply line fitting. 

Disconnect two converter support braces from carburetor assembly. 

[FIGURE: A18737A.gif]

Remove two AIR system hoses forward of the check valves. Move them out 
of the way for clearance. 

Disconnect left-side coolant hose at the converter and move it out of 
the way. 

[FIGURE: A18738A.gif]

Remove four carburetor assembly mounting bolts. 

 CAUTION: DO NOT allow any foreign material to fall into the intake manifold. 

Carefully tip the carburetor fore and aft to break the seal. Lift 
assembly and bring it forward enough to access the right side coolant hose 
clamp.

Disconnect the right-side coolant hose. 

Remove carburetor assembly. 

 Carburetor Assembly, 7.0L LPG 

[FIGURE: A19052A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: DO NOT allow any foreign material to enter the intake manifold. 

Make sure all old gasket material is removed from lower surface of the 
throttle body and upper mounting surface of intake manifold.

Install a new throttle body gasket on the intake manifold. Do not use 
the old gasket. 

Carefully position carburetor assembly in front of its mounting 
location. Connect right side coolant hose. 

Carefully position carburetor assembly on the intake manifold. Install 
and tighten carburetor assembly mounting bolts to 17-24 Nm (12-18 lb-ft).

Reconnect left side coolant hose. 

Tighten converter support brace nuts to 17-24 Nm (12-18 lb-ft). 

Reconnect LPG fuel supply line to carburetor assembly. 

Reconnect PCV hose, vacuum lines and all electrical connectors. 

Reconnect throttle linkages. Tighten return spring bracket bolt to 8-11 
Nm (70-105 lb-in).

Refill radiator with coolant to specifications. 

Open manual LPG fuel valves at the LPG fuel tanks. 

Start engine momentarily then shut off ignition (to actuate 
Fuelock® and charge fuel system). 

Check for leaks at fuel supply line fitting using a soap solution.

Reinstall air cleaner assembly. 

Restart engine and check performance. Recheck coolant level.

the cam plunger and plunger spring, that are no longer retained by the cam 
assembly. 

Remove the rod retainer and the governor lever from the governor 
housing. 

Remove the four governor cover diaphragm retaining screws. Remove the 
governor cover and the diaphragm. 

[FIGURE: A18741B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: All fasteners must be finger-tightened before actually being tightened 
snug. 

Install the governor cover and diaphragm. Tighten the four retaining 
screws until snug. Use care not to cross-thread or overtighten screws. 

Install the governor lever and rod retainer into the governor housing.

Position the plunger spring, cam plunger and fast idle cam in the 
governor assembly. 

Install the governor housing seal and governor housing to the main 
body. Tighten the three retaining screws until snug. 

Install the governor lever, washer and retaining nut. Tighten the nut 
until snug. 

Connect the governor vacuum hose to the vacuum nipple. 

Position the governor spring and install the gasket and governor 
housing cover. 

Install the felt seal, lockwasher and fast idle control lever. Tighten 
nut until snug. 

Make sure the servo cable is not kinked, bent or twisted. 

Reattach lever linkage. 

Reconnect servo electric connector. 

Install air cleaner assembly.

Section 03D-04B: Governor, Electronic Control, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Governor System, Electronic Controlled

The electronic governor system is comprised of a governor control 
module (GCM) and a carburetor control subsystem. 

The function of the governor control module is to limit engine speed to 
a predetermined maximum and still allow full power output upon demand close to 
governed speed. The governor mechanism on the carburetor uses vacuum to 
provide the actuating force to modulate throttles. Precise control of the 
system is achieved by regulating governor and secondary diaphragm vacuum 
levels with a solenoid valve actuated by an electronic control unit. 

 Governor Control Module (GCM) 

The GCM is a solid state device which senses engine speed from the 
ignition primary circuit (tach signal) and tailors an electrical signal which 
is transmitted to the carburetor control subsystem. The governor solenoid 
output signal from the GCM goes to the governor solenoid in the form of a 20 
Hz pulse. For every cycle (one every one-twentieth of a second) there is a 
portion of that time devoted to "on" time and the remaining portion is devoted 
to "off" time. The percentage of "on" time for the cycle is defined as duty 
cycle. Duty cycle is the means by which the GCM compensates for a wide range 
of governed engine conditions and it varies depending on engine speed. 

 WARNING: DO NOT PARK OR SERVICE A LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED VEHICLE 
NEAR ANY SOURCE OF FIRE, SUCH AS OPEN FLAME, CIGARETTES OR SMOKING MATERIALS, 
SPARKS, EXCESSIVE HEAT, WELDING, OR BODY GRINDING. AVOID PLACING THE VEHICLE 
NEAR ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT THAT DISCHARGES SPARKS THROUGH NORMAL OPERATION, FOR 
EXAMPLE, MOTORS, ELECTRICAL SWITCHES, AND RADIO TRANSMISSION EQUIPMENT. AVOID 
STORING OR SERVICING A VEHICLE OVER SEWER DRAINS, LUBRICATION PITS, SUB-FLOOR 
LEVEL ROOMS, OR OTHER LOW-LYING AREAS. IF ANY SOURCE OF FIRE OR IGNITION 
CONTACTS LPG VAPOR, A FIRE CAN RESULT. 

 WARNING: UNLESS NECESSARY, DO NOT RELEASE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) DURING 
SERVICE, AND DO NOT OPEN THE STOP-FILL VALVE WHILE A VEHICLE IS INSIDE A 
BUILDING. WHEN SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM, SHUT OFF THE LPG FUEL TANK AND RUN 
THE ENGINE OUT OF FUEL BEFORE DISCONNECTING FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENTS. IF THE LPG 
FUEL TANK IS BEING SERVICED, HAVE THE FUEL EVACUATED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL AT A 
LOCAL LPG FUEL STATION. LPG VAPORIZES AT NORMAL BAROMETRIC PRESSURE AT 
TEMPERATURES ABOVE -42°C (-44°F), AND CAN EXPAND TO APPROXIMATELY 270 
TIMES ITS VOLUME AS A LIQUID. UNNECESSARY VENTING OF LPG FUEL CREATES FIRE AND 
HEALTH HAZARDS THAT CAN LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY OR ILLNESS. 

 WARNING: LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL TANKS MUST BE DRAINED BY TRAINED 
PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO USE SHOP AIR PRESSURE TO FORCE LPG FUEL FROM 
THE TANKS. NORMAL FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1724 KPA (160 PSI) AT 
ROOM TEMPERATURE. CONNECTING A SHOP AIR HOSE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM COULD RESULT 
IN FUEL FLOWING BACK INTO THE SERVICE AIR SYSTEM, AND RESULT IN FIRE OR 
EXPLOSION. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE PAINT DRYING OVENS FOR LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED 
VEHICLES. THE HEAT OF PAINT DRYING OVENS WILL INCREASE PRESSURE IN THE FUEL 
TANKS. THIS CAN CAUSE VENTING OF THE LPG FUEL VAPOR INTO THE OVEN RESULTING IN 
FIRE FROM HEAT OR SPARK IN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. IF LPG FUEL IS CONFINED IN AN 
OVEN, THERE IS ALSO A RISK OF EXPLOSION IF THE FUEL IS IGNITED. WHEN 
REFINISHING THE BODY PANELS OF LPG-FUELED VEHICLES, SPOT PAINT THE AFFECTED 
AREA AND USE SPOT DRYING METHODS. 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY THE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) ENGINE FUEL SYSTEM 
CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS, OR REPLACE COMPONENTS WITH PARTS THAT DO NOT MEET 
FORD SPECIFICATIONS. FORD SPECIFIED PARTS ARE AVAILABLE AT AUTHORIZED FORD 
DEALERS. THE LPG FUEL STORAGE SYSTEM MUST CONFORM TO NATIONAL FIRE PROTECTION 
ASSOCIATION STANDARD NO. 58, AND SIMILAR CANADIAN GAS ASSOCIATION STANDARDS. 
THESE STANDARDS DEFINE THE SPECIALLY-APPROVED MATERIALS, COMPONENT 
CONSTRUCTION, AND THE SYSTEM INSTALLATION ON ALL VEHICLES, WHICH IS PRECISELY 
CALIBRATED FOR EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE USE OF DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS 
COULD PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT COULD RESULT IN FIRE, EXPLOSION 
AND PERSONAL INJURY, ENGINE DAMAGE, OR NONCOMPLIANCE TO CURRENT EMISSION 
STANDARDS. 

 WARNING: AVOID INHALING LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) OR OCCUPYING CONFINED 
AREAS CONTAINING LPG. LPG IS HEAVIER THAN AIR. THE HEAVIER GAS CAN DISPLACE OR 
"PUSH" FRESH AIR OUT OF AN AREA. IN LARGE QUANTITIES PROPANE CAN DISPLACE 
ENOUGH OXYGEN TO MAKE THE SURROUNDING AIR UNFIT TO BREATHE AND POSSIBLY CAUSE 
ILLNESS. IF A PERSON BREATHES LPG OR AIR WHICH LACKS OXYGEN DUE TO THE 
PRESENCE OF LPG, HEADACHE, DIZZINESS, AND WEAKNESS IN THE EXTREMITIES CAN 
RESULT. IN SEVERE CASES, PROLONGED EXPOSURE TO LPG-FOULED AIR CAN CAUSE 
SUFFOCATION.

IN THE EVENT OF EXPOSURE TO LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG), MOVE THE 
VICTIM IMMEDIATELY TO FRESH AIR AND CONTACT A PHYSICIAN OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY 
PERSONNEL FOR ARTIFICIAL RESPIRATION OR OTHER REQUIRED TREATMENT. 

 CAUTION: If a confined area, such as a lubrication pit, has been subject to 
liquified petroleum gas (LPG), the area must be checked for adequate oxygen 
levels by local health department personnel before being entered. Otherwise, 
illness or suffocation can result. 

 Carburetor Control System 

The purpose of the carburetor control subsystem is to convert the 
electronic signals received from the GCM to a mechanical means of holding the 
throttle at the correct position to obtain the desired engine speed for 
adequate combustion. The following component groups are used to achieve this 
function: 

governor control mechanism 

electronic governor solenoid and cover assembly 

 Governor Control Mechanism 

The primary purpose of the governor control mechanism is to convert the 
regulated governor vacuum into a throttle position that will provide the 
proper engine-governed speed. This transformation of forces is achieved by the 
following: 

throttle-to-throttle shaft clutch 

governor vacuum supply and venturi vacuum restriction 

governor diaphragm and linkage 

governor spring 

The purpose of the throttle-to-throttle shaft clutch mechanism is to 
allow the governor system to overcome the throttle position held by the 
operator during engine overspeed conditions. Governor vacuum source consists 
of a vacuum pump, vacuum reservoir, regulator and check valve.

The governor diaphragm and its associated linkage is the means by which 
a vacuum is converted into a mechanical force to close the throttle. The 
governor spring has two functions: it loads the throttle shaft against the 
throttle-to-throttle shaft clutch mechanism, and it is used as a governor 
calibration tool imposing a precise counterforce against the governor 
diaphragm during governor operations. 

[FIGURE: A19051A.gif]

 Governor Control Module Solenoid and Cover Assembly 

Within the governor solenoid and cover assembly is the governor control 
valve. 

The governor control valve is normally spring-loaded closed below 
governed speed, sealing off the vacuum source in the carburetor and at the 
same time allowing atmospheric pressure to be applied to the governor 
diaphragm. With no governor signal being developed against the governor 
diaphragm, the primary throttle plates will follow the operator's foot due to 
the force from the governor return spring.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Governor, Electronic Control

 Inspection and Verification 

Before applying the diagnostic procedures, it is important to note that 
the governor control module receives 12 volts across pins 1 and 8 of the edge 
connector. Pin 2 of the edge connector is an ignition input from the negative 
primary side of the ignition coil. Pin 5 of the edge connector is a square 
wave output to the carburetor-mounted governor solenoid. 

The following checks should be made initially in response to any 
concern about governor operation.

Check throttle linkage and carburetor throttle plates to confirm proper 
idle position (closed throttles) and proper wide open position. 

Check governor solenoid and cover assembly attachment to governor 
housing (four screws) for secure assembly. 

Check secondary operating lever and shaft assembly to make sure it is 
properly connected and operating freely. 

Check electrical connections for breaks or loose wires at 
harness-to-GCM junction and also at harness-to-carburetor pigtail junction.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Governor Servo, Electronic 

 Removal 

The governor servo assembly can be removed from the carburetor assembly 
while it is mounted on the vehicle. 

Remove air cleaner assembly for clearance. 

Disconnect servo electrical connector. 

Remove choke control lever and nut, lockwasher, and felt seal. 

Remove governor housing cover and gasket. 

Remove governor spring. 

Disconnect governor vacuum hose. 

Remove governor lever retaining nut and washer and remove governor 
lever. 

Remove the three governor housing screws. Remove the governor housing 
from the main body. Remove the governor housing seal. 

Remove the fast idle cam retainer. Carefully remove the fast idle cam. 
Remove the cam plunger and plunger spring which are no longer retained by the 
cam assembly. 

Remove the rod retainer and the governor lever from the governor 
housing. 

Remove the four governor diaphragm retaining screws. Remove the 
governor and the diaphragm.

[FIGURE: A18741B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: All fasteners must be finger-tightened before actually being tightened 
to snug. 

Install the governor and diaphragm. Tighten the four retaining screws 
until snug. Do not crossthread or overtighten screws. 

Install the governor lever and rod retainer into the governor housing.

Position the plunger spring, cam plunger and fast idle cam in the 
governor assembly. 

Install the governor housing seal and governor housing to the main body 
and tighten the three retaining screws until snug. 

Install the governor lever washer and retaining nut. Tighten the nut 
until snug. 

Connect the governor vacuum hose to the housing cover nipple. 

Position the governor spring and install the gasket and governor 
housing cover. 

Install the felt seal, lockwasher and choke control lever. Tighten nut 
until snug. 

Make sure the servo cable is not kinked, bent or twisted. 

Reattach lever linkage. 

Reconnect servo electric connector. 

Install air cleaner assembly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Belts, Accessory

F700 vehicles are equipped with Vee type of accessory drive belts. The 
belt type is selected for each engine based on performance requirements. To 
ensure maximum life, replacement belts must be of the same type as originally 
installed. These belts must be properly adjusted at all times. Loose belt(s) 
will result in slippage, which can cause a noise complaint or improper 
accessory operation (generator will not charge, etc.). Overly tight belts will 
place severe loads on accessory bearings.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Drive Belts, Accessory

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the original concern by operating the engine to duplicate the 
condition.

Inspect to determine if any of the following mechanical concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Drive belt cracking/chunking/wear

Drive belt noise or squeal

Pulley misaligned or excessive pulley runout

If the concern(s) remain after the inspection, determine the symptoms 
and proceed to the following symptom chart.

 Symptom Chart — Accessory Drive Belt Diagnosis 

 ACCESSORY DRIVE BELT DIAGNOSIS 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Excessive Noise

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE accessory if 
necessary. REPLACE belt.

Belt Squeal

Loose belt.

CHECK condition and tension of all belts. REPLACE belts or ADJUST 
tension of manually tensioned belts as necessary.

Rattle

Loose pulley or accessory.

CHECK for looseness and TIGHTEN.

Belt Chirp

Misaligned power steering pulley.

REPLACE power steering pulley.

Severe Belt Flutter

Loose belt.

CHECK belt tension and ADJUST (manually tensioned belts only) if 
necessary. CHECK condition of belt and REPLACE if necessary.

Frayed Belt

Belt not seated correctly.

REPLACE belt and VERIFY correct belt seating.

Severely misaligned pulley.

Use a straightedge to CHECK for severe angular misalignment between 
adjacent pulleys. CORRECT as necessary.

Belt too tight.

REPLACE belt.

Belt worn out.

REPLACE belt.

Severely Glazed Belt

Seized accessory.

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE if necessary. 
REPLACE belt.

Loose belt.

REPLACE belt.

Improper Accessory Operation (Power Steering or Air Conditioning 
Doesn't Work, Engine Overheats or Battery Doesn't Charge)

Loose belt.

CHECK belt for looseness or glazing and REPLACE or ADJUST tension of 
manually tensioned belts, if necessary.

Belt Jumps Off Pulley

Greatly misaligned pulleys.

CHECK for misalignment between adjacent pulleys.

Belt not seated correctly (poly-V belt).

REPLACE belt and VERIFY correct seating.

Pulley wobble.

VERIFY that no pulley wobbles during engine operation. Conditions 
causing wobble are: bent pulley, bent accessory shaft, rear face of pulley not 
seated flat against mating surface.

Excessive crankshaft end play.

REBUILD engine.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Replacement

 Air Conditioner Compressor 

 Removal 

Remove power take-off drive belts (if so equipped).

Loosen nut on air conditioner compressor mounting bracket.

Loosen jam nut on belt tensioner. Turn bolt on tensioner 
counterclockwise until drive belt is loose enough to remove from A/C compressor.

Remove drive belt from idler pulley and crankshaft pulley. Discard old 
belt.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Adjust belt tension.

Tighten jam nut on belt tensioner to 40 Nm (30 lb-ft).

Tighten nut on A/C compressor pivot bolt to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft).

 Brake Compressor/Pump/Air Injection Pump (Right Side) 

 Removal 

Remove power take-off drive belts (if so equipped) as outlined.

Remove A/C compressor drive belt, if so equipped.

Loosen pivot bolt on secondary air injection pump (right side).

Loosen jam nut on air injector pump belt tensioner. Turn bolt on 
tensioner counterclockwise until drive belt is loose enough to remove from 
vehicle.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten jam nut and pivot bolt.

 Power Steering/Alternator/Air Injection Pump (Left Side) 

 Removal 

Remove power take-off (if so equipped), air conditioner compressor, and 
brake pump belts.

Loosen pivot bolt on secondary air injection pump (right side). Loosen 
jam nut on tensioner assembly.

Loosen jam nut on air injector pump belt tensioner. Turn bolt on 
tensioner counterclockwise until drive belt is loose enough to remove from 
vehicle.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Adjust belt tension.

Tighten pivot bolt.

 Power Take-Off (PTO) 

 Removal 

Loosen mounting bolts on power take-off (PTO).

Loosen jam nut on PTO tensioner bracket.

Turn adjustment nut on tensioner counterclockwise to loosen drive 
belts. Remove drive belts.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Power take-off (PTO) uses two matched v-belts; both drive belts must be 
replaced at the same time.

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten jam nut. 

Tighten mounting bolts to 90-112 Nm (66-83 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fan and Clutch, High Mount

 Removal 

Partially drain the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Loosen clamp and remove upper radiator hose from radiator.

Remove six screws retaining radiator shroud to radiator.

 CAUTION: Clutch assembly has a left-hand thread and must be rotated clockwise 
to remove it. 

Remove fan and clutch assembly by turning clutch assembly shaft bolt 
and removing from power take-off pulley. Remove fan and clutch assembly and 
shroud from vehicle.

Remove four bolts and washers retaining fan blade to clutch assembly. 
Separate fan blade and clutch assembly.

 Installation 

Install fan blade on clutch assembly with four washers and bolts. 
Tighten bolts to 34-40 Nm (25-30 lb-ft).

Position radiator shroud, fan and clutch assembly in vehicle.

 CAUTION: Clutch assembly has a left-hand thread and must be rotated 
counterclockwise to tighten it. 

Install fan and clutch assembly on power take-off pulley by turning 
clutch assembly shaft until tight.

Install radiator shroud on radiator with six screws. Tighten screws.

Install upper radiator hose on radiator. Position and tighten clamp.

Refill cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

ADJUSTMENTS

Drive Belt Adjustment

 Power Take-Off (PTO) (If So Equipped) 

Loosen three mounting bolts and jam nut on PTO pulley and bearing 
assembly.

Turn adjustment nut clockwise or counterclockwise to achieve correct 
belt tension.

Tighten jam nut and mounting bolts.

 A/C Compressor 

Loosen nut on A/C compressor mounting bracket.

Loosen jam nut on A/C compressor belt tensioner. Turn bolt clockwise or 
counterclockwise to achieve correct belt tension.

Tighten jam nut and nut on A/C compressor mounting bracket.

 Secondary Air Injection (Right Side) and Brake Compressor/Pump 

Loosen nut on secondary air injection pump pivot mounting bolt.

Loosen jam nut on air injection pump drive belt tensioner. Turn bolt on 
tensioner clockwise to add tension or counterclockwise to decrease tension. 
Tighten jam nut on air injection pump tensioner and nut on pivot mounting bolt.

 Secondary Air Injection (Left Side), Alternator and Power Steering Pump 

Loosen pivot mounting bolt and jam nut.

Turn bolt on belt tensioner clockwise or counterclockwise to achieve 
correct belt tension.

Tighten jam nut and pivot mounting bolt.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Motor 

 WARNING: WHEN SERVICING STARTER MOTOR OR PERFORMING ANY MAINTENANCE IN THE AREA 
OF THE STARTER MOTOR, NOTE THE HEAVY GAUGE INPUT LEAD CONNECTED TO THE STARTER 
SOLENOID IS HOT AT ALL TIMES. 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Raise vehicle on a hoist.

Remove retaining bolts and starter motor shield.

 CAUTION: When disconnecting hardshell connector at starter motor solenoid 
S-terminal, grasp the plastic shell and pull off. Do not pull on wire. Be 
careful to pull straight off to prevent damage to connector and S-terminal. If 
any part of connection is damaged, replace damaged components. 

Disconnect battery cable and push-on connector from starter solenoid.

Remove starter motor retaining bolts and starter. 

 Installation 

Position starter motor on engine and install upper retaining bolt. 

Position ground cable and install lower retaining bolt.

Tighten retaining bolts to 20.3-27.0 Nm (15-20 lb-ft). 

Connect starter solenoid S-terminal wire. Be careful to push straight 
on and make sure connector locks in position with a notable click or detent. 

Install battery cable and retaining nut on solenoid B-terminal. Tighten 
nut to 9-13 Nm (80-120 lb-in). 

Position starter motor shield and install retaining bolts.

Lower vehicle. 

Connect battery ground cable.

 Disassembly 

Remove positive brush connector from solenoid motor (M) terminal. 

Remove solenoid retaining screws and starter solenoid. 

Remove through-bolts and separate drive end housing from starter frame. 
Remove housing seal assembly from drive end housing. Remove drive and gear 
assembly from drive end housing. 

Remove drive lever from drive assembly. Remove stop ring and stop ring 
retainer from shaft assembly, then remove drive assembly from shaft assembly. 
Push Truarc® E-ring off shaft assembly, and separate stationary gear 
assembly from shaft assembly. 

Remove brush plate screws and brush end plate from starter frame. 
Remove brush assembly and push armature assembly out of starter frame. 

 Assembly 

Install armature assembly in starter frame.

Apply a thin coating of Ford Teflon® Lubricant D2AZ-19590-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C111-A on both ends of armature 
shaft and spline.

Install brush assembly. Make sure brushes fit over commutator.

Apply grease to bearing bore in brush end plate.

Push back grommet onto starter frame and attach brush end plate with 
brush plate screws. Tighten to 2.3-3.4 Nm (20-30 lb-in). 

Apply grease to shaft assembly spline and place stationary gear 
assembly over shaft assembly.

Install armature thrust washer and push Truarc® E-ring onto 
shaft assembly.

Place drive assembly onto shaft assembly and install stop ring and stop 
ring retainer.

Attach drive lever to drive assembly. 

Grease and install planet gears. 

Apply grease to drive end housing bushing bearing bore (approximately 
one-quarter full).

Install drive gear assembly into drive end housing, making sure to line 
up bolt holes in drive gear assembly and drive end housing.

 Place gear retainer over drive gear assembly.

Install housing seal assembly into drive end housing. 

Position starter frame to drive end housing and install through-bolts. 
Tighten to 5.0-9.5 Nm (45-84 lb-in). 

Correctly position starter solenoid to drive end housing. Make sure 
that solenoid plunger is attached through drive lever (bottom solenoid 
terminal (M) should have a metal strip attached to it). Tighten starter 
solenoid bolts to 5.1-9.6 Nm (45-85 lb-in). 

Attach positive brush connector to starter solenoid (bottom terminal). 
Tighten nut to 9-13 Nm (80-120 lb-in). 

Check that starter motor no-load current draw is within specification. 
Refer to Section 03-06 .

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Drive Replacement 

Remove positive brush connector from solenoid motor (M) terminal. 
Remove solenoid retaining screws and remove starter solenoid. 

Remove through-bolts and separate drive end housing from starter frame. 

Remove housing seal assembly from drive end housing.

Remove drive gear assembly from drive end housing and detach drive 
lever.

remove drive assembly.

equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C111-A on shaft assembly spline.

Install new drive assembly on shaft assembly. Install new stop ring and 
stop ring retainer. Attach drive lever. 

Partially fill drive end housing bushing bearing bore with grease 
(approximately one-quarter full). Install drive gear assembly in drive end 
housing, making sure to line up bolt holes in drive gear assembly and drive 
end housing. 

Install housing seal assembly in drive end housing. 

Position starter frame to drive end housing and install through-bolts. 
Tighten to 5.0-9.5 Nm (45-84 lb-in). 

Install starter solenoid. Refer to Starter Motor, Assembly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition System

The 7.0L LPG engine is equipped with a Duraspark II ignition system.

The Duraspark II ignition includes a primary and a secondary circuit. 

The primary circuit consists of the following: 

battery 

ignition switch 

ballast resistor — start bypass (wires) 

ignition coil primary winding 

ignition control module 

distributor stator assembly 

The secondary circuit consists of the following: 

ignition coil secondary winding 

distributor rotor 

distributor cap 

ignition wires 

spark plugs 

Vacuum and centrifugal advance are used to vary spark timing according 
to changes in engine load and speed.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition Coil

With the key in RUN, primary circuit current flows from the battery, 
through the ignition switch, the ballast resistor, the ignition coil primary 
(BAT-TACH), the ignition control module (green wire), and back to the battery 
through the ignition system ground in the distributor (black wire). This 
current flow causes a magnetic field to be built up in the ignition coil. When 
the poles on the armature and stator assembly align, the ignition control 
module turns the primary circuit off, collapsing the magnetic field in the 
ignition coil. The collapsing field induces a high voltage in the ignition 
coil secondary winding. The ignition coil wire conducts the high voltage to 
the distributor where the cap and rotor distribute it to the appropriate spark 
plug. 

A timing circuit in the ignition control module turns the primary 
current back on after a short period of time. High voltage is produced each 
time the magnetic field is built up and collapsed. 

The red ignition control module wire provides operating voltage for the 
ignition control module's electronic components in RUN mode. The white wire 
provides voltage for the ignition control module during START mode. START 
BYPASS provides increased voltage for the ignition coil during START mode.

PAGE 4398
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-07: Ignition, Distributor, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition Control Module

The ignition control module controls the current through the ignition 
coil primary winding. The module turns on the current between firing points to 
build up a magnetic field around the coil windings. It then turns the current 
off on a signal from the stator assembly pickup coil.

================================================================================
PAGE 4399
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-07: Ignition, Distributor, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Distributor 

The distributor provides a signal to the ignition control module. This 
signal is generated as the armature, attached to the distributor shaft, 
rotates past the stator assembly. The rotating armature causes fluctuations in 
a magnetic field produced by the stator assembly magnet. These fluctuations 
induce a voltage in the stator assembly pickup coil. This signal is directed 
to the ignition module by the vehicle wiring harness. 

 Distributor Identification 

The distributor assembly can be identified through the part number 
information stamped on a metal tag attached to the distributor by a vacuum 
advance assembly attaching screw. 

[FIGURE: B4088E.gif]

 Centrifugal Spark Advance Mechanism 

The centrifugal advance mechanism varies the relationship of the 
armature to the stator assembly. The sleeve and plate assembly, on which the 
armature is mounted, rotates in relation to the distributor shaft. This 
rotation is caused by centrifugal weights moving in response to engine rpm. 
The movement of the centrifugal weights changes the initial relationship of 
the armature to the stator assembly by rotating the sleeve and plate assembly 
ahead of its static position on the distributor shaft. This results in spark 
advance. The rate of movement of the centrifugal weights is controlled by 
calibrated springs. 

 Vacuum Spark Advance Mechanism 

A single diaphragm assembly is used to obtain vacuum spark advance. The 
single diaphragm assembly also varies the armature-to-stator relationship to 
provide spark advance. In this case, the stator assembly position is changed 
by means of vacuum applied to the diaphragm assembly. Vacuum applied to the 
diaphragm assembly causes the diaphragm and attached diaphragm rod to move, 
compressing the advance spring. This movement of the diaphragm rod, which is 
attached to the stator assembly, causes the stator assembly to move with 
respect to the armature. This changes the initial armature-to-stator assembly 
relationship established during initial timing set, causing spark advance. The 
stator assembly is mounted on the lower plate assembly which, along with the 
diaphragm assembly, is attached to the distributor base. 

[FIGURE: B42261A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Service Precautions

Before servicing any Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) engine, please note 
the following warnings. 

 WARNING: DO NOT PARK OR SERVICE A LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED VEHICLE 
NEAR ANY SOURCE OF FIRE, SUCH AS OPEN FLAME, CIGARETTES OR SMOKING MATERIALS, 
SPARKS, EXCESSIVE HEAT, WELDING, OR BODY GRINDING. AVOID PLACING THE VEHICLE 
NEAR ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT THAT DISCHARGES SPARKS THROUGH NORMAL OPERATION, FOR 
EXAMPLE, MOTORS, ELECTRICAL SWITCHES, AND RADIO TRANSMISSION EQUIPMENT. AVOID 
STORING OR SERVICING A VEHICLE OVER SEWER DRAINS, LUBRICATION PITS, SUB-FLOOR 
LEVEL ROOMS, OR OTHER LOW-LYING AREAS. IF ANY SOURCE OF FIRE OR IGNITION 
CONTACTS (LPG) VAPOR, A FIRE COULD RESULT. 

 WARNING: DO NOT NEEDLESSLY RELEASE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) DURING SERVICE, 
AND DO NOT OPEN THE STOP-FILL VALVE WHILE A VEHICLE IS INSIDE A BUILDING. WHEN 
SERVICING THE LPG FUEL SYSTEM, SHUT OFF THE LPG FUEL TANK AND RUN THE ENGINE 
OUT OF FUEL BEFORE DISCONNECTING FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENTS. IF THE LPG FUEL TANK 
IS BEING SERVICED, HAVE THE FUEL EVACUATED BY TRAINED PERSONNEL AT A LOCAL LPG 
FUEL STATION. LPG VAPORIZES AT NORMAL BAROMETRIC PRESSURE AT TEMPERATURES 
ABOVE -42°C (-44°F), AND CAN EXPAND TO APPROXIMATELY 270 TIMES ITS 
VOLUME AS A LIQUID. UNNECESSARY VENTING OF LPG FUEL CAN CREATE FIRES AND 
HEALTH HAZARDS WHICH CAN LEAD TO PERSONAL INJURY OR ILLNESS. 

 WARNING: LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) FUEL TANKS MUST BE DRAINED BY TRAINED 
PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO USE SHOP AIR PRESSURE TO FORCE LPG FUEL FROM 
THE TANKS. NORMAL FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1724 KPA (160 PSI) AT 
ROOM TEMPERATURE. CONNECTING A SHOP AIR HOSE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM COULD RESULT 
IN FUEL FLOWING BACK INTO THE SERVICE AIR SYSTEM, AND RESULT IN FIRE OR 
EXPLOSION. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE PAINT DRYING OVENS FOR LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)-FUELED 
VEHICLES. THE HEAT OF PAINT DRYING OVENS WILL INCREASE PRESSURE IN THE FUEL 
TANKS. THIS CAN CAUSE VENTING OF THE LPG FUEL VAPOR INTO THE OVEN, RESULTING 
IN FIRE FROM HEAT OR SPARK IN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. IF FUEL IS CONFINED IN AN 
OVEN, THERE IS ALSO A RISK OF EXPLOSION IF THE FUEL IS IGNITED. WHEN 
REFINISHING THE BODY PANELS OF LPG-FUELED VEHICLES, SPOT PAINT THE AFFECTED 
AREA AND USE SPOT DRYING METHODS. 

 WARNING: DO NOT MODIFY THE LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) ENGINE FUEL SYSTEM 
CONFIGURATION OR COMPONENTS, OR REPLACE COMPONENTS WITH PARTS THAT DO NOT MEET 
FORD SPECIFICATIONS. FORD SPECIFIED PARTS ARE AVAILABLE AT AUTHORIZED FORD 
DEALERS. THE LPG FUEL STORAGE SYSTEM MUST CONFORM TO NATIONAL FIRE PROTECTION 
ASSOCIATION STANDARD NO. 58, AND SIMILAR CANADIAN GAS ASSOCIATION STANDARDS. 
THESE STANDARDS DEFINE THE SPECIALLY-APPROVED MATERIALS, COMPONENT 
CONSTRUCTION, AND THE SYSTEM INSTALLED ON ALL VEHICLES, WHICH IS PRECISELY 
CALIBRATED FOR EFFICIENT OPERATION. THE USE OF DIFFERENT PARTS OR MATERIALS 
CAN PRODUCE AN UNTESTED CONFIGURATION THAT CAN RESULT IN FIRE, EXPLOSION AND 
PERSONAL INJURY, ENGINE DAMAGE, OR NONCOMPLIANCE TO CURRENT EMISSION 
STANDARDS. 

 WARNING: AVOID INHALING LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) OR OCCUPYING CONFINED 
AREAS CONTAINING LPG. LPG IS HEAVIER THAN AIR. THE HEAVIER GAS CAN DISPLACE OR 
"PUSH" FRESH AIR OUT OF AN AREA. IN LARGE QUANTITIES LPG CAN DISPLACE ENOUGH 
OXYGEN TO MAKE THE SURROUNDING AIR UNFIT TO BREATH, AND POSSIBLY CAUSE 
ILLNESS. IF A PERSON BREATHES LPG OR AIR THAT LACKS OXYGEN DUE TO THE PRESENCE 
OF LPG, HEADACHE, DIZZINESS, AND WEAKNESS IN THE EXTREMITIES CAN RESULT. IN 
SEVERE CASES, PROLONGED EXPOSURE CAN CAUSE SUFFOCATION. 

 WARNING: IN THE EVENT OF EXPOSURE TO LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG), MOVE THE 
VICTIM IMMEDIATELY TO FRESH AIR AND CONTACT A PHYSICIAN OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY 
PERSONNEL FOR ARTIFICIAL RESPIRATION OR OTHER REQUIRED TREATMENT. 

 WARNING: IF A CONFINED AREA, SUCH AS A LUBRICATION PIT, HAS BEEN SUBJECT TO 
LIQUIFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG), THE AREA SHOULD BE CHECKED FOR ADEQUATE OXYGEN 
LEVELS BY LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL BEFORE BEING ENTERED. OTHERWISE, 
ILLNESS OR SUFFOCATION CAN RESULT.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Distributor 

 Removal 

Remove distributor cap and adapter. Position cap and ignition wires to 
one side. 

Disconnect and plug diaphragm assembly hose. 

Separate distributor connector from wiring harness. 

Rotate engine to align stator assembly pole and any armature pole. 

[FIGURE: B35091B.gif]

Scribe a mark on distributor body and engine block to indicate position 
of distributor in engine, and position of rotor. 

Remove distributor hold-down bolt and clamp. 

Remove distributor from engine. Do not rotate engine while distributor 
is removed. 

 Installation 

If engine was rotated while distributor was removed, proceed as follows: 

Rotate engine until number 1 piston is on compression stroke. 

Align timing marks for correct initial timing. 

Install distributor with rotor pointing at number 1 terminal position 
in cap, and armature and stator assembly poles aligned. 

Make sure oil pump intermediate shaft engages distributor shaft 
properly. If necessary, crank engine after distributor gear is partially 
engaged in order to engage oil pump intermediate shaft and fully seat 
distributor in block. 

If it was necessary to crank engine, again rotate engine until number 1 
piston is on compression stroke and align timing marks for correct initial 
timing. 

Rotate distributor in block to align armature and stator assembly pole. 
Verify rotor is pointing at number 1 cap terminal. 

Install distributor hold-down bolt and clamp. Do not tighten at this 
time. 

If engine was not rotated while distributor was removed and original 
distributor is being installed, proceed as follows: 

Position distributor in engine with rotor and distributor aligning with 
previously scribed mark. Armature and stator assembly poles should also align 
if distributor is fully seated in block and properly installed. Crank engine, 
if necessary, to fully seat distributor in block. 

Install distributor hold-down bolt and clamp. Do not tighten at this 
time. 

If engine was not rotated while distributor was removed and new 
distributor is being installed, proceed as follows: 

Rotate engine until number 1 piston is on compression stroke.

Align timing marks for correct initial timing.

Install distributor with rotor pointing at number 1 terminal position 
in cap, and armature and stator assembly poles aligned.

Make sure oil pump intermediate shaft engages distributor shaft 
properly. If necessary, crank engine after distributor gear is partially 
engaged in order to engage oil pump intermediate shaft and fully seat 
distributor in block.

If it was necessary to crank engine, again rotate engine until number 1 
piston is on compression stroke and align timing marks for correct initial 
timing.

Rotate distributor in block to align armature and stator assembly pole. 
Verify rotor is pointing at number 1 cap terminal.

Install distributor hold-down bolt and clamp. Do not tighten at this 
time.

If, in Steps 1 and 2 above, the armature and stator assembly poles 
cannot be aligned by rotating distributor in block, pull distributor out of 
block enough to disengage distributor gear and rotate distributor shaft to 
engage a different distributor gear tooth and reinstall distributor. Repeat 
Steps 1, 2 and 3 as necessary. 

Connect distributor to wiring harness. 

Install distributor adapter, cap and ignition wires. Check that 
ignition wires are securely connected to distributor cap and spark plugs. 

Set initial timing per specification on Vehicle Emission Control 
Information Decal. 

Tighten distributor hold-down bolt to 23-34 Nm (17-25 lb-ft). 

Check initial timing. Refer to Vehicle Emission Control Information 
Decal and Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual(Can be 
purchased as a separate item.) or Technical Service Bulletin Special 
Specification Issue for Distributors.

Connect diaphragm assembly hose.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bracket, Ignition Coil

 Removal 

Disconnect wiring connector and ignition coil wire at ignition coil.

Loosen ignition coil to bracket retaining screw and remove ignition coil.

Remove ignition coil bracket retaining screws and remove bracket.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Whenever an ignition wire is removed from a spark plug, ignition coil 
or distributor cap terminal, silicone compound must be applied to the spark 
plug wire boot before it is reconnected. Using a small, clean tool, lightly 
coat the entire inner surface of the boot with Silicone Dielectric Compound 
D7AZ-19A331-A (Motorcraft WA-10) or equivalent meeting Ford specification

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Ignition Wires 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spark Plug Wire Remover

T74P-6666-A

The ignition wires include the spark plug wires connecting the 
distributor cap to the spark plugs and the ignition coil wire connecting the 
distributor cap to the high voltage terminal of the ignition coil. 

These wires are designed to reduce radio interference caused by high 
voltage discharges in the ignition system. 

Do not, under any circumstances, puncture an ignition wire with any 
type of probing device. 

 Removal 

Using Spark Plug Wire Remover T74P-6666-A, grasp and twist the spark 
plug wire boot back and forth.

Pull the boot off the plug. Do not pull directly on the spark plug 
wire. It can separate from its terminal inside the spark plug wire boot. 

[FIGURE: B3496E.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Whenever an ignition wire is removed from a spark plug, ignition coil 
or distributor cap terminal, silicone compound must be applied to the spark 
plug wire boot before it is reconnected. Using a small, clean tool, lightly 
coat the entire inner surface of the boot with Silicone Dielectric Compound 
D7AZ-19A331-A (Motorcraft WA-10) or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESE-M1C171-A. 

Attach each wire to proper terminal of distributor cap. Be certain 
wires are fully seated on terminals. 

Remove wire separators from old wire set and install them on new set in 
approximately same position. 

Connect wires to proper spark plugs. Install ignition coil wire. Be 
certain all wires are fully seated on terminals.

================================================================================
PAGE 4410
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-07: Ignition, Distributor, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spark Plugs 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spark Plug Wire Remover

T74P-6666-A

 Removal 

Remove spark plug wire from spark plug using Spark Plug Wire Remover 
Tool T74P-6666-A with a twisting-pulling motion. Do not pull directly on spark 
plug wire. 

Inspect spark plug wires for physical damage. Replace as necessary. 

Remove foreign debris around each spark plug port with compressed air.

Remove spark plug. 

 Installation 

Set spark plug gap to 0.711-0.813 mm (0.028-0.032 inch).

Install spark plug and tighten to 9-20 Nm (7-15 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Whenever an ignition wire is removed from a spark plug, ignition coil 
or distributor cap terminal, silicone compound must be applied to the spark 
plug wire boot before it is reconnected. Using a small, clean tool, lightly 
coat the entire inner surface of the boot with Silicone Dielectric Compound 
D7AZ-19A331-A (Motorcraft WA-10) or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESE-M1C171-A. 

Coat the inside of the spark plug wire boot with silicone compound and 
install on spark plug.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Ballast Resistor

The ignition ballast resistor is actually a specific length of special 
wire. It is used to limit the primary ignition circuit current in the RUN 
mode. It is part of the vehicle wiring harness inside the passenger 
compartment. Under no circumstances should it be cut, spliced or replaced by 
any other type of non-resistance wire.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Diaphragm

 Removal 

Remove distributor cap, rotor and adapter. 

Disconnect diaphragm assembly vacuum hose. 

Remove E-clip securing diaphragm rod to stator assembly pin. Lift 
diaphragm rod off stator assembly. 

Remove two diaphragm and identification tag screws. 

Remove diaphragm assembly from distributor base. 

 Installation 

Adjust new diaphragm assembly following manufacturer's instructions. 

Install diaphragm assembly and identification tag on distributor base 
and tighten to a minimum of 1.7 Nm (15 lb-in). 

Place diaphragm rod on stator assembly pin and install E-clip. 

Connect vacuum hose. 

Install adapter, rotor and cap.

Section 03D-12: Air Intake System, 7.0L LPG Engine

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Induction System

The air induction system supplies clean air to the carburetor assembly. 
Outside air enters the tube assembly mounted to the radiator support, and 
flows through the engine air cleaner intake duct and into the engine air 
cleaner. From there, the air is filtered through the air filter element and 
then travels through the outlet tube and into the carburetor assembly.

================================================================================
PAGE 4426
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-12: Air Intake System, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Cleaner Element

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a 
clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering the engine. 

The air cleaner element is a dry-type, chemically treated and pleated 
paper air filtering element that permits airflow through the air induction 
system, while filtering out unwanted dust, dirt and debris.

================================================================================
PAGE 4427
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-12: Air Intake System, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Restriction Indicator

Some air cleaners are equipped with a direct-mounted air restriction 
indicator (mounted to the cover of the air cleaner) that indicates when the 
air cleaner needs servicing. When the yellow diaphragm reaches the red marker 
of the restriction gauge/indicator, the air cleaner needs servicing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a 
clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering the engine. 

Loosen latches or remove wing nut. 

Remove air cleaner housing cover. 

Remove wing nut retaining the air cleaner element to the air cleaner 
housing. 

Remove the air cleaner element gently to reduce the amount of dust 
dislodged. There will be some initial resistance, similar to breaking the seal 
on a jar. Gently move the end of the air cleaner element up and down and side 
to side or twist to break the seal.

[FIGURE: V8451A.gif]

Avoid dislodging dust from the air cleaner element. Gently pull the air 
cleaner element out of the air cleaner housing. Avoid knocking the air cleaner 
element against the air cleaner housing.

[FIGURE: V8452A.gif]

 Installation 

Before installing a new air cleaner element in the housing air cleaner, 
make sure the following conditions exist: 

gasket surfaces clean and undamaged 

air cleaner housing outlet tube clean and undamaged 

air cleaner element dry and free of holes, ruptures, damaged gaskets or 
dents in end covers and liners 

air cleaner element retaining nut or bolt has the gasket washer 
attached and in good condition. 

Install the air cleaner element in the air cleaner housing and tighten 
the wing nut. Make sure the rubber face of the washer seals against the air 
cleaner element. 

Install the air cleaner housing cover onto the air cleaner housing. 

Tighten wing nut or secure latches.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Inlet Restriction Check 

The best method for determining dry-type air cleaner maintenance 
periods is by checking the air restriction indicator, if so equipped. A visual 
inspection of the air cleaner element will not ascertain the need for service. 
The air cleaner element should be serviced at regularly scheduled maintenance 
intervals.

[FIGURE: DV0675A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4434
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-12: Air Intake System, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Cleaner Element 

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a 
clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering the engine. 

Inspect the air cleaner element for indications of air leaks that can 
allow unfiltered air to enter the engine. Check for dust streaks that may 
indicate a poor seal with the air cleaner housing. Always replace a restricted 
air cleaner element. Do not attempt to clean air cleaner elements.

================================================================================
PAGE 4435
================================================================================
1999 F and B-Series

Section 03D-12: Air Intake System, 7.0L LPG Engine

1999 F700 Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Engine Air Cleaner Housing

 CAUTION: If the air cleaner element or air cleaner housing is removed, use a 
clean shop rag to prevent contaminants from entering the engine. 

Always clean the sealing surface of the air cleaner housing outlet 
tube. Dust on the outer diameter of the air cleaner housing outlet tube can 
hinder an effective seal and cause leakage. Make sure all contaminants are 
removed before the new air cleaner element is inserted. 

[FIGURE: V8453A.gif]

Always clean the inside of the air cleaner housing outlet tube 
carefully. Dirt accidentally transferred to the inside of the air cleaner 
housing outlet tube will reach the engine and cause wear. Use care not to 
damage the air cleaner element sealing area on the air cleaner housing outlet 
tube. 

[FIGURE: V8454A.gif]

Check the old air cleaner element. It can aid in the detection of 
foreign material on the sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of 
dust on the clean air side of the air cleaner element seal is the tell-tale 
sign. If dust exists, make sure the cause is removed before installing a new 
air cleaner element. 

[FIGURE: V8455A.gif]

Inspect the new air cleaner element for damage. Always look for 
possible shipping or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside 
of the open end (the sealing area). Check for cuts, etc. Do not use a damaged 
air cleaner element.

[FIGURE: V8456A.gif]

After the air cleaner element and other parts are found to be in good 
condition, assemble the parts. Install the air cleaner element and tighten the 
wing nut (if so equipped). Make sure the rubber face of washer seals against 
the air cleaner element. Install the air cleaner housing cover and air cleaner 
element into the air cleaner housing. Tighten wing nut or secure latches.

Check connections and ducts for air-tight fit. Make sure all clamps, 
flange connections and air cleaner mounting bolts are tight. Seal any leaks in 
the clean air ducting immediately — they permit dirt to enter the engine 
directly. All ducts, from air cleaner housing to engine, must be tight.
