the 1998 F and B Body, Chassis Service Manual.

Remove the LH and RH front bumper brackets. For additional information, 
refer to Section 01-19 in the 1998 F and B Body, Chassis Service Manual.

Drain the engine cooling system. For additional information, refer to 
 Section 03-03 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Drain the engine oil.

If the vehicle is equipped with an A/C system, recover the refrigerant. 
For additional information, refer to Section 12-00 in the 1998 F and B Body, 
Chassis Service Manual.

Remove the cooling module. For additional information, refer to Cooling 
Module in this section.

If the vehicle is equipped with a transmission cooler, drain the 
transmission oil. For additional information, refer to Section 07-01A in the 
1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

If the vehicle is equipped with air brakes, drain the air system.

If the vehicle is equipped with hydraulic brakes, drain the brake pump 
and brake pump reservoir portion of the brake system.

Remove the steering gear. For additional information, refer to Section 11-02A in the 1998 F and B Body, Chassis Service Manual.

Disconnect the power steering supply hose from the power steering pump.

Remove two nuts, power steering cooler and power steering reservoir as 
an assembly.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with a transmission oil cooler, perform this 
step.

Loosen the radiator lower tube clamp. Disconnect the transmission 
cooler lines. Remove nuts, washers, bolts and the transmission oil cooler.

Remove bolts, washers, nuts and number one crossmember.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with hydraulic brakes, perform this step.

Disconnect the brake hoses from the brake pump and brake pump reservoir.

Remove nut, washers, bolts and radiator brace rod.

Remove the turbocharger inlet tube and engine air cleaner housing as an 
assembly. For additional information, refer to Section 03A-12 in the 1998 F 
and B Powertrain, Service Manual.

Remove heater hose bracket bolt. Disconnect heater water hose from the 
radiator lower tube and position aside.

Remove the radiator lower tube.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an A/C system, perform this step.

Disconnect the suction line at the suction accumulator/drier. Discard 
the captured O-ring seal.

Disconnect the heater water hose from the coolant fitting and position 
aside.

Label and disconnect the generator and engine coolant temperature (ECT) 
sensor electrical connectors.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an A/C system, perform this step.

Disconnect the A/C compressor electrical connector.

Remove engine wiring harness retaining clamp nuts from the valve cover. 
Position the engine wiring harness aside.

Remove the exhaust clamp. Disconnect the exhaust system from the 
turbocharger.

Label and disconnect the intake air heating grid electrical leads.

Disconnect the engine oil pressure (EOP) gauge line at the EOP sensor.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an air brake system, perform this step.

Disconnect the air compressor discharge line and governor air lines. 
Position them aside.

Disconnect the engine control module (ECM), water in fuel sensor, fuel 
pressure sensor, 16 Pin, and two inline electrical connectors.

[FIGURE: DA1840A.gif]

Disconnect the fuel heater electrical connector.

Label and disconnect the starter motor electrical leads.

Disconnect the fuel lines at the fuel tank.

Remove the exhaust system.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with a manual transmission, perform Steps 25 
through 27.

Remove the gearshift assembly. Remove the screws and separate the shift 
lever boot from the floor. Remove the interior trim as required. Remove the 
transmission floor cover plate if additional access space is required.

Remove the capscrews. Position the shift lever assembly aside. Remove 
the shift lever assembly. Cover the hole in the shift control housing to 
prevent contamination. For additional information, refer to the appropriate 
Group 07 transmission section in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain 
Service Manual.

Disconnect the clutch linkage at the transmission. For additional 
information, refer to Section 08-02 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain 
Service Manual.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an AT-series automatic transmission, 
perform this step.

Disconnect the selector control cable at the transmission. For 
additional information, refer to Section 07-01A in the 1998 F and B 
Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with a transmission cooler, perform this step.

Disconnect transmission oil cooler lines. Remove all of the 
transmission oil cooler line retaining clamps from the transmission.

Label and disconnect the transmission electrical connectors.

Remove the battery ground cable retaining bolt and battery positive 
cable retaining clamp bolt from the flywheel housing. Position the battery 
cables aside.

[FIGURE: DA1841A.gif]

Disconnect the tachometer sensor electrical connector.

[FIGURE: DA1842A.gif]

Disconnect the driveshaft. For additional information, refer to Section 05-01 in the F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Remove bolts, washers, nuts and the rear engine support caps.

Support the powertrain assembly.

Install the engine lifting equipment. Use a suitable lifting chain 
connected to the front lifting eye and a lifting crane rated at minimum 
6000-lb capacity by manufacturer.

Position a suitable transmission jack under the transmission. Secure 
the transmission to the jack.

Remove two upper bolts from front engine support.

Remove the nuts, washers and bolts from the top of LH and RH front 
spring hangers. For additional information, refer to Section 04-01 in the 1998 
F and B Body, Chassis Service Manual.

Remove the bolts, washers, nuts and the number two crossmember.

Move the powertrain assembly forward until the transmission jack 
reaches the front axle.

Lower the engine and support the front engine mount. Use two suitable 
jack stands rated at a minimum 6,000-capacity by the manufacturer and a 
suitable length of wood with a minimum 4-inch x 6-inch dimension.

Remove the powertrain assembly from the vehicle.

Remove the lifting chain. Install a load leveling sling. Use a suitable 
load leveling sling rated a minimum 6,000-lb capacity by the manufacturer.

Raise the engine.

Remove the strap from the transmission.

Level the powertrain assembly.

Remove the transmission jack.

Move the powertrain assembly out of the vehicle.

Support the powertrain assembly. Use suitable jack stands rated at a 
minimum 6,000-lb capacity by the manufacturer and a suitable transmission jack.

 Installation 

Raise the powertrain assembly and remove the jack stands and the 
transmission jack. Use a suitable load leveling sling and lifting crane rated 
at a minimum 6000-lb capacity by manufacturer.

 CAUTION: Use care not to damage any engine components, lines, filters, and 
electrical wiring during the installation of the powertrain assembly. 

Move the powertrain assembly into the vehicle until the transmission is 
behind the front axle.

Support the powertrain assembly.

Install a suitable transmission jack under the transmission. Secure the 
transmission to the jack.

Lower the engine and support the front engine mount. Use two suitable 
jack stands rated at a minimum 6000-lb capacity by the manufacturer and a 
suitable length of wood with a minimum 4-inch x 6-inch dimension.

Remove the load leveling sling and connect a suitable lifting chain 
rated at a minimum 6000-lb capacity by the manufacturer to the front lifting 
eye.

Move the powertrain assembly rearward until aligned with engine mount 
insulators.

Install the number two crossmember, bolts, washers and nuts.

Install bolts, washers and nuts to the top of the LH and RH front 
spring hangers. For additional information, refer to Section 04-01 in the 1998 
F and B Body, Chassis Service Manual.

Install two upper bolts in the front engine support.

Install the two rear engine support caps, bolts, washers and nuts.

Connect the driveshaft. For additional information, refer to Section 05-01 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Connect the tachometer electrical connector.

[FIGURE: DA1842A.gif]

Route the battery cables. Install the battery ground cable retaining 
bolt and battery positive cable retaining clamp bolt in the flywheel housing.

[FIGURE: DA1841A.gif]

Connect the transmission electrical connectors as noted during removal.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with a transmission cooler, perform this step.

Route and connect the transmission oil cooler lines. Install all of the 
transmission oil cooler line retaining clamps as noted during removal.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an AT-series automatic transmission, 
perform this step.

Connect the selector cable to the transmission. For additional 
information, refer to Section 07-01A in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, 
Drivetrain Service Manual.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with a manual transmission, perform Steps 16 
through 21.

Connect the clutch linkage. For additional information, refer to 
 Section 08-02 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Align the shift block and yoke notches in the neutral position.

Position the gasket

1999 F800 Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Engine — B5.9 Encore (ISB)

 Disassembly 

Separate the engine from the transmission. For additional information, 
refer to the appropriate Group 07 transmission section in the 1998 F and B 
Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with a manual transmission, perform this step.

Remove the clutch. For additional information, refer to Section 08-01 
in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Remove the tachometer sensor.

[FIGURE: DA1843A.gif]

Remove the fuel lines, fitting, and check valve. Before removing, note 
the flow direction of the check valve.

Remove the bolt and air cleaner brace from the air intake duct.

Remove the bolt and battery cable bracket from the flywheel housing.

Remove the bolts and starter motor.

Remove bolt, nut and engine oil dipstick tube.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with hydraulic brakes, perform this step.

Remove two nuts and power steering pump. Discard the power steering 
pump gasket.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with air brakes, perform steps 10 through 13.

Label and disconnect the air compressor coolant lines at the engine. 
Remove the fittings.

Disconnect the air compressor oil supply line from the air compressor. 
Disconnect the air compressor oil return line from the oil pan. Remove the 
fitting. Remove two bolts and nuts. Remove the air compressor and power 
steering pump as an assembly. Discard the air compressor gasket.

Remove the air compressor oil supply line and fitting from the engine.

Remove two bolts and air compressor mounting block.

Loosen the hose clamp. Remove bolt, washer, nut and engine oil fill tube.

Remove nuts, washers and engine oil fill tube bracket.

Remove the accessory drive belts.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with hydraulic brakes, perform this step.

Remove the three bolts and brake pump assembly.

Remove the cooling fan and hub. For additional information, refer to 
 Section 03E-03 .

Remove the nut, flatwasher, lockwasher, bolts and generator. Discard 
the lockwasher.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an A/C system, perform this step.

Remove bolts, washers and A/C compressor.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is not equipped with an A/C system, perform this step.

Remove bolts and idler pulley.

Remove the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor and fitting.

Disconnect the engine oil pressure (EOP) gauge line. Remove the 
fitting. Remove two bolts and the exhaust manifold heat shield, air cleaner 
mounting bracket and EOP gauge line as an assembly.

[FIGURE: DA1844A.gif]

Remove the engine coolant supply and overflow hose.

Remove the heater water hose fittings.

Remove the turbocharger inlet duct.

Remove bolt and transmission oil dipstick tube bracket.

Raise the engine off of the jack stands. Remove the bolts, washers and 
the front engine mount. Remove the bolts, washers and the two rear engine 
mounts.

Place the engine on a suitable engine stand or in a suitable engine 
shipping container.

 Assembly 

Remove the engine from the engine stand or shipping container. Use a 
suitable lifting crane rated at a minimum 6,000-lb capacity by the manufacturer.

Install the front engine mount, washers and bolts. Install the two rear 
engine mounts, washers and bolts. Tighten the bolts to 203-277 Nm 
(150-205 lb-ft).

Lower and support the engine. Use suitable jack stands rated at a 
minimum 6,000-lb capacity by the manufacturer.

Install the transmission oil dipstick tube bracket and bolt.

Apply Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A to the fitting 
threads. Install the heater water hose fittings.

Install the turbocharger inlet duct.

Install the engine coolant supply and overflow hose.

Install the exhaust manifold heat shield, air cleaner mounting bracket 
and engine oil pressure (EOP) gauge line assembly and two bolts. Install the 
EOP gauge line fitting. Connect the EOP gauge line.

[FIGURE: DA1844A.gif]

Apply Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A to the engine 
coolant temperature (ECT) sensor and fitting threads. Install the engine 
coolant temperature (ECT) fitting and sensor.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is not equipped with an A/C system, perform this step.

Install the idler pulley and bolts.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with an A/C system, perform this step.

Install the A/C compressor, washers and bolts. Tighten the bolts to 
40-55 Nm (30-40 lb-ft).

Install the generator, bolts, new lockwashers, flatwasher and nut.

Install the cooling fan and hub. For additional information, refer to 
 Section 03E-03 .

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with hydraulic brakes, perform this step.

Install the brake pump and bracket assembly and bolts. Tighten the 
bolts to 45-65 Nm (33-47 lb-ft).

Install the accessory drive belt(s).

Install the oil fill tube bracket, nuts and washers.

Install the oil fill tube, bolt, washer and nut. Tighten the hose clamp.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with air brakes, perform steps 18 through 21.

Install the air compressor mounting block and bolts. Tighten the bolt 
to 60-95 Nm (44-70 lb-ft).

Install the fitting and air compressor oil supply line.

Install a new air compressor gasket, air compressor and power steering 
pump assembly, two nuts and bolts. Install the air compressor oil return line 
fitting in the oil pan. Connect the air compressor oil return and supply 
lines. Tighten the nuts to 60-95 Nm (44-70 lb-ft). Tighten the bolts to 
54-82 Nm (40-60 lb-ft).

Apply Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A to the threads. 
Install the air compressor coolant line fittings. Connect the air compressor 
coolant lines.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with hydraulic brakes, perform this step.

Install a new power steering pump gasket, power steering pump, and 
nuts. Tighten the nuts to 60-95 Nm (44-70 lb-ft).

Install the engine oil dipstick tube, nut and bolt.

Install the starter motor and bolts. Tighten the bolts to 40-64 
Nm (30-46 lb-ft).

Install the battery cable bracket and bolt at the flywheel housing.

Install the air cleaner brace and bolt on the air intake duct.

Install the check valve, fitting, and fuel lines as noted.

[FIGURE: DA1843A.gif]

Install the tachometer sensor.

 NOTE: If the vehicle is equipped with a manual transmission, perform this step.

Install the clutch. For additional information, refer to Section 08-01 
in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Install the transmission, For additional information, refer to the 
appropriate Group 07 transmission section in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, 
Drivetrain Service Manual.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Hose, Upper

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery negative cable(s).

Drain the engine coolant. For additional information, refer to Section 03-03 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Remove the air cleaner inlet tube.

Loosen clamp retaining rubber extension hose to upper radiator hose neck.

Loosen clamp retaining rubber extension hose to thermostat housing. 
Remove upper radiator hose from vehicle.

Loosen clamps retaining rubber extension hoses to upper radiator hose 
tube. Replace upper radiator hose components as needed.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten clamps to 9-11 Nm (80-97 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Lower Hose Tube

 Removal 

 NOTE: Replace the cooling system tubes whenever they become damaged or 
deteriorated.

Disconnect battery negative cable(s).

Drain cooling system. For additional information, refer to Section 03-03 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

Loosen clamp retaining heater return hose to lower radiator hose tube. 
Remove heater hose from tube.

Loosen clamp retaining rubber extension hose to lower radiator hose neck.

Loosen clamp retaining rubber extension hose to the water inlet

tube. Replace lower radiator hose components as needed.

Tighten clamps to 9-11 Nm (80-97 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator

 Removal 

 NOTE: When removing the radiator, the tilt hood must be supported.

Drain the cooling system. For additional information, refer to Section 03-03 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual.

If the vehicle is equipped with air conditioning, recover the 
refrigerant. For additional information, refer to Section 12-00 in the 1998 F 
and B Body, Chassis Service Manual.

Support the hood. Disconnect the spring-loaded hood support cables.

On a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission, loosen the 
retaining clamp and disconnect lower radiator hose at the radiator.

On a vehicle equipped with a manual transmission, remove the radiator 
lower hose as outlined in this section.

Remove the radiator upper hose as outlined in this section.

Loosen retaining clamp and disconnect the vent hose at the radiator 
coolant recovery reservoir.

Loosen retaining clamp and disconnect coolant supply hose at the 
reservoir.

Loosen retaining clamp and disconnect radiator expansion hose at the 
reservoir.

Disconnect the reservoir overflow hose.

Disconnect the low coolant level warning sensor wire connector.

Remove the four retaining screws and the reservoir.

If the vehicle is equipped with air conditioning, remove the nut 
retaining the air conditioner lines to the radiator.

If the vehicle is equipped with air conditioning, disconnect the A/C 
lines from the condenser. For additional information, refer to Section 12-03A 
in the 1998 F and B Body, Chassis Service Manual.

Remove retaining screws and fan shroud.

Loosen clamps and disconnect the tubes at charge air cooler.

Remove the nuts and bolts retaining the radiator support brackets to 
the radiator support braces and the radiator support. Remove the radiator 
support brackets.

Remove the retaining nuts and the power steering fluid reservoir from 
the radiator. Support the power steering reservoir.

Attach lifting equipment to the radiator. Remove the four radiator top 
bolts. Loosen the two radiator lower bolts.

Carefully remove the foam padding from the bottom of the radiator.

With an assistant, lift and remove the radiator from the vehicle.

 Installation 

Follow the removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten the radiator mounting bolts to 75-102 Nm (55-75 lb-ft).

Tighten the power steering reservoir nuts to 49 Nm (36 lb-ft).

Tighten the radiator support bracket nuts and bolts to 49 Nm (36 
lb-ft).

Tighten the charge air cooler tube clamps to 12 Nm (9 lb-ft).

Tighten fan shroud screws to 11 Nm (8 lb-ft).

Tighten the nut retaining the A/C lines to the radiator to 49 Nm 
(36 lb-ft).

Tighten radiator coolant recovery reservoir screws to 11 Nm (8 
lb-ft).

Tighten the radiator hose clamps to 9-11 Nm (80-97 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Coolant Recovery Reservoir

 WARNING: DO NOT STAND IN LINE WITH OR NEAR RADIATOR COOLING FAN WHEN REVVING 
ENGINE. 

 Removal 

Drain the radiator until the coolant is out of the radiator coolant 
recovery reservoir.

Loosen retaining clamp and disconnect coolant supply hose at the 
reservoir.

Loosen retaining clamp and disconnect vent hose at the reservoir.

Loosen the retaining clamp and disconnect radiator expansion tube at 
the reservoir.

Disconnect the overflow tube from the reservoir.

Remove the four retaining screws and the reservoir.

 Installation 

Follow the removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten reservoir retaining screws to 11 Nm (8 lb-ft).

Tighten clamps to 9-11 Nm (80-97 lb-in).

Fill and bleed the cooling system. For additional information, refer to 
 Section 03-03 in the 1998 F and B Powertrain, Drivetrain Service Manual. Check 
for coolant leaks and proper coolant level after the engine has reached normal 
operating temperatures.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fan and Clutch 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Fan Clutch Pulley Holder

T84T-6312-C

Fan Clutch Nut Wrench

T83T-6312-B

 Removal 

Remove the fan shroud.

 CAUTION: The clutch assembly nut has a left-hand thread and must be rotated 
clockwise for removal. 

Remove the clutch assembly from the fan clutch adapter by turning the 
nut, which is part of the clutch, using Fan Clutch Pulley Holder T84T-6312-C 
and Fan Clutch Nut Wrench T83T-6312-B. 

Remove the fan and clutch as an assembly. 

Remove the bolts or nuts attaching the fan to the clutch, if necessary. 

 Installation 

Install the bolts or nuts attaching the fan to the clutch. Tighten to 
34-40 Nm (25-30 lb-ft). 

 CAUTION: The clutch assembly nut has a left-hand thread and must be rotated 
counterclockwise for tightening. 

Install the clutch/fan assembly on the fan clutch adapter by turning 
the large nut, which is part of the clutch. Tighten to 89-111 Nm (66-82 
lb-ft) using Fan Clutch Pulley Holder T84T-6312-C and Fan Clutch Nut Wrench 
T83T-6312-B. 

Install the fan shroud.

 Removal 

Remove the fan shroud.

 CAUTION: The clutch assembly nut has a left-hand thread and must be rotated 
clockwise for removal. 

Remove the clutch assembly from the fan clutch adapter by turning the 
nut, which is part of the clutch, using Fan Clutch Pulley Holder T84T-6312-C 
and Fan Clutch Nut Wrench T83T-6312-B.

Remove the fan and clutch as an assembly.

Remove fan clutch adapter retaining bolts and adapter.

Remove accessory drive pulley, if so equipped, and fan pulley.

Remove bolts securing fan drive to cylinder block.

Remove bolt securing fan bearing retainer and pulley to fan spacer.

Remove fan bearing retainer and spacer.

Remove snap ring and remove bearing.

 Installation 

Install bearing and snap ring.

Install spacer, bearing retainer and bolt. Tighten bolt securely.

Position fan drive to cylinder block and install bolts. Tighten bolts 
securely.

Install fan pulley first, then accessory drive pulley and fan clutch 
adapter onto pulley-to-fan spacer.

Align holes in pulleys, adapter and spacer and install bolts. Tighten 
bolt securely.

 CAUTION: The clutch assembly nut has a left-hand thread and must be rotated 
counterclockwise for tightening. 

Install the clutch/fan assembly on the fan clutch adapter by turning 
the large nut, which is part of the clutch. Tighten to 89-111 Nm (66-82 
lb-ft) using Fan Clutch Pulley Holder T84T-6312-C and Fan Clutch Nut Wrench 
T83T-6312-B.

Install the fan shroud.

Section 03E-12: Air Intake, Cummins B5.9 Encore Diesel Engine

1999 F800 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Induction System

Air is pulled into the engine through an air filter. Clean air is very 
important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt can damage the 
cylinders very quickly. 

On turbocharged and aftercooled engines, the intake airflow is from the 
air cleaner to the turbocharger. It is then routed to the charge air cooler 
located in front of the radiator. Air leaves the charge air cooler and is 
routed to the intake manifold where it is forced into the cylinders and used 
for combustion. The charge air cooler reduces the temperature of the intake 
air, which lowers combustion chamber temperatures, which in turn reduces NOx 
emissions. Also, cooling the intake air makes it more dense, allowing more 
fuel to be injected into the engine to increase the power-to-weight ratio.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Charge Air Cooler

 Removal 

Remove the hood support and rest hood on a suitable surface.

Remove the condenser line retainers at RH side of the radiator.

Rest air conditioning condenser on front chassis.

Remove oil cooler hose retainer and fasteners and rest oil cooler on 
front chassis.

Disconnect charge air cooler inlet and outlet tubes.

Remove charge air cooler to radiator fasteners.

Tilt charge air cooler toward front of vehicle and remove.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.
